title: 1 John 1:1–4
context: The apostle testifies to what was from the beginning: the Word of life, heard, seen, looked upon, and touched. That eternal life was with the Father and has been made manifest, so that hearers may have fellowship with the apostolic company—and that fellowship is with the Father and His Son Jesus Christ. He writes that joy may be complete.
text: 1 John 1:1–4 1 John The apostle testifies to what was from the beginning: the Word of life, heard, seen, looked upon, and touched. That eternal life was with the Father and has been made manifest, so that hearers may have fellowship with the apostolic company—and that fellowship is with the Father and His Son Jesus Christ. He writes that joy may be complete. That which was from the beginning, that which we have heard, that which we have seen with our eyes, that which we saw, and our hands touched, concerning the Word of life 1 John 1:1 (and the life was revealed, and we have seen, and testify, and declare to you the life, the eternal life, which was with the Father, and was revealed to us); 1 John 1:2 that which we have seen and heard we declare to you, that you also may have fellowship with us. Yes, and our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ. 1 John 1:3 And we write these things to you, that our joy may be fulfilled. 1 John 1:4

title: 1 John 1:5–10
context: The message heard from Him is that God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all. Fellowship-talk while walking in darkness is a lie; walking in the light brings fellowship and cleansing by the Son’s blood. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves; if we confess, He is faithful and righteous to forgive and to cleanse. Claiming we have not sinned makes Him a liar.
text: 1 John 1:5–10 1 John The message heard from Him is that God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all. Fellowship-talk while walking in darkness is a lie; walking in the light brings fellowship and cleansing by the Son’s blood. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves; if we confess, He is faithful and righteous to forgive and to cleanse. Claiming we have not sinned makes Him a liar. This is the message which we have heard from him and announce to you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. 1 John 1:5 If we say that we have fellowship with him and walk in the darkness, we lie and don’t tell the truth. 1 John 1:6 But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin. 1 John 1:7 If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. 1 John 1:8 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. 1 John 1:9 If we say that we haven’t sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us. 1 John 1:10

title: 1 John 2:1–6
context: John writes so that they may not sin—and if anyone does sin, they have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous, the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only but for the whole world. Knowing him is proved by keeping his commandments; the one who claims to abide in him must walk as he walked.
text: 1 John 2:1–6 1 John John writes so that they may not sin—and if anyone does sin, they have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous, the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only but for the whole world. Knowing him is proved by keeping his commandments; the one who claims to abide in him must walk as he walked. My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous. 1 John 2:1 And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world. 1 John 2:2 This is how we know that we know him: if we keep his commandments. 1 John 2:3 One who says, “I know him,” and doesn’t keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth isn’t in him. 1 John 2:4 But God’s love has most certainly been perfected in whoever keeps his word. This is how we know that we are in him: 1 John 2:5 he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked. 1 John 2:6

title: 1 John 2:15–17
context: John warns his readers not to love the world, meaning the system of desire and pride that sets itself against God. Craving, greed of the eyes, and boastful pride do not come from the Father. The world is passing away, but the one who does God’s will lasts forever.
text: 1 John 2:15–17 1 John John warns his readers not to love the world, meaning the system of desire and pride that sets itself against God. Craving, greed of the eyes, and boastful pride do not come from the Father. The world is passing away, but the one who does God’s will lasts forever. Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him. 1 John 2:15 For all that is in the world—the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life—isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s. 1 John 2:16 The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever. 1 John 2:17

title: 1 John 2:18–27
context: These are the end times: antichrist was heard of, and many antichrists have come. They went out from us but were not of us; had they been, they would have continued. The anointing from the Holy One teaches. The liar denies that Jesus is the Christ, denying Father and Son. What was heard from the beginning must abide—and with it, the promise of eternal life. Abide in Him.
text: 1 John 2:18–27 1 John These are the end times: antichrist was heard of, and many antichrists have come. They went out from us but were not of us; had they been, they would have continued. The anointing from the Holy One teaches. The liar denies that Jesus is the Christ, denying Father and Son. What was heard from the beginning must abide—and with it, the promise of eternal life. Abide in Him. Little children, these are the end times, and as you heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have arisen. By this we know that it is the final hour. 1 John 2:18 They went out from us, but they didn’t belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have continued with us. But they left, that they might be revealed that none of them belong to us. 1 John 2:19 You have an anointing from the Holy One, and you all have knowledge. 1 John 2:20 I have not written to you because you don’t know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is of the truth. 1 John 2:21 Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, he who denies the Father and the Son. 1 John 2:22 Whoever denies the Son doesn’t have the Father. He who confesses the Son has the Father also. 1 John 2:23 Therefore, as for you, let that remain in you which you heard from the beginning. If that which you heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son, and in the Father. 1 John 2:24 This is the promise which he promised us, the eternal life. 1 John 2:25 These things I have written to you concerning those who would lead you astray. 1 John 2:26 As for you, the anointing which you received from him remains in you, and you don’t need for anyone to teach you. But as his anointing teaches you concerning all things, and is true, and is no lie, and even as it taught you, you will remain in him. 1 John 2:27

title: 1 John 2:28–29
context: John gathers the whole church again as little children and repeats the charge of verse 27: remain in him. The reason looks forward to Christ’s appearing, when those who remain will have boldness instead of shame. Verse 29 then opens the next movement of the letter. Because God is righteous, a life that practices righteousness shows the family likeness of those born of him.
text: 1 John 2:28–29 1 John John gathers the whole church again as little children and repeats the charge of verse 27: remain in him. The reason looks forward to Christ’s appearing, when those who remain will have boldness instead of shame. Verse 29 then opens the next movement of the letter. Because God is righteous, a life that practices righteousness shows the family likeness of those born of him. Now, little children, remain in him, that when he appears, we may have boldness and not be ashamed before him at his coming. 1 John 2:28 If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him. 1 John 2:29

title: 1 John 2:7–14
context: The commandment is old—from the beginning—and new, true in Him and in them, because the darkness is passing and the true light is shining. Love of the brother remains in the light; hatred walks blind. John writes to children, fathers, and young men: sins forgiven, the One from the beginning known, the evil one overcome, the Father known, the word abiding.
text: 1 John 2:7–14 1 John The commandment is old—from the beginning—and new, true in Him and in them, because the darkness is passing and the true light is shining. Love of the brother remains in the light; hatred walks blind. John writes to children, fathers, and young men: sins forgiven, the One from the beginning known, the evil one overcome, the Father known, the word abiding. Brothers, I write no new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning. 1 John 2:7 Again, I write a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines. 1 John 2:8 He who says he is in the light and hates his brother is in the darkness even until now. 1 John 2:9 He who loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no occasion for stumbling in him. 1 John 2:10 But he who hates his brother is in the darkness, and walks in the darkness, and doesn’t know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes. 1 John 2:11 I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name’s sake. 1 John 2:12 I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, little children, because you know the Father. 1 John 2:13 I have written to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one. 1 John 2:14

title: 1 John 3:1–10
context: See how great a love the Father has given: we are called children of God, and that is what we are. What we will be has not appeared; we will be like him when He appears. Everyone who hopes in Him purifies himself. Whoever remains in Him does not go on sinning; whoever is born of God does not live in sin, because God’s seed remains in him. By this the children of God are revealed, and of the devil are evident.
text: 1 John 3:1–10 1 John See how great a love the Father has given: we are called children of God, and that is what we are. What we will be has not appeared; we will be like him when He appears. Everyone who hopes in Him purifies himself. Whoever remains in Him does not go on sinning; whoever is born of God does not live in sin, because God’s seed remains in him. By this the children of God are revealed, and of the devil are evident. See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him. 1 John 3:1 Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is. 1 John 3:2 Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure. 1 John 3:3 Everyone who sins also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness. 1 John 3:4 You know that he was revealed to take away our sins, and no sin is in him. 1 John 3:5 Whoever remains in him doesn’t sin. Whoever sins hasn’t seen him and doesn’t know him. 1 John 3:6 Little children, let no one lead you astray. He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous. 1 John 3:7 He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. To this end the Son of God was revealed: that he might destroy the works of the devil. 1 John 3:8 Whoever is born of God doesn’t commit sin, because his seed remains in him, and he can’t sin, because he is born of God. 1 John 3:9 In this the children of God are revealed, and the children of the devil. Whoever doesn’t do righteousness is not of God, neither is he who doesn’t love his brother. 1 John 3:10

title: 1 John 3:11–24
context: The message from the beginning is that we should love one another—not as Cain. Love of the brothers is how we know we have passed from death to life. He laid down His life for us; we ought to lay down ours, and open our goods to the brother in need. Love in deed and truth reassures the heart. The commandment is to believe in the name of His Son and love one another. We know He abides by the Spirit He has given.
text: 1 John 3:11–24 1 John The message from the beginning is that we should love one another—not as Cain. Love of the brothers is how we know we have passed from death to life. He laid down His life for us; we ought to lay down ours, and open our goods to the brother in need. Love in deed and truth reassures the heart. The commandment is to believe in the name of His Son and love one another. We know He abides by the Spirit He has given. For this is the message which you heard from the beginning, that we should love one another— 1 John 3:11 unlike Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. Why did he kill him? Because his deeds were evil, and his brother’s righteous. 1 John 3:12 Don’t be surprised, my brothers, if the world hates you. 1 John 3:13 We know that we have passed out of death into life, because we love the brothers. He who doesn’t love his brother remains in death. 1 John 3:14 Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him. 1 John 3:15 By this we know love, because he laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. 1 John 3:16 But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him? 1 John 3:17 My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth. 1 John 3:18 And by this we know that we are of the truth and persuade our hearts before him, 1 John 3:19 because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things. 1 John 3:20 Beloved, if our hearts don’t condemn us, we have boldness toward God; 1 John 3:21 so whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do the things that are pleasing in his sight. 1 John 3:22 This is his commandment, that we should believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, even as he commanded. 1 John 3:23 He who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him. By this we know that he remains in us, by the Spirit which he gave us. 1 John 3:24

title: 1 John 4:1–6
context: Do not believe every spirit; test the spirits, because many false prophets have gone out. Every spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God; the one that does not is the spirit of antichrist already in the world. The children of God have overcome them, because He who is in them is greater. The world listens to its own; whoever knows God listens to the apostolic testimony.
text: 1 John 4:1–6 1 John Do not believe every spirit; test the spirits, because many false prophets have gone out. Every spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God; the one that does not is the spirit of antichrist already in the world. The children of God have overcome them, because He who is in them is greater. The world listens to its own; whoever knows God listens to the apostolic testimony. Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. 1 John 4:1 By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God, 1 John 4:2 and every spirit who doesn’t confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God; and this is the spirit of the Antichrist, of whom you have heard that it comes. Now it is in the world already. 1 John 4:3 You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world. 1 John 4:4 They are of the world. Therefore they speak of the world, and the world hears them. 1 John 4:5 We are of God. He who knows God listens to us. He who is not of God doesn’t listen to us. By this we know the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error. 1 John 4:6

title: 1 John 4:7–21
context: Beloved, let’s love one another: love is of God; and God is love. His love was made manifest in sending His only born Son into the world as the atoning sacrifice for our sins, the Savior of the world. We love him, because he first loved us; whoever loves God should also love his brother. Fear is cast out where love is perfected.
text: 1 John 4:7–21 1 John Beloved, let’s love one another: love is of God; and God is love. His love was made manifest in sending His only born Son into the world as the atoning sacrifice for our sins, the Savior of the world. We love him, because he first loved us; whoever loves God should also love his brother. Fear is cast out where love is perfected. Beloved, let’s love one another, for love is of God; and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God. 1 John 4:7 He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love. 1 John 4:8 By this God’s love was revealed in us, that God has sent his only born Son into the world that we might live through him. 1 John 4:9 In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins. 1 John 4:10 Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another. 1 John 4:11 No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us. 1 John 4:12 By this we know that we remain in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. 1 John 4:13 We have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as the Savior of the world. 1 John 4:14 Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God. 1 John 4:15 We know and have believed the love which God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him. 1 John 4:16 In this, love has been made perfect among us, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment, because as he is, even so we are in this world. 1 John 4:17 There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment. He who fears is not made perfect in love. 1 John 4:18 We love him, because he first loved us. 1 John 4:19 If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen? 1 John 4:20 This commandment we have from him, that he who loves God should also love his brother. 1 John 4:21

title: 1 John 5:1–12
context: John ties together faith, love, and obedience: everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ is born of God and loves God’s children. Faith overcomes the world. Water, blood, and Spirit testify to the Son, and God’s testimony is that eternal life is found in him: whoever has the Son has life.
text: 1 John 5:1–12 1 John John ties together faith, love, and obedience: everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ is born of God and loves God’s children. Faith overcomes the world. Water, blood, and Spirit testify to the Son, and God’s testimony is that eternal life is found in him: whoever has the Son has life. Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him. 1 John 5:1 By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and keep his commandments. 1 John 5:2 For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous. 1 John 5:3 For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith. 1 John 5:4 Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? 1 John 5:5 This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and the blood. It is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth. 1 John 5:6 For there are three who testify: 1 John 5:7 the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and the three agree as one. 1 John 5:8 If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater; for this is God’s testimony which he has testified concerning his Son. 1 John 5:9 He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. He who doesn’t believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has given concerning his Son. 1 John 5:10 The testimony is this: that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. 1 John 5:11 He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life. 1 John 5:12

title: 1 John 5:13–21
context: John writes to those who believe in the name of the Son of God, that they may know they have eternal life. Confidence in prayer according to His will; a brother sinning not unto death may be asked for; there is sin leading to death. The one born of God does not go on sinning; we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one. The Son has come and given understanding: This is the true God and eternal life. Keep yourselves from idols.
text: 1 John 5:13–21 1 John John writes to those who believe in the name of the Son of God, that they may know they have eternal life. Confidence in prayer according to His will; a brother sinning not unto death may be asked for; there is sin leading to death. The one born of God does not go on sinning; we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one. The Son has come and given understanding: This is the true God and eternal life. Keep yourselves from idols. These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God. 1 John 5:13 This is the boldness which we have toward him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he listens to us. 1 John 5:14 And if we know that he listens to us, whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions which we have asked of him. 1 John 5:15 If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life for those who sin not leading to death. There is sin leading to death. I don’t say that he should make a request concerning this. 1 John 5:16 All unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin not leading to death. 1 John 5:17 We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin, but he who was born of God keeps himself, and the evil one doesn’t touch him. 1 John 5:18 We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one. 1 John 5:19 We know that the Son of God has come and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true; and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life. 1 John 5:20 Little children, keep yourselves from idols. 1 John 5:21

title: 1 Timothy 1:1–2
context: Paul greets Timothy as his true child in faith, calling himself an apostle by the order of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ, our hope. The blessing adds mercy to grace and peace—a tender word for a young minister standing in a hard charge.
text: 1 Timothy 1:1–2 1 Timothy Paul greets Timothy as his true child in faith, calling himself an apostle by the order of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ, our hope. The blessing adds mercy to grace and peace—a tender word for a young minister standing in a hard charge. Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ according to the commandment of God our Savior and the Lord Jesus Christ our hope, 1 Timothy 1:1 to Timothy, my true child in faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. 1 Timothy 1:2

title: 1 Timothy 1:12–17
context: Paul thanks Christ Jesus who strengthened him and appointed him to service, though he had been a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent opponent. Mercy met his ignorant unbelief; grace overflowed with faith and love; and the trustworthy saying is that Christ came to save sinners—Paul the foremost, a pattern of perfect patience for those who would believe—crowned with doxology to the King of the ages.
text: 1 Timothy 1:12–17 1 Timothy Paul thanks Christ Jesus who strengthened him and appointed him to service, though he had been a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent opponent. Mercy met his ignorant unbelief; grace overflowed with faith and love; and the trustworthy saying is that Christ came to save sinners—Paul the foremost, a pattern of perfect patience for those who would believe—crowned with doxology to the King of the ages. I thank him who enabled me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to service, 1 Timothy 1:12 although I used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor, and insolent. However, I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief. 1 Timothy 1:13 The grace of our Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus. 1 Timothy 1:14 The saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief. 1 Timothy 1:15 However, for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first, Jesus Christ might display all his patience for an example of those who were going to believe in him for eternal life. 1 Timothy 1:16 Now to the King eternal, immortal, invisible, to God who alone is wise, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen. 1 Timothy 1:17

title: 1 Timothy 1:18–20
context: Paul entrusts this charge to Timothy in line with earlier prophecies, that he may wage the good warfare, holding faith and a good conscience. Some have shipwrecked that faith; Hymenaeus and Alexander are named, handed over to Satan that they might be taught not to blaspheme.
text: 1 Timothy 1:18–20 1 Timothy Paul entrusts this charge to Timothy in line with earlier prophecies, that he may wage the good warfare, holding faith and a good conscience. Some have shipwrecked that faith; Hymenaeus and Alexander are named, handed over to Satan that they might be taught not to blaspheme. I commit this instruction to you, my child Timothy, according to the prophecies which were given to you before, that by them you may wage the good warfare, 1 Timothy 1:18 holding faith and a good conscience, which some having thrust away made a shipwreck concerning the faith, 1 Timothy 1:19 of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I delivered to Satan that they might be taught not to blaspheme. 1 Timothy 1:20

title: 1 Timothy 1:3–11
context: Paul reminds Timothy why he remained at Ephesus: to command certain men not to teach a different doctrine or lose themselves in myths and endless genealogies. The aim of the charge is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith; the law is good when used lawfully, and sound doctrine accords with the gospel of the blessed God’s glory.
text: 1 Timothy 1:3–11 1 Timothy Paul reminds Timothy why he remained at Ephesus: to command certain men not to teach a different doctrine or lose themselves in myths and endless genealogies. The aim of the charge is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith; the law is good when used lawfully, and sound doctrine accords with the gospel of the blessed God’s glory. As I urged you when I was going into Macedonia, stay at Ephesus that you might command certain men not to teach a different doctrine, 1 Timothy 1:3 and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies, which cause disputes rather than God’s stewardship, which is in faith. 1 Timothy 1:4 But the goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith, 1 Timothy 1:5 from which things some, having missed the mark, have turned away to vain talking, 1 Timothy 1:6 desiring to be teachers of the law, though they understand neither what they say nor about what they strongly affirm. 1 Timothy 1:7 But we know that the law is good if a person uses it lawfully, 1 Timothy 1:8 as knowing this, that law is not made for a righteous person, but for the lawless and insubordinate, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, 1 Timothy 1:9 for the sexually immoral, for homosexuals, for slave-traders, for liars, for perjurers, and for any other thing contrary to the sound doctrine, 1 Timothy 1:10 according to the Good News of the glory of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust. 1 Timothy 1:11

title: 1 Timothy 2:1–7
context: Paul turns from charge to Timothy toward the church’s public life: first of all, pray for all people, including kings, so that a quiet, godly life may flourish. The reason is soteriological and Christological: God our Savior desires all people to be saved; there is one mediator, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all—the testimony Paul was appointed to preach among the Gentiles.
text: 1 Timothy 2:1–7 1 Timothy Paul turns from charge to Timothy toward the church’s public life: first of all, pray for all people, including kings, so that a quiet, godly life may flourish. The reason is soteriological and Christological: God our Savior desires all people to be saved; there is one mediator, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all—the testimony Paul was appointed to preach among the Gentiles. I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men, 1 Timothy 2:1 for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence. 1 Timothy 2:2 For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, 1 Timothy 2:3 who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth. 1 Timothy 2:4 For there is one God and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, 1 Timothy 2:5 who gave himself as a ransom for all, the testimony at the proper time, 1 Timothy 2:6 to which I was appointed a preacher and an apostle—I am telling the truth in Christ, not lying—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth. 1 Timothy 2:7

title: 1 Timothy 2:8–15
context: From prayer for all people Paul turns to how the gathered church should look: men praying in every place without anger or quarreling; women adorned with modesty, self-control, and good works rather than display. A woman is to learn quietly; Paul does not permit her to teach or exercise authority over a man, grounding the charge in Adam formed first and Eve deceived, then adding the hard pastoral word that she will be saved through her childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with self-control.
text: 1 Timothy 2:8–15 1 Timothy From prayer for all people Paul turns to how the gathered church should look: men praying in every place without anger or quarreling; women adorned with modesty, self-control, and good works rather than display. A woman is to learn quietly; Paul does not permit her to teach or exercise authority over a man, grounding the charge in Adam formed first and Eve deceived, then adding the hard pastoral word that she will be saved through her childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with self-control. I desire therefore that the men in every place pray, lifting up holy hands without anger and doubting. 1 Timothy 2:8 In the same way, that women also adorn themselves in decent clothing, with modesty and propriety, not with braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothing, 1 Timothy 2:9 but with good works, which is appropriate for women professing godliness. 1 Timothy 2:10 Let a woman learn in quietness with full submission. 1 Timothy 2:11 But I don’t permit a woman to teach, nor to exercise authority over a man, but to be in quietness. 1 Timothy 2:12 For Adam was formed first, then Eve. 1 Timothy 2:13 Adam wasn’t deceived, but the woman, being deceived, has fallen into disobedience; 1 Timothy 2:14 but she will be saved through her childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness with sobriety. 1 Timothy 2:15

title: 1 Timothy 3:1–7
context: Paul turns from household prayer to household office: the saying is trustworthy that aspiring to overseer is desiring a noble task. The overseer must be above reproach—a one-woman man, sober, hospitable, good at teaching; not violent or greedy—managing his own house well, not a recent convert, and well thought of by outsiders, lest he fall into the devil’s snare.
text: 1 Timothy 3:1–7 1 Timothy Paul turns from household prayer to household office: the saying is trustworthy that aspiring to overseer is desiring a noble task. The overseer must be above reproach—a one-woman man, sober, hospitable, good at teaching; not violent or greedy—managing his own house well, not a recent convert, and well thought of by outsiders, lest he fall into the devil’s snare. This is a faithful saying: someone who seeks to be an overseer desires a good work. 1 Timothy 3:1 The overseer therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sensible, modest, hospitable, good at teaching; 1 Timothy 3:2 not a drinker, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous; 1 Timothy 3:3 one who rules his own house well, having children in subjection with all reverence; 1 Timothy 3:4 (for how could someone who doesn’t know how to rule his own house take care of God’s assembly?) 1 Timothy 3:5 not a new convert, lest being puffed up he fall into the same condemnation as the devil. 1 Timothy 3:6 Moreover he must have good testimony from those who are outside, to avoid falling into reproach and the snare of the devil. 1 Timothy 3:7

title: 1 Timothy 3:14–16
context: Paul explains why he is writing: so Timothy will know how to conduct himself in God’s household, the church that upholds the truth. He then cites what may be an early hymn about Christ, tracing his path from incarnation to ascension. Church order rests on the person and work of Christ.
text: 1 Timothy 3:14–16 1 Timothy Paul explains why he is writing: so Timothy will know how to conduct himself in God’s household, the church that upholds the truth. He then cites what may be an early hymn about Christ, tracing his path from incarnation to ascension. Church order rests on the person and work of Christ. These things I write to you, hoping to come to you shortly, 1 Timothy 3:14 but if I wait long, that you may know how men ought to behave themselves in God’s house, which is the assembly of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. 1 Timothy 3:15 Without controversy, the mystery of godliness is great: God was revealed in the flesh, justified in the spirit, seen by angels, preached among the nations, believed on in the world, and received up in glory. 1 Timothy 3:16

title: 1 Timothy 3:8–13
context: Deacons likewise must be dignified, truthful in speech, free of wine and dishonest gain, holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. They are tested first, then they serve. Their wives (or the women) must be dignified and faithful; deacons too are one-woman men who manage households well. Those who serve well gain a good standing and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
text: 1 Timothy 3:8–13 1 Timothy Deacons likewise must be dignified, truthful in speech, free of wine and dishonest gain, holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. They are tested first, then they serve. Their wives (or the women) must be dignified and faithful; deacons too are one-woman men who manage households well. Those who serve well gain a good standing and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus. Servants, in the same way, must be reverent, not double-tongued, not addicted to much wine, not greedy for money, 1 Timothy 3:8 holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. 1 Timothy 3:9 Let them also first be tested; then let them serve if they are blameless. 1 Timothy 3:10 Their wives in the same way must be reverent, not slanderers, temperate, and faithful in all things. 1 Timothy 3:11 Let servants be husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well. 1 Timothy 3:12 For those who have served well gain for themselves a good standing and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus. 1 Timothy 3:13

title: 1 Timothy 4:1–5
context: Paul warns that the Spirit has expressly foretold a departure from the faith in later times, driven by deceiving spirits and teaching from liars whose consciences are seared. Their rules forbid marriage and certain foods. Paul answers that everything God created is good and is to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth, because it is made holy by God’s word and prayer.
text: 1 Timothy 4:1–5 1 Timothy Paul warns that the Spirit has expressly foretold a departure from the faith in later times, driven by deceiving spirits and teaching from liars whose consciences are seared. Their rules forbid marriage and certain foods. Paul answers that everything God created is good and is to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth, because it is made holy by God’s word and prayer. But the Spirit says expressly that in later times some will fall away from the faith, paying attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons, 1 Timothy 4:1 through the hypocrisy of men who speak lies, branded in their own conscience as with a hot iron, 1 Timothy 4:2 forbidding marriage and commanding to abstain from foods which God created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth. 1 Timothy 4:3 For every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving. 1 Timothy 4:4 For it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer. 1 Timothy 4:5

title: 1 Timothy 4:6–16
context: Timothy will be a good servant of Christ Jesus if he reminds the brothers of these things, nourished in the words of the faith and of good doctrine. He is to refuse irreverent myths, train for godliness, and set his hope on the living God, the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe. He must command and teach, be an example despite youth, devote himself to public reading, exhortation, and teaching, not neglect the gift given by prophecy with the elders’ hands, practice these things, and watch himself and the teaching—so saving himself and his hearers.
text: 1 Timothy 4:6–16 1 Timothy Timothy will be a good servant of Christ Jesus if he reminds the brothers of these things, nourished in the words of the faith and of good doctrine. He is to refuse irreverent myths, train for godliness, and set his hope on the living God, the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe. He must command and teach, be an example despite youth, devote himself to public reading, exhortation, and teaching, not neglect the gift given by prophecy with the elders’ hands, practice these things, and watch himself and the teaching—so saving himself and his hearers. If you instruct the brothers of these things, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished in the words of the faith and of the good doctrine which you have followed. 1 Timothy 4:6 But refuse profane and old wives’ fables. Exercise yourself toward godliness. 1 Timothy 4:7 For bodily exercise has some value, but godliness has value in all things, having the promise of the life which is now and of that which is to come. 1 Timothy 4:8 This saying is faithful and worthy of all acceptance. 1 Timothy 4:9 For to this end we both labor and suffer reproach, because we have set our trust in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe. 1 Timothy 4:10 Command and teach these things. 1 Timothy 4:11 Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity. 1 Timothy 4:12 Until I come, pay attention to reading, to exhortation, and to teaching. 1 Timothy 4:13 Don’t neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the elders. 1 Timothy 4:14 Be diligent in these things. Give yourself wholly to them, that your progress may be revealed to all. 1 Timothy 4:15 Pay attention to yourself and to your teaching. Continue in these things, for in doing this you will save both yourself and those who hear you. 1 Timothy 4:16

title: 1 Timothy 5:1–8
context: Paul trains Timothy to treat the congregation as a household: older men as fathers, younger as brothers, women as mothers and sisters in all purity. He then honors true widows, insists that families provide first, and warns that neglect of one's own house is a denial of the faith.
text: 1 Timothy 5:1–8 1 Timothy Paul trains Timothy to treat the congregation as a household: older men as fathers, younger as brothers, women as mothers and sisters in all purity. He then honors true widows, insists that families provide first, and warns that neglect of one's own house is a denial of the faith. Don’t rebuke an older man, but exhort him as a father; the younger men as brothers; 1 Timothy 5:1 the elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, in all purity. 1 Timothy 5:2 Honor widows who are widows indeed. 1 Timothy 5:3 But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn first to show piety toward their own family and to repay their parents, for this is acceptable in the sight of God. 1 Timothy 5:4 Now she who is a widow indeed and desolate, has her hope set on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day. 1 Timothy 5:5 But she who gives herself to pleasure is dead while she lives. 1 Timothy 5:6 Also command these things, that they may be without reproach. 1 Timothy 5:7 But if anyone doesn’t provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. 1 Timothy 5:8

title: 1 Timothy 5:17–25
context: Paul moves from enrolled widows to elders: those who rule well, especially in preaching and teaching, are worthy of double honor, for Scripture forbids muzzling the ox and says the laborer is worthy of his wages. Charges need two or three witnesses; persistent sin is rebuked publicly; Timothy must not prejudge, not lay hands hastily, and remember that both sins and good works will come to light.
text: 1 Timothy 5:17–25 1 Timothy Paul moves from enrolled widows to elders: those who rule well, especially in preaching and teaching, are worthy of double honor, for Scripture forbids muzzling the ox and says the laborer is worthy of his wages. Charges need two or three witnesses; persistent sin is rebuked publicly; Timothy must not prejudge, not lay hands hastily, and remember that both sins and good works will come to light. Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching. 1 Timothy 5:17 For the Scripture says, “You shall not muzzle the ox when it treads out the grain.” And, “The laborer is worthy of his wages.” 1 Timothy 5:18 Don’t receive an accusation against an elder except at the word of two or three witnesses. 1 Timothy 5:19 Those who sin, reprove in the sight of all, that the rest also may be in fear. 1 Timothy 5:20 I command you in the sight of God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the chosen angels, that you observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by partiality. 1 Timothy 5:21 Lay hands hastily on no one. Don’t be a participant in other people’s sins. Keep yourself pure. 1 Timothy 5:22 Be no longer a drinker of water only, but use a little wine for your stomach’s sake and your frequent infirmities. 1 Timothy 5:23 Some men’s sins are evident, preceding them to judgment, and some also follow later. 1 Timothy 5:24 In the same way also there are good works that are obvious, and those that are otherwise can’t be hidden. 1 Timothy 5:25

title: 1 Timothy 5:9–16
context: Paul sets an enrollment for older widows of proven life—one-husband faithfulness, hospitality, care for the afflicted—while refusing younger widows whose passions may pull them from a pledged service. He would have them marry and manage homes, and he keeps the church's burden for those who are truly widows.
text: 1 Timothy 5:9–16 1 Timothy Paul sets an enrollment for older widows of proven life—one-husband faithfulness, hospitality, care for the afflicted—while refusing younger widows whose passions may pull them from a pledged service. He would have them marry and manage homes, and he keeps the church's burden for those who are truly widows. Let no one be enrolled as a widow under sixty years old, having been the wife of one man, 1 Timothy 5:9 being approved by good works, if she has brought up children, if she has been hospitable to strangers, if she has washed the saints’ feet, if she has relieved the afflicted, and if she has diligently followed every good work. 1 Timothy 5:10 But refuse younger widows, for when they have grown wanton against Christ, they desire to marry, 1 Timothy 5:11 having condemnation, because they have rejected their first pledge. 1 Timothy 5:12 Besides, they also learn to be idle, going about from house to house. Not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, saying things which they ought not. 1 Timothy 5:13 I desire therefore that the younger widows marry, bear children, rule the household, and give no occasion to the adversary for insulting. 1 Timothy 5:14 For already some have turned away after Satan. 1 Timothy 5:15 If any man or woman who believes has widows, let them relieve them, and don’t let the assembly be burdened, that it might relieve those who are widows indeed. 1 Timothy 5:16

title: 1 Timothy 6:1–2
context: Paul addresses believers already living under a first-century yoke: honor masters so that God’s name and the teaching are not blasphemed. Those with believing masters must not despise them as mere equals; they should serve all the better, because those who benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
text: 1 Timothy 6:1–2 1 Timothy Paul addresses believers already living under a first-century yoke: honor masters so that God’s name and the teaching are not blasphemed. Those with believing masters must not despise them as mere equals; they should serve all the better, because those who benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things. Let as many as are bondservants under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine not be blasphemed. 1 Timothy 6:1 Those who have believing masters, let them not despise them because they are brothers, but rather let them serve them, because those who partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things. 1 Timothy 6:2

title: 1 Timothy 6:11–16
context: Timothy, addressed as a man of God, must flee greed and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, and gentleness. He is to fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which he was called, and keep the commandment unstained until Christ appears: before God who gives life to all things, and before the blessed and only Ruler.
text: 1 Timothy 6:11–16 1 Timothy Timothy, addressed as a man of God, must flee greed and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, steadfastness, and gentleness. He is to fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which he was called, and keep the commandment unstained until Christ appears: before God who gives life to all things, and before the blessed and only Ruler. But you, man of God, flee these things, and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness. 1 Timothy 6:11 Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, and you confessed the good confession in the sight of many witnesses. 1 Timothy 6:12 I command you before God who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus who before Pontius Pilate testified the good confession, 1 Timothy 6:13 that you keep the commandment without spot, blameless until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, 1 Timothy 6:14 which at the right time he will show, who is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords. 1 Timothy 6:15 He alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen nor can see, to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen. 1 Timothy 6:16

title: 1 Timothy 6:17–21
context: The rich in this present age must not be haughty or set their hope on uncertain riches, but on the living God, who richly provides everything to enjoy. They are to be rich in good works, generous, storing a foundation for the future, and so take hold of what is truly life. Timothy must guard the entrusted deposit, avoid irreverent babble falsely called knowledge, and remember that some have already wandered from the faith. Grace be with you.
text: 1 Timothy 6:17–21 1 Timothy The rich in this present age must not be haughty or set their hope on uncertain riches, but on the living God, who richly provides everything to enjoy. They are to be rich in good works, generous, storing a foundation for the future, and so take hold of what is truly life. Timothy must guard the entrusted deposit, avoid irreverent babble falsely called knowledge, and remember that some have already wandered from the faith. Grace be with you. Charge those who are rich in this present age that they not be arrogant, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy; 1 Timothy 6:17 that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to share; 1 Timothy 6:18 laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold of eternal life. 1 Timothy 6:19 Timothy, guard that which is committed to you, turning away from the empty chatter and oppositions of what is falsely called knowledge, 1 Timothy 6:20 which some profess, and thus have wandered from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen. 1 Timothy 6:21

title: 1 Timothy 6:3–10
context: Paul names the teacher who will not consent to the sound words of Jesus and to the doctrine which is according to godliness: conceit, controversy, and the fantasy that godliness is a means of gain. True gain is godliness with contentment; we brought nothing in and take nothing out. The love of money is a root of evils, and by that craving some have already wandered from the faith.
text: 1 Timothy 6:3–10 1 Timothy Paul names the teacher who will not consent to the sound words of Jesus and to the doctrine which is according to godliness: conceit, controversy, and the fantasy that godliness is a means of gain. True gain is godliness with contentment; we brought nothing in and take nothing out. The love of money is a root of evils, and by that craving some have already wandered from the faith. If anyone teaches a different doctrine and doesn’t consent to sound words, the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness, 1 Timothy 6:3 he is conceited, knowing nothing, but obsessed with arguments, disputes, and word battles, from which come envy, strife, insulting, evil suspicions, 1 Timothy 6:4 constant friction of people of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. Withdraw yourself from such. 1 Timothy 6:5 But godliness with contentment is great gain. 1 Timothy 6:6 For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out. 1 Timothy 6:7 But having food and clothing, we will be content with that. 1 Timothy 6:8 But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation, a snare, and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction. 1 Timothy 6:9 For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows. 1 Timothy 6:10

title: 2 John 1:1–6
context: The elder writes to the chosen lady and her children: love in the truth that abides forever; grace, mercy, and peace from the Father and the Father’s Son; joy that some of her children walk in the truth; then the old commandment, that we love one another. This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments.
text: 2 John 1:1–6 2 John The elder writes to the chosen lady and her children: love in the truth that abides forever; grace, mercy, and peace from the Father and the Father’s Son; joy that some of her children walk in the truth; then the old commandment, that we love one another. This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth, and not I only, but also all those who know the truth, 2 John 1:1 for the truth’s sake, which remains in us, and it will be with us forever: 2 John 1:2 Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us, from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love. 2 John 1:3 I rejoice greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, even as we have been commanded by the Father. 2 John 1:4 Now I beg you, dear lady, not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another. 2 John 1:5 This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it. 2 John 1:6

title: 2 John 1:7–13
context: The elder warns that many deceivers have gone out into the world, people who won’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh—the deceiver and the antichrist. Watch, so as not to lose what was worked for; whoever goes on ahead and doesn’t remain in the teaching of Christ doesn’t have God. Do not receive such a one into the house or greet him, or you take part in his wicked works. Then paper yields to the hope of face-to-face speech, and the elect sister’s children greet her.
text: 2 John 1:7–13 2 John The elder warns that many deceivers have gone out into the world, people who won’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh—the deceiver and the antichrist. Watch, so as not to lose what was worked for; whoever goes on ahead and doesn’t remain in the teaching of Christ doesn’t have God. Do not receive such a one into the house or greet him, or you take part in his wicked works. Then paper yields to the hope of face-to-face speech, and the elect sister’s children greet her. For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who don’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the Antichrist. 2 John 1:7 Watch yourselves, that we don’t lose the things which we have accomplished, but that we receive a full reward. 2 John 1:8 Whoever transgresses and doesn’t remain in the teaching of Christ doesn’t have God. He who remains in the teaching has both the Father and the Son. 2 John 1:9 If anyone comes to you and doesn’t bring this teaching, don’t receive him into your house, and don’t welcome him, 2 John 1:10 for he who welcomes him participates in his evil deeds. 2 John 1:11 Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you and to speak face to face, that our joy may be made full. 2 John 1:12 The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen. 2 John 1:13

title: 2 Peter 1:1–11
context: Peter greets believers who share the same precious faith through the righteousness of Jesus Christ, God and Savior. God’s power has already supplied everything needed for life and godliness, and through his promises believers share in the divine nature. Peter therefore calls them to add virtue upon virtue, from faith to love, and to make their calling and election sure, so that they will receive a rich welcome into Christ’s eternal kingdom.
text: 2 Peter 1:1–11 2 Peter Peter greets believers who share the same precious faith through the righteousness of Jesus Christ, God and Savior. God’s power has already supplied everything needed for life and godliness, and through his promises believers share in the divine nature. Peter therefore calls them to add virtue upon virtue, from faith to love, and to make their calling and election sure, so that they will receive a rich welcome into Christ’s eternal kingdom. Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and Savior, Jesus Christ: 2 Peter 1:1 Grace to you and peace be multiplied in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord, 2 Peter 1:2 seeing that his divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and virtue, 2 Peter 1:3 by which he has granted to us his precious and exceedingly great promises; that through these you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption that is in the world by lust. 2 Peter 1:4 Yes, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply moral excellence; and in moral excellence, knowledge; 2 Peter 1:5 and in knowledge, self-control; and in self-control, perseverance; and in perseverance, godliness; 2 Peter 1:6 and in godliness, brotherly affection; and in brotherly affection, love. 2 Peter 1:7 For if these things are yours and abound, they make you to not be idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. 2 Peter 1:8 For he who lacks these things is blind, seeing only what is near, having forgotten the cleansing from his old sins. 2 Peter 1:9 Therefore, brothers, be more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do these things, you will never stumble. 2 Peter 1:10 For thus you will be richly supplied with the entrance into the eternal Kingdom of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. 2 Peter 1:11

title: 2 Peter 1:12–21
context: Knowing that his death is near, Peter resolves to keep reminding his readers of the truth so they will remember it after he is gone. He insists that the apostles did not invent clever myths; they were eyewitnesses of Christ’s majesty at the transfiguration and heard the Father’s voice. Prophetic Scripture is even more certain, because it did not originate in human will; holy men spoke as the Holy Spirit carried them along.
text: 2 Peter 1:12–21 2 Peter Knowing that his death is near, Peter resolves to keep reminding his readers of the truth so they will remember it after he is gone. He insists that the apostles did not invent clever myths; they were eyewitnesses of Christ’s majesty at the transfiguration and heard the Father’s voice. Prophetic Scripture is even more certain, because it did not originate in human will; holy men spoke as the Holy Spirit carried them along. Therefore I will not be negligent to remind you of these things, though you know them and are established in the present truth. 2 Peter 1:12 I think it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by reminding you, 2 Peter 1:13 knowing that the putting off of my tent comes swiftly, even as our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me. 2 Peter 1:14 Yes, I will make every effort that you may always be able to remember these things even after my departure. 2 Peter 1:15 For we didn’t follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty. 2 Peter 1:16 For he received from God the Father honor and glory when the voice came to him from the Majestic Glory, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” 2 Peter 1:17 We heard this voice come out of heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain. 2 Peter 1:18 We have the more sure word of prophecy; and you do well that you heed it as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts, 2 Peter 1:19 knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of private interpretation. 2 Peter 1:20 For no prophecy ever came by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke, being moved by the Holy Spirit. 2 Peter 1:21

title: 2 Peter 2:1–10
context: As false prophets once rose in Israel, false teachers will rise among the church, secretly introducing destructive heresies and even denying the Master who bought them. Many will follow their immoral ways, and greed will drive them to exploit believers. Peter points to God’s past judgments on sinning angels, the ancient world in the flood, and Sodom and Gomorrah, and to his rescue of Noah and Lot, as proof that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly and to hold the unrighteous for judgment.
text: 2 Peter 2:1–10 2 Peter As false prophets once rose in Israel, false teachers will rise among the church, secretly introducing destructive heresies and even denying the Master who bought them. Many will follow their immoral ways, and greed will drive them to exploit believers. Peter points to God’s past judgments on sinning angels, the ancient world in the flood, and Sodom and Gomorrah, and to his rescue of Noah and Lot, as proof that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly and to hold the unrighteous for judgment. But false prophets also arose among the people, as false teachers will also be among you, who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master who bought them, bringing on themselves swift destruction. 2 Peter 2:1 Many will follow their immoral ways, and as a result, the way of the truth will be maligned. 2 Peter 2:2 In covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words: whose sentence now from of old doesn’t linger, and their destruction will not slumber. 2 Peter 2:3 For if God didn’t spare angels when they sinned, but cast them down to Tartarus, and committed them to pits of darkness to be reserved for judgment; 2 Peter 2:4 and didn’t spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought a flood on the world of the ungodly, 2 Peter 2:5 and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, condemned them to destruction, having made them an example to those who would live in an ungodly way, 2 Peter 2:6 and delivered righteous Lot, who was very distressed by the lustful life of the wicked 2 Peter 2:7 (for that righteous man dwelling among them was tormented in his righteous soul from day to day with seeing and hearing lawless deeds), 2 Peter 2:8 then the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment, 2 Peter 2:9 but chiefly those who walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement and despise authority. Daring, self-willed, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignitaries, 2 Peter 2:10

title: 2 Peter 2:11–22
context: Peter describes the false teachers in vivid terms: they slander what they do not understand, revel in pleasure, are full of adultery and greed, and follow the path of Balaam. They are waterless springs and mists driven by a storm, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption. Those who have escaped the world’s defilements through knowing Christ and then become entangled again end up worse off than before, like a dog returning to its vomit.
text: 2 Peter 2:11–22 2 Peter Peter describes the false teachers in vivid terms: they slander what they do not understand, revel in pleasure, are full of adultery and greed, and follow the path of Balaam. They are waterless springs and mists driven by a storm, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption. Those who have escaped the world’s defilements through knowing Christ and then become entangled again end up worse off than before, like a dog returning to its vomit. whereas angels, though greater in might and power, don’t bring a slanderous judgment against them before the Lord. 2 Peter 2:11 But these, as unreasoning creatures, born natural animals to be taken and destroyed, speaking evil in matters about which they are ignorant, will in their destroying surely be destroyed, 2 Peter 2:12 receiving the wages of unrighteousness; people who count it pleasure to revel in the daytime, spots and defects, reveling in their deceit while they feast with you; 2 Peter 2:13 having eyes full of adultery, and who can’t cease from sin, enticing unsettled souls, having a heart trained in greed, accursed children! 2 Peter 2:14 Forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing; 2 Peter 2:15 but he was rebuked for his own disobedience. A speechless donkey spoke with a man’s voice and stopped the madness of the prophet. 2 Peter 2:16 These are wells without water, clouds driven by a storm, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever. 2 Peter 2:17 For, uttering great swelling words of emptiness, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by licentiousness, those who are indeed escaping from those who live in error; 2 Peter 2:18 promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him. 2 Peter 2:19 For if, after they have escaped the defilement of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in it and overcome, the last state has become worse for them than the first. 2 Peter 2:20 For it would be better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them. 2 Peter 2:21 But it has happened to them according to the true proverb, “The dog turns to his own vomit again,” and “the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire.” 2 Peter 2:22

title: 2 Peter 3:1–10
context: Peter writes his second letter to stir up their minds to remember the prophets and the apostles’ command. Scoffers will come mocking the promise of Christ’s return, claiming nothing has changed since creation. Peter replies that they forget God’s word created the world and judged it by water, and the same word has reserved the present world for fire. With the Lord a day is like a thousand years; he is not slow but patient, not wishing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance. The day of the Lord will come like a thief.
text: 2 Peter 3:1–10 2 Peter Peter writes his second letter to stir up their minds to remember the prophets and the apostles’ command. Scoffers will come mocking the promise of Christ’s return, claiming nothing has changed since creation. Peter replies that they forget God’s word created the world and judged it by water, and the same word has reserved the present world for fire. With the Lord a day is like a thousand years; he is not slow but patient, not wishing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance. The day of the Lord will come like a thief. This is now, beloved, the second letter that I have written to you; and in both of them I stir up your sincere mind by reminding you 2 Peter 3:1 that you should remember the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets and the commandment of us, the apostles of the Lord and Savior, 2 Peter 3:2 knowing this first, that in the last days mockers will come, walking after their own lusts 2 Peter 3:3 and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? For, from the day that the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.” 2 Peter 3:4 For they willfully forget that there were heavens from of old, and an earth formed out of water and amid water by the word of God, 2 Peter 3:5 by which means the world that existed then, being overflowed with water, perished. 2 Peter 3:6 But the heavens that exist now and the earth, by the same word have been stored up for fire, being reserved against the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men. 2 Peter 3:7 But don’t forget this one thing, beloved, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. 2 Peter 3:8 The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance. 2 Peter 3:9 But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will be dissolved with fervent heat; and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. 2 Peter 3:10

title: 2 Peter 3:11–18
context: Since all these things will be dissolved, believers should live holy and godly lives as they wait for and hasten the day of God, looking for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells. They should be found at peace and blameless, counting the Lord’s patience as salvation, as Paul also wrote, though some twist his hard sayings. Peter warns them not to be carried away and to grow in the grace and knowledge of Jesus Christ.
text: 2 Peter 3:11–18 2 Peter Since all these things will be dissolved, believers should live holy and godly lives as they wait for and hasten the day of God, looking for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells. They should be found at peace and blameless, counting the Lord’s patience as salvation, as Paul also wrote, though some twist his hard sayings. Peter warns them not to be carried away and to grow in the grace and knowledge of Jesus Christ. Therefore, since all these things will be destroyed like this, what kind of people ought you to be in holy living and godliness, 2 Peter 3:11 looking for and earnestly desiring the coming of the day of God, which will cause the burning heavens to be dissolved, and the elements will melt with fervent heat? 2 Peter 3:12 But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells. 2 Peter 3:13 Therefore, beloved, seeing that you look for these things, be diligent to be found in peace, without defect and blameless in his sight. 2 Peter 3:14 Regard the patience of our Lord as salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also, according to the wisdom given to him, wrote to you, 2 Peter 3:15 as also in all of his letters, speaking in them of these things. In those, there are some things that are hard to understand, which the ignorant and unsettled twist, as they also do to the other Scriptures, to their own destruction. 2 Peter 3:16 You therefore, beloved, knowing these things beforehand, beware, lest being carried away with the error of the wicked, you fall from your own steadfastness. 2 Peter 3:17 But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and forever. Amen. 2 Peter 3:18

title: 2 Timothy 1:1–7
context: Paul greets Timothy as his beloved child, an apostle through the will of God, in keeping with the promise of the life which is in Christ Jesus. He thanks God as he prays night and day, longs to see Timothy, recalls the sincere faith of Lois and Eunice now dwelling in him, and urges him to fan into flame the gift given through the laying on of hands—for God gave a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
text: 2 Timothy 1:1–7 2 Timothy Paul greets Timothy as his beloved child, an apostle through the will of God, in keeping with the promise of the life which is in Christ Jesus. He thanks God as he prays night and day, longs to see Timothy, recalls the sincere faith of Lois and Eunice now dwelling in him, and urges him to fan into flame the gift given through the laying on of hands—for God gave a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control. Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, according to the promise of the life which is in Christ Jesus, 2 Timothy 1:1 to Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. 2 Timothy 1:2 I thank God, whom I serve as my forefathers did, with a pure conscience. How unceasing is my memory of you in my petitions, night and day 2 Timothy 1:3 longing to see you, remembering your tears, that I may be filled with joy; 2 Timothy 1:4 having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, in you also. 2 Timothy 1:5 For this cause, I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands. 2 Timothy 1:6 For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control. 2 Timothy 1:7

title: 2 Timothy 1:15–18
context: Paul names a hard fact: all who are in Asia turned away from him, Phygelus and Hermogenes among them. Against that desertion he asks mercy for the household of Onesiphorus, who often refreshed him, was not ashamed of his chains, searched him out in Rome, and had served well at Ephesus—that he may find the Lord’s mercy in that day.
text: 2 Timothy 1:15–18 2 Timothy Paul names a hard fact: all who are in Asia turned away from him, Phygelus and Hermogenes among them. Against that desertion he asks mercy for the household of Onesiphorus, who often refreshed him, was not ashamed of his chains, searched him out in Rome, and had served well at Ephesus—that he may find the Lord’s mercy in that day. This you know, that all who are in Asia turned away from me, of whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes. 2 Timothy 1:15 May the Lord grant mercy to the house of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain, 2 Timothy 1:16 but when he was in Rome, he sought me diligently and found me 2 Timothy 1:17 (the Lord grant to him to find the Lord’s mercy in that day); and in how many things he served at Ephesus, you know very well. 2 Timothy 1:18

title: 2 Timothy 1:8–14
context: Paul charges Timothy not to be ashamed of the Lord’s testimony or of the apostle in chains, but to share gospel-suffering by God’s power. That power belongs to the God who saved and called them by his own purpose and grace, given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times and now revealed in the Savior who abolished death; Paul is not ashamed, and Timothy must follow the pattern of sound words and guard the good deposit by the Spirit.
text: 2 Timothy 1:8–14 2 Timothy Paul charges Timothy not to be ashamed of the Lord’s testimony or of the apostle in chains, but to share gospel-suffering by God’s power. That power belongs to the God who saved and called them by his own purpose and grace, given to us in Christ Jesus before eternal times and now revealed in the Savior who abolished death; Paul is not ashamed, and Timothy must follow the pattern of sound words and guard the good deposit by the Spirit. Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God, 2 Timothy 1:8 who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal, 2 Timothy 1:9 but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and brought life and immortality to light through the Good News. 2 Timothy 1:10 For this I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles. 2 Timothy 1:11 For this cause I also suffer these things. Yet I am not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to guard that which I have committed to him against that day. 2 Timothy 1:12 Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 1:13 That good thing which was committed to you, guard through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. 2 Timothy 1:14

title: 2 Timothy 2:1–7
context: Paul charges Timothy, his child, to grow strong in Christ Jesus’ grace and to pass on what he has heard to faithful men who can teach others. Soldier, athlete, and farmer pictures press undivided endurance, and the Lord himself will give understanding.
text: 2 Timothy 2:1–7 2 Timothy Paul charges Timothy, his child, to grow strong in Christ Jesus’ grace and to pass on what he has heard to faithful men who can teach others. Soldier, athlete, and farmer pictures press undivided endurance, and the Lord himself will give understanding. You therefore, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 2:1 The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also. 2 Timothy 2:2 You therefore must endure hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 2:3 No soldier on duty entangles himself in the affairs of life, that he may please him who enrolled him as a soldier. 2 Timothy 2:4 Also, if anyone competes in athletics, he isn’t crowned unless he has competed by the rules. 2 Timothy 2:5 The farmer who labors must be the first to get a share of the crops. 2 Timothy 2:6 Consider what I say, and may the Lord give you understanding in all things. 2 Timothy 2:7

title: 2 Timothy 2:14–19
context: Timothy must remind the church not to quarrel about words, but to present himself to God as an approved worker, properly handling the Word of Truth. Irreverent babble spreads like gangrene—Hymenaeus and Philetus have already upset some—yet God’s firm foundation stands with its double seal.
text: 2 Timothy 2:14–19 2 Timothy Timothy must remind the church not to quarrel about words, but to present himself to God as an approved worker, properly handling the Word of Truth. Irreverent babble spreads like gangrene—Hymenaeus and Philetus have already upset some—yet God’s firm foundation stands with its double seal. Remind them of these things, charging them in the sight of the Lord that they don’t argue about words to no profit, to the subverting of those who hear. 2 Timothy 2:14 Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, a workman who doesn’t need to be ashamed, properly handling the Word of Truth. 2 Timothy 2:15 But shun empty chatter, for it will go further in ungodliness, 2 Timothy 2:16 and those words will consume like gangrene, of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus: 2 Timothy 2:17 men who have erred concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection is already past, and overthrowing the faith of some. 2 Timothy 2:18 However, God’s firm foundation stands, having this seal: “The Lord knows those who are his,” and, “Let every one who names the name of the Lord depart from unrighteousness.” 2 Timothy 2:19

title: 2 Timothy 2:20–26
context: In a great house some vessels are for honor and some for dishonor; anyone who cleanses himself from what is dishonorable is useful to the Master. The Lord’s servant flees youthful passions, refuses foolish controversies, and corrects opponents with gentleness, hoping God may grant repentance and escape from the devil’s snare.
text: 2 Timothy 2:20–26 2 Timothy In a great house some vessels are for honor and some for dishonor; anyone who cleanses himself from what is dishonorable is useful to the Master.
