Daniel 1:4 The king appointed for them a daily portion of the king’s delicacies and of the wine which he drank, and that they should be nourished three years, that at its end they should stand before the king. Daniel 1:5 Now among these of the children of Judah were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Daniel 1:6 The prince of the eunuchs gave names to them: to Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego. Daniel 1:7

title: Daniel 1:17–21
context: God gives the four youths knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; Daniel is given understanding in visions and dreams. At the appointed time they stand before Nebuchadnezzar. None is found like them; in every matter of wisdom the king finds them ten times better than the magicians of his realm. Daniel remains to the first year of Cyrus.
text: Daniel 1:17–21 Daniel God gives the four youths knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; Daniel is given understanding in visions and dreams. At the appointed time they stand before Nebuchadnezzar. None is found like them; in every matter of wisdom the king finds them ten times better than the magicians of his realm. Daniel remains to the first year of Cyrus. Now as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom; and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams. Daniel 1:17 At the end of the days which the king had appointed for bringing them in, the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar. Daniel 1:18 The king talked with them; and among them all was found no one like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Therefore they stood before the king. Daniel 1:19 In every matter of wisdom and understanding concerning which the king inquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters who were in all his realm. Daniel 1:20 Daniel continued even to the first year of King Cyrus. Daniel 1:21

title: Daniel 1:8–16
context: Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king’s delicacies and wine, and asks the prince of the eunuchs. God gives him favor and compassion; the chief still fears the king. Daniel proposes a ten-day test of vegetables and water. At the end they look better than those who ate of the king’s delicacies, and the steward keeps them on that diet.
text: Daniel 1:8–16 Daniel Daniel resolves not to defile himself with the king’s delicacies and wine, and asks the prince of the eunuchs. God gives him favor and compassion; the chief still fears the king. Daniel proposes a ten-day test of vegetables and water. At the end they look better than those who ate of the king’s delicacies, and the steward keeps them on that diet. But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s delicacies, nor with the wine which he drank. Therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself. Daniel 1:8 Now God made Daniel find kindness and compassion in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs. Daniel 1:9 The prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has appointed your food and your drink. For why should he see your faces worse looking than the youths who are of your own age? Then you would endanger my head with the king.” Daniel 1:10 Then Daniel said to the steward whom the prince of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: Daniel 1:11 “Test your servants, I beg you, ten days; and let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink. Daniel 1:12 Then let our faces be examined before you, and the face of the youths who eat of the king’s delicacies; and as you see, deal with your servants.” Daniel 1:13 So he listened to them in this matter, and tested them for ten days. Daniel 1:14 At the end of ten days, their faces appeared fairer and they were fatter in flesh than all the youths who ate of the king’s delicacies. Daniel 1:15 So the steward took away their delicacies and the wine that they were given to drink, and gave them vegetables. Daniel 1:16

title: Daniel 10:1–9
context: In the third year of Cyrus a true word about a great conflict is revealed to Daniel, named Belteshazzar. He mourns three weeks, stands by the Tigris, and sees a man clothed in linen whose glory leaves him alone, strengthless, and fallen on his face.
text: Daniel 10:1–9 Daniel In the third year of Cyrus a true word about a great conflict is revealed to Daniel, named Belteshazzar. He mourns three weeks, stands by the Tigris, and sees a man clothed in linen whose glory leaves him alone, strengthless, and fallen on his face. In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a message was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the message was true, even a great warfare. He understood the message, and had understanding of the vision. Daniel 10:1 In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three whole weeks. Daniel 10:2 I ate no pleasant food. No meat or wine came into my mouth. I didn’t anoint myself at all, until three whole weeks were fulfilled. Daniel 10:3 In the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel, Daniel 10:4 I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, there was a man clothed in linen, whose waist was adorned with pure gold of Uphaz. Daniel 10:5 His body also was like beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as flaming torches. His arms and his feet were like burnished bronze. The voice of his words was like the voice of a multitude. Daniel 10:6 I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, for the men who were with me didn’t see the vision, but a great quaking fell on them, and they fled to hide themselves. Daniel 10:7 So I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; for my face grew deathly pale, and I retained no strength. Daniel 10:8 Yet I heard the voice of his words. When I heard the voice of his words, then I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face toward the ground. Daniel 10:9

title: Daniel 10:10–21
context: A hand lifts trembling Daniel: man greatly loved, fear not—your words were heard. The prince of Persia withstood the messenger twenty-one days; Michael came. Strengthened again, Daniel is told of a fight against Persia, of Greece, and of the book of truth beside which only Michael, your prince, contends.
text: Daniel 10:10–21 Daniel A hand lifts trembling Daniel: man greatly loved, fear not—your words were heard. The prince of Persia withstood the messenger twenty-one days; Michael came. Strengthened again, Daniel is told of a fight against Persia, of Greece, and of the book of truth beside which only Michael, your prince, contends. Behold, a hand touched me, which set me on my knees and on the palms of my hands. Daniel 10:10 He said to me, “Daniel, you greatly beloved man, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright, for I have been sent to you, now.” When he had spoken this word to me, I stood trembling. Daniel 10:11 Then he said to me, “Don’t be afraid, Daniel; for from the first day that you set your heart to understand, and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard. I have come for your words’ sake. Daniel 10:12 But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days; but, behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me because I remained there with the kings of Persia. Daniel 10:13 Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision is yet for many days.” Daniel 10:14 When he had spoken these words to me, I set my face toward the ground and was mute. Daniel 10:15 Behold, one in the likeness of the sons of men touched my lips. Then I opened my mouth, and spoke and said to him who stood before me, “My lord, by reason of the vision my sorrows have overtaken me, and I retain no strength. Daniel 10:16 For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? For as for me, immediately there remained no strength in me. There was no breath left in me.” Daniel 10:17 Then one like the appearance of a man touched me again, and he strengthened me. Daniel 10:18 He said, “Greatly beloved man, don’t be afraid. Peace be to you. Be strong. Yes, be strong.” When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.” Daniel 10:19 Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to fight with the prince of Persia. When I go out, behold, the prince of Greece will come. Daniel 10:20 But I will tell you that which is inscribed in the writing of truth. There is no one who holds with me against these but Michael your prince. Daniel 10:21

title: Daniel 11:1–19
context: The angel continues the last vision: he stood to confirm Darius the Mede, then shows the truth of Persian kings, a mighty Greek king whose kingdom is broken toward four winds, and the long wars of the kings of the south. Also the children of the north—all as they touch the people of God and the glorious land—until the northern king stumbles and is not found.
text: Daniel 11:1–19 Daniel The angel continues the last vision: he stood to confirm Darius the Mede, then shows the truth of Persian kings, a mighty Greek king whose kingdom is broken toward four winds, and the long wars of the kings of the south. Also the children of the north—all as they touch the people of God and the glorious land—until the northern king stumbles and is not found. “As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him. Daniel 11:1 “Now I will show you the truth. Behold, three more kings will stand up in Persia. The fourth will be far richer than all of them. When he has grown strong through his riches, he will stir up all against the realm of Greece. Daniel 11:2 A mighty king will stand up, who will rule with great dominion, and do according to his will. Daniel 11:3 When he stands up, his kingdom will be broken and will be divided toward the four winds of the sky, but not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom will be plucked up, even for others besides these. Daniel 11:4 “The king of the south will be strong. One of his princes will become stronger than him, and have dominion. His dominion will be a great dominion. Daniel 11:5 At the end of years they will join themselves together; and the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not retain the strength of her arm. He will also not stand, nor will his arm; but she will be given up, with those who brought her, and he who became the father of her, and he who strengthened her in those times. Daniel 11:6 “But out of a shoot from her roots one will stand up in his place, who will come to the army and will enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and will deal against them and will prevail. Daniel 11:7 He will also carry their gods with their molten images, and with their goodly vessels of silver and of gold, captive into Egypt. He will refrain some years from the king of the north. Daniel 11:8 He will come into the realm of the king of the south, but he will return into his own land. Daniel 11:9 His sons will wage war, and will assemble a multitude of great forces which will come on, and overflow, and pass through. They will return and wage war, even to his fortress. Daniel 11:10 “The king of the south will be moved with anger and will come out and fight with him, even with the king of the north. He will send out a great multitude, and the multitude will be given into his hand. Daniel 11:11 The multitude will be carried off, and his heart will be exalted. He will cast down tens of thousands, but he won’t prevail. Daniel 11:12 The king of the north will return, and will send out a multitude greater than the former. He will come on at the end of the times, even of years, with a great army and with abundant supplies. Daniel 11:13 “In those times many will stand up against the king of the south. Also the children of the violent among your people will lift themselves up to establish the vision, but they will fall. Daniel 11:14 So the king of the north will come and cast up a mound, and take a well-fortified city. The forces of the south won’t stand, neither will his select troops, neither will there be any strength to stand. Daniel 11:15 But he who comes against him will do according to his own will, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the glorious land, and destruction will be in his hand. Daniel 11:16 He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and with him equitable conditions. He will perform them. He will give him the daughter of women, to destroy the kingdom, but she will not stand, and won’t be for him. Daniel 11:17 After this he will turn his face to the islands, and will take many, but a prince will cause the reproach offered by him to cease. Yes, moreover, he will cause his reproach to turn on him. Daniel 11:18 Then he will turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land; but he will stumble and fall, and won’t be found. Daniel 11:19

title: Daniel 11:20–35
context: The angel continues the last vision: after the northern king of vv. 1–19 stumbles, a raiser of tribute stands in his place and is quickly broken; then a contemptible person seizes the kingdom by flatteries, sweeps armies and the prince of the covenant, acts deceitfully, sets his heart against the holy covenant, and with apostates profanes the sanctuary, takes away the regular offering, and sets up the abomination—while those who know their God stand firm, the wise instruct many, and some of the wise stumble to be refined until the appointed time.
text: Daniel 11:20–35 Daniel The angel continues the last vision: after the northern king of vv. 1–19 stumbles, a raiser of tribute stands in his place and is quickly broken; then a contemptible person seizes the kingdom by flatteries, sweeps armies and the prince of the covenant, acts deceitfully, sets his heart against the holy covenant, and with apostates profanes the sanctuary, takes away the regular offering, and sets up the abomination—while those who know their God stand firm, the wise instruct many, and some of the wise stumble to be refined until the appointed time. “Then one who will cause a tax collector to pass through the kingdom to maintain its glory will stand up in his place; but within a few days he shall be destroyed, not in anger, and not in battle. Daniel 11:20 “In his place a contemptible person will stand up, to whom they had not given the honor of the kingdom; but he will come in a time of security, and will obtain the kingdom by flatteries. Daniel 11:21 The overwhelming forces will be overwhelmed from before him, and will be broken. Yes, also the prince of the covenant. Daniel 11:22 After the treaty made with him he will work deceitfully; for he will come up and will become strong with few people. Daniel 11:23 In a time of security he will come even on the fattest places of the province. He will do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers’ fathers. He will scatter among them prey, plunder, and wealth. Yes, he will devise his plans against the strongholds, but only for a time. Daniel 11:24 “He will stir up his power and his courage against the king of the south with a great army; and the king of the south will wage war in battle with an exceedingly great and mighty army, but he won’t stand; for they will devise plans against him. Daniel 11:25 Yes, those who eat of his delicacies will destroy him, and his army will be swept away. Many will fall down slain. Daniel 11:26 As for both these kings, their hearts will be to do evil, and they will speak lies at one table; but it won’t prosper, for the end will still be at the appointed time. Daniel 11:27 Then he will return into his land with great wealth. His heart will be against the holy covenant. He will take action, and return to his own land. Daniel 11:28 “He will return at the appointed time and come into the south; but it won’t be in the latter time as it was in the former. Daniel 11:29 For ships of Kittim will come against him. Therefore he will be grieved, and will return, and have indignation against the holy covenant, and will take action. He will even return, and have regard to those who forsake the holy covenant. Daniel 11:30 “Forces from him will profane the sanctuary, even the fortress, and will take away the continual burnt offering. Then they will set up the abomination that makes desolate. Daniel 11:31 He will corrupt those who do wickedly against the covenant by flatteries; but the people who know their God will be strong and take action. Daniel 11:32 “Those who are wise among the people will instruct many; yet they will fall by the sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder, many days. Daniel 11:33 Now when they fall, they will be helped with a little help; but many will join themselves to them with flatteries. Daniel 11:34 Some of those who are wise will fall—to refine them, and to purify, and to make them white, even to the time of the end, because it is yet for the time appointed. Daniel 11:35

title: Daniel 11:36–45
context: The vision closes with the king who does as he pleases: he exalts himself above every god, honors a god of fortresses, overflows countries, enters the glorious land, and plants his palace tents between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain—yet he comes to his end, and no one will help him. The angel tells it so the church may wait the appointed indignation.
text: Daniel 11:36–45 Daniel The vision closes with the king who does as he pleases: he exalts himself above every god, honors a god of fortresses, overflows countries, enters the glorious land, and plants his palace tents between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain—yet he comes to his end, and no one will help him. The angel tells it so the church may wait the appointed indignation. “The king will do according to his will. He will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and will speak marvelous things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the indignation is accomplished, for that which is determined will be done. Daniel 11:36 He won’t regard the gods of his fathers, or the desire of women, or regard any god; for he will magnify himself above all. Daniel 11:37 But in their place, he will honor the god of fortresses. He will honor a god whom his fathers didn’t know with gold, silver, and with precious stones and pleasant things. Daniel 11:38 He will deal with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign god. He will increase with glory whoever acknowledges him. He will cause them to rule over many, and will divide the land for a price. Daniel 11:39 “At the time of the end the king of the south will contend with him; and the king of the north will come against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, with horsemen, and with many ships. He will enter into the countries, and will overflow and pass through. Daniel 11:40 He will enter also into the glorious land, and many countries will be overthrown; but these will be delivered out of his hand: Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon. Daniel 11:41 He will also stretch out his hand on the countries. The land of Egypt won’t escape. Daniel 11:42 But he will have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt. The Libyans and the Ethiopians will follow his steps. Daniel 11:43 But news out of the east and out of the north will trouble him; and he will go out with great fury to destroy and utterly to sweep away many. Daniel 11:44 He will plant the tents of his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him. Daniel 11:45

title: Daniel 12:1–4
context: The final vision reaches its climax beyond the wars of kings. Michael arises in an unprecedented time of distress, yet everyone written in the book is delivered. Daniel 12:2 is the Old Testament’s clearest statement of bodily resurrection to everlasting life or everlasting shame. Daniel is told to seal the book until the time of the end.
text: Daniel 12:1–4 Daniel The final vision reaches its climax beyond the wars of kings. Michael arises in an unprecedented time of distress, yet everyone written in the book is delivered. Daniel 12:2 is the Old Testament’s clearest statement of bodily resurrection to everlasting life or everlasting shame. Daniel is told to seal the book until the time of the end. “At that time Michael will stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there will be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time. At that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book. Daniel 12:1 Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. Daniel 12:2 Those who are wise will shine as the brightness of the expanse. Those who turn many to righteousness will shine as the stars forever and ever. Daniel 12:3 But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book, even to the time of the end. Many will run back and forth, and knowledge will be increased.” Daniel 12:4

title: Daniel 12:5–13
context: Daniel looks again: two others stand there, one on each bank of the river. Someone asks the man clothed in linen, above the waters, how long to the end of these wonders. Both hands rise toward heaven: a time, times, and a half a time; when they have finished breaking in pieces the holy people’s power ends, these things are finished. Daniel hears and does not understand. Go your way—the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end. Many will purify themselves; the wicked will do wickedly; the wise shall understand. From the taking away of the continual burnt offering and the setting up of the abomination that makes desolate there will be 1,290 days; blessed is the one who waits and reaches the 1,335. Go your way until the end: rest, and stand in your inheritance at the end of the days.
text: Daniel 12:5–13 Daniel Daniel looks again: two others stand there, one on each bank of the river. Someone asks the man clothed in linen, above the waters, how long to the end of these wonders. Both hands rise toward heaven: a time, times, and a half a time; when they have finished breaking in pieces the holy people’s power ends, these things are finished. Daniel hears and does not understand. Go your way—the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end. Many will purify themselves; the wicked will do wickedly; the wise shall understand. From the taking away of the continual burnt offering and the setting up of the abomination that makes desolate there will be 1,290 days; blessed is the one who waits and reaches the 1,335. Go your way until the end: rest, and stand in your inheritance at the end of the days. Then I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others stood, one on the river bank on this side, and the other on the river bank on that side. Daniel 12:5 One said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long will it be to the end of these wonders?” Daniel 12:6 I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and swore by him who lives forever that it will be for a time, times, and a half; and when they have finished breaking in pieces the power of the holy people, all these things will be finished. Daniel 12:7 I heard, but I didn’t understand. Then I said, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?” Daniel 12:8 He said, “Go your way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end. Daniel 12:9 Many will purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined, but the wicked will do wickedly; and none of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand. Daniel 12:10 “From the time that the continual burnt offering is taken away and the abomination that makes desolate set up, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days. Daniel 12:11 Blessed is he who waits, and comes to the one thousand three hundred thirty-five days. Daniel 12:12 “But go your way until the end; for you will rest, and will stand in your inheritance at the end of the days.” Daniel 12:13

title: Daniel 2:1–16
context: In his second year Nebuchadnezzar is troubled by dreams he cannot recover. Magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans are summoned; they ask to hear the dream first. The king demands both dream and interpretation on pain of death, then a decree to destroy all the wise men. Daniel, sought with his companions, answers Arioch with prudence and asks the king for time to show the interpretation.
text: Daniel 2:1–16 Daniel In his second year Nebuchadnezzar is troubled by dreams he cannot recover. Magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans are summoned; they ask to hear the dream first. The king demands both dream and interpretation on pain of death, then a decree to destroy all the wise men. Daniel, sought with his companions, answers Arioch with prudence and asks the king for time to show the interpretation. In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep went from him. Daniel 2:1 Then the king commanded that the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans be called to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king. Daniel 2:2 The king said to them, “I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.” Daniel 2:3 Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language, “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.” Daniel 2:4 The king answered the Chaldeans, “The thing has gone from me. If you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut in pieces, and your houses will be made a dunghill. Daniel 2:5 But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts, rewards, and great honor. Therefore show me the dream and its interpretation.” Daniel 2:6 They answered the second time and said, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.” Daniel 2:7 The king answered, “I know of a certainty that you are trying to gain time, because you see the thing has gone from me. Daniel 2:8 But if you don’t make known to me the dream, there is but one law for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until the situation changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can show me its interpretation.” Daniel 2:9 The Chaldeans answered the king and said, “There is not a man on the earth who can show the king’s matter, because no king, lord, or ruler has asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean. Daniel 2:10 It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.” Daniel 2:11 Because of this, the king was angry and very furious, and commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed. Daniel 2:12 So the decree went out, and the wise men were to be slain. They sought Daniel and his companions to be slain. Daniel 2:13 Then Daniel returned answer with counsel and prudence to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon. Daniel 2:14 He answered Arioch the king’s captain, “Why is the decree so urgent from the king?” Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel. Daniel 2:15 Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation. Daniel 2:16

title: Daniel 2:17–30
context: Daniel tells Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah to ask the God of heaven for mercy. The mystery is revealed in a night vision; Daniel blesses God, who changes times and kings and gives wisdom. He asks Arioch to spare the wise men, is brought before the king, and confesses that no court guild can show the mystery—there is a God in heaven who reveals it, not because of Daniel’s surplus wisdom.
text: Daniel 2:17–30 Daniel Daniel tells Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah to ask the God of heaven for mercy. The mystery is revealed in a night vision; Daniel blesses God, who changes times and kings and gives wisdom. He asks Arioch to spare the wise men, is brought before the king, and confesses that no court guild can show the mystery—there is a God in heaven who reveals it, not because of Daniel’s surplus wisdom. Then Daniel went to his house and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions: Daniel 2:17 that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret, that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon. Daniel 2:18 Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven. Daniel 2:19 Daniel answered, “Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for wisdom and might are his. Daniel 2:20 He changes the times and the seasons. He removes kings and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding. Daniel 2:21 He reveals the deep and secret things. He knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him. Daniel 2:22 I thank you and praise you, O God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the king’s matter.” Daniel 2:23 Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said this to him: “Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will show to the king the interpretation.” Daniel 2:24 Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king in haste, and said this to him: “I have found a man of the children of the captivity of Judah who will make known to the king the interpretation.” Daniel 2:25 The king answered Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen, and its interpretation?” Daniel 2:26 Daniel answered before the king, and said, “The secret which the king has demanded can’t be shown to the king by wise men, enchanters, magicians, or soothsayers; Daniel 2:27 but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be in the latter days. Your dream and the visions of your head on your bed are these: Daniel 2:28 “As for you, O king, your thoughts came on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what will happen. Daniel 2:29 But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any wisdom that I have more than any living, but to the intent that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and that you may know the thoughts of your heart. Daniel 2:30

title: Daniel 2:31–45
context: Daniel tells the forgotten dream: a great image of gold, silver, bronze, iron, and mixed feet, struck by a stone cut without hands. The image becomes chaff; the stone becomes a mountain filling the earth. Interpretation: Nebuchadnezzar is the head of gold; three kingdoms follow; in their days the God of heaven sets up a kingdom which will never be destroyed. Historic Christian reading: the stone is Christ’s kingdom.
text: Daniel 2:31–45 Daniel Daniel tells the forgotten dream: a great image of gold, silver, bronze, iron, and mixed feet, struck by a stone cut without hands. The image becomes chaff; the stone becomes a mountain filling the earth. Interpretation: Nebuchadnezzar is the head of gold; three kingdoms follow; in their days the God of heaven sets up a kingdom which will never be destroyed. Historic Christian reading: the stone is Christ’s kingdom. “You, O king, saw, and behold, a great image. This image, which was mighty, and whose brightness was excellent, stood before you; and its appearance was terrifying. Daniel 2:31 As for this image, its head was of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze, Daniel 2:32 its legs of iron, its feet part of iron and part of clay. Daniel 2:33 You saw until a stone was cut out without hands, which struck the image on its feet that were of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces. Daniel 2:34 Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were broken in pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away, so that no place was found for them. The stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth. Daniel 2:35 “This is the dream; and we will tell its interpretation before the king. Daniel 2:36 You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the glory. Daniel 2:37 Wherever the children of men dwell, he has given the animals of the field and the birds of the sky into your hand, and has made you rule over them all. You are the head of gold. Daniel 2:38 “After you, another kingdom will arise that is inferior to you; and another third kingdom of bronze, which will rule over all the earth. Daniel 2:39 The fourth kingdom will be strong as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and subdues all things; and as iron that crushes all these, it will break in pieces and crush. Daniel 2:40 Whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay and part of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but there will be in it of the strength of the iron, because you saw the iron mixed with miry clay. Daniel 2:41 As the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle. Daniel 2:42 Whereas you saw the iron mixed with miry clay, they will mingle themselves with the seed of men; but they won’t cling to one another, even as iron does not mix with clay. Daniel 2:43 “In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, nor will its sovereignty be left to another people; but it will break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever. Daniel 2:44 Because you saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold, the great God has made known to the king what will happen hereafter. The dream is certain, and its interpretation sure.” Daniel 2:45

title: Daniel 2:46–49
context: Nebuchadnezzar falls on his face and pays homage to Daniel, ordering offering and incense. He confesses Daniel’s God as God of gods, Lord of kings, and revealer of mysteries. He honors Daniel with gifts, rule of the province, and charge of the wise men. At Daniel’s request, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego are set over the province’s affairs; Daniel remains at court.
text: Daniel 2:46–49 Daniel Nebuchadnezzar falls on his face and pays homage to Daniel, ordering offering and incense. He confesses Daniel’s God as God of gods, Lord of kings, and revealer of mysteries. He honors Daniel with gifts, rule of the province, and charge of the wise men. At Daniel’s request, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego are set over the province’s affairs; Daniel remains at court. Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, worshiped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an offering and sweet odors to him. Daniel 2:46 The king answered to Daniel, and said, “Of a truth your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.” Daniel 2:47 Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts, and made him rule over the whole province of Babylon and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon. Daniel 2:48 Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon, but Daniel was in the king’s gate. Daniel 2:49

title: Daniel 3:1–12
context: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a sixty-cubit golden image in the plain of Dura and gathers officials for its dedication. At the sound of music, peoples, nations, and languages are commanded to fall down and worship, or be cast into a furnace. All fall down. Certain Chaldeans accuse the Jews: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom the king appointed over the province, do not serve his gods or worship the image.
text: Daniel 3:1–12 Daniel Nebuchadnezzar sets up a sixty-cubit golden image in the plain of Dura and gathers officials for its dedication. At the sound of music, peoples, nations, and languages are commanded to fall down and worship, or be cast into a furnace. All fall down. Certain Chaldeans accuse the Jews: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, whom the king appointed over the province, do not serve his gods or worship the image. Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was sixty cubits and its width six cubits. He set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon. Daniel 3:1 Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up. Daniel 3:2 Then the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces were gathered together to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up. Daniel 3:3 Then the herald cried aloud, “To you it is commanded, peoples, nations, and languages, Daniel 3:4 that whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up. Daniel 3:5 Whoever doesn’t fall down and worship shall be cast into the middle of a burning fiery furnace the same hour.” Daniel 3:6 Therefore at that time, when all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, all the peoples, the nations, and the languages fell down and worshiped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up. Daniel 3:7 Therefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near and brought accusation against the Jews. Daniel 3:8 They answered Nebuchadnezzar the king, “O king, live for ever! Daniel 3:9 You, O king, have made a decree that every man who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music shall fall down and worship the golden image; Daniel 3:10 and whoever doesn’t fall down and worship shall be cast into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Daniel 3:11 There are certain Jews whom you have appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, have not respected you. They don’t serve your gods, and don’t worship the golden image which you have set up.” Daniel 3:12

title: Daniel 3:13–23
context: In furious rage Nebuchadnezzar brings the three and offers a last chance: worship the image, or the furnace. Who is that god who will deliver? They answer that they need not debate it. Their God is able to deliver; but if not, they will not serve the king’s gods or worship the image. The furnace is heated seven times; mighty men bind them; the flame kills the executioners; the three fall bound into the fire.
text: Daniel 3:13–23 Daniel In furious rage Nebuchadnezzar brings the three and offers a last chance: worship the image, or the furnace. Who is that god who will deliver? They answer that they need not debate it. Their God is able to deliver; but if not, they will not serve the king’s gods or worship the image. The furnace is heated seven times; mighty men bind them; the flame kills the executioners; the three fall bound into the fire. Then Nebuchadnezzar in rage and fury commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought. Then these men were brought before the king. Daniel 3:13 Nebuchadnezzar answered them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you don’t serve my gods and you don’t worship the golden image which I have set up? Daniel 3:14 Now if you are ready whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and worship the image which I have made, good; but if you don’t worship, you shall be cast the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Who is that god who will deliver you out of my hands?” Daniel 3:15 Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter. Daniel 3:16 If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. Daniel 3:17 But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.” Daniel 3:18 Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace seven times more than it was usually heated. Daniel 3:19 He commanded certain mighty men who were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace. Daniel 3:20 Then these men were bound in their pants, their tunics, and their mantles, and their other clothes, and were cast into the middle of the burning fiery furnace. Daniel 3:21 Therefore because the king’s commandment was urgent and the furnace exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Daniel 3:22 These three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the middle of the burning fiery furnace. Daniel 3:23

title: Daniel 3:24–30
context: Nebuchadnezzar is astonished: three were cast bound into the fire; he sees four unbound, walking, unhurt, the fourth like a son of the gods. He calls the three out as servants of the Most High. Officials inspect: no power of fire, no singed hair, no smell. He blesses their God, who sent his angel and delivered servants who trusted Him. A decree: none may speak against this God. The three are promoted in the province.
text: Daniel 3:24–30 Daniel Nebuchadnezzar is astonished: three were cast bound into the fire; he sees four unbound, walking, unhurt, the fourth like a son of the gods. He calls the three out as servants of the Most High. Officials inspect: no power of fire, no singed hair, no smell. He blesses their God, who sent his angel and delivered servants who trusted Him. A decree: none may speak against this God. The three are promoted in the province. Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished and rose up in haste. He spoke and said to his counselors, “Didn’t we cast three men bound into the middle of the fire?” They answered the king, “True, O king.” Daniel 3:24 He answered, “Look, I see four men loose, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.” Daniel 3:25 Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace. He spoke and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you servants of the Most High God, come out, and come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the middle of the fire. Daniel 3:26 The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed. The smell of fire wasn’t even on them. Daniel 3:27 Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and have yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god except their own God. Daniel 3:28 Therefore I make a decree that every people, nation, and language which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill, because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.” Daniel 3:29 Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon. Daniel 3:30

title: Daniel 4:1–18
context: Nebuchadnezzar’s edict frames the chapter: signs of the Most High, whose kingdom is everlasting. At ease in his palace he dreams of a great tree that feeds all flesh. A watcher from heaven orders it cut down, the stump left, a beast’s mind given for seven times—so that the living may know the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will. Magicians fail; Daniel is asked to interpret.
text: Daniel 4:1–18 Daniel Nebuchadnezzar’s edict frames the chapter: signs of the Most High, whose kingdom is everlasting. At ease in his palace he dreams of a great tree that feeds all flesh. A watcher from heaven orders it cut down, the stump left, a beast’s mind given for seven times—so that the living may know the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will. Magicians fail; Daniel is asked to interpret. Nebuchadnezzar the king, to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you. Daniel 4:1 It has seemed good to me to show the signs and wonders that the Most High God has worked toward me. Daniel 4:2 How great are his signs! How mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. His dominion is from generation to generation. Daniel 4:3 I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace. Daniel 4:4 I saw a dream which made me afraid; and the thoughts on my bed and the visions of my head troubled me. Daniel 4:5 Therefore I made a decree to bring in all the wise men of Babylon before me, that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream. Daniel 4:6 Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers came in; and I told them the dream, but they didn’t make known to me its interpretation. Daniel 4:7 But at last, Daniel came in before me, whose name was Belteshazzar according to the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. I told the dream before him, saying, Daniel 4:8 “Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation. Daniel 4:9 These were the visions of my head on my bed: I saw, and behold, a tree in the middle of the earth; and its height was great. Daniel 4:10 The tree grew and was strong. Its height reached to the sky and its sight to the end of all the earth. Daniel 4:11 Its leaves were beautiful, and it had much fruit, and in it was food for all. The animals of the field had shade under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it. Daniel 4:12 “I saw in the visions of my head on my bed, and behold, a holy watcher came down from the sky. Daniel 4:13 He cried aloud and said this: ‘Cut down the tree, and cut off its branches! Shake off its leaves and scatter its fruit! Let the animals get away from under it and the birds from its branches. Daniel 4:14 Nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and bronze, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of the sky. Let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth. Daniel 4:15 Let his heart be changed from man’s, and let an animal’s heart be given to him. Then let seven times pass over him. Daniel 4:16 “‘The sentence is by the decree of the watchers and the demand by the word of the holy ones, to the intent that the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will, and sets up over it the lowest of men.’ Daniel 4:17 “This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, have seen; and you, Belteshazzar, declare the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able, for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.” Daniel 4:18

title: Daniel 4:19–27
context: Daniel is dismayed, then interprets: the tree is the king; a watcher has decreed he will be driven to the beasts until he knows the Most High rules in the stump means the kingdom will be confirmed when he knows Heaven rules. Counsel: break off sins by righteousness and mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of prosperity.
text: Daniel 4:19–27 Daniel Daniel is dismayed, then interprets: the tree is the king; a watcher has decreed he will be driven to the beasts until he knows the Most High rules in the stump means the kingdom will be confirmed when he knows Heaven rules. Counsel: break off sins by righteousness and mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of prosperity. Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stricken mute for a while, and his thoughts troubled him. The king answered, “Belteshazzar, don’t let the dream or the interpretation trouble you.” Belteshazzar answered, “My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation to your adversaries. Daniel 4:19 The tree that you saw, which grew and was strong, whose height reached to the sky and its sight to all the earth; Daniel 4:20 whose leaves were beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and in it was food for all; under which the animals of the field lived, and on whose branches the birds of the sky had their habitation— Daniel 4:21 it is you, O king, that have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth. Daniel 4:22 “Whereas the king saw a holy watcher coming down from the sky and saying, ‘Cut down the tree, and destroy it; nevertheless leave the stump of its roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and bronze, in the tender grass of the field, and let it be wet with the dew of the sky. Let his portion be with the animals of the field, until seven times pass over him.’ Daniel 4:23 “This is the interpretation, O king, and it is the decree of the Most High, which has come on my lord the king: Daniel 4:24 You will be driven from men and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field. You will be made to eat grass as oxen, and will be wet with the dew of the sky, and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will. Daniel 4:25 Whereas it was commanded to leave the stump of the roots of the tree, your kingdom will be restored to you after you learn that Heaven rules. Daniel 4:26 Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.” Daniel 4:27

title: Daniel 4:28–37
context: Daniel had urged the king to break off his sins while there was time (4:27), and this closing scene shows a year of that mercy wasted in a single rooftop boast. The humbling falls exactly as the dream foretold, and when it lifts, Nebuchadnezzar himself tells the story, praising the God whose dominion outlasts every empire. The chapter matters because a pagan king ends it confessing that the Most High rules and is able to humble those who walk in pride; that is the lesson Daniel will later press on Belshazzar in chapter 5.
text: Daniel 4:28–37 Daniel Daniel had urged the king to break off his sins while there was time (4:27), and this closing scene shows a year of that mercy wasted in a single rooftop boast. The humbling falls exactly as the dream foretold, and when it lifts, Nebuchadnezzar himself tells the story, praising the God whose dominion outlasts every empire. The chapter matters because a pagan king ends it confessing that the Most High rules and is able to humble those who walk in pride; that is the lesson Daniel will later press on Belshazzar in chapter 5. All this came on the King Nebuchadnezzar. Daniel 4:28 At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon. Daniel 4:29 The king spoke and said, “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?” Daniel 4:30 While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice came from the sky, saying, “O King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: ‘The kingdom has departed from you. Daniel 4:31 You shall be driven from men, and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field. You shall be made to eat grass like oxen. Seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he will.’” Daniel 4:32 This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men and ate grass like oxen; and his body was wet with the dew of the sky until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws. Daniel 4:33 At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me; and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation. Daniel 4:34 All the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; and he does according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth; and no one can stop his hand, or ask him, “What are you doing?” Daniel 4:35 At the same time my understanding returned to me; and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and brightness returned to me. My counselors and my lords sought me; and I was established in my kingdom, and excellent greatness was added to me. Daniel 4:36 Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and extol and honor the King of heaven; for all his works are truth, and his ways justice; and those who walk in pride he is able to abase. Daniel 4:37

title: Daniel 5:1–12
context: King Belshazzar throws a great feast to a thousand lords, drinks from the golden vessels taken from the house which was at Jerusalem; and praises gods of gold and stone. Fingers of a man’s hand write on the palace plaster; the king’s color fails and his wise men cannot read; the queen comes in and names Daniel, in whom an excellent spirit was found.
text: Daniel 5:1–12 Daniel King Belshazzar throws a great feast to a thousand lords, drinks from the golden vessels taken from the house which was at Jerusalem; and praises gods of gold and stone. Fingers of a man’s hand write on the palace plaster; the king’s color fails and his wise men cannot read; the queen comes in and names Daniel, in whom an excellent spirit was found. Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand. Daniel 5:1 Belshazzar, while he tasted the wine, commanded that the golden and silver vessels which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem be brought to him, that the king and his lords, his wives and his concubines, might drink from them. Daniel 5:2 Then they brought the golden vessels that were taken out of the temple of God’s house which was at Jerusalem; and the king and his lords, his wives and his concubines, drank from them. Daniel 5:3 They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of bronze, of iron, of wood, and of stone. Daniel 5:4 In the same hour, the fingers of a man’s hand came out and wrote near the lamp stand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace. The king saw the part of the hand that wrote. Daniel 5:5 Then the king’s face was changed in him, and his thoughts troubled him; and the joints of his thighs were loosened, and his knees struck one against another. Daniel 5:6 The king cried aloud to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. The king spoke and said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing and shows me its interpretation shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.” Daniel 5:7 Then all the king’s wise men came in; but they could not read the writing, and couldn’t make known to the king the interpretation. Daniel 5:8 Then King Belshazzar was greatly troubled, and his face was changed in him, and his lords were perplexed. Daniel 5:9 The queen by reason of the words of the king and his lords came into the banquet house. The queen spoke and said, “O king, live forever; don’t let your thoughts trouble you, nor let your face be changed. Daniel 5:10 There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of your father, light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him. The king, Nebuchadnezzar, your father—yes, the king, your father—made him master of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and soothsayers, Daniel 5:11 because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, interpreting of dreams, showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will show the interpretation.” Daniel 5:12

title: Daniel 5:13–23
context: Daniel is brought in before Belshazzar, offered purple, gold, and third place in the kingdom, and refuses to be paid for the reading. He recites how the Most High gave Nebuchadnezzar kingship and then humbled him, and rebukes Belshazzar for not humbling his heart though he knew all this, for drinking from the temple vessels, and for praising idols while not honoring the God in whose hand is his breath.
text: Daniel 5:13–23 Daniel Daniel is brought in before Belshazzar, offered purple, gold, and third place in the kingdom, and refuses to be paid for the reading. He recites how the Most High gave Nebuchadnezzar kingship and then humbled him, and rebukes Belshazzar for not humbling his heart though he knew all this, for drinking from the temple vessels, and for praising idols while not honoring the God in whose hand is his breath. Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Are you that Daniel of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father brought out of Judah? Daniel 5:13 I have heard of you, that the spirit of the gods is in you and that light, understanding, and excellent wisdom are found in you. Daniel 5:14 Now the wise men, the enchanters, have been brought in before me, that they should read this writing, and make known to me its interpretation; but they could not show the interpretation of the thing. Daniel 5:15 But I have heard of you, that you can give interpretations and dissolve doubts. Now if you can read the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold around your neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.” Daniel 5:16 Then Daniel answered before the king, “Let your gifts be to yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation. Daniel 5:17 “To you, king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom, and greatness, and glory, and majesty. Daniel 5:18 Because of the greatness that he gave him, all the peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. He killed whom he wanted to, and he kept alive whom he wanted to. He raised up whom he wanted to, and he put down whom he wanted to. Daniel 5:19 But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him. Daniel 5:20 He was driven from the sons of men, and his heart was made like the animals’, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. He was fed with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until he knew that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and that he sets up over it whomever he will. Daniel 5:21 “You, his son, Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this, Daniel 5:22 but have lifted up yourself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your lords, your wives, and your concubines, have drunk wine from them. You have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which don’t see, or hear, or know; and you have not glorified the God in whose hand your breath is, and whose are all your ways. Daniel 5:23

title: Daniel 5:24–31
context: Daniel names the hand as sent from the Most High, reads Mene, Mene, Tekel, and Parsin, and interprets: God has numbered the days of the kingdom and brought it to an end; the king has been weighed and found wanting; the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians. Belshazzar still clothes Daniel in purple and gold as third ruler. That very night the Chaldean king is killed; Darius the Mede receives the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.
text: Daniel 5:24–31 Daniel Daniel names the hand as sent from the Most High, reads Mene, Mene, Tekel, and Parsin, and interprets: God has numbered the days of the kingdom and brought it to an end; the king has been weighed and found wanting; the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians. Belshazzar still clothes Daniel in purple and gold as third ruler. That very night the Chaldean king is killed; Darius the Mede receives the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old. Then the part of the hand was sent from before him, and this writing was inscribed. Daniel 5:24 “This is the writing that was inscribed: ‘MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.’ Daniel 5:25 “This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE: God has counted your kingdom, and brought it to an end. Daniel 5:26 TEKEL: you are weighed in the balances, and are found wanting. Daniel 5:27 PERES: your kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.” Daniel 5:28 Then Belshazzar commanded, and they clothed Daniel with purple, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made proclamation concerning him, that he should be the third ruler in the kingdom. Daniel 5:29 In that night Belshazzar the Chaldean King was slain. Daniel 5:30 Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old. Daniel 5:31

title: Daniel 6:1–10
context: Darius sets 120 satraps over the kingdom and three high officials over them; Daniel is one of the three and is distinguished, so the king plans to set him over the whole realm. Enemies find no complaint except concerning the law of his God. They procure a thirty-day interdict: whoever petitions any god or man except the king is cast into the den of lions. The king signs. When Daniel knew the document was signed, he went into his house—windows open toward Jerusalem—knelt three times a day, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had always done.
text: Daniel 6:1–10 Daniel Darius sets 120 satraps over the kingdom and three high officials over them; Daniel is one of the three and is distinguished, so the king plans to set him over the whole realm. Enemies find no complaint except concerning the law of his God. They procure a thirty-day interdict: whoever petitions any god or man except the king is cast into the den of lions. The king signs. When Daniel knew the document was signed, he went into his house—windows open toward Jerusalem—knelt three times a day, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had always done. It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom one hundred twenty local governors, who should be throughout the whole kingdom; Daniel 6:1 and over them three presidents, of whom Daniel was one, that these local governors might give account to them, and that the king should suffer no loss. Daniel 6:2 Then this Daniel was distinguished above the presidents and the local governors, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm. Daniel 6:3 Then the presidents and the local governors sought to find occasion against Daniel as touching the kingdom; but they could find no occasion or fault, because he was faithful. There wasn’t any error or fault found in him. Daniel 6:4 Then these men said, “We won’t find any occasion against this Daniel, unless we find it against him concerning the law of his God.” Daniel 6:5 Then these presidents and local governors assembled together to the king, and said this to him, “King Darius, live forever! Daniel 6:6 All the presidents of the kingdom, the deputies and the local governors, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to make a strong decree, that whoever asks a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions. Daniel 6:7 Now, O king, establish the decree and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.” Daniel 6:8 Therefore King Darius signed the writing and the decree. Daniel 6:9 When Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house (now his windows were open in his room toward Jerusalem) and he kneeled on his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did before. Daniel 6:10

title: Daniel 6:11–18
context: Men come by agreement and find Daniel making petition and supplication before his God. They cite the injunction; the king answers that the law of the Medes and Persians stands and cannot be revoked. They accuse Daniel the exile of paying no attention to the king or the signed injunction. The king is much distressed, sets his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and labors till sundown to rescue him; they insist the law cannot be changed. Daniel is cast into the den of lions. The king says, May Your God whom you serve continually, he will deliver you. A stone is laid on the mouth of the den and sealed with the king’s signet and his lords’. The king goes to his palace, fasts, takes no diversions, and sleep flees from him.

The king goes to his palace, fasts, takes no diversions, and sleep flees from him. Then these men assembled together, and found Daniel making petition and supplication before his God. Daniel 6:11 Then they came near, and spoke before the king concerning the king’s decree: “Haven’t you signed a decree that every man who makes a petition to any god or man within thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions?” The king answered, “This thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.” Daniel 6:12 Then they answered and said before the king, “That Daniel, who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, doesn’t respect you, O king, nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition three times a day.” Daniel 6:13 Then the king, when he heard these words, was very displeased, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him. Daniel 6:14 Then these men assembled together to the king, and said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians, that no decree nor statute which the king establishes may be changed.” Daniel 6:15 Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Your God whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.” Daniel 6:16 A stone was brought, and laid on the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel. Daniel 6:17 Then the king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting. No musical instruments were brought before him; and his sleep fled from him. Daniel 6:18

title: Daniel 6:19–28
context: At dawn Darius rushes to the lions’ den and finds Daniel alive; God sent his angel, and Daniel trusted him. The accusers suffer the fate they planned for him. Darius issues a decree honoring Daniel’s God as the living God whose kingdom endures. The story closes with Daniel prospering under Darius and Cyrus.
text: Daniel 6:19–28 Daniel At dawn Darius rushes to the lions’ den and finds Daniel alive; God sent his angel, and Daniel trusted him. The accusers suffer the fate they planned for him. Darius issues a decree honoring Daniel’s God as the living God whose kingdom endures. The story closes with Daniel prospering under Darius and Cyrus. Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste to the den of lions. Daniel 6:19 When he came near to Daniel in the den, he cried with a troubled voice. The king spoke and said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, is your God, whom you serve continually, able to deliver you from the lions?” Daniel 6:20 Then Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever! Daniel 6:21 My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me, because innocence was found in me before him; and also before you, O king, I have done no harm.” Daniel 6:22 Then the king was exceedingly glad, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God. Daniel 6:23 The king commanded, and they brought those men who had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions—them, their children, and their wives; and the lions mauled them, and broke all their bones in pieces before they came to the bottom of the den. Daniel 6:24 Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: “Peace be multiplied to you. Daniel 6:25 “I make a decree that in all the dominion of my kingdom men tremble and fear before the God of Daniel. “For he is the living God, and steadfast forever. His kingdom is that which will not be destroyed. His dominion will be even to the end. Daniel 6:26 He delivers and rescues. He works signs and wonders in heaven and in earth, who has delivered Daniel from the power of the lions.” Daniel 6:27 So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian. Daniel 6:28

title: Daniel 7:1–14
context: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel sees a dream: four winds stir the great sea; four great beasts come up, different from one another. The first is like a lion with eagles’ wings, then made to stand as a man. A man is given to it. A bear raised on one side has three ribs were in its mouth. A leopard has four wings of a bird and four heads. A fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful, with iron teeth and ten horns; a little horn with eyes like a man’s and a mouth speaking great things. Thrones are placed; the Ancient of Days takes his seat; the court sits; the books are opened; the beast is killed; the rest of the animals have their lives prolonged for a season. Then with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man comes to the Ancient of Days and is presented before him; to him is given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him—an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away, a kingdom that will not be destroyed.
text: Daniel 7:1–14 Daniel In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel sees a dream: four winds stir the great sea; four great beasts come up, different from one another. The first is like a lion with eagles’ wings, then made to stand as a man. A man is given to it. A bear raised on one side has three ribs were in its mouth. A leopard has four wings of a bird and four heads. A fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful, with iron teeth and ten horns; a little horn with eyes like a man’s and a mouth speaking great things. Thrones are placed; the Ancient of Days takes his seat; the court sits; the books are opened; the beast is killed; the rest of the animals have their lives prolonged for a season. Then with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man comes to the Ancient of Days and is presented before him; to him is given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him—an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away, a kingdom that will not be destroyed. In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and visions of his head while on his bed. Then he wrote the dream and told the sum of the matters. Daniel 7:1 Daniel spoke and said, “I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the sky broke out on the great sea. Daniel 7:2 Four great animals came up from the sea, different from one another. Daniel 7:3 “The first was like a lion, and had eagle’s wings. I watched until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the earth and made to stand on two feet as a man. A man’s heart was given to it. Daniel 7:4 “Behold, there was another animal, a second, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. They said this to it: ‘Arise! Devour much flesh!’ Daniel 7:5 “After this I saw, and behold, another, like a leopard, which had on its back four wings of a bird. The animal also had four heads; and dominion was given to it. Daniel 7:6 “After this I saw in the night visions, and, behold, there was a fourth animal, awesome, powerful, and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth. It devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet. It was different from all the animals that were before it. It had ten horns. Daniel 7:7 “I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots; and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking arrogantly. Daniel 7:8 “I watched until thrones were placed, and one who was Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire. Daniel 7:9 A fiery stream issued and came out from before him. Thousands of thousands ministered to him. Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The judgment was set. The books were opened. Daniel 7:10 “I watched at that time because of the voice of the arrogant words which the horn spoke. I watched even until the animal was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire. Daniel 7:11 As for the rest of the animals, their dominion was taken away; yet their lives were prolonged for a season and a time. Daniel 7:12 “I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before him. Daniel 7:13 Dominion was given him, and glory, and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away, and his kingdom one that will not be destroyed. Daniel 7:14

title: Daniel 7:15–28
context: Troubled by his vision, Daniel asks an attendant to explain it. The four beasts are four kingdoms, but the kingdom will finally be given to the saints of the Most High. The fourth beast’s arrogant horn wages war against the saints for a set time until the court sits and his dominion is taken away. Daniel keeps the matter in his heart, shaken by what he has seen.
text: Daniel 7:15–28 Daniel Troubled by his vision, Daniel asks an attendant to explain it. The four beasts are four kingdoms, but the kingdom will finally be given to the saints of the Most High. The fourth beast’s arrogant horn wages war against the saints for a set time until the court sits and his dominion is taken away. Daniel keeps the matter in his heart, shaken by what he has seen. “As for me, Daniel, my spirit was grieved within my body, and the visions of my head troubled me. Daniel 7:15 I came near to one of those who stood by, and asked him the truth concerning all this. “So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things. Daniel 7:16 ‘These great animals, which are four, are four kings, who will arise out of the earth. Daniel 7:17 But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.’ Daniel 7:18 “Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth animal, which was different from all of them, exceedingly terrible, whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of bronze; which devoured, broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet; Daniel 7:19 and concerning the ten horns that were on its head and the other horn which came up, and before which three fell, even that horn that had eyes and a mouth that spoke arrogantly, whose look was more stout than its fellows. Daniel 7:20 I saw, and the same horn made war with the saints, and prevailed against them, Daniel 7:21 until the Ancient of Days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the Most High, and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom. Daniel 7:22 “So he said, ‘The fourth animal will be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms, and will devour the whole earth, and will tread it down and break it in pieces. Daniel 7:23 As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise out of this kingdom. Another will arise after them; and he will be different from the former, and he will put down three kings. Daniel 7:24 He will speak words against the Most High, and will wear out the saints of the Most High. He will plan to change the times and the law; and they will be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time. Daniel 7:25 “‘But the judgment will be set, and they will take away his dominion, to consume and to destroy it to the end. Daniel 7:26 The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, will be given to the people of the saints of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him.’ Daniel 7:27 “Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face was changed in me; but I kept the matter in my heart.” Daniel 7:28

title: Daniel 8:1–14
context: In the third year of Belshazzar a vision appears to Daniel, after that which appeared at the first. He sees in the vision: Susa the citadel, in Elam, at the Ulai canal. A ram with two horns, one higher and later, charging west, north, and south; he became great. A male goat from the west, without touching the ground; a notable horn between his eyes. He struck the ram, broke both horns, trampled him. The goat became exceedingly great; the great horn was broken; four notable horns toward the four winds. Out of one, a little horn, grew toward the south, the east, and the glorious land. It grew to the host of heaven; some of the army and of the stars thrown down. It became great as the prince of the army; the regular burnt offering taken away; the sanctuary overthrown. A host given over with the continual burnt offering because of transgression; truth thrown to the ground; it acted and prospered. A holy one: how long? Two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings. Then the sanctuary will be restored to its rightful state.
text: Daniel 8:1–14 Daniel In the third year of Belshazzar a vision appears to Daniel, after that which appeared at the first. He sees in the vision: Susa the citadel, in Elam, at the Ulai canal. A ram with two horns, one higher and later, charging west, north, and south; he became great. A male goat from the west, without touching the ground; a notable horn between his eyes.
