There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah didn’t show them. Isaiah 39:2 Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah, and asked him, “What did these men say? From where did they come to you?” Hezekiah said, “They have come from a country far from me, even from Babylon.” Isaiah 39:3 Then he asked, “What have they seen in your house?” Hezekiah answered, “They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them.” Isaiah 39:4 Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of Armies: Isaiah 39:5 ‘Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up until today, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says the LORD. Isaiah 39:6 ‘They will take away your sons who will issue from you, whom you shall father, and they will be eunuchs in the king of Babylon’s palace.’” Isaiah 39:7 Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The LORD’s word which you have spoken is good.” He said moreover, “For there will be peace and truth in my days.” Isaiah 39:8

title: Isaiah 4:1–6
context: After men fall by the sword, seven women take hold of one man, asking only his name to take away reproach. In that day, the LORD’s branch of the Lord is beautiful, the land’s fruit the honor of Israel’s survivors. Whoever is left in Zion is called holy, recorded for life, when the Lord has washed the daughters’ filth and Jerusalem’s blood by the spirit of justice and burning. Over Zion He creates cloud and fire; a booth for shade and shelter.
text: Isaiah 4:1–6 Isaiah After men fall by the sword, seven women take hold of one man, asking only his name to take away reproach. In that day, the LORD’s branch of the Lord is beautiful, the land’s fruit the honor of Israel’s survivors. Whoever is left in Zion is called holy, recorded for life, when the Lord has washed the daughters’ filth and Jerusalem’s blood by the spirit of justice and burning. Over Zion He creates cloud and fire; a booth for shade and shelter. Seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, “We will eat our own bread, and wear our own clothing. Just let us be called by your name. Take away our reproach.” Isaiah 4:1 In that day, the LORD’s branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Israel. Isaiah 4:2 It will happen that he who is left in Zion and he who remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy, even everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem, Isaiah 4:3 when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from within it, by the spirit of justice and by the spirit of burning. Isaiah 4:4 The LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night, for over all the glory will be a canopy. Isaiah 4:5 There will be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain. Isaiah 4:6

title: Isaiah 40:1–11
context: A new word after judgment: Comfort, comfort my people. Jerusalem’s warfare is ended, iniquity pardoned, double received. A voice in the wilderness prepares the LORD’s way; glory will be revealed, all flesh will see it. All flesh is grass, but the word of our God stands forever. Zion, herald of good news, is told to say to Judah, Behold your God—He comes with might as a shepherd who gathers lambs and gently leads.
text: Isaiah 40:1–11 Isaiah A new word after judgment: Comfort, comfort my people. Jerusalem’s warfare is ended, iniquity pardoned, double received. A voice in the wilderness prepares the LORD’s way; glory will be revealed, all flesh will see it. All flesh is grass, but the word of our God stands forever. Zion, herald of good news, is told to say to Judah, Behold your God—He comes with might as a shepherd who gathers lambs and gently leads. “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God. Isaiah 40:1 “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.” Isaiah 40:2 The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of the LORD in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God. Isaiah 40:3 Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low. The uneven shall be made level, and the rough places a plain. Isaiah 40:4 The LORD’s glory shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it.” Isaiah 40:5 The voice of one saying, “Cry out!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field. Isaiah 40:6 The grass withers, the flower fades, because the LORD’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass. Isaiah 40:7 The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.” Isaiah 40:8 You who tell good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who tell good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength! Lift it up! Don’t be afraid! Say to the cities of Judah, “Behold, your God!” Isaiah 40:9 Behold, the Lord GOD will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him. Isaiah 40:10 He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young. Isaiah 40:11

title: Isaiah 40:12–31
context: After comfort and the shepherd, Isaiah asks who has measured waters and heavens, who taught the LORD, and to whom God may be likened. Nations are a drop; idols are wood that will not move; He sits above the circle of the earth, calls the starry host by name, and answers Jacob’s complaint: the everlasting God does not faint. Youths fall; those who wait for the LORD renew their strength.
text: Isaiah 40:12–31 Isaiah After comfort and the shepherd, Isaiah asks who has measured waters and heavens, who taught the LORD, and to whom God may be likened. Nations are a drop; idols are wood that will not move; He sits above the circle of the earth, calls the starry host by name, and answers Jacob’s complaint: the everlasting God does not faint. Youths fall; those who wait for the LORD renew their strength. Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the dust of the earth in a measuring basket, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance? Isaiah 40:12 Who has directed the LORD’s Spirit, or has taught him as his counselor? Isaiah 40:13 Who did he take counsel with, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding? Isaiah 40:14 Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, and are regarded as a speck of dust on a balance. Behold, he lifts up the islands like a very little thing. Isaiah 40:15 Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering. Isaiah 40:16 All the nations are like nothing before him. They are regarded by him as less than nothing, and vanity. Isaiah 40:17 To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him? Isaiah 40:18 A workman has cast an image, and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it. Isaiah 40:19 He who is too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot. He seeks a skillful workman to set up a carved image for him that will not be moved. Isaiah 40:20 Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? Haven’t you been told from the beginning? Haven’t you understood from the foundations of the earth? Isaiah 40:21 It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in, Isaiah 40:22 who brings princes to nothing, who makes the judges of the earth meaningless. Isaiah 40:23 They are planted scarcely. They are sown scarcely. Their stock has scarcely taken root in the ground. He merely blows on them, and they wither, and the whirlwind takes them away as stubble. Isaiah 40:24 “To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?” says the Holy One. Isaiah 40:25 Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their army by number. He calls them all by name. By the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, not one is lacking. Isaiah 40:26 Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and the justice due me is disregarded by my God”? Isaiah 40:27 Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable. Isaiah 40:28 He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might. Isaiah 40:29 Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall; Isaiah 40:30 but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint. Isaiah 40:31

title: Isaiah 41:1–20
context: The LORD summons the coastlands to silence and judgment. Who has raised up one from the east, and who called the generations from the beginning? He is the first and with the last. Coastlands fear and idol-craftsmen nail their god so it cannot move; but Israel is named servant, Jacob chosen, seed of Abraham—fear not, I am with you. Worm Jacob is made a threshing sledge; the poor and needy are given water in the desert, that they may know the Holy One of Israel has done it.
text: Isaiah 41:1–20 Isaiah The LORD summons the coastlands to silence and judgment. Who has raised up one from the east, and who called the generations from the beginning? He is the first and with the last. Coastlands fear and idol-craftsmen nail their god so it cannot move; but Israel is named servant, Jacob chosen, seed of Abraham—fear not, I am with you. Worm Jacob is made a threshing sledge; the poor and needy are given water in the desert, that they may know the Holy One of Israel has done it. “Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near, then let them speak. Let’s meet together for judgment. Isaiah 41:1 Who has raised up one from the east? Who called him to his feet in righteousness? He hands over nations to him and makes him rule over kings. He gives them like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow. Isaiah 41:2 He pursues them and passes by safely, even by a way that he had not gone with his feet. Isaiah 41:3 Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, the first, and with the last, I am he.” Isaiah 41:4 The islands have seen, and fear. The ends of the earth tremble. They approach, and come. Isaiah 41:5 Everyone helps his neighbor. They say to their brothers, “Be strong!” Isaiah 41:6 So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. He who smooths with the hammer encourages him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, “It is good;” and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter. Isaiah 41:7 “But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham my friend, Isaiah 41:8 you whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant. I have chosen you and have not cast you away.’ Isaiah 41:9 Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness. Isaiah 41:10 Behold, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. Those who strive with you will be like nothing, and shall perish. Isaiah 41:11 You will seek them, and won’t find them, even those who contend with you. Those who war against you will be as nothing, as a nonexistent thing. Isaiah 41:12 For I, the LORD your God, will hold your right hand, saying to you, ‘Don’t be afraid. I will help you.’ Isaiah 41:13 Don’t be afraid, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I will help you,” says the LORD. “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 41:14 Behold, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and will make the hills like chaff. Isaiah 41:15 You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in the LORD. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 41:16 The poor and needy seek water, and there is none. Their tongue fails for thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them. Isaiah 41:17 I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water. Isaiah 41:18 I will put cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I will set cypress trees, pine, and box trees together in the desert; Isaiah 41:19 that they may see, know, consider, and understand together, that the LORD’s hand has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it. Isaiah 41:20

title: Isaiah 41:21–29
context: The LORD, King of Jacob, summons the idols to court: set forth your case, bring your proofs, tell us the former things and the things to come, that we may know you are gods. They cannot do good or harm; they are nothing, and an abomination is he who chooses them. God stirred one from the north and from the rising of the sun to trample rulers as mortar; none of the images declared it beforehand. Zion is given a herald of good news, and the molten images are wind.
text: Isaiah 41:21–29 Isaiah The LORD, King of Jacob, summons the idols to court: set forth your case, bring your proofs, tell us the former things and the things to come, that we may know you are gods. They cannot do good or harm; they are nothing, and an abomination is he who chooses them. God stirred one from the north and from the rising of the sun to trample rulers as mortar; none of the images declared it beforehand. Zion is given a herald of good news, and the molten images are wind. Produce your cause,” says the LORD. “Bring out your strong reasons!” says the King of Jacob. Isaiah 41:21 “Let them announce and declare to us what will happen! Declare the former things, what they are, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them; or show us things to come. Isaiah 41:22 Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do good, or do evil, that we may be dismayed, and see it together. Isaiah 41:23 Behold, you are nothing, and your work is nothing. He who chooses you is an abomination. Isaiah 41:24 “I have raised up one from the north, and he has come, from the rising of the sun, one who calls on my name, and he shall come on rulers as on mortar, and as the potter treads clay. Isaiah 41:25 Who has declared it from the beginning, that we may know? and before, that we may say, ‘He is right’? Surely, there is no one who declares. Surely, there is no one who shows. Surely, there is no one who hears your words. Isaiah 41:26 I am the first to say to Zion, ‘Behold, look at them;’ and I will give one who brings good news to Jerusalem. Isaiah 41:27 When I look, there is no man, even among them there is no counselor who, when I ask, can answer a word. Isaiah 41:28 Behold, all of their deeds are vanity and nothing. Their molten images are wind and confusion. Isaiah 41:29

title: Isaiah 42:1–9
context: After the Cyrus-token of chapter 41, the LORD sets forth a more eminent servant: chosen, upheld, Spirit-endowed, who will bring justice to the nations without crying in the street. He won’t break a bruised reed or quench a dimly burning wick; he will not fail or be discouraged until justice is established, and the islands wait for his law. God the LORD, he who created the heavens and gives breath to its people, calls this servant in righteousness—a covenant for the people and a light for the nations—to open blind eyes and bring prisoners from darkness. His name is the LORD; his glory he will not give to idols; former things have come to pass, and he declares new things before they spring forth.
text: Isaiah 42:1–9 Isaiah After the Cyrus-token of chapter 41, the LORD sets forth a more eminent servant: chosen, upheld, Spirit-endowed, who will bring justice to the nations without crying in the street. He won’t break a bruised reed or quench a dimly burning wick; he will not fail or be discouraged until justice is established, and the islands wait for his law. God the LORD, he who created the heavens and gives breath to its people, calls this servant in righteousness—a covenant for the people and a light for the nations—to open blind eyes and bring prisoners from darkness. His name is the LORD; his glory he will not give to idols; former things have come to pass, and he declares new things before they spring forth. “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights: I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations. Isaiah 42:1 He will not shout, nor raise his voice, nor cause it to be heard in the street. Isaiah 42:2 He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice. Isaiah 42:3 He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has set justice on the earth, and the islands wait for his law.” Isaiah 42:4 God the LORD, he who created the heavens and stretched them out, he who spread out the earth and that which comes out of it, he who gives breath to its people and spirit to those who walk in it, says: Isaiah 42:5 “I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness. I will hold your hand. I will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations, Isaiah 42:6 to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison. Isaiah 42:7 “I am the LORD. That is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images. Isaiah 42:8 Behold, the former things have happened and I declare new things. I tell you about them before they come up.” Isaiah 42:9

title: Isaiah 42:10–17
context: After the Servant-song of 42:1–9, the coastlands are called to sing a new song: praise from the end of the earth, from sea and desert, Kedar and Sela, mountains and islands. The LORD will go out like a mighty man, stirring zeal like a man of war; he has held his peace a long time, and now cries out like a woman in labor. Mountains and hills are laid waste, rivers turned to islands; he leads the blind by a way they do not know, darkness into light, and he does not forsake them. Those who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, “You are our gods,” will be turned back and utterly disappointed.
text: Isaiah 42:10–17 Isaiah After the Servant-song of 42:1–9, the coastlands are called to sing a new song: praise from the end of the earth, from sea and desert, Kedar and Sela, mountains and islands. The LORD will go out like a mighty man, stirring zeal like a man of war; he has held his peace a long time, and now cries out like a woman in labor. Mountains and hills are laid waste, rivers turned to islands; he leads the blind by a way they do not know, darkness into light, and he does not forsake them. Those who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, “You are our gods,” will be turned back and utterly disappointed. Sing to the LORD a new song, and his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is therein, the islands and their inhabitants. Isaiah 42:10 Let the wilderness and its cities raise their voices, with the villages that Kedar inhabits. Let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Let them shout from the top of the mountains! Isaiah 42:11 Let them give glory to the LORD, and declare his praise in the islands. Isaiah 42:12 The LORD will go out like a mighty man. He will stir up zeal like a man of war. He will raise a war cry. Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his enemies. Isaiah 42:13 “I have been silent a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a travailing woman. I will both gasp and pant. Isaiah 42:14 I will destroy mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs. I will make the rivers islands, and will dry up the pools. Isaiah 42:15 I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know. I will lead them in paths that they don’t know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them. Isaiah 42:16 “Those who trust in engraved images, who tell molten images, ‘You are our gods,’ will be turned back. They will be utterly disappointed. Isaiah 42:17

title: Isaiah 42:18–25
context: After the new song and the warrior of 42:10–17, the address turns: Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see. The servant and messenger here are not the Christ-Servant of 42:1–9 but historic Judah—those who had the Law, saw many things, and would not observe. It pleased the LORD, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law and make it honorable; yet this is a people robbed and plundered, trapped in holes, taken as spoil with no one to say, “Restore them!” Who gave Jacob to the looter? The LORD, against whom they sinned; he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and they did not take it to heart.
text: Isaiah 42:18–25 Isaiah After the new song and the warrior of 42:10–17, the address turns: Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see. The servant and messenger here are not the Christ-Servant of 42:1–9 but historic Judah—those who had the Law, saw many things, and would not observe. It pleased the LORD, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law and make it honorable; yet this is a people robbed and plundered, trapped in holes, taken as spoil with no one to say, “Restore them!” Who gave Jacob to the looter? The LORD, against whom they sinned; he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and they did not take it to heart. “Hear, you deaf, and look, you blind, that you may see. Isaiah 42:18 Who is blind, but my servant? Or who is as deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is as blind as he who is at peace, and as blind as the LORD’s servant? Isaiah 42:19 You see many things, but don’t observe. His ears are open, but he doesn’t listen. Isaiah 42:20 It pleased the LORD, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law and make it honorable. Isaiah 42:21 But this is a robbed and plundered people. All of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prisons. They have become captives, and no one delivers, and a plunder, and no one says, ‘Restore them!’ Isaiah 42:22 Who is there among you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come? Isaiah 42:23 Who gave Jacob as plunder, and Israel to the robbers? Didn’t the LORD, he against whom we have sinned? For they would not walk in his ways, and they disobeyed his law. Isaiah 42:24 Therefore he poured the fierceness of his anger on him, and the strength of battle. It set him on fire all around, but he didn’t know. It burned him, but he didn’t take it to heart.” Isaiah 42:25

title: Isaiah 43:1–13
context: After the plundered servant of 42:18–25, the word turns: But now the LORD, who created Jacob and formed Israel, says: Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you; you are mine. Waters and rivers will not overwhelm them, nor fire consume them; Egypt, Cush, and Seba are given as ransom because they are precious and loved. Offspring are gathered from east and west, sons and daughters from the ends of the earth, everyone called by his name and created for his glory. Nations assemble to prove their idols; Israel is the LORD’s witness: before him no god was formed, besides him there is no savior, and none can deliver from his hand or turn his work back.
text: Isaiah 43:1–13 Isaiah After the plundered servant of 42:18–25, the word turns: But now the LORD, who created Jacob and formed Israel, says: Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you; you are mine. Waters and rivers will not overwhelm them, nor fire consume them; Egypt, Cush, and Seba are given as ransom because they are precious and loved. Offspring are gathered from east and west, sons and daughters from the ends of the earth, everyone called by his name and created for his glory. Nations assemble to prove their idols; Israel is the LORD’s witness: before him no god was formed, besides him there is no savior, and none can deliver from his hand or turn his work back. But now the LORD who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine. Isaiah 43:1 When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you. Isaiah 43:2 For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place. Isaiah 43:3 Since you have been precious and honored in my sight, and I have loved you, therefore I will give people in your place, and nations instead of your life. Isaiah 43:4 Don’t be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east, and gather you from the west. Isaiah 43:5 I will tell the north, ‘Give them up!’ and tell the south, ‘Don’t hold them back! Bring my sons from far away, and my daughters from the ends of the earth— Isaiah 43:6 everyone who is called by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.’” Isaiah 43:7 Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears. Isaiah 43:8 Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the peoples be assembled. Who among them can declare this, and show us former things? Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified, or let them hear, and say, “That is true.” Isaiah 43:9 “You are my witnesses,” says the LORD, “With my servant whom I have chosen; that you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he. Before me there was no God formed, neither will there be after me. Isaiah 43:10 I myself am the LORD. Besides me, there is no savior. Isaiah 43:11 I have declared, I have saved, and I have shown, and there was no strange god among you. Therefore you are my witnesses”, says the LORD, “and I am God. Isaiah 43:12 Yes, since the day was, I am he. There is no one who can deliver out of my hand. I will work, and who can hinder it?” Isaiah 43:13

title: Isaiah 43:14–21
context: After the witnesses of 43:1–13—Fear not, I am he, none can turn back his work—the Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, sends to Babylon and brings the Chaldeans down as fugitives in the ships in which they rejoice. He is the LORD, Creator of Israel, their King. The same God who made a way in the sea and quenched Pharaoh’s chariot and horse now says, Remember the former things: he is doing a new thing, a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, water for the wild beasts and for his chosen people, whom he formed for himself that they might declare his praise.
text: Isaiah 43:14–21 Isaiah After the witnesses of 43:1–13—Fear not, I am he, none can turn back his work—the Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, sends to Babylon and brings the Chaldeans down as fugitives in the ships in which they rejoice. He is the LORD, Creator of Israel, their King. The same God who made a way in the sea and quenched Pharaoh’s chariot and horse now says, Remember the former things: he is doing a new thing, a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, water for the wild beasts and for his chosen people, whom he formed for himself that they might declare his praise. The LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: “For your sake, I have sent to Babylon, and I will bring all of them down as fugitives, even the Chaldeans, in the ships of their rejoicing. Isaiah 43:14 I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.” Isaiah 43:15 The LORD, who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters, Isaiah 43:16 who brings out the chariot and horse, the army and the mighty man (they lie down together, they shall not rise; they are extinct, they are quenched like a wick) says: Isaiah 43:17 “Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old. Isaiah 43:18 Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert. Isaiah 43:19 The animals of the field, the jackals and the ostriches, shall honor me, because I give water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen, Isaiah 43:20 the people which I formed for myself, that they might declare my praise. Isaiah 43:21

title: Isaiah 43:22–28
context: After the new thing of 43:14–21—Babylon brought down, a way in the wilderness, rivers in the desert, a people formed for himself that they might declare his praise—the word turns on Jacob: Yet you have not called on me; you have been weary of me, Israel. They have not brought sheep or honored him with sacrifices; they have burdened him with their sins and wearied him with their iniquities. He himself blots out their transgressions for his own sake and will not remember their sins, then summons them to argue their case; their first father sinned and their mediators transgressed, and therefore he will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.
text: Isaiah 43:22–28 Isaiah After the new thing of 43:14–21—Babylon brought down, a way in the wilderness, rivers in the desert, a people formed for himself that they might declare his praise—the word turns on Jacob: Yet you have not called on me; you have been weary of me, Israel. They have not brought sheep or honored him with sacrifices; they have burdened him with their sins and wearied him with their iniquities. He himself blots out their transgressions for his own sake and will not remember their sins, then summons them to argue their case; their first father sinned and their mediators transgressed, and therefore he will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult. Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; but you have been weary of me, Israel. Isaiah 43:22 You have not brought me any of your sheep for burnt offerings, neither have you honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense. Isaiah 43:23 You have bought me no sweet cane with money, nor have you filled me with the fat of your sacrifices, but you have burdened me with your sins. You have wearied me with your iniquities. Isaiah 43:24 I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins. Isaiah 43:25 Put me in remembrance. Let us plead together. Declare your case, that you may be justified. Isaiah 43:26 Your first father sinned, and your teachers have transgressed against me. Isaiah 43:27 Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.” Isaiah 43:28

title: Isaiah 44:1–8
context: After 43:22–28—Jacob weary of the LORD, empty cult, sins that wearied him, blotting out for his own sake, an empty courtroom, first father and mediators, princes of the sanctuary profaned and Jacob delivered to destruction—the word turns: But now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen. The LORD who made them and formed them from the womb says Fear not to Jacob and Jeshurun; he will pour water on him who is thirsty, and his Spirit upon their offspring, and they shall spring up like willows by streams. One will say, I am the LORD’s; another will name himself by Israel. Then the King of Israel and his Redeemer: I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God; you are my witnesses; there is no Rock.
text: Isaiah 44:1–8 Isaiah After 43:22–28—Jacob weary of the LORD, empty cult, sins that wearied him, blotting out for his own sake, an empty courtroom, first father and mediators, princes of the sanctuary profaned and Jacob delivered to destruction—the word turns: But now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen. The LORD who made them and formed them from the womb says Fear not to Jacob and Jeshurun; he will pour water on him who is thirsty, and his Spirit upon their offspring, and they shall spring up like willows by streams. One will say, I am the LORD’s; another will name himself by Israel. Then the King of Israel and his Redeemer: I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God; you are my witnesses; there is no Rock. Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen. Isaiah 44:1 This is what the LORD who made you, and formed you from the womb, who will help you says: “Don’t be afraid, Jacob my servant; and you, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen. Isaiah 44:2 For I will pour water on him who is thirsty, and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your descendants, and my blessing on your offspring; Isaiah 44:3 and they will spring up among the grass, as willows by the watercourses. Isaiah 44:4 One will say, ‘I am the LORD’s.’ Another will be called by the name of Jacob; and another will write with his hand ‘to the LORD,’ and honor the name of Israel.” Isaiah 44:5 This is what the LORD, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, the LORD of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God. Isaiah 44:6 Who is like me? Who will call, and will declare it, and set it in order for me, since I established the ancient people? Let them declare the things that are coming, and that will happen. Isaiah 44:7 Don’t fear, neither be afraid. Haven’t I declared it to you long ago, and shown it? You are my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? Indeed, there is not. I don’t know any other Rock.” Isaiah 44:8

title: Isaiah 44:21–28
context: After 44:9–20—fashioners of idols are nothing; craftsmen are mere men; the same wood serves for fire and for a god; they pray Deliver me to a block of wood; their eyes are shut so they cannot see; a deluded heart cannot ask, Isn’t this thing in my right hand a lie?—the word turns: Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I have formed you. You will not be forgotten; transgressions blotted like a cloud; return, for I have redeemed you. Heavens, earth, mountains, and forest sing: the LORD has redeemed Jacob. Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb says: I am the LORD, who makes all things; who frustrates the signs of the liars, who confirms the word of his servant, who says of Jerusalem, She will be inhabited, who says to the deep, Be dry, who says of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my purpose; Jerusalem built; the temple’s foundation laid.
text: Isaiah 44:21–28 Isaiah After 44:9–20—fashioners of idols are nothing; craftsmen are mere men; the same wood serves for fire and for a god; they pray Deliver me to a block of wood; their eyes are shut so they cannot see; a deluded heart cannot ask, Isn’t this thing in my right hand a lie?—the word turns: Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I have formed you. You will not be forgotten; transgressions blotted like a cloud; return, for I have redeemed you. Heavens, earth, mountains, and forest sing: the LORD has redeemed Jacob. Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb says: I am the LORD, who makes all things; who frustrates the signs of the liars, who confirms the word of his servant, who says of Jerusalem, She will be inhabited, who says to the deep, Be dry, who says of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my purpose; Jerusalem built; the temple’s foundation laid. Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I have formed you. You are my servant. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me. Isaiah 44:21 I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you. Isaiah 44:22 Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, all of your trees, for the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel. Isaiah 44:23 The LORD, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb says: “I am the LORD, who makes all things; who alone stretches out the heavens; who spreads out the earth by myself; Isaiah 44:24 who frustrates the signs of the liars, and makes diviners mad; who turns wise men backward, and makes their knowledge foolish; Isaiah 44:25 who confirms the word of his servant, and performs the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be inhabited;’ and of the cities of Judah, ‘They will be built,’ and ‘I will raise up its waste places;’ Isaiah 44:26 who says to the deep, ‘Be dry,’ and ‘I will dry up your rivers,’ Isaiah 44:27 who says of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure,’ even saying of Jerusalem, ‘She will be built;’ and of the temple, ‘Your foundation will be laid.’” Isaiah 44:28

title: Isaiah 44:9–20
context: After 44:1–8—Don’t be afraid, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun, my chosen; water on the thirsty and the Spirit on their offspring; I am the first and the last, and there is no God besides me; you are my witnesses; there is no other Rock—the word turns: everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses don’t see, nor know. Craftsmen are only human; the same tree is fuel, bread, and a god; they pray Deliver me to a block of wood; a deluded heart cannot say, Isn’t there a lie in my right hand?
text: Isaiah 44:9–20 Isaiah After 44:1–8—Don’t be afraid, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun, my chosen; water on the thirsty and the Spirit on their offspring; I am the first and the last, and there is no God besides me; you are my witnesses; there is no other Rock—the word turns: everyone who makes an engraved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses don’t see, nor know. Craftsmen are only human; the same tree is fuel, bread, and a god; they pray Deliver me to a block of wood; a deluded heart cannot say, Isn’t there a lie in my right hand? Everyone who makes a carved image is vain. The things that they delight in will not profit. Their own witnesses don’t see, nor know, that they may be disappointed. Isaiah 44:9 Who has fashioned a god, or molds an image that is profitable for nothing? Isaiah 44:10 Behold, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them stand up. They will fear. They will be put to shame together. Isaiah 44:11 The blacksmith takes an ax, works in the coals, fashions it with hammers, and works it with his strong arm. He is hungry, and his strength fails; he drinks no water, and is faint. Isaiah 44:12 The carpenter stretches out a line. He marks it out with a pencil. He shapes it with planes. He marks it out with compasses, and shapes it like the figure of a man, with the beauty of a man, to reside in a house. Isaiah 44:13 He cuts down cedars for himself, and takes the cypress and the oak, and strengthens for himself one among the trees of the forest. He plants a cypress tree, and the rain nourishes it. Isaiah 44:14 Then it will be for a man to burn; and he takes some of it and warms himself. Yes, he burns it and bakes bread. Yes, he makes a god and worships it; he makes it a carved image, and falls down to it. Isaiah 44:15 He burns part of it in the fire. With part of it, he eats meat. He roasts a roast and is satisfied. Yes, he warms himself and says, “Aha! I am warm. I have seen the fire.” Isaiah 44:16 The rest of it he makes into a god, even his engraved image. He bows down to it and worships, and prays to it, and says, “Deliver me, for you are my god!” Isaiah 44:17 They don’t know, neither do they consider, for he has shut their eyes, that they can’t see, and their hearts, that they can’t understand. Isaiah 44:18 No one thinks, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, “I have burned part of it in the fire. Yes, I have also baked bread on its coals. I have roasted meat and eaten it. Shall I make the rest of it into an abomination? Shall I bow down to a tree trunk?” Isaiah 44:19 He feeds on ashes. A deceived heart has turned him aside; and he can’t deliver his soul, nor say, “Isn’t there a lie in my right hand?” Isaiah 44:20

title: Isaiah 45:1–13
context: The LORD addresses Cyrus, the Persian conqueror, as his anointed, whose conquests serve Israel’s restoration though Cyrus does not know him. God declares himself sole Creator of light and darkness, well-being and calamity. Those who question his use of a pagan king are like clay arguing with the potter.
text: Isaiah 45:1–13 Isaiah The LORD addresses Cyrus, the Persian conqueror, as his anointed, whose conquests serve Israel’s restoration though Cyrus does not know him. God declares himself sole Creator of light and darkness, well-being and calamity. Those who question his use of a pagan king are like clay arguing with the potter. The LORD says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held to subdue nations before him and strip kings of their armor, to open the doors before him, and the gates shall not be shut: Isaiah 45:1 “I will go before you and make the rough places smooth. I will break the doors of bronze in pieces and cut apart the bars of iron. Isaiah 45:2 I will give you the treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places, that you may know that it is I, the LORD, who calls you by your name, even the God of Israel. Isaiah 45:3 For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel my chosen, I have called you by your name. I have given you a title, though you have not known me. Isaiah 45:4 I am the LORD, and there is no one else. Besides me, there is no God. I will strengthen you, though you have not known me, Isaiah 45:5 that they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is no one besides me. I am the LORD, and there is no one else. Isaiah 45:6 I form the light and create darkness. I make peace and create calamity. I am the LORD, who does all these things. Isaiah 45:7 Rain, you heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, that it may produce salvation, and let it cause righteousness to spring up with it. I, the LORD, have created it. Isaiah 45:8 Woe to him who strives with his Maker— a clay pot among the clay pots of the earth! Shall the clay ask him who fashions it, ‘What are you making?’ or your work, ‘He has no hands’? Isaiah 45:9 Woe to him who says to a father, ‘What have you become the father of?’ or to a mother, ‘What have you given birth to?’” Isaiah 45:10 The LORD, the Holy One of Israel and his Maker says: “You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the work of my hands! Isaiah 45:11 I have made the earth, and created man on it. I, even my hands, have stretched out the heavens. I have commanded all their army. Isaiah 45:12 I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight. He shall build my city, and he shall let my exiles go free, not for price nor reward,” says the LORD of Armies. Isaiah 45:13

title: Isaiah 45:14–25
context: Following the Cyrus oracle of 45:1–13—God grasps his anointed’s hand, rebukes the clay that quarrels with its potter, and raises Cyrus to rebuild the city and free the exiles without payment—the chapter widens. The labor of Egypt and the traders of Ethiopia and Seba come over to Israel and confess that God is with her; the prophet names a God who hides himself yet saves; and the invitation goes out to all the ends of the earth to turn and be saved.
text: Isaiah 45:14–25 Isaiah Following the Cyrus oracle of 45:1–13—God grasps his anointed’s hand, rebukes the clay that quarrels with its potter, and raises Cyrus to rebuild the city and free the exiles without payment—the chapter widens. The labor of Egypt and the traders of Ethiopia and Seba come over to Israel and confess that God is with her; the prophet names a God who hides himself yet saves; and the invitation goes out to all the ends of the earth to turn and be saved. The LORD says: “The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you, and they will be yours. They will go after you. They shall come over in chains. They will bow down to you. They will make supplication to you: ‘Surely God is in you; and there is no one else. There is no other god. Isaiah 45:14 Most certainly you are a God who has hidden yourself, God of Israel, the Savior.’” Isaiah 45:15 They will be disappointed, yes, confounded, all of them. Those who are makers of idols will go into confusion together. Isaiah 45:16 Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. You will not be disappointed nor confounded to ages everlasting. Isaiah 45:17 For the LORD who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it and didn’t create it a waste, who formed it to be inhabited says: “I am the LORD. There is no other. Isaiah 45:18 I have not spoken in secret, in a place of the land of darkness. I didn’t say to the offspring of Jacob, ‘Seek me in vain.’ I, the LORD, speak righteousness. I declare things that are right. Isaiah 45:19 “Assemble yourselves and come. Draw near together, you who have escaped from the nations. Those have no knowledge who carry the wood of their engraved image, and pray to a god that can’t save. Isaiah 45:20 Declare and present it. Yes, let them take counsel together. Who has shown this from ancient time? Who has declared it of old? Haven’t I, the LORD? There is no other God besides me, a just God and a Savior. There is no one besides me. Isaiah 45:21 “Look to me, and be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other. Isaiah 45:22 I have sworn by myself. The word has gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and will not be revoked, that to me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall take an oath. Isaiah 45:23 They will say of me, ‘There is righteousness and strength only in the LORD.’” Even to him will men come. All those who raged against him will be disappointed. Isaiah 45:24 All the offspring of Israel will be justified in the LORD, and will rejoice! Isaiah 45:25

title: Isaiah 46:1–13
context: After the call to the ends of the earth in 45:14–25, where every knee is to bow and Israel’s offspring are justified in the LORD, the scene turns to Babylon’s gods. Bel and Nebo are loaded onto tired animals as baggage, while the LORD reminds Jacob that he has carried them from birth and will carry them into old age. He alone tells the end from the beginning, calls a bird of prey from the east, and brings his righteousness near to stubborn hearts.
text: Isaiah 46:1–13 Isaiah After the call to the ends of the earth in 45:14–25, where every knee is to bow and Israel’s offspring are justified in the LORD, the scene turns to Babylon’s gods. Bel and Nebo are loaded onto tired animals as baggage, while the LORD reminds Jacob that he has carried them from birth and will carry them into old age. He alone tells the end from the beginning, calls a bird of prey from the east, and brings his righteousness near to stubborn hearts. Bel bows down. Nebo stoops. Their idols are carried by animals, and on the livestock. The things that you carried around are heavy loads, a burden for the weary. Isaiah 46:1 They stoop and they bow down together. They could not deliver the burden, but they have gone into captivity. Isaiah 46:2 “Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been carried from their birth, that have been carried from the womb. Isaiah 46:3 Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver. Isaiah 46:4 “To whom will you compare me, and consider my equal, and compare me, as if we were the same? Isaiah 46:5 Some pour out gold from the bag, and weigh silver in the balance. They hire a goldsmith, and he makes it a god. They fall down— yes, they worship. Isaiah 46:6 They bear it on their shoulder. They carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands there. It cannot move from its place. Yes, one may cry to it, yet it can not answer. It cannot save him out of his trouble. Isaiah 46:7 “Remember this, and show yourselves men. Bring it to mind again, you transgressors. Isaiah 46:8 Remember the former things of old; for I am God, and there is no other. I am God, and there is none like me. Isaiah 46:9 I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done. I say: My counsel will stand, and I will do all that I please. Isaiah 46:10 I call a ravenous bird from the east, the man of my counsel from a far country. Yes, I have spoken. I will also bring it to pass. I have planned. I will also do it. Isaiah 46:11 Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted, who are far from righteousness! Isaiah 46:12 I bring my righteousness near. It is not far off, and my salvation will not wait. I will grant salvation to Zion, my glory to Israel. Isaiah 46:13

title: Isaiah 47:1–15
context: Chapter 46 showed Babylon’s idols carried off as burdens while the LORD carries his people and announces the end from the beginning. Now Babylon herself is addressed: the pampered virgin daughter must come down from her throne and sit in the dust, grind at the millstones, and be exposed. She showed no mercy to God’s people and boasted, I am, and there is no other; her sorceries and astrologers will not save her.
text: Isaiah 47:1–15 Isaiah Chapter 46 showed Babylon’s idols carried off as burdens while the LORD carries his people and announces the end from the beginning. Now Babylon herself is addressed: the pampered virgin daughter must come down from her throne and sit in the dust, grind at the millstones, and be exposed. She showed no mercy to God’s people and boasted, I am, and there is no other; her sorceries and astrologers will not save her. “Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans. For you will no longer be called tender and delicate. Isaiah 47:1 Take the millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil, lift up your skirt, uncover your legs, and wade through the rivers. Isaiah 47:2 Your nakedness will be uncovered. Yes, your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance, and will spare no one.” Isaiah 47:3 Our Redeemer, the LORD of Armies is his name, is the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 47:4 “Sit in silence, and go into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. For you shall no longer be called the mistress of kingdoms. Isaiah 47:5 I was angry with my people. I profaned my inheritance and gave them into your hand. You showed them no mercy. You laid a very heavy yoke on the aged. Isaiah 47:6 You said, ‘I will be a princess forever,’ so that you didn’t lay these things to your heart, nor did you remember the results. Isaiah 47:7 “Now therefore hear this, you who are given to pleasures, who sit securely, who say in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no one else besides me. I won’t sit as a widow, neither will I know the loss of children.’ Isaiah 47:8 But these two things will come to you in a moment in one day: the loss of children and widowhood. They will come on you in their full measure, in the multitude of your sorceries, and the great abundance of your enchantments. Isaiah 47:9 For you have trusted in your wickedness. You have said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and your knowledge has perverted you. You have said in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no one else besides me.’ Isaiah 47:10 Therefore disaster will come on you. You won’t know when it dawns. Mischief will fall on you. You won’t be able to put it away. Desolation will come on you suddenly, which you don’t understand. Isaiah 47:11 “Stand now with your enchantments and with the multitude of your sorceries, in which you have labored from your youth, as if you might profit, as if you might prevail. Isaiah 47:12 You are wearied in the multitude of your counsels. Now let the astrologers, the stargazers, and the monthly prognosticators stand up and save you from the things that will happen to you. Isaiah 47:13 Behold, they are like stubble. The fire will burn them. They won’t deliver themselves from the power of the flame. It won’t be a coal to warm at or a fire to sit by. Isaiah 47:14 The things that you labored in will be like this: those who have trafficked with you from your youth will each wander in his own way. There will be no one to save you. Isaiah 47:15

title: Isaiah 48:1–11
context: After Babylon’s humiliation in chapter 47, the LORD turns back to his own people. The house of Jacob swears by his name but not in truth or righteousness. God reminds them that he announced former things long ago so they could not credit their idols, and now reveals new, hidden things. He has refined them in the furnace of affliction, and for his own name’s sake he restrains his anger and will not give his glory to another.
text: Isaiah 48:1–11 Isaiah After Babylon’s humiliation in chapter 47, the LORD turns back to his own people. The house of Jacob swears by his name but not in truth or righteousness. God reminds them that he announced former things long ago so they could not credit their idols, and now reveals new, hidden things. He has refined them in the furnace of affliction, and for his own name’s sake he restrains his anger and will not give his glory to another. “Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, and have come out of the waters of Judah. You swear by the LORD’s name, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness— Isaiah 48:1 for they call themselves citizens of the holy city, and rely on the God of Israel; the LORD of Armies is his name. Isaiah 48:2 I have declared the former things from of old. Yes, they went out of my mouth, and I revealed them. I did them suddenly, and they happened. Isaiah 48:3 Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your brow bronze; Isaiah 48:4 therefore I have declared it to you from of old; before it came to pass I showed it to you; lest you should say, ‘My idol has done them. My engraved image and my molten image has commanded them.’ Isaiah 48:5 You have heard it. Now see all this. And you, won’t you declare it? “I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things, which you have not known. Isaiah 48:6 They are created now, and not from of old. Before today, you didn’t hear them, lest you should say, ‘Behold, I knew them.’ Isaiah 48:7 Yes, you didn’t hear. Yes, you didn’t know. Yes, from of old your ear was not opened, for I knew that you dealt very treacherously, and were called a transgressor from the womb. Isaiah 48:8 For my name’s sake, I will defer my anger, and for my praise, I hold it back for you so that I don’t cut you off. Isaiah 48:9 Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver. I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction. Isaiah 48:10 For my own sake, for my own sake, I will do it; for how would my name be profaned? I will not give my glory to another. Isaiah 48:11

title: Isaiah 48:12–22
context: Chapter 48 opened with a rebuke to Israel’s hollow religion and a reminder that God declared the former things before they happened and refined his people for his name’s sake. Now he calls Jacob to listen again: he is the first and the last, the Maker of heaven and earth, the one who has summoned Cyrus against Babylon. The chapter ends with a lament for peace they could have had, the command to go out from Babylon, and a warning that there is no peace for the wicked.
text: Isaiah 48:12–22 Isaiah Chapter 48 opened with a rebuke to Israel’s hollow religion and a reminder that God declared the former things before they happened and refined his people for his name’s sake. Now he calls Jacob to listen again: he is the first and the last, the Maker of heaven and earth, the one who has summoned Cyrus against Babylon. The chapter ends with a lament for peace they could have had, the command to go out from Babylon, and a warning that there is no peace for the wicked. “Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he. I am the first. I am also the last. Isaiah 48:12 Yes, my hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spread out the heavens. when I call to them, they stand up together. Isaiah 48:13 “Assemble yourselves, all of you, and hear! Who among them has declared these things? He whom the LORD loves will do what he likes to Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans. Isaiah 48:14 I, even I, have spoken. Yes, I have called him. I have brought him and he shall make his way prosperous. Isaiah 48:15 “Come near to me and hear this: “From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it happened, I was there.” Now the Lord GOD has sent me with his Spirit. Isaiah 48:16 The LORD, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way that you should go. Isaiah 48:17 Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river and your righteousness like the waves of the sea. Isaiah 48:18 Your offspring also would have been as the sand and the descendants of your body like its grains. His name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.” Isaiah 48:19 Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With the sound of joyful shouting announce this, tell it even to the end of the earth; say, “The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!” Isaiah 48:20 They didn’t thirst when he led them through the deserts. He caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them. He also split the rock and the waters gushed out. Isaiah 48:21 “There is no peace”, says the LORD, “for the wicked.” Isaiah 48:22

title: Isaiah 49:1–7
context: The Servant of the LORD addresses coastlands and peoples from afar: called from the womb, a mouth like a sword, named Israel in whom God will be glorified. Labor among Jacob seemed vain, yet the LORD makes him a light to the nations so that salvation reaches the end of the earth; the despised servant of rulers will see kings arise.
text: Isaiah 49:1–7 Isaiah The Servant of the LORD addresses coastlands and peoples from afar: called from the womb, a mouth like a sword, named Israel in whom God will be glorified. Labor among Jacob seemed vain, yet the LORD makes him a light to the nations so that salvation reaches the end of the earth; the despised servant of rulers will see kings arise. Listen, islands, to me. Listen, you peoples, from afar: the LORD has called me from the womb; from the inside of my mother, he has mentioned my name. Isaiah 49:1 He has made my mouth like a sharp sword. He has hidden me in the shadow of his hand. He has made me a polished shaft. He has kept me close in his quiver. Isaiah 49:2 He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” Isaiah 49:3 But I said, “I have labored in vain. I have spent my strength in vain for nothing; yet surely the justice due to me is with the LORD, and my reward with my God.” Isaiah 49:4 Now the LORD, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, says to bring Jacob again to him, and to gather Israel to him, for I am honorable in the LORD’s eyes, and my God has become my strength. Isaiah 49:5 Indeed, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I will also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.” Isaiah 49:6 The LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, says to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers: “Kings shall see and rise up, princes, and they shall worship, because of the LORD who is faithful, even the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.” Isaiah 49:7

title: Isaiah 49:14–26
context: Zion says the LORD has forsaken her; he answers that a woman may forget her nursing child, yet he will not forget, for he has engraved her on his palms. Children crowd the waste places; captives of the mighty are rescued; all flesh shall know that he is the LORD, Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
text: Isaiah 49:14–26 Isaiah Zion says the LORD has forsaken her; he answers that a woman may forget her nursing child, yet he will not forget, for he has engraved her on his palms. Children crowd the waste places; captives of the mighty are rescued; all flesh shall know that he is the LORD, Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.” Isaiah 49:14 “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you! Isaiah 49:15 Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands. Your walls are continually before me. Isaiah 49:16 Your children hurry. Your destroyers and those who devastated you will leave you. Isaiah 49:17 Lift up your eyes all around, and see: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live,” says the LORD, “you shall surely clothe yourself with them all as with an ornament, and dress yourself with them, like a bride. Isaiah 49:18 “For, as for your waste and your desolate places, and your land that has been destroyed, surely now that land will be too small for the inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away. Isaiah 49:19 The children of your bereavement will say in your ears, ‘This place is too small for me. Give me a place to live in.’ Isaiah 49:20 Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I have been bereaved of my children and am alone, an exile, and wandering back and forth? Who has brought these up? Behold, I was left alone. Where were these?’” Isaiah 49:21 The Lord GOD says, “Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and lift up my banner to the peoples. They shall bring your sons in their bosom, and your daughters shall be carried on their shoulders. Isaiah 49:22 Kings shall be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the earth, and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; and those who wait for me won’t be disappointed.” Isaiah 49:23 Shall the plunder be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captives be delivered? Isaiah 49:24 But the LORD says, “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the plunder retrieved from the fierce, for I will contend with him who contends with you and I will save your children. Isaiah 49:25 I will feed those who oppress you with their own flesh; and they will be drunk on their own blood, as with sweet wine. Then all flesh shall know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.” Isaiah 49:26

title: Isaiah 49:8–13
context: The LORD answers the Servant in a time of favor and a day of salvation, keeps him and gives him for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land. Prisoners are told to come out; They shall not hunger nor thirst; mountains become a road; they come from afar; heavens and earth sing because the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on the afflicted.
text: Isaiah 49:8–13 Isaiah The LORD answers the Servant in a time of favor and a day of salvation, keeps him and gives him for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land. Prisoners are told to come out; They shall not hunger nor thirst; mountains become a road; they come from afar; heavens and earth sing because the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on the afflicted. The LORD says, “I have answered you in an acceptable time. I have helped you in a day of salvation. I will preserve you and give you for a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to make them inherit the desolate heritage, Isaiah 49:8 saying to those who are bound, ‘Come out!’; to those who are in darkness, ‘Show yourselves!’ “They shall feed along the paths, and their pasture shall be on all treeless heights. Isaiah 49:9 They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them, for he who has mercy on them will lead them. He will guide them by springs of water. Isaiah 49:10 I will make all my mountains a road, and my highways shall be exalted. Isaiah 49:11 Behold, these shall come from afar, and behold, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.” Isaiah 49:12 Sing, heavens, and be joyful, earth! Break out into singing, mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted. Isaiah 49:13

title: Isaiah 5:1–7
context: Isaiah sings for his beloved a song of a vineyard on a fertile hill. The beloved digs, clears stones, plants choice vines, builds a tower, hews a vat, and looks for grapes. Wild grapes come. Jerusalem and Judah are told to judge. What could have been done more to do? The hedge will be removed, the wall broken, briers will grow, the clouds commanded not to rain. The vineyard is the house of Israel; Judah his pleasant planting. He looked for justice, and behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, an outcry.
text: Isaiah 5:1–7 Isaiah Isaiah sings for his beloved a song of a vineyard on a fertile hill. The beloved digs, clears stones, plants choice vines, builds a tower, hews a vat, and looks for grapes. Wild grapes come. Jerusalem and Judah are told to judge. What could have been done more to do? The hedge will be removed, the wall broken, briers will grow, the clouds commanded not to rain. The vineyard is the house of Israel; Judah his pleasant planting. He looked for justice, and behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, an outcry. Let me sing for my well beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a very fruitful hill. Isaiah 5:1 He dug it up, gathered out its stones, planted it with the choicest vine, built a tower in the middle of it, and also cut out a wine press in it. He looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes. Isaiah 5:2 “Now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, please judge between me and my vineyard. Isaiah 5:3 What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? Why, when I looked for it to yield grapes, did it yield wild grapes? Isaiah 5:4 Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will take away its hedge, and it will be eaten up. I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled down. Isaiah 5:5 I will lay it a wasteland. It won’t be pruned or hoed, but it will grow briers and thorns. I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain on it.” Isaiah 5:6 For the vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant. He looked for justice, but behold, oppression, for righteousness, but behold, a cry of distress. Isaiah 5:7

title: Isaiah 5:18–30
context: Woe to those who haul sin with cart ropes and dare the Holy One to hurry. Woe to those who swap good and evil, who are wise in their own eyes, heroes at drink, who acquit for a bribe. Fire eats stubble: they have rejected the law. His anger is kindled; the hand is still stretched out. He whistles for nations from the end of the earth. They come swift, unsleeping, hoofs like flint, roaring like lions. On that day, darkness over the land.
text: Isaiah 5:18–30 Isaiah Woe to those who haul sin with cart ropes and dare the Holy One to hurry. Woe to those who swap good and evil, who are wise in their own eyes, heroes at drink, who acquit for a bribe. Fire eats stubble: they have rejected the law. His anger is kindled; the hand is still stretched out. He whistles for nations from the end of the earth. They come swift, unsleeping, hoofs like flint, roaring like lions. On that day, darkness over the land. Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, and wickedness as with cart rope, Isaiah 5:18 who say, “Let him make haste, let him hasten his work, that we may see it; let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!” Isaiah 5:19 Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter! Isaiah 5:20 Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight! Isaiah 5:21 Woe to those who are mighty to drink wine, and champions at mixing strong drink; Isaiah 5:22 who acquit the guilty for a bribe, but deny justice for the innocent! Isaiah 5:23 Therefore as the tongue of fire devours the stubble, and as the dry grass sinks down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust, because they have rejected the law of the LORD of Armies, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 5:24 Therefore the LORD’s anger burns against his people, and he has stretched out his hand against them and has struck them. The mountains tremble, and their dead bodies are as refuse in the middle of the streets. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out. Isaiah 5:25 He will lift up a banner to the nations from far away, and he will whistle for them from the end of the earth. Behold, they will come speedily and swiftly. Isaiah 5:26 No one shall be weary nor stumble among them; no one shall slumber nor sleep, neither shall the belt of their waist be untied, nor the strap of their sandals be broken, Isaiah 5:27 whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent. Their horses’ hoofs will be like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind. Isaiah 5:28 Their roaring will be like a lioness. They will roar like young lions. Yes, they shall roar, and seize their prey and carry it off, and there will be no one to deliver. Isaiah 5:29 They will roar against them in that day like the roaring of the sea. If one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress. The light is darkened in its clouds. Isaiah 5:30

title: Isaiah 5:8–17
context: After the vineyard’s wild grapes, woes fall on those who join house to house until they dwell alone, and on those who rise early for drink and feast without regarding the Lord’s work. Many houses will stand empty; ten acres yield a bath. Therefore the people go into captivity for lack of knowledge; Sheol opens wide. Man is humbled; the LORD of Armies is exalted in justice. Then lambs graze, and nomads eat the ruins of the rich.
text: Isaiah 5:8–17 Isaiah After the vineyard’s wild grapes, woes fall on those who join house to house until they dwell alone, and on those who rise early for drink and feast without regarding the Lord’s work. Many houses will stand empty; ten acres yield a bath. Therefore the people go into captivity for lack of knowledge; Sheol opens wide. Man is humbled; the LORD of Armies is exalted in justice. Then lambs graze, and nomads eat the ruins of the rich. Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field, until there is no room, and you are made to dwell alone in the middle of the land! Isaiah 5:8 In my ears, the LORD of Armies says: “Surely many houses will be desolate, even great and beautiful, unoccupied. Isaiah 5:9 For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah.” Isaiah 5:10 Woe to those who rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink, who stay late into the night, until wine inflames them! Isaiah 5:11 The harp, lyre, tambourine, and flute, with wine, are at their feasts; but they don’t respect the work of the LORD, neither have they considered the operation of his hands. Isaiah 5:12 Therefore my people go into captivity for lack of knowledge. Their honorable men are famished, and their multitudes are parched with thirst. Isaiah 5:13 Therefore Sheol has enlarged its desire, and opened its mouth without measure; and their glory, their multitude, their pomp, and he who rejoices among them, descend into it. Isaiah 5:14 So man is brought low, mankind is humbled, and the eyes of the arrogant ones are humbled; Isaiah 5:15 but the LORD of Armies is exalted in justice, and God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness. Isaiah 5:16 Then the lambs will graze as in their pasture, and strangers will eat the ruins of the rich. Isaiah 5:17

title: Isaiah 50:1–11
context: The LORD asks Judah for a bill of divorce and names no bankrupt creditor: they were sold for iniquities, the mother sent away for transgressions. The Servant’s ear is opened; he is not rebellious, gives his back to those who beat me, and is not put to shame; those who walk in darkness must trust the LORD, while torch-kindlers lie down in torment.
text: Isaiah 50:1–11 Isaiah The LORD asks Judah for a bill of divorce and names no bankrupt creditor: they were sold for iniquities, the mother sent away for transgressions. The Servant’s ear is opened; he is not rebellious, gives his back to those who beat me, and is not put to shame; those who walk in darkness must trust the LORD, while torch-kindlers lie down in torment. The LORD says, “Where is the bill of your mother’s divorce, with which I have put her away? Or to which of my creditors have I sold you? Behold, you were sold for your iniquities, and your mother was put away for your transgressions. Isaiah 50:1 Why, when I came, was there no one? When I called, why was there no one to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it can’t redeem? Or have I no power to deliver? Behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea. I make the rivers a wilderness. Their fish stink because there is no water, and die of thirst. Isaiah 50:2 I clothe the heavens with blackness. I make sackcloth their covering.” Isaiah 50:3 The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him who is weary. He awakens morning by morning, he awakens my ear to hear as those who are taught. Isaiah 50:4 The Lord GOD has opened my ear. I was not rebellious. I have not turned back. Isaiah 50:5 I gave my back to those who beat me, and my cheeks to those who plucked off the hair. I didn’t hide my face from shame and spitting. Isaiah 50:6 For the Lord GOD will help me. Therefore I have not been confounded. Therefore I have set my face like a flint, and I know that I won’t be disappointed. Isaiah 50:7 He who justifies me is near. Who will bring charges against me? Let us stand up together. Who is my adversary? Let him come near to me. Isaiah 50:8 Behold, the Lord GOD will help me! Who is he who will condemn me? Behold, they will all grow old like a garment. The moths will eat them up. Isaiah 50:9 Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? He who walks in darkness and has no light, let him trust in the LORD’s name, and rely on his God. Isaiah 50:10 Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who adorn yourselves with torches around yourselves, walk in the flame of your fire, and among the torches that you have kindled. You will have this from my hand: you will lie down in sorrow. Isaiah 50:11

title: Isaiah 51:1–8
context: Those who pursue righteousness are told to look to Abraham and Sarah—the rock and the quarry—because the LORD who called one man can still comfort Zion’s wastes like Eden. A law goes out as light to the peoples; his righteousness and salvation outlast heavens and earth, so the people in whose heart is his law need not fear the reproach of men.
text: Isaiah 51:1–8 Isaiah Those who pursue righteousness are told to look to Abraham and Sarah—the rock and the quarry—because the LORD who called one man can still comfort Zion’s wastes like Eden. A law goes out as light to the peoples; his righteousness and salvation outlast heavens and earth, so the people in whose heart is his law need not fear the reproach of men. “Listen to me, you who follow after righteousness, you who seek the LORD. Look to the rock you were cut from, and to the quarry you were dug from. Isaiah 51:1 Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, I blessed him, and made him many. Isaiah 51:2 For the LORD has comforted Zion. He has comforted all her waste places, and has made her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found in them, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody. Isaiah 51:3 “Listen to me, my people; and hear me, my nation, for a law will go out from me, and I will establish my justice for a light to the peoples. Isaiah 51:4 My righteousness is near. My salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The islands will wait for me, and they will trust my arm. Isaiah 51:5 Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth beneath; for the heavens will vanish away like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment. Its inhabitants will die in the same way, but my salvation will be forever, and my righteousness will not be abolished. Isaiah 51:6 “Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law. Don’t fear the reproach of men, and don’t be dismayed at their insults. Isaiah 51:7 For the moth will eat them up like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool; but my righteousness will be forever, and my salvation to all generations.” Isaiah 51:8

title: Isaiah 51:17–23
context: Jerusalem is told to wake herself and stand after drinking from the LORD's hand the cup of his wrath to the dregs—the historic staggering of Judah. Then the gospel turn: that cup is taken from her hand and put into the hand of her tormentors, who had made her back like the street.
text: Isaiah 51:17–23 Isaiah Jerusalem is told to wake herself and stand after drinking from the LORD's hand the cup of his wrath to the dregs—the historic staggering of Judah. Then the gospel turn: that cup is taken from her hand and put into the hand of her tormentors, who had made her back like the street. Awake, awake! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the LORD’s hand the cup of his wrath. You have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it. Isaiah 51:17 There is no one to guide her among all the sons to whom she has given birth; and there is no one who takes her by the hand among all the sons whom she has brought up. Isaiah 51:18 These two things have happened to you— who will grieve with you?— desolation and destruction, and famine and the sword. How can I comfort you? Isaiah 51:19 Your sons have fainted. They lie at the head of all the streets, like an antelope in a net. They are full of the LORD’s wrath, the rebuke of your God. Isaiah 51:20 Therefore now hear this, you afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine: Isaiah 51:21 Your Lord GOD, your God who pleads the cause of his people, says, “Behold, I have taken out of your hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my wrath. You will not drink it any more. Isaiah 51:22 I will put it into the hand of those who afflict you, who have said to your soul, ‘Bow down, that we may walk over you;’ and you have laid your back as the ground, like a street to those who walk over.” Isaiah 51:23

title: Isaiah 51:9–16
context: The godly cry Awake, awake to the arm that cut Rahab and pierced the dragon at the sea, and the LORD answers: I, even I, am he who comforts you; do not fear the dying oppressor.
