He who is bowed down shall be set free; the LORD who stirs the sea puts his words in the mouth and covers with his hand, and says to Zion, You are my people.
text: Isaiah 51:9–16 Isaiah The godly cry Awake, awake to the arm that cut Rahab and pierced the dragon at the sea, and the LORD answers: I, even I, am he who comforts you; do not fear the dying oppressor. He who is bowed down shall be set free; the LORD who stirs the sea puts his words in the mouth and covers with his hand, and says to Zion, You are my people. Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of the LORD! Awake, as in the days of old, the generations of ancient times. Isn’t it you who cut Rahab in pieces, who pierced the monster? Isaiah 51:9 Isn’t it you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep; who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over? Isaiah 51:10 Those ransomed by the LORD will return, and come with singing to Zion. Everlasting joy shall be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away. Isaiah 51:11 “I, even I, am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of man who shall die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass? Isaiah 51:12 Have you forgotten the LORD your Maker, who stretched out the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth? Do you live in fear continually all day because of the fury of the oppressor, when he prepares to destroy? Where is the fury of the oppressor? Isaiah 51:13 The captive exile will speedily be freed. He will not die and go down into the pit. His bread won’t fail. Isaiah 51:14 For I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar. the LORD of Armies is his name. Isaiah 51:15 I have put my words in your mouth and have covered you in the shadow of my hand, that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth, and tell Zion, ‘You are my people.’” Isaiah 51:16

title: Isaiah 52:1–12
context: Zion is told to awake and put on her strength and beautiful garments: historic Jerusalem, shake yourself from the dust, O captive daughter. Then the gospel turn: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news; the LORD has redeemed Jerusalem; depart, go out from there—not in haste, for the LORD will go before you.
text: Isaiah 52:1–12 Isaiah Zion is told to awake and put on her strength and beautiful garments: historic Jerusalem, shake yourself from the dust, O captive daughter. Then the gospel turn: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news; the LORD has redeemed Jerusalem; depart, go out from there—not in haste, for the LORD will go before you. Awake, awake! Put on your strength, Zion. Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city, for from now on the uncircumcised and the unclean will no more come into you. Isaiah 52:1 Shake yourself from the dust! Arise, sit up, Jerusalem! Release yourself from the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion! Isaiah 52:2 For the LORD says, “You were sold for nothing; and you will be redeemed without money.” Isaiah 52:3 For the Lord GOD says: “My people went down at the first into Egypt to live there; and the Assyrian has oppressed them without cause. Isaiah 52:4 “Now therefore, what do I do here,” says the LORD, “seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Those who rule over them mock,” says the LORD, “and my name is blasphemed continually all day long. Isaiah 52:5 Therefore my people shall know my name. Therefore they shall know in that day that I am he who speaks. Behold, it is I.” Isaiah 52:6 How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!” Isaiah 52:7 Your watchmen lift up their voice. Together they sing; for they shall see eye to eye when the LORD returns to Zion. Isaiah 52:8 Break out into joy! Sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem; for the LORD has comforted his people. He has redeemed Jerusalem. Isaiah 52:9 The LORD has made his holy arm bare in the eyes of all the nations. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God. Isaiah 52:10 Depart! Depart! Go out from there! Touch no unclean thing! Go out from among her! Cleanse yourselves, you who carry the LORD’s vessels. Isaiah 52:11 For you shall not go out in haste, neither shall you go by flight; for the LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard. Isaiah 52:12

title: Isaiah 52:13–15
context: After Zion awakes and goes out of Babylon not in haste, a new prophecy opens: Behold, my servant will deal wisely. He will be exalted and lifted up. Many were astonished at a visage marred beyond human semblance; so he will cleanse many nations, and kings shut their mouths at him.
text: Isaiah 52:13–15 Isaiah After Zion awakes and goes out of Babylon not in haste, a new prophecy opens: Behold, my servant will deal wisely. He will be exalted and lifted up. Many were astonished at a visage marred beyond human semblance; so he will cleanse many nations, and kings shut their mouths at him. Behold, my servant will deal wisely. He will be exalted and lifted up, and will be very high. Isaiah 52:13 Just as many were astonished at you— his appearance was marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men— Isaiah 52:14 so he will cleanse many nations. Kings will shut their mouths at him; for they will see that which had not been told them, and they will understand that which they had not heard. Isaiah 52:15

title: Isaiah 53:1–12
context: The fourth servant song continues from 52:13: who has believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed? The Servant grows up like a root from dry ground, despised, a man of sorrows; yet he bears our griefs, is pierced for our transgressions, and the LORD lays on him the iniquity of us all. Like a lamb led to the slaughter he opens not his mouth; cut off from the land of the living, he makes his soul an offering for guilt, justifies many and made intercession for the transgressors.
text: Isaiah 53:1–12 Isaiah The fourth servant song continues from 52:13: who has believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed? The Servant grows up like a root from dry ground, despised, a man of sorrows; yet he bears our griefs, is pierced for our transgressions, and the LORD lays on him the iniquity of us all. Like a lamb led to the slaughter he opens not his mouth; cut off from the land of the living, he makes his soul an offering for guilt, justifies many and made intercession for the transgressors. Who has believed our message? To whom has the LORD’s arm been revealed? Isaiah 53:1 For he grew up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of dry ground. He has no good looks or majesty. When we see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. Isaiah 53:2 He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom men hide their face; and we didn’t respect him. Isaiah 53:3 Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted. Isaiah 53:4 But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed. Isaiah 53:5 All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all. Isaiah 53:6 He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he didn’t open his mouth. Isaiah 53:7 He was taken away by oppression and judgment. As for his generation, who considered that he was cut off out of the land of the living and stricken for the disobedience of my people? Isaiah 53:8 They made his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death, although he had done no violence, nor was any deceit in his mouth. Isaiah 53:9 Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him. He has caused him to suffer. When you make his soul an offering for sin, he will see his offspring. He will prolong his days and the LORD’s pleasure will prosper in his hand. Isaiah 53:10 After the suffering of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. My righteous servant will justify many by the knowledge of himself; and he will bear their iniquities. Isaiah 53:11 Therefore I will give him a portion with the great. He will divide the plunder with the strong, because he poured out his soul to death and was counted with the transgressors; yet he bore the sins of many and made intercession for the transgressors. Isaiah 53:12

title: Isaiah 54:1–10
context: After the Servant's guilt offering, Zion is told to sing, O barren one: historic Jerusalem, desolate in exile, shall have more children than the married. Enlarge the tent; offspring will possess the nations and people desolate cities. Fear not: your Maker is your husband, the Holy One of Israel your Redeemer. For a brief moment he deserted her; with everlasting love he will have compassion. This is like the waters of Noah: mountains may depart, but his covenant of peace will not be removed.
text: Isaiah 54:1–10 Isaiah After the Servant's guilt offering, Zion is told to sing, O barren one: historic Jerusalem, desolate in exile, shall have more children than the married. Enlarge the tent; offspring will possess the nations and people desolate cities. Fear not: your Maker is your husband, the Holy One of Israel your Redeemer. For a brief moment he deserted her; with everlasting love he will have compassion. This is like the waters of Noah: mountains may depart, but his covenant of peace will not be removed. “Sing, barren, you who didn’t give birth! Break out into singing, and cry aloud, you who didn’t travail with child! For more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife,” says the LORD. Isaiah 54:1 “Enlarge the place of your tent, and let them stretch out the curtains of your habitations; don’t spare; lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes. Isaiah 54:2 For you will spread out on the right hand and on the left; and your offspring will possess the nations and settle in desolate cities. Isaiah 54:3 “Don’t be afraid, for you will not be ashamed. Don’t be confounded, for you will not be disappointed. For you will forget the shame of your youth. You will remember the reproach of your widowhood no more. Isaiah 54:4 For your Maker is your husband; the LORD of Armies is his name. The Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer. He will be called the God of the whole earth. Isaiah 54:5 For the LORD has called you as a wife forsaken and grieved in spirit, even a wife of youth, when she is cast off,” says your God. Isaiah 54:6 “For a small moment I have forsaken you, but I will gather you with great mercies. Isaiah 54:7 In overflowing wrath I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting loving kindness I will have mercy on you,” says the LORD your Redeemer. Isaiah 54:8 “For this is like the waters of Noah to me; for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah will no more go over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you, nor rebuke you. Isaiah 54:9 For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed, but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says the LORD who has mercy on you. Isaiah 54:10

title: Isaiah 54:11–17
context: The barren of 54:1–10 is now the storm-tossed city: O afflicted one, not comforted, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. Children taught by the LORD; established in righteousness, far from oppression. If anyone gathers against you, it is not from me; the smith and the ravager are his creatures. No weapon formed against you will prevail; This is the heritage of the LORD’s servants, and their righteousness is of me, says the LORD, their vindication from him.
text: Isaiah 54:11–17 Isaiah The barren of 54:1–10 is now the storm-tossed city: O afflicted one, not comforted, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. Children taught by the LORD; established in righteousness, far from oppression. If anyone gathers against you, it is not from me; the smith and the ravager are his creatures. No weapon formed against you will prevail; This is the heritage of the LORD’s servants, and their righteousness is of me, says the LORD, their vindication from him. “You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. Isaiah 54:11 I will make your pinnacles of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones. Isaiah 54:12 All your children will be taught by the LORD, and your children’s peace will be great. Isaiah 54:13 You will be established in righteousness. You will be far from oppression, for you will not be afraid, and far from terror, for it shall not come near you. Isaiah 54:14 Behold, they may gather together, but not by me. Whoever gathers together against you will fall because of you. Isaiah 54:15 “Behold, I have created the blacksmith who fans the coals into flame, and forges a weapon for his work; and I have created the destroyer to destroy. Isaiah 54:16 No weapon that is formed against you will prevail; and you will condemn every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of the LORD’s servants, and their righteousness is of me,” says the LORD. Isaiah 54:17

title: Isaiah 55:1–13
context: After Zion’s rebuilt walls, the cry is, Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters; buy wine and milk without money. Historic exiles going out in joy, then the gospel: an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, nations running to the Holy One of Israel. Seek the LORD while he may be found; let the wicked forsake his way; my thoughts are not your thoughts. As rain waters the earth, so shall my word accomplish what I purpose. Instead of the thorn, the cypress—an everlasting sign that will not be cut off. Do not split this invitation.
text: Isaiah 55:1–13 Isaiah After Zion’s rebuilt walls, the cry is, Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters; buy wine and milk without money. Historic exiles going out in joy, then the gospel: an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, nations running to the Holy One of Israel. Seek the LORD while he may be found; let the wicked forsake his way; my thoughts are not your thoughts. As rain waters the earth, so shall my word accomplish what I purpose. Instead of the thorn, the cypress—an everlasting sign that will not be cut off. Do not split this invitation. “Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. Isaiah 55:1 Why do you spend money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which doesn’t satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in richness. Isaiah 55:2 Turn your ear, and come to me. Hear, and your soul will live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David. Isaiah 55:3 Behold, I have given him for a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples. Isaiah 55:4 Behold, you shall call a nation that you don’t know; and a nation that didn’t know you shall run to you, because of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he has glorified you.” Isaiah 55:5 Seek the LORD while he may be found. Call on him while he is near. Isaiah 55:6 Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon. Isaiah 55:7 “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways,” says the LORD. Isaiah 55:8 “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts. Isaiah 55:9 For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater; Isaiah 55:10 so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do. Isaiah 55:11 For you shall go out with joy, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands. Isaiah 55:12 Instead of the thorn the cypress tree will come up; and instead of the brier the myrtle tree will come up. It will make a name for the LORD, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.” Isaiah 55:13

title: Isaiah 56:1–8
context: After the Servant’s work and the free invitation of chapter 55, the Lord commands justice and righteousness because his salvation is near. Foreigners and eunuchs who hold the covenant are promised a name in his house; the mountain becomes a house of prayer for all peoples, and the God who gathers Israel’s outcasts will gather still others.
text: Isaiah 56:1–8 Isaiah After the Servant’s work and the free invitation of chapter 55, the Lord commands justice and righteousness because his salvation is near. Foreigners and eunuchs who hold the covenant are promised a name in his house; the mountain becomes a house of prayer for all peoples, and the God who gathers Israel’s outcasts will gather still others. The LORD says: “Maintain justice and do what is right, for my salvation is near and my righteousness will soon be revealed. Isaiah 56:1 Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast; who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.” Isaiah 56:2 Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD speak, saying, “The LORD will surely separate me from his people.” Do not let the eunuch say, “Behold, I am a dry tree.” Isaiah 56:3 For the LORD says, “To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose the things that please me, and hold fast to my covenant, Isaiah 56:4 I will give them in my house and within my walls a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not be cut off. Isaiah 56:5 Also the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to serve him, and to love the LORD’s name, to be his servants, everyone who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it, and holds fast my covenant, Isaiah 56:6 I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.” Isaiah 56:7 The Lord GOD, who gathers the outcasts of Israel, says, “I will yet gather others to him, in addition to his own who are gathered.” Isaiah 56:8

title: Isaiah 56:9–12
context: The welcome of foreigners and eunuchs turns to a summons of wild beasts against a people whose watchmen are blind. Priests and shepherds sleep, crave, and toast tomorrow, while the flock is left to be devoured.
text: Isaiah 56:9–12 Isaiah The welcome of foreigners and eunuchs turns to a summons of wild beasts against a people whose watchmen are blind. Priests and shepherds sleep, crave, and toast tomorrow, while the flock is left to be devoured. All you animals of the field, come to devour, all you animals in the forest. Isaiah 56:9 His watchmen are blind. They are all without knowledge. They are all mute dogs. They can’t bark— dreaming, lying down, loving to slumber. Isaiah 56:10 Yes, the dogs are greedy. They can never have enough. They are shepherds who can’t understand. They have all turned to their own way, each one to his gain, from every quarter. Isaiah 56:11 “Come,” they say, “I will get wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and tomorrow will be as today, great beyond measure.” Isaiah 56:12

title: Isaiah 57:1–13
context: While drunk watchmen sleep, the righteous perish and enter peace. The Lord then summons a people of sorcery and spiritual adultery: child-sacrifice in the valleys, beds on high places, envoys to a foreign king even to Sheol. Idols will not profit; the one who takes refuge in the Lord will possess the land, and inherit the holy mountain.
text: Isaiah 57:1–13 Isaiah While drunk watchmen sleep, the righteous perish and enter peace. The Lord then summons a people of sorcery and spiritual adultery: child-sacrifice in the valleys, beds on high places, envoys to a foreign king even to Sheol. Idols will not profit; the one who takes refuge in the Lord will possess the land, and inherit the holy mountain. The righteous perish, and no one lays it to heart. Merciful men are taken away, and no one considers that the righteous is taken away from the evil. Isaiah 57:1 He enters into peace. They rest in their beds, each one who walks in his uprightness. Isaiah 57:2 “But draw near here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes. Isaiah 57:3 Whom do you mock? Against whom do you make a wide mouth and stick out your tongue? Aren’t you children of disobedience and offspring of falsehood, Isaiah 57:4 you who inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every green tree; who kill the children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks? Isaiah 57:5 Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion. They, they are your lot. You have even poured a drink offering to them. You have offered an offering. Shall I be appeased for these things? Isaiah 57:6 On a high and lofty mountain you have set your bed. You also went up there to offer sacrifice. Isaiah 57:7 You have set up your memorial behind the doors and the posts, for you have exposed yourself to someone besides me, and have gone up. You have enlarged your bed and made a covenant for yourself with them. You loved what you saw on their bed. Isaiah 57:8 You went to the king with oil, increased your perfumes, sent your ambassadors far off, and degraded yourself even to Sheol. Isaiah 57:9 You were wearied with the length of your ways; yet you didn’t say, ‘It is in vain.’ You found a reviving of your strength; therefore you weren’t faint. Isaiah 57:10 “Whom have you dreaded and feared, so that you lie, and have not remembered me, nor laid it to your heart? Haven’t I held my peace for a long time, and you don’t fear me? Isaiah 57:11 I will declare your righteousness; and as for your works, they will not benefit you. Isaiah 57:12 When you cry, let those whom you have gathered deliver you, but the wind will take them. A breath will carry them all away, but he who takes refuge in me will possess the land, and will inherit my holy mountain.” Isaiah 57:13

title: Isaiah 57:14–21
context: After the idolatry of 57:1–13, a voice commands the way to be built up. The High and Holy One dwells with the contrite, will not contend forever, heals the backslider, and creates “Peace, peace” for the far and the near. The wicked remain a tossing sea: no peace for them.
text: Isaiah 57:14–21 Isaiah After the idolatry of 57:1–13, a voice commands the way to be built up. The High and Holy One dwells with the contrite, will not contend forever, heals the backslider, and creates “Peace, peace” for the far and the near. The wicked remain a tossing sea: no peace for them. He will say, “Build up, build up, prepare the way! Remove the stumbling-block out of the way of my people.” Isaiah 57:14 For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite. Isaiah 57:15 For I will not contend forever, neither will I always be angry; for the spirit would faint before me, and the souls whom I have made. Isaiah 57:16 I was angry because of the iniquity of his covetousness and struck him. I hid myself and was angry; and he went on backsliding in the way of his heart. Isaiah 57:17 I have seen his ways, and will heal him. I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners. Isaiah 57:18 I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near,” says the LORD; “and I will heal them.” Isaiah 57:19 But the wicked are like the troubled sea; for it can’t rest and its waters cast up mire and mud. Isaiah 57:20 “There is no peace”, says my God, “for the wicked.” Isaiah 57:21

title: Isaiah 58:1–14
context: The Lord commands a trumpet cry against Jacob’s sin. Daily seeking and fasting are unmasked: pleasure, oppression, quarreling. The fast he chooses looses yokes, shares bread, houses the poor, and honors the Sabbath. Then light, healing, rebuilt ruins, and the heritage of Jacob follow, for the LORD’s mouth has spoken.
text: Isaiah 58:1–14 Isaiah The Lord commands a trumpet cry against Jacob’s sin. Daily seeking and fasting are unmasked: pleasure, oppression, quarreling. The fast he chooses looses yokes, shares bread, houses the poor, and honors the Sabbath. Then light, healing, rebuilt ruins, and the heritage of Jacob follow, for the LORD’s mouth has spoken. “Cry aloud! Don’t spare! Lift up your voice like a trumpet! Declare to my people their disobedience, and to the house of Jacob their sins. Isaiah 58:1 Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways. As a nation that did righteousness, and didn’t forsake the ordinance of their God, they ask of me righteous judgments. They delight to draw near to God. Isaiah 58:2 ‘Why have we fasted,’ they say, ‘and you don’t see? Why have we afflicted our soul, and you don’t notice?’ “Behold, in the day of your fast you find pleasure, and oppress all your laborers. Isaiah 58:3 Behold, you fast for strife and contention, and to strike with the fist of wickedness. You don’t fast today so as to make your voice to be heard on high. Isaiah 58:4 Is this the fast that I have chosen? A day for a man to humble his soul? Is it to bow down his head like a reed, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under himself? Will you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD? Isaiah 58:5 “Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of wickedness, to undo the straps of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke? Isaiah 58:6 Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh? Isaiah 58:7 Then your light will break out as the morning, and your healing will appear quickly; then your righteousness shall go before you, and the LORD’s glory will be your rear guard. Isaiah 58:8 Then you will call, and the LORD will answer. You will cry for help, and he will say, ‘Here I am.’ “If you take away from among you the yoke, finger pointing, and speaking wickedly; Isaiah 58:9 and if you pour out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will rise in darkness, and your obscurity will be as the noonday; Isaiah 58:10 and the LORD will guide you continually, satisfy your soul in dry places, and make your bones strong. You will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters don’t fail. Isaiah 58:11 Those who will be of you will build the old waste places. You will raise up the foundations of many generations. You will be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of Paths with Dwellings. Isaiah 58:12 “If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the LORD honorable, and honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words, Isaiah 58:13 then you will delight yourself in the LORD, and I will make you to ride on the high places of the earth, and I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father;” for the LORD’s mouth has spoken it. Isaiah 58:14

title: Isaiah 59:1–13
context: The Lord’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Iniquity has made the separation: bloodied hands, lying lips, adder eggs, crooked roads with no peace. The people then confess: we grope like the blind, hope for justice and find none, because our transgressions are multiplied and we know our iniquities.
text: Isaiah 59:1–13 Isaiah The Lord’s hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. Iniquity has made the separation: bloodied hands, lying lips, adder eggs, crooked roads with no peace. The people then confess: we grope like the blind, hope for justice and find none, because our transgressions are multiplied and we know our iniquities. Behold, the LORD’s hand is not shortened, that it can’t save; nor his ear dull, that it can’t hear. Isaiah 59:1 But your iniquities have separated you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he will not hear. Isaiah 59:2 For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity. Your lips have spoken lies. Your tongue mutters wickedness. Isaiah 59:3 No one sues in righteousness, and no one pleads in truth. They trust in vanity and speak lies. They conceive mischief and give birth to iniquity. Isaiah 59:4 They hatch adders’ eggs and weave the spider’s web. He who eats of their eggs dies; and that which is crushed breaks out into a viper. Isaiah 59:5 Their webs won’t become garments. They won’t cover themselves with their works. Their works are works of iniquity, and acts of violence are in their hands. Isaiah 59:6 Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity. Desolation and destruction are in their paths. Isaiah 59:7 They don’t know the way of peace; and there is no justice in their ways. They have made crooked paths for themselves; whoever goes in them doesn’t know peace. Isaiah 59:8 Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness doesn’t overtake us. We look for light, but see darkness; for brightness, but we walk in obscurity. Isaiah 59:9 We grope for the wall like the blind. Yes, we grope as those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were twilight. Among those who are strong, we are like dead men. Isaiah 59:10 We all roar like bears and moan sadly like doves. We look for justice, but there is none, for salvation, but it is far off from us. Isaiah 59:11 For our transgressions are multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us; for our transgressions are with us, and as for our iniquities, we know them: Isaiah 59:12 transgressing and denying the LORD, and turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood. Isaiah 59:13

title: Isaiah 59:14–21
context: After the confession of 59:1–13, justice is turned back in the square and the one who departs from evil becomes a prey. The Lord sees there is no intercessor; his own arm brings salvation. A Redeemer comes to Zion, to the people of Jacob who turn from disobedience, and the covenant of Spirit and word will not depart from their mouth forever.
text: Isaiah 59:14–21 Isaiah After the confession of 59:1–13, justice is turned back in the square and the one who departs from evil becomes a prey. The Lord sees there is no intercessor; his own arm brings salvation. A Redeemer comes to Zion, to the people of Jacob who turn from disobedience, and the covenant of Spirit and word will not depart from their mouth forever. Justice is turned away backward, and righteousness stands far away; for truth has fallen in the street, and uprightness can’t enter. Isaiah 59:14 Yes, truth is lacking; and he who departs from evil makes himself a prey. The LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice. Isaiah 59:15 He saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor. Therefore his own arm brought salvation to him; and his righteousness sustained him. Isaiah 59:16 He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head. He put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a mantle. Isaiah 59:17 According to their deeds, he will repay as appropriate: wrath to his adversaries, recompense to his enemies. He will repay the islands their due. Isaiah 59:18 So they will fear the LORD’s name from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun; for he will come as a rushing stream, which the LORD’s breath drives. Isaiah 59:19 “A Redeemer will come to Zion, and to those who turn from disobedience in Jacob,” says the LORD. Isaiah 59:20 “As for me, this is my covenant with them,” says the LORD. “My Spirit who is on you, and my words which I have put in your mouth shall not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your offspring, nor out of the mouth of your offspring’s offspring,” says the LORD, “from now on and forever.” Isaiah 59:21

title: Isaiah 6:1–13
context: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the Lord on a throne, high and lifted up; seraphim cry Holy, holy, holy. Thresholds shake; the house fills with smoke. Woe is me—unclean lips among an unclean people. A coal from the altar touches his mouth: guilt taken away, sin atoned. Whom shall I send, who will go for us? Here am I. Go: keep hearing, do not understand; make the heart dull, lest they turn and be healed. How long? Until cities lie waste. A tenth remains and is burned again; the holy seed is the stump.
text: Isaiah 6:1–13 Isaiah In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the Lord on a throne, high and lifted up; seraphim cry Holy, holy, holy. Thresholds shake; the house fills with smoke. Woe is me—unclean lips among an unclean people. A coal from the altar touches his mouth: guilt taken away, sin atoned. Whom shall I send, who will go for us? Here am I. Go: keep hearing, do not understand; make the heart dull, lest they turn and be healed. How long? Until cities lie waste. A tenth remains and is burned again; the holy seed is the stump. In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple. Isaiah 6:1 Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew. Isaiah 6:2 One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!” Isaiah 6:3 The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke. Isaiah 6:4 Then I said, “Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips and I live among a people of unclean lips, for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Armies!” Isaiah 6:5 Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar. Isaiah 6:6 He touched my mouth with it, and said, “Behold, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin forgiven.” Isaiah 6:7 I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!” Isaiah 6:8 He said, “Go, and tell this people, ‘You hear indeed, but don’t understand. You see indeed, but don’t perceive.’ Isaiah 6:9 Make the heart of this people fat. Make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.” Isaiah 6:10 Then I said, “Lord, how long?” He answered, “Until cities are waste without inhabitant, houses without man, the land becomes utterly waste, Isaiah 6:11 and the LORD has removed men far away, and the forsaken places are many within the land. Isaiah 6:12 If there is a tenth left in it, that also will in turn be consumed, as a terebinth, and as an oak whose stump remains when they are cut down, so the holy seed is its stump.” Isaiah 6:13

title: Isaiah 60:1–9
context: After the Redeemer of 59:20, Zion is told to arise: the Lord’s glory has risen, while darkness covers the peoples. Nations and kings come to her light; sons and daughters return; sea-wealth, Midian’s camels, Sheba’s gold and frankincense, Kedar’s flocks, and Tarshish ships bring children and praise to the Holy One who has made her beautiful.
text: Isaiah 60:1–9 Isaiah After the Redeemer of 59:20, Zion is told to arise: the Lord’s glory has risen, while darkness covers the peoples. Nations and kings come to her light; sons and daughters return; sea-wealth, Midian’s camels, Sheba’s gold and frankincense, Kedar’s flocks, and Tarshish ships bring children and praise to the Holy One who has made her beautiful. “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the LORD’s glory has risen on you! Isaiah 60:1 For behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but the LORD will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you. Isaiah 60:2 Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising. Isaiah 60:3 “Lift up your eyes all around, and see: they all gather themselves together. They come to you. Your sons will come from far away, and your daughters will be carried in arms. Isaiah 60:4 Then you shall see and be radiant, and your heart will thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea will be turned to you. The wealth of the nations will come to you. Isaiah 60:5 A multitude of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah. All from Sheba will come. They will bring gold and frankincense, and will proclaim the praises of the LORD. Isaiah 60:6 All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered together to you. The rams of Nebaioth will serve you. They will be accepted as offerings on my altar; and I will beautify my glorious house. Isaiah 60:7 “Who are these who fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows? Isaiah 60:8 Surely the islands will wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring your sons from far away, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you. Isaiah 60:9

title: Isaiah 60:10–22
context: Foreigners build Zion’s walls and kings minister, after wrath, in favor. Gates stay open for the nations’ wealth; Lebanon beautifies the sanctuary; afflicters bow and name her the City of the Lord. God himself is everlasting light. The people are his planting, and he will hasten it in its time.
text: Isaiah 60:10–22 Isaiah Foreigners build Zion’s walls and kings minister, after wrath, in favor. Gates stay open for the nations’ wealth; Lebanon beautifies the sanctuary; afflicters bow and name her the City of the Lord. God himself is everlasting light. The people are his planting, and he will hasten it in its time. “Foreigners will build up your walls, and their kings will serve you; for in my wrath I struck you, but in my favor I have had mercy on you. Isaiah 60:10 Your gates also shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night, that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations, and their kings led captive. Isaiah 60:11 For that nation and kingdom that will not serve you shall perish; yes, those nations shall be utterly wasted. Isaiah 60:12 “The glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the cypress tree, the pine, and the box tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious. Isaiah 60:13 The sons of those who afflicted you will come bowing to you; and all those who despised you will bow themselves down at the soles of your feet. They will call you the LORD’s City, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 60:14 “Whereas you have been forsaken and hated, so that no one passed through you, I will make you an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations. Isaiah 60:15 You will also drink the milk of the nations, and will nurse from royal breasts. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. Isaiah 60:16 For bronze I will bring gold; for iron I will bring silver; for wood, bronze, and for stones, iron. I will also make peace your governor, and righteousness your ruler. Isaiah 60:17 Violence shall no more be heard in your land, nor desolation or destruction within your borders; but you will call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise. Isaiah 60:18 The sun will be no more your light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon give light to you, but the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory. Isaiah 60:19 Your sun will not go down any more, nor will your moon withdraw itself; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end. Isaiah 60:20 Then your people will all be righteous. They will inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. Isaiah 60:21 The little one will become a thousand, and the small one a strong nation. I, the LORD, will do this quickly in its time.” Isaiah 60:22

title: Isaiah 61:1–11
context: The anointed Servant brings good news, liberty, and the year of the Lord’s favor with a day of vengeance, to comfort Zion’s mourners. Ruins rise; strangers tend flocks; the people are named priests under an everlasting covenant. Garments of salvation clothe the church. Jesus reads 61:1–2 at Nazareth (Luke 4:16–21).
text: Isaiah 61:1–11 Isaiah The anointed Servant brings good news, liberty, and the year of the Lord’s favor with a day of vengeance, to comfort Zion’s mourners. Ruins rise; strangers tend flocks; the people are named priests under an everlasting covenant. Garments of salvation clothe the church. Jesus reads 61:1–2 at Nazareth (Luke 4:16–21). The Lord GOD’s Spirit is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound, Isaiah 61:1 to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn, Isaiah 61:2 to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may be glorified. Isaiah 61:3 They will rebuild the old ruins. They will raise up the former devastated places. They will repair the ruined cities that have been devastated for many generations. Isaiah 61:4 Strangers will stand and feed your flocks. Foreigners will work your fields and your vineyards. Isaiah 61:5 But you will be called the LORD’s priests. Men will call you the servants of our God. You will eat the wealth of the nations. You will boast in their glory. Isaiah 61:6 Instead of your shame you will have double. Instead of dishonor, they will rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess double. Everlasting joy will be to them. Isaiah 61:7 “For I, the LORD, love justice. I hate robbery and iniquity. I will give them their reward in truth and I will make an everlasting covenant with them. Isaiah 61:8 Their offspring will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge them, that they are the offspring which the LORD has blessed.” Isaiah 61:9 I will greatly rejoice in the LORD! My soul will be joyful in my God, for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels. Isaiah 61:10 For as the earth produces its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring up, so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations. Isaiah 61:11

title: Isaiah 62:1–12
context: The prophet will not keep silent until Zion’s righteousness shines and her salvation burns like a torch. Forsaken names are changed: Hephzibah, Beulah; watchmen take no rest; a highway is cleared; the Holy People are Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken. Historic restoration after exile comes first; the church is the same people under the gospel. Bridegroom joy and a sworn harvest belong to that one story.
text: Isaiah 62:1–12 Isaiah The prophet will not keep silent until Zion’s righteousness shines and her salvation burns like a torch. Forsaken names are changed: Hephzibah, Beulah; watchmen take no rest; a highway is cleared; the Holy People are Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken. Historic restoration after exile comes first; the church is the same people under the gospel. Bridegroom joy and a sworn harvest belong to that one story. For Zion’s sake I will not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her righteousness shines out like the dawn, and her salvation like a burning lamp. Isaiah 62:1 The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory. You will be called by a new name, which the LORD’s mouth will name. Isaiah 62:2 You will also be a crown of beauty in the LORD’s hand, and a royal diadem in your God’s hand. Isaiah 62:3 You will not be called Forsaken any more, nor will your land be called Desolate any more; but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married. Isaiah 62:4 For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you. Isaiah 62:5 I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem. They will never be silent day nor night. You who call on the LORD, take no rest, Isaiah 62:6 and give him no rest until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise on the earth. Isaiah 62:7 The LORD has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, “Surely I will no more give your grain to be food for your enemies, and foreigners will not drink your new wine, for which you have labored, Isaiah 62:8 but those who have harvested it will eat it, and praise the LORD. Those who have gathered it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.” Isaiah 62:9 Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way of the people! Build up, build up the highway! Gather out the stones! Lift up a banner for the peoples. Isaiah 62:10 Behold, the LORD has proclaimed to the end of the earth: “Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your salvation comes! Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him!’” Isaiah 62:11 They will call them “The Holy People, The LORD’s Redeemed”. You will be called “Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken”. Isaiah 62:12

title: Isaiah 63:1–6
context: A watchman asks who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah, marching in the greatness of his strength. The Speaker answers: It is I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save; he has trodden the winepress alone, and no one was with him. Historic Edom is Esau’s land, the church’s old enemy; the winepress is the Lord’s own judgment. Canonical reading often hears the same Lord in Christ who treads (Rev 19 borrows the image)—one warrior.
text: Isaiah 63:1–6 Isaiah A watchman asks who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah, marching in the greatness of his strength. The Speaker answers: It is I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save; he has trodden the winepress alone, and no one was with him. Historic Edom is Esau’s land, the church’s old enemy; the winepress is the Lord’s own judgment. Canonical reading often hears the same Lord in Christ who treads (Rev 19 borrows the image)—one warrior. Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? Who is this who is glorious in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his strength? “It is I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save.” Isaiah 63:1 Why is your clothing red, and your garments like him who treads in the wine vat? Isaiah 63:2 “I have trodden the wine press alone. Of the peoples, no one was with me. Yes, I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my wrath. Their lifeblood is sprinkled on my garments, and I have stained all my clothing. Isaiah 63:3 For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redeemed has come. Isaiah 63:4 I looked, and there was no one to help; and I wondered that there was no one to uphold. Therefore my own arm brought salvation to me. My own wrath upheld me. Isaiah 63:5 I trod down the peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my wrath. I poured their lifeblood out on the earth.” Isaiah 63:6

title: Isaiah 63:15–19
context: The prophet now pleads for historic Israel: look down from heaven; where is your zeal and your mighty acts? The yearning of your heart and your compassion are held back. You are our Father, though Abraham doesn’t know us. Why do you make us wander from your ways and harden our heart? Return for the sake of your servants; we have become like those you never ruled. This is a covenant plea after the Exodus recital. The same Father still hears the church that is called by his name.
text: Isaiah 63:15–19 Isaiah The prophet now pleads for historic Israel: look down from heaven; where is your zeal and your mighty acts? The yearning of your heart and your compassion are held back. You are our Father, though Abraham doesn’t know us. Why do you make us wander from your ways and harden our heart? Return for the sake of your servants; we have become like those you never ruled. This is a covenant plea after the Exodus recital. The same Father still hears the church that is called by his name. Look down from heaven, and see from the habitation of your holiness and of your glory. Where are your zeal and your mighty acts? The yearning of your heart and your compassion is restrained toward me. Isaiah 63:15 For you are our Father, though Abraham doesn’t know us, and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, LORD, are our Father. Our Redeemer from everlasting is your name. Isaiah 63:16 O LORD, why do you make us wander from your ways, and harden our heart from your fear? Return for your servants’ sake, the tribes of your inheritance. Isaiah 63:17 Your holy people possessed it but a little while. Our adversaries have trodden down your sanctuary. Isaiah 63:18 We have become like those over whom you never ruled, like those who were not called by your name. Isaiah 63:19

title: Isaiah 63:7–14
context: The prophet will recount the Lord’s steadfast love toward the house of Israel: he said they were his people, became their Savior, and the angel of his presence saved them. This is a recital of Exodus mercy—Moses, the divided waters, the Holy Spirit, rest in the valley. They rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit; then he remembered the days of old. Historic then gospel: the Lord who carried them all the days of old still leads his people to make for himself a glorious name.
text: Isaiah 63:7–14 Isaiah The prophet will recount the Lord’s steadfast love toward the house of Israel: he said they were his people, became their Savior, and the angel of his presence saved them. This is a recital of Exodus mercy—Moses, the divided waters, the Holy Spirit, rest in the valley. They rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit; then he remembered the days of old. Historic then gospel: the Lord who carried them all the days of old still leads his people to make for himself a glorious name. I will tell of the loving kindnesses of the LORD and the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD has given to us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he has given to them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses. Isaiah 63:7 For he said, “Surely, they are my people, children who will not deal falsely;” so he became their Savior. Isaiah 63:8 In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them. He bore them, and carried them all the days of old. Isaiah 63:9 But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. Therefore he turned and became their enemy, and he himself fought against them. Isaiah 63:10 Then he remembered the days of old, Moses and his people, saying, “Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who put his Holy Spirit among them?” Isaiah 63:11 Who caused his glorious arm to be at Moses’ right hand? Who divided the waters before them, to make himself an everlasting name? Isaiah 63:12 Who led them through the depths, like a horse in the wilderness, so that they didn’t stumble? Isaiah 63:13 As the livestock that go down into the valley, the LORD’s Spirit caused them to rest. So you led your people to make yourself a glorious name. Isaiah 63:14

title: Isaiah 64:1–12
context: The plea of 63:15–19 continues: Oh that you would tear the heavens, that you would come down; Sinai’s mountains still set the pattern. Historic Judah confesses uncleanness, a burned temple, and cities gone wilderness, and names the Lord Father and potter. This is covenant prayer after exile. The same Father still hears the church that is the work of his hand.
text: Isaiah 64:1–12 Isaiah The plea of 63:15–19 continues: Oh that you would tear the heavens, that you would come down; Sinai’s mountains still set the pattern. Historic Judah confesses uncleanness, a burned temple, and cities gone wilderness, and names the Lord Father and potter. This is covenant prayer after exile. The same Father still hears the church that is the work of his hand. Oh that you would tear the heavens, that you would come down, that the mountains might quake at your presence— Isaiah 64:1 as when fire kindles the brushwood, and the fire causes the water to boil. Make your name known to your adversaries, that the nations may tremble at your presence! Isaiah 64:2 When you did awesome things which we didn’t look for, you came down, and the mountains quaked at your presence. Isaiah 64:3 For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, nor has the eye seen a God besides you, who works for him who waits for him. Isaiah 64:4 You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, those who remember you in your ways. Behold, you were angry, and we sinned. We have been in sin for a long time. Shall we be saved? Isaiah 64:5 For we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment. We all fade like a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away. Isaiah 64:6 There is no one who calls on your name, who stirs himself up to take hold of you; for you have hidden your face from us, and have consumed us by means of our iniquities. Isaiah 64:7 But now, LORD, you are our Father. We are the clay and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand. Isaiah 64:8 Don’t be furious, LORD. Don’t remember iniquity forever. Look and see, we beg you, we are all your people. Isaiah 64:9 Your holy cities have become a wilderness. Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation. Isaiah 64:10 Our holy and our beautiful house where our fathers praised you is burned with fire. All our pleasant places are laid waste. Isaiah 64:11 Will you hold yourself back for these things, LORD? Will you keep silent and punish us very severely? Isaiah 64:12

title: Isaiah 65:1–16
context: The Lord answers the plea of chapters 63–64. He was ready to be found by a nation not called by his name; he spread out his hands all day to a rebellious people who sacrificed in gardens, sat in tombs, and said, Keep to yourself. Yet as new wine in the cluster, he will not destroy them all: offspring from Jacob, chosen servants on the mountains, Sharon and Achor for those who sought him. Fortune and Destiny get a sword; servants eat and drink. Historic Judah and the nations first, then the gospel Paul reads here (Rom 10:20–21).
text: Isaiah 65:1–16 Isaiah The Lord answers the plea of chapters 63–64. He was ready to be found by a nation not called by his name; he spread out his hands all day to a rebellious people who sacrificed in gardens, sat in tombs, and said, Keep to yourself. Yet as new wine in the cluster, he will not destroy them all: offspring from Jacob, chosen servants on the mountains, Sharon and Achor for those who sought him. Fortune and Destiny get a sword; servants eat and drink. Historic Judah and the nations first, then the gospel Paul reads here (Rom 10:20–21). “I am inquired of by those who didn’t ask. I am found by those who didn’t seek me. I said, ‘See me, see me,’ to a nation that was not called by my name. Isaiah 65:1 I have spread out my hands all day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts; Isaiah 65:2 a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks; Isaiah 65:3 who sit among the graves, and spend nights in secret places; who eat pig’s meat, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels; Isaiah 65:4 who say, ‘Stay by yourself, don’t come near to me, for I am holier than you.’ These are smoke in my nose, a fire that burns all day. Isaiah 65:5 “Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will repay, yes, I will repay into their bosom Isaiah 65:6 your own iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together”, says the LORD, “who have burned incense on the mountains, and blasphemed me on the hills. Therefore I will first measure their work into their bosom.” Isaiah 65:7 The LORD says, “As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one says, ‘Don’t destroy it, for a blessing is in it:’ so I will do for my servants’ sake, that I may not destroy them all. Isaiah 65:8 I will bring offspring out of Jacob, and out of Judah an inheritor of my mountains. My chosen will inherit it, and my servants will dwell there. Isaiah 65:9 Sharon will be a fold of flocks, and the valley of Achor a place for herds to lie down in, for my people who have sought me. Isaiah 65:10 “But you who forsake the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who prepare a table for Fortune, and who fill up mixed wine to Destiny; Isaiah 65:11 I will destine you to the sword, and you will all bow down to the slaughter; because when I called, you didn’t answer. When I spoke, you didn’t listen; but you did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.” Isaiah 65:12 Therefore the Lord GOD says, “Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed. Isaiah 65:13 Behold, my servants will sing for joy of heart, but you will cry for sorrow of heart, and will wail for anguish of spirit. Isaiah 65:14 You will leave your name for a curse to my chosen, and the Lord GOD will kill you. He will call his servants by another name, Isaiah 65:15 so that he who blesses himself on the earth will bless himself in the God of truth; and he who swears on the earth will swear by the God of truth; because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes. Isaiah 65:16

title: Isaiah 65:17–25
context: After the servants’ new name, the Lord creates new heavens and a new earth; former troubles are not remembered. Jerusalem is created a joy; no more weeping; long life; houses built and inhabited; they call and he answers; wolf and lamb graze together; they shall not hurt in all my holy mountain. Historic Zion after exile comes first; then the gospel church and the last renewal in Christ. Wesley and Calvin both read a new face on the world in the Messiah’s kingdom; they do not chart a thousand years against each other.

Isaiah 65:17 But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create; for, behold, I create Jerusalem to be a delight, and her people a joy. Isaiah 65:18 I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and delight in my people; and the voice of weeping and the voice of crying will be heard in her no more. Isaiah 65:19 “No more will there be an infant who only lives a few days, nor an old man who has not filled his days; for the child will die one hundred years old, and the sinner being one hundred years old will be accursed. Isaiah 65:20 They will build houses and inhabit them. They will plant vineyards and eat their fruit. Isaiah 65:21 They will not build and another inhabit. They will not plant and another eat; for the days of my people will be like the days of a tree, and my chosen will long enjoy the work of their hands. Isaiah 65:22 They will not labor in vain nor give birth for calamity; for they are the offspring of the LORD’s blessed and their descendants with them. Isaiah 65:23 It will happen that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear. Isaiah 65:24 The wolf and the lamb will feed together. The lion will eat straw like the ox. Dust will be the serpent’s food. They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain,” says the LORD. Isaiah 65:25

title: Isaiah 66:1–6
context: Heaven is his throne and earth his footstool; the house they would build cannot contain him. He looks to the humble, contrite, and those who tremble at his word. Formal sacrifice without that heart is like killing a man or blessing an idol. He called and no one answered. Those who tremble are hated and cast out by brothers who say, Let the Lord be glorified; a voice from the temple renders recompense. Historic Judah’s temple first, then the gospel church Stephen reads here (Acts 7:49).
text: Isaiah 66:1–6 Isaiah Heaven is his throne and earth his footstool; the house they would build cannot contain him. He looks to the humble, contrite, and those who tremble at his word. Formal sacrifice without that heart is like killing a man or blessing an idol. He called and no one answered. Those who tremble are hated and cast out by brothers who say, Let the Lord be glorified; a voice from the temple renders recompense. Historic Judah’s temple first, then the gospel church Stephen reads here (Acts 7:49). The LORD says: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build to me? Where will I rest? Isaiah 66:1 For my hand has made all these things, and so all these things came to be,” says the LORD: “but I will look to this man, even to he who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at my word. Isaiah 66:2 He who kills an ox is as he who kills a man; he who sacrifices a lamb, as he who breaks a dog’s neck; he who offers an offering, as he who offers pig’s blood; he who burns frankincense, as he who blesses an idol. Yes, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations. Isaiah 66:3 I also will choose their delusions, and will bring their fears on them, because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they didn’t listen, but they did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.” Isaiah 66:4 Hear the LORD’s word, you who tremble at his word: “Your brothers who hate you, who cast you out for my name’s sake, have said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified, that we may see your joy;’ but it is those who shall be disappointed. Isaiah 66:5 A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the LORD that repays his enemies what they deserve. Isaiah 66:6

title: Isaiah 66:15–24
context: The Lord comes in fire; by fire and sword he judges all flesh. Garden-purifiers who eat the abomination end together. He gathers nations and tongues to see his glory; survivors go to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan, and the coastlands; brothers come for an offering to the holy mountain; some he takes for priests. As the new heavens remain, so shall offspring and name; all flesh worships from sabbath to sabbath; they look on the rebel dead, worm and fire unquenched.
text: Isaiah 66:15–24 Isaiah The Lord comes in fire; by fire and sword he judges all flesh. Garden-purifiers who eat the abomination end together. He gathers nations and tongues to see his glory; survivors go to Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan, and the coastlands; brothers come for an offering to the holy mountain; some he takes for priests. As the new heavens remain, so shall offspring and name; all flesh worships from sabbath to sabbath; they look on the rebel dead, worm and fire unquenched. For, behold, the LORD will come with fire, and his chariots will be like the whirlwind; to give his anger with fierceness, and his rebuke with flames of fire. Isaiah 66:15 For the LORD will execute judgment by fire and by his sword on all flesh; and those slain by the LORD will be many. Isaiah 66:16 “Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves to go to the gardens, following one in the middle, eating pig’s meat, abominable things, and the mouse, they shall come to an end together,” says the LORD. Isaiah 66:17 “For I know their works and their thoughts. The time comes that I will gather all nations and languages, and they will come, and will see my glory. Isaiah 66:18 “I will set a sign among them, and I will send those who escape of them to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, to far-away islands, who have not heard my fame, nor have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the nations. Isaiah 66:19 They shall bring all your brothers out of all the nations for an offering to the LORD, on horses, in chariots, in litters, on mules, and on camels, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, as the children of Israel bring their offering in a clean vessel into the LORD’s house. Isaiah 66:20 Of them I will also select priests and Levites,” says the LORD. Isaiah 66:21 “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says the LORD, “so your offspring and your name shall remain. Isaiah 66:22 It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” says the LORD. Isaiah 66:23 “They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched, and they will be loathsome to all mankind.” Isaiah 66:24

title: Isaiah 66:7–14
context: Before Zion is in labor she gives birth; a land is born in a day; the Lord who brings to birth will not shut the womb. Rejoice with Jerusalem, all who love her and mourn over her; nurse from her consoling breast. Peace flows like a river, the glory of the nations like a stream; he comforts as a mother comforts. Bones flourish; the hand of the Lord is known to his servants. Historic Zion after exile comes first; then the sudden gospel church.
text: Isaiah 66:7–14 Isaiah Before Zion is in labor she gives birth; a land is born in a day; the Lord who brings to birth will not shut the womb. Rejoice with Jerusalem, all who love her and mourn over her; nurse from her consoling breast. Peace flows like a river, the glory of the nations like a stream; he comforts as a mother comforts. Bones flourish; the hand of the Lord is known to his servants. Historic Zion after exile comes first; then the sudden gospel church. “Before she travailed, she gave birth. Before her pain came, she delivered a son. Isaiah 66:7 Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Shall a land be born in one day? Shall a nation be born at once? For as soon as Zion travailed, she gave birth to her children. Isaiah 66:8 Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to be delivered?” says the LORD. “Shall I who cause to give birth shut the womb?” says your God. Isaiah 66:9 “Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all you who love her. Rejoice for joy with her, all you who mourn over her; Isaiah 66:10 that you may nurse and be satisfied at the comforting breasts; that you may drink deeply, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory.” Isaiah 66:11 For the LORD says, “Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream, and you will nurse. You will be carried on her side, and will be dandled on her knees. Isaiah 66:12 As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.” Isaiah 66:13 You will see it, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones will flourish like the tender grass. The LORD’s hand will be known among his servants; and he will have indignation against his enemies. Isaiah 66:14

title: Isaiah 7:1–9
context: In the days of Ahaz, Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel come up against Jerusalem and cannot yet attack. The house of David shakes like trees in the wind. The Lord sends Isaiah with Shear-jashub to the upper pool: be quiet; do not fear two smoldering stumps. Their counsel—to set the son of Tabeel in Judah—shall not stand. Damascus remains Rezin’s head; within sixty-five years Ephraim is shattered. If you will not believe, surely you shall not be firm at all.
text: Isaiah 7:1–9 Isaiah In the days of Ahaz, Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel come up against Jerusalem and cannot yet attack. The house of David shakes like trees in the wind. The Lord sends Isaiah with Shear-jashub to the upper pool: be quiet; do not fear two smoldering stumps. Their counsel—to set the son of Tabeel in Judah—shall not stand. Damascus remains Rezin’s head; within sixty-five years Ephraim is shattered. If you will not believe, surely you shall not be firm at all. In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it. Isaiah 7:1 David’s house was told, “Syria is allied with Ephraim.” His heart trembled, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the forest tremble with the wind. Isaiah 7:2 Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out now to meet Ahaz, you, and Shearjashub your son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the fuller’s field. Isaiah 7:3 Tell him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. Don’t be afraid, neither let your heart be faint because of these two tails of smoking torches, for the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah. Isaiah 7:4 Because Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah, have plotted evil against you, saying, Isaiah 7:5 “Let’s go up against Judah, and tear it apart, and let’s divide it among ourselves, and set up a king within it, even the son of Tabeel.” Isaiah 7:6 This is what the Lord GOD says: “It shall not stand, neither shall it happen.” Isaiah 7:7 For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim shall be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a people. Isaiah 7:8 The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If you will not believe, surely you shall not be established.’” Isaiah 7:9

title: Isaiah 7:10–25
context: The Lord speaks again to Ahaz, saying, Ask a sign, deep as Sheol or high as heaven. Ahaz will not ask; he says he will not tempt the LORD. The house of David wearies God. Therefore the Lord himself gives a sign: the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, Immanuel. Curds and honey until he knows to refuse evil. Before the boy knows, the land of the two kings is deserted. Then days worse than Ephraim’s split—the king of Assyria. The Lord whistles for fly and bee; a hired razor shaves head to beard. Survivors keep a cow and two sheep among briers.
text: Isaiah 7:10–25 Isaiah The Lord speaks again to Ahaz, saying, Ask a sign, deep as Sheol or high as heaven. Ahaz will not ask; he says he will not tempt the LORD. The house of David wearies God. Therefore the Lord himself gives a sign: the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, Immanuel. Curds and honey until he knows to refuse evil. Before the boy knows, the land of the two kings is deserted. Then days worse than Ephraim’s split—the king of Assyria. The Lord whistles for fly and bee; a hired razor shaves head to beard. Survivors keep a cow and two sheep among briers. The LORD spoke again to Ahaz, saying, Isaiah 7:10 “Ask a sign of the LORD your God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above.” Isaiah 7:11 But Ahaz said, “I won’t ask. I won’t tempt the LORD.” Isaiah 7:12 He said, “Listen now, house of David. Is it not enough for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my God also? Isaiah 7:13 Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. Isaiah 7:14 He shall eat butter and honey when he knows to refuse the evil and choose the good. Isaiah 7:15 For before the child knows to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land whose two kings you abhor shall be forsaken. Isaiah 7:16 The LORD will bring on you, on your people, and on your father’s house days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria. Isaiah 7:17 It will happen in that day that the LORD will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria. Isaiah 7:18 They shall come, and shall all rest in the desolate valleys, in the clefts of the rocks, on all thorn hedges, and on all pastures. Isaiah 7:19 In that day the Lord will shave with a razor that is hired in the parts beyond the River, even with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet; and it shall also consume the beard. Isaiah 7:20 It shall happen in that day that a man shall keep alive a young cow, and two sheep. Isaiah 7:21 It shall happen, that because of the abundance of milk which they shall give he shall eat butter, for everyone will eat butter and honey that is left within the land. Isaiah 7:22 It will happen in that day that every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand silver shekels, will be for briers and thorns. Isaiah 7:23 People will go there with arrows and with bow, because all the land will be briers and thorns. Isaiah 7:24 All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending out of oxen, and for sheep to tread on.” Isaiah 7:25

title: Isaiah 8:1–10
context: The Lord tells Isaiah to write Maher-shalal-hash-baz on a large tablet in common characters, with Uriah and Zechariah as witnesses. The prophetess bears a son by that name: before the boy can cry father or mother, Damascus’s wealth and Samaria’s spoil go by the king of Assyria. This people refuses Shiloah’s gentle waters and rejoices in Rezin; so the Lord brings the River—Assyria—over its banks, through Judah, to the neck, filling Immanuel’s land. Peoples, be shattered. Counsel will not stand: God is with us.
text: Isaiah 8:1–10 Isaiah The Lord tells Isaiah to write Maher-shalal-hash-baz on a large tablet in common characters, with Uriah and Zechariah as witnesses. The prophetess bears a son by that name: before the boy can cry father or mother, Damascus’s wealth and Samaria’s spoil go by the king of Assyria. This people refuses Shiloah’s gentle waters and rejoices in Rezin; so the Lord brings the River—Assyria—over its banks, through Judah, to the neck, filling Immanuel’s land. Peoples, be shattered. Counsel will not stand: God is with us. The LORD said to me, “Take a large tablet, and write on it with a man’s pen, ‘For Maher Shalal Hash Baz’; Isaiah 8:1 and I will take for myself faithful witnesses to testify: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.” Isaiah 8:2 I went to the prophetess, and she conceived, and bore a son. Then the LORD said to me, “Call his name ‘Maher Shalal Hash Baz.’ Isaiah 8:3 For before the child knows how to say, ‘My father’ and ‘My mother,’ the riches of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried away by the king of Assyria.” Isaiah 8:4 The LORD spoke to me yet again, saying, Isaiah 8:5 “Because this people has refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah’s son; Isaiah 8:6 now therefore, behold, the Lord brings upon them the mighty flood waters of the River: the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will come up over all its channels, and go over all its banks. Isaiah 8:7 It will sweep onward into Judah. It will overflow and pass through. It will reach even to the neck. The stretching out of its wings will fill the width of your land, O Immanuel. Isaiah 8:8 Make an uproar, you peoples, and be broken in pieces! Listen, all you from far countries: dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered! Isaiah 8:9 Take counsel together, and it will be brought to nothing; speak the word, and it will not stand, for God is with us.” Isaiah 8:10

title: Isaiah 8:11–22
context: The Lord, with a strong hand, warns Isaiah not to walk in this people’s way. Do not call conspiracy what they call conspiracy, or fear their fear. Honor the Lord of hosts as holy: He is sanctuary and a stone of offense to both houses, a snare to Jerusalem; many stumble. Bind the testimony among disciples. Isaiah waits while the Lord hides His face. He and the children given him are signs. Do not inquire of mediums; to the teaching and the testimony. The rest pass hungry through the land into thick darkness.
text: Isaiah 8:11–22 Isaiah The Lord, with a strong hand, warns Isaiah not to walk in this people’s way. Do not call conspiracy what they call conspiracy, or fear their fear. Honor the Lord of hosts as holy: He is sanctuary and a stone of offense to both houses, a snare to Jerusalem; many stumble. Bind the testimony among disciples. Isaiah waits while the Lord hides His face. He and the children given him are signs. Do not inquire of mediums; to the teaching and the testimony. The rest pass hungry through the land into thick darkness. For the LORD spoke this to me with a strong hand, and instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying, Isaiah 8:11 “Don’t call a conspiracy all that this people call a conspiracy. Don’t fear their threats or be terrorized. Isaiah 8:12 The LORD of Armies is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must fear. He is the one you must dread. Isaiah 8:13 He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a stumbling stone and a rock that makes them fall. For the people of Jerusalem, he will be a trap and a snare. Isaiah 8:14 Many will stumble over it, fall, be broken, be snared, and be captured.” Isaiah 8:15 Wrap up the covenant. Seal the law among my disciples. Isaiah 8:16 I will wait for the LORD, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. Isaiah 8:17 Behold, I and the children whom the LORD has given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the LORD of Armies, who dwells in Mount Zion. Isaiah 8:18 When they tell you, “Consult with those who have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter,” shouldn’t a people consult with their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living? Isaiah 8:19 Turn to the law and to the covenant! If they don’t speak according to this word, surely there is no morning for them. Isaiah 8:20 They will pass through it, very distressed and hungry. It will happen that when they are hungry, they will worry, and curse their king and their God. They will turn their faces upward, Isaiah 8:21 then look to the earth and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They will be driven into thick darkness. Isaiah 8:22

title: Isaiah 9:1–7
context: No more gloom for her who was in anguish. Former time: Zebulun and Naphtali brought into contempt; latter time: the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations, made glorious. A people who walked in darkness see a great light. The nation is multiplied, joy increased like harvest and spoil. The yoke, staff, and rod are broken as in the day of Midian; war-boots and bloody garments burn. For a child is born, a son given: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of his government and peace no end, on David’s throne, forever.
