The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this.
text: Isaiah 9:1–7 Isaiah No more gloom for her who was in anguish. Former time: Zebulun and Naphtali brought into contempt; latter time: the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations, made glorious. A people who walked in darkness see a great light. The nation is multiplied, joy increased like harvest and spoil. The yoke, staff, and rod are broken as in the day of Midian; war-boots and bloody garments burn. For a child is born, a son given: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Of his government and peace no end, on David’s throne, forever. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this. But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations. Isaiah 9:1 The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. The light has shined on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death. Isaiah 9:2 You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the plunder. Isaiah 9:3 For the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken as in the day of Midian. Isaiah 9:4 For all the armor of the armed man in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in blood, will be for burning, fuel for the fire. Isaiah 9:5 For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. Isaiah 9:6 Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, on David’s throne, and on his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with justice and with righteousness from that time on, even forever. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will perform this. Isaiah 9:7

title: Isaiah 9:8–21
context: The Lord sent a word into Jacob; it falls on Israel. Ephraim and Samaria, proud, say: bricks have fallen, we will build with cut stone; sycamores down, we will put cedars. The Lord raises Rezin’s adversaries. Syrians east, Philistines west, devour with open mouth. His anger is not turned away; his hand is stretched out still. They have not turned to him who struck them. Head and tail cut off in one day: honored man and lying prophet. Guides lead astray; the guided are swallowed. No compassion on fatherless and widows; everyone godless. Wickedness burns. The land is scorched; brother will not spare brother. Manasseh, Ephraim, and both against Judah. His hand is stretched out still.
text: Isaiah 9:8–21 Isaiah The Lord sent a word into Jacob; it falls on Israel. Ephraim and Samaria, proud, say: bricks have fallen, we will build with cut stone; sycamores down, we will put cedars. The Lord raises Rezin’s adversaries. Syrians east, Philistines west, devour with open mouth. His anger is not turned away; his hand is stretched out still. They have not turned to him who struck them. Head and tail cut off in one day: honored man and lying prophet. Guides lead astray; the guided are swallowed. No compassion on fatherless and widows; everyone godless. Wickedness burns. The land is scorched; brother will not spare brother. Manasseh, Ephraim, and both against Judah. His hand is stretched out still. The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel. Isaiah 9:8 All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart, Isaiah 9:9 “The bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.” Isaiah 9:10 Therefore the LORD will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies, Isaiah 9:11 The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and they will devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. Isaiah 9:12 Yet the people have not turned to him who struck them, neither have they sought the LORD of Armies. Isaiah 9:13 Therefore the LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day. Isaiah 9:14 The elder and the honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail. Isaiah 9:15 For those who lead this people lead them astray; and those who are led by them are destroyed. Isaiah 9:16 Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. Isaiah 9:17 For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke. Isaiah 9:18 Through the LORD of Armies’ wrath, the land is burned up; and the people are the fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother. Isaiah 9:19 One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm: Isaiah 9:20 Manasseh eating Ephraim and Ephraim eating Manasseh, and they together will be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. Isaiah 9:21

title: John 1:1–18
context: John’s prologue announces that the Word was with God and was God, the agent of creation and the source of life and light. John the Baptist came to bear witness to the light. The true light, which gives light to everyone, came into the world, but the world did not know him and his own people did not receive him. Yet to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God, born not of human will but of God. The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth. Both traditions affirm the deity and incarnation of Christ wholeheartedly. They differ on verses 9 and 12–13.
text: John 1:1–18 John John’s prologue announces that the Word was with God and was God, the agent of creation and the source of life and light. John the Baptist came to bear witness to the light. The true light, which gives light to everyone, came into the world, but the world did not know him and his own people did not receive him. Yet to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God, born not of human will but of God. The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth. Both traditions affirm the deity and incarnation of Christ wholeheartedly. They differ on verses 9 and 12–13. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. John 1:1 The same was in the beginning with God. John 1:2 All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made. John 1:3 In him was life, and the life was the light of men. John 1:4 The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it. John 1:5 There came a man sent from God, whose name was John. John 1:6 The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him. John 1:7 He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light. John 1:8 The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world. John 1:9 He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognize him. John 1:10 He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him. John 1:11 But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name: John 1:12 who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. John 1:13 The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth. John 1:14 John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’” John 1:15 From his fullness we all received grace upon grace. John 1:16 For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ. John 1:17 No one has seen God at any time. The only born Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him. John 1:18

title: John 1:19–28
context: Priests and Levites from Jerusalem interrogate the Baptist; he denies being the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet, and identifies himself as Isaiah’s wilderness voice, pointing to One already standing among them.
text: John 1:19–28 John Priests and Levites from Jerusalem interrogate the Baptist; he denies being the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet, and identifies himself as Isaiah’s wilderness voice, pointing to One already standing among them. This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?” John 1:19 He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.” John 1:20 They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the prophet?” He answered, “No.” John 1:21 They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?” John 1:22 He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.” John 1:23 The ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees. John 1:24 They asked him, “Why then do you baptize if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?” John 1:25 John answered them, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know. John 1:26 He is the one who comes after me, who is preferred before me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.” John 1:27 These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing. John 1:28

title: John 1:29–34
context: The next day John sees Jesus and announces the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world, testifies to the Spirit remaining on him, and declares that this is the Son of God.
text: John 1:29–34 John The next day John sees Jesus and announces the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world, testifies to the Spirit remaining on him, and declares that this is the Son of God. The next day, he saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world! John 1:29 This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’ John 1:30 I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptizing in water, that he would be revealed to Israel.” John 1:31 John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him. John 1:32 I didn’t recognize him, but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘On whomever you will see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ John 1:33 I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.” John 1:34

title: John 1:35–42
context: Two of John’s disciples follow Jesus after “Behold the Lamb”; they come and see; Andrew finds Simon and brings him; Jesus names him Cephas.
text: John 1:35–42 John Two of John’s disciples follow Jesus after “Behold the Lamb”; they come and see; Andrew finds Simon and brings him; Jesus names him Cephas. Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples, John 1:35 and he looked at Jesus as he walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!” John 1:36 The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus. John 1:37 Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), “where are you staying?” John 1:38 He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour. John 1:39 One of the two who heard John and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother. John 1:40 He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ). John 1:41 He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter). John 1:42

title: John 1:43–51
context: Jesus finds Philip (“Follow me”); Philip finds Nathanael; prejudice about Nazareth yields to “Come and see”; Jesus names him an Israelite without deceit, having seen him under the fig tree; Nathanael confesses Son of God and King of Israel; Jesus promises heaven opened on the Son of Man.
text: John 1:43–51 John Jesus finds Philip (“Follow me”); Philip finds Nathanael; prejudice about Nazareth yields to “Come and see”; Jesus names him an Israelite without deceit, having seen him under the fig tree; Nathanael confesses Son of God and King of Israel; Jesus promises heaven opened on the Son of Man. On the next day, he was determined to go out into Galilee, and he found Philip. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.” John 1:43 Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. John 1:44 Philip found Nathanael, and said to him, “We have found him of whom Moses in the law and also the prophets, wrote: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.” John 1:45 Nathanael said to him, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.” John 1:46 Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and said about him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!” John 1:47 Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.” John 1:48 Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are King of Israel!” John 1:49 Jesus answered him, “Because I told you, ‘I saw you underneath the fig tree,’ do you believe? You will see greater things than these!” John 1:50 He said to him, “Most certainly, I tell you all, hereafter you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.” John 1:51

title: John 10:1–21
context: Jesus describes himself as the door of the sheep and the good shepherd. Thieves climb in another way, but the shepherd enters by the door, calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out, and they follow because they know his voice. Jesus is the door: whoever enters through him will be saved. He came so that the sheep may have abundant life. As the good shepherd, he lays down his life for the sheep, knows his own and is known by them, and has other sheep not of this fold whom he must bring. He lays down his life of his own accord and has authority to take it up again. The passage is central to the debate over the extent of the atonement.
text: John 10:1–21 John Jesus describes himself as the door of the sheep and the good shepherd. Thieves climb in another way, but the shepherd enters by the door, calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out, and they follow because they know his voice. Jesus is the door: whoever enters through him will be saved. He came so that the sheep may have abundant life. As the good shepherd, he lays down his life for the sheep, knows his own and is known by them, and has other sheep not of this fold whom he must bring. He lays down his life of his own accord and has authority to take it up again. The passage is central to the debate over the extent of the atonement. “Most certainly, I tell you, one who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheep fold, but climbs up some other way, is a thief and a robber. John 10:1 But one who enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. John 10:2 The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out. John 10:3 Whenever he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice. John 10:4 They will by no means follow a stranger, but will flee from him; for they don’t know the voice of strangers.” John 10:5 Jesus spoke this parable to them, but they didn’t understand what he was telling them. John 10:6 Jesus therefore said to them again, “Most certainly, I tell you, I am the sheep’s door. John 10:7 All who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep didn’t listen to them. John 10:8 I am the door. If anyone enters in by me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and will find pasture. John 10:9 The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly. John 10:10 “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. John 10:11 He who is a hired hand, and not a shepherd, who doesn’t own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and flees. The wolf snatches the sheep and scatters them. John 10:12 The hired hand flees because he is a hired hand and doesn’t care for the sheep. John 10:13 I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I’m known by my own; John 10:14 even as the Father knows me, and I know the Father. I lay down my life for the sheep. John 10:15 I have other sheep which are not of this fold. I must bring them also, and they will hear my voice. They will become one flock with one shepherd. John 10:16 Therefore the Father loves me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again. John 10:17 No one takes it away from me, but I lay it down by myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. I received this commandment from my Father.” John 10:18 Therefore a division arose again among the Jews because of these words. John 10:19 Many of them said, “He has a demon and is insane! Why do you listen to him?” John 10:20 Others said, “These are not the sayings of one possessed by a demon. It isn’t possible for a demon to open the eyes of the blind, is it?” John 10:21

title: John 10:22–42
context: At the Feast of Dedication, the Jews press Jesus to say plainly whether he is the Christ. He replies that he has told them and that his works bear witness, but they do not believe because they are not among his sheep. His sheep hear his voice and follow him. He gives them eternal life, they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of his hand or the Father’s. He and the Father are one. When they try to stone him for blasphemy, he appeals to Scripture and his works, then withdraws beyond the Jordan, where many believe. Verses 26–29 are a key text in the debate over election and eternal security.
text: John 10:22–42 John At the Feast of Dedication, the Jews press Jesus to say plainly whether he is the Christ. He replies that he has told them and that his works bear witness, but they do not believe because they are not among his sheep. His sheep hear his voice and follow him. He gives them eternal life, they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of his hand or the Father’s. He and the Father are one. When they try to stone him for blasphemy, he appeals to Scripture and his works, then withdraws beyond the Jordan, where many believe. Verses 26–29 are a key text in the debate over election and eternal security. It was the Feast of the Dedication at Jerusalem. John 10:22 It was winter, and Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s porch. John 10:23 The Jews therefore came around him and said to him, “How long will you hold us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.” John 10:24 Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you don’t believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name, these testify about me. John 10:25 But you don’t believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I told you. John 10:26 My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. John 10:27 I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. John 10:28 My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand. John 10:29 I and the Father are one.” John 10:30 Therefore the Jews took up stones again to stone him. John 10:31 Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of those works do you stone me?” John 10:32 The Jews answered him, “We don’t stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God.” John 10:33 Jesus answered them, “Isn’t it written in your law, ‘I said, you are gods’? John 10:34 If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came (and the Scripture can’t be broken), John 10:35 do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You blaspheme,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’? John 10:36 If I don’t do the works of my Father, don’t believe me. John 10:37 But if I do them, though you don’t believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.” John 10:38 They sought again to seize him, and he went out of their hand. John 10:39 He went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was baptizing at first, and he stayed there. John 10:40 Many came to him. They said, “John indeed did no sign, but everything that John said about this man is true.” John 10:41 Many believed in him there. John 10:42

title: John 11:1–16
context: Lazarus of Bethany is ill. The sisters send word to the Lord who loves him. Jesus says the illness is for the glory of God, then stays two days where he is. He walks toward Judea despite the recent attempt to stone him, calls Lazarus’s death sleep, and is glad for the disciples’ sake that he was not there, so that they may believe. Thomas says, Let’s go too, so that we may die with him.
text: John 11:1–16 John Lazarus of Bethany is ill. The sisters send word to the Lord who loves him. Jesus says the illness is for the glory of God, then stays two days where he is. He walks toward Judea despite the recent attempt to stone him, calls Lazarus’s death sleep, and is glad for the disciples’ sake that he was not there, so that they may believe. Thomas says, Let’s go too, so that we may die with him. Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister, Martha. John 11:1 It was that Mary who had anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick. John 11:2 The sisters therefore sent to him, saying, “Lord, behold, he for whom you have great affection is sick.” John 11:3 But when Jesus heard it, he said, “This sickness is not to death, but for the glory of God, that God’s Son may be glorified by it.” John 11:4 Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus. John 11:5 When therefore he heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was. John 11:6 Then after this he said to the disciples, “Let’s go into Judea again.” John 11:7 The disciples asked him, “Rabbi, the Jews were just trying to stone you. Are you going there again?” John 11:8 Jesus answered, “Aren’t there twelve hours of daylight? If a man walks in the day, he doesn’t stumble, because he sees the light of this world. John 11:9 But if a man walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light isn’t in him.” John 11:10 He said these things, and after that, he said to them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going so that I may awake him out of sleep.” John 11:11 The disciples therefore said, “Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover.” John 11:12 Now Jesus had spoken of his death, but they thought that he spoke of taking rest in sleep. John 11:13 So Jesus said to them plainly then, “Lazarus is dead. John 11:14 I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, so that you may believe. Nevertheless, let’s go to him.” John 11:15 Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, “Let’s also go, that we may die with him.” John 11:16

title: John 11:17–27
context: Jesus arrives in Bethany four days after Lazarus has been buried. Martha meets him with grief and faith mixed together, and Jesus declares, ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’ Her confession that he is the Christ, the Son of God, comes before the miracle, not after it.
text: John 11:17–27 John Jesus arrives in Bethany four days after Lazarus has been buried. Martha meets him with grief and faith mixed together, and Jesus declares, ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’ Her confession that he is the Christ, the Son of God, comes before the miracle, not after it. So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already. John 11:17 Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away. John 11:18 Many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother. John 11:19 Then when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house. John 11:20 Therefore Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died. John 11:21 Even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.” John 11:22 Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.” John 11:23 Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” John 11:24 Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies. John 11:25 Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” John 11:26 She said to him, “Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, he who comes into the world.” John 11:27

title: John 11:28–44
context: Martha calls Mary aside and tells her privately that the Teacher has come and is asking for her. Mary rises quickly; mourners follow, thinking she goes to the tomb. She falls at Jesus’ feet with the same if you would have been here. He is deeply moved, asks where they laid him, and weeps. At the cave he says, Take away the stone. Martha names the four-day odor. If you believed, you would see God’s glory. He thanks the Father aloud so that the crowd may believe the Father sent him, then cries, Lazarus, come out. The dead man comes bound; Jesus says, Free him, and let him go.
text: John 11:28–44 John Martha calls Mary aside and tells her privately that the Teacher has come and is asking for her. Mary rises quickly; mourners follow, thinking she goes to the tomb. She falls at Jesus’ feet with the same if you would have been here. He is deeply moved, asks where they laid him, and weeps. At the cave he says, Take away the stone. Martha names the four-day odor. If you believed, you would see God’s glory. He thanks the Father aloud so that the crowd may believe the Father sent him, then cries, Lazarus, come out. The dead man comes bound; Jesus says, Free him, and let him go. When she had said this, she went away and called Mary, her sister, secretly, saying, “The Teacher is here and is calling you.” John 11:28 When she heard this, she arose quickly and went to him. John 11:29 Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was in the place where Martha met him. John 11:30 Then the Jews who were with her in the house and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, saying, “She is going to the tomb to weep there.” John 11:31 Therefore when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.” John 11:32 When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit and was troubled, John 11:33 and said, “Where have you laid him?” They told him, “Lord, come and see.” John 11:34 Jesus wept. John 11:35 The Jews therefore said, “See how much affection he had for him!” John 11:36 Some of them said, “Couldn’t this man, who opened the eyes of him who was blind, have also kept this man from dying?” John 11:37 Jesus therefore, again groaning in himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it. John 11:38 Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.” John 11:39 Jesus said to her, “Didn’t I tell you that if you believed, you would see God’s glory?” John 11:40 So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, “Father, I thank you that you listened to me. John 11:41 I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.” John 11:42 When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!” John 11:43 He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Free him, and let him go.” John 11:44

title: John 11:45–57
context: Many of the Jews who came to Mary and seen what Jesus did believed in him; some went to the Pharisees. The council panics over signs and Rome. Caiaphas, high priest that year, says it is better that one man die for the people than that the nation perish. Now he didn’t say this of his own accord: he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but to gather into one the scattered children of God. From that day they plot to kill him. Jesus no longer walks openly, but stays at Ephraim. Passover is near; they look for him in the temple; orders are out for his arrest.
text: John 11:45–57 John Many of the Jews who came to Mary and seen what Jesus did believed in him; some went to the Pharisees. The council panics over signs and Rome. Caiaphas, high priest that year, says it is better that one man die for the people than that the nation perish. Now he didn’t say this of his own accord: he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but to gather into one the scattered children of God. From that day they plot to kill him. Jesus no longer walks openly, but stays at Ephraim. Passover is near; they look for him in the temple; orders are out for his arrest. Therefore many of the Jews who came to Mary and saw what Jesus did believed in him. John 11:45 But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them the things which Jesus had done. John 11:46 The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, “What are we doing? For this man does many signs. John 11:47 If we leave him alone like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.” John 11:48 But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all, John 11:49 nor do you consider that it is advantageous for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation not perish.” John 11:50 Now he didn’t say this of himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, John 11:51 and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God who are scattered abroad. John 11:52 So from that day forward they took counsel that they might put him to death. John 11:53 Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed from there into the country near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim. He stayed there with his disciples. John 11:54 Now the Passover of the Jews was at hand. Many went up from the country to Jerusalem before the Passover, to purify themselves. John 11:55 Then they sought for Jesus and spoke with one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think—that he isn’t coming to the feast at all?” John 11:56 Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had commanded that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, that they might seize him. John 11:57

title: John 12:1–8
context: Six days before Passover, Jesus returns to Bethany, where Lazarus—raised—reclines at table. Mary pours costly nard on His feet and wipes them with her hair; the house fills with fragrance. Judas objects in the name of the poor. Jesus defends her: the act is for His burial, and they will not always have Him.
text: John 12:1–8 John Six days before Passover, Jesus returns to Bethany, where Lazarus—raised—reclines at table. Mary pours costly nard on His feet and wipes them with her hair; the house fills with fragrance. Judas objects in the name of the poor. Jesus defends her: the act is for His burial, and they will not always have Him. Then, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, who had been dead, whom he raised from the dead. John 12:1 So they made him a supper there. Martha served, but Lazarus was one of those who sat at the table with him. John 12:2 Therefore Mary took a pound of ointment of pure nard, very precious, and anointed Jesus’ feet and wiped his feet with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment. John 12:3 Then Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, one of his disciples, who would betray him, said, John 12:4 “Why wasn’t this ointment sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?” John 12:5 Now he said this, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief, and having the money box, used to steal what was put into it. John 12:6 But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. She has kept this for the day of my burial. John 12:7 For you always have the poor with you, but you don’t always have me.” John 12:8

title: John 12:20–36
context: Some Greeks ask to see Jesus, and he announces that the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. A grain of wheat must die to bear much fruit, and whoever loves his life loses it. Jesus’ soul is troubled, but he will not ask to be saved from this hour; he came for it. A voice from heaven answers his prayer to glorify the Father’s name. Now is the judgment of this world and the casting out of its ruler, and when he is lifted up, Jesus will draw all people to himself. He urges the crowd to believe in the light while they have it. Verse 32 is a key text in the debate over the Father’s drawing in 6:44.
text: John 12:20–36 John Some Greeks ask to see Jesus, and he announces that the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. A grain of wheat must die to bear much fruit, and whoever loves his life loses it. Jesus’ soul is troubled, but he will not ask to be saved from this hour; he came for it. A voice from heaven answers his prayer to glorify the Father’s name. Now is the judgment of this world and the casting out of its ruler, and when he is lifted up, Jesus will draw all people to himself. He urges the crowd to believe in the light while they have it. Verse 32 is a key text in the debate over the Father’s drawing in 6:44. Now there were certain Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast. John 12:20 Therefore, these came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.” John 12:21 Philip came and told Andrew, and in turn, Andrew came with Philip, and they told Jesus. John 12:22 Jesus answered them, “The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. John 12:23 Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit. John 12:24 He who loves his life will lose it. He who hates his life in this world will keep it to eternal life. John 12:25 If anyone serves me, let him follow me. Where I am, there my servant will also be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him. John 12:26 “Now my soul is troubled. What shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this time’? But I came to this time for this cause. John 12:27 Father, glorify your name!” Then a voice came out of the sky, saying, “I have both glorified it and will glorify it again.” John 12:28 Therefore the multitude who stood by and heard it said that it had thundered. Others said, “An angel has spoken to him.” John 12:29 Jesus answered, “This voice hasn’t come for my sake, but for your sakes. John 12:30 Now is the judgment of this world. Now the prince of this world will be cast out. John 12:31 And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.” John 12:32 But he said this, signifying by what kind of death he should die. John 12:33 The multitude answered him, “We have heard out of the law that the Christ remains forever. How do you say, ‘The Son of Man must be lifted up’? Who is this Son of Man?” John 12:34 Jesus therefore said to them, “Yet a little while the light is with you. Walk while you have the light, that darkness doesn’t overtake you. He who walks in the darkness doesn’t know where he is going. John 12:35 While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become children of light.” Jesus said these things, and he departed and hid himself from them. John 12:36

title: John 12:37–50
context: Despite all his signs, the people did not believe in Jesus. John explains this by quoting Isaiah: “Lord, who has believed our report?” and “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart.” They could not believe. Yet many rulers believed secretly, loving human praise more than God’s. Jesus then cries out that whoever believes in him believes in the one who sent him. He came as light so that whoever believes may not remain in darkness. He came not to judge the world but to save it, though his word will judge those who reject it. Verses 39–40 are among the strongest statements of divine hardening in the Gospels, and the two traditions read them differently.
text: John 12:37–50 John Despite all his signs, the people did not believe in Jesus. John explains this by quoting Isaiah: “Lord, who has believed our report?” and “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart.” They could not believe. Yet many rulers believed secretly, loving human praise more than God’s. Jesus then cries out that whoever believes in him believes in the one who sent him. He came as light so that whoever believes may not remain in darkness. He came not to judge the world but to save it, though his word will judge those who reject it. Verses 39–40 are among the strongest statements of divine hardening in the Gospels, and the two traditions read them differently. But though he had done so many signs before them, yet they didn’t believe in him, John 12:37 that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: “Lord, who has believed our report? To whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?” John 12:38 For this cause they couldn’t believe, for Isaiah said again: John 12:39 “He has blinded their eyes and he hardened their heart, lest they should see with their eyes, and perceive with their heart, and would turn, and I would heal them.” John 12:40 Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory, and spoke of him. John 12:41 Nevertheless, even many of the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they didn’t confess it, so that they wouldn’t be put out of the synagogue, John 12:42 for they loved men’s praise more than God’s praise. John 12:43 Jesus cried out and said, “Whoever believes in me, believes not in me, but in him who sent me. John 12:44 He who sees me sees him who sent me. John 12:45 I have come as a light into the world, that whoever believes in me may not remain in the darkness. John 12:46 If anyone listens to my sayings and doesn’t believe, I don’t judge him. For I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. John 12:47 He who rejects me, and doesn’t receive my sayings, has one who judges him. The word that I spoke will judge him in the last day. John 12:48 For I spoke not from myself, but the Father who sent me gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak. John 12:49 I know that his commandment is eternal life. The things therefore which I speak, even as the Father has said to me, so I speak.” John 12:50

title: John 12:9–19
context: A large crowd comes not only for Jesus but to see Lazarus; the chief priests plot to kill the raised man because many are believing. The next day pilgrims take palms and cry Hosanna to the King of Israel. Jesus sits on a young donkey, as Zechariah wrote. The disciples do not understand until He is glorified; Pharisees lament that the world has gone after Him.
text: John 12:9–19 John A large crowd comes not only for Jesus but to see Lazarus; the chief priests plot to kill the raised man because many are believing. The next day pilgrims take palms and cry Hosanna to the King of Israel. Jesus sits on a young donkey, as Zechariah wrote. The disciples do not understand until He is glorified; Pharisees lament that the world has gone after Him. A large crowd therefore of the Jews learned that he was there; and they came, not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead. John 12:9 But the chief priests conspired to put Lazarus to death also, John 12:10 because on account of him many of the Jews went away and believed in Jesus. John 12:11 On the next day a great multitude had come to the feast. When they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, John 12:12 they took the branches of the palm trees and went out to meet him, and cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!” John 12:13 Jesus, having found a young donkey, sat on it. As it is written, John 12:14 “Don’t be afraid, daughter of Zion. Behold, your King comes, sitting on a donkey’s colt.” John 12:15 His disciples didn’t understand these things at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written about him, and that they had done these things to him. John 12:16 The multitude therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead was testifying about it. John 12:17 For this cause also the multitude went and met him, because they heard that he had done this sign. John 12:18 The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, “See how you accomplish nothing. Behold, the world has gone after him.” John 12:19

title: John 13:1–17
context: Before the feast, Jesus knows His hour has come to depart to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the end. During supper, knowing the Father had given all things into His hands, He washes the disciples’ feet, including the coming betrayer. Peter resists, then overcorrects. Unless He washes them, they have no share with Him. He interprets the act: a servant is not greater than his lord; they will be blessed if they do these things.
text: John 13:1–17 John Before the feast, Jesus knows His hour has come to depart to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the end. During supper, knowing the Father had given all things into His hands, He washes the disciples’ feet, including the coming betrayer. Peter resists, then overcorrects. Unless He washes them, they have no share with Him. He interprets the act: a servant is not greater than his lord; they will be blessed if they do these things. Now before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that his time had come that he would depart from this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end. John 13:1 During supper, the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him, John 13:2 Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came from God and was going to God, John 13:3 arose from supper, and laid aside his outer garments. He took a towel and wrapped a towel around his waist. John 13:4 Then he poured water into the basin, and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to wipe them with the towel that was wrapped around him. John 13:5 Then he came to Simon Peter. He said to him, “Lord, do you wash my feet?” John 13:6 Jesus answered him, “You don’t know what I am doing now, but you will understand later.” John 13:7 Peter said to him, “You will never wash my feet!” Jesus answered him, “If I don’t wash you, you have no part with me.” John 13:8 Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!” John 13:9 Jesus said to him, “Someone who has bathed only needs to have his feet washed, but is completely clean. You are clean, but not all of you.” John 13:10 For he knew him who would betray him; therefore he said, “You are not all clean.” John 13:11 So when he had washed their feet, put his outer garment back on, and sat down again, he said to them, “Do you know what I have done to you? John 13:12 You call me, ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord.’ You say so correctly, for so I am. John 13:13 If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet. John 13:14 For I have given you an example, that you should also do as I have done to you. John 13:15 Most certainly I tell you, a servant is not greater than his lord, neither is one who is sent greater than he who sent him. John 13:16 If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them. John 13:17

title: John 13:18–30
context: He is not speaking of all of them. Scripture must be fulfilled: he who ate bread lifted his heel. He tells them before it happens so they will believe. The one who receives whom He sends receives Him and the Sender. Troubled in spirit, He discloses that one will betray Him. The beloved disciple, at Peter’s nod, asks who. Jesus dips the morsel, gives it to Judas; Satan enters him. “What you do, do quickly.” Judas goes out. It was night.
text: John 13:18–30 John He is not speaking of all of them. Scripture must be fulfilled: he who ate bread lifted his heel. He tells them before it happens so they will believe. The one who receives whom He sends receives Him and the Sender. Troubled in spirit, He discloses that one will betray Him. The beloved disciple, at Peter’s nod, asks who. Jesus dips the morsel, gives it to Judas; Satan enters him. “What you do, do quickly.” Judas goes out. It was night. I don’t speak concerning all of you. I know whom I have chosen; but that the Scripture may be fulfilled, ‘He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.’ John 13:18 From now on, I tell you before it happens, that when it happens, you may believe that I am he. John 13:19 Most certainly I tell you, he who receives whomever I send, receives me; and he who receives me, receives him who sent me.” John 13:20 When Jesus had said this, he was troubled in spirit, and testified, “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.” John 13:21 The disciples looked at one another, perplexed about whom he spoke. John 13:22 One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was at the table, leaning against Jesus’ chest. John 13:23 Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, and said to him, “Tell us who it is of whom he speaks.” John 13:24 He, leaning back, as he was, on Jesus’ chest, asked him, “Lord, who is it?” John 13:25 Jesus therefore answered, “It is he to whom I will give this piece of bread when I have dipped it.” So when he had dipped the piece of bread, he gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. John 13:26 After the piece of bread, then Satan entered into him. Then Jesus said to him, “What you do, do quickly.” John 13:27 Now nobody at the table knew why he said this to him. John 13:28 For some thought, because Judas had the money box, that Jesus said to him, “Buy what things we need for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor. John 13:29 Therefore having received that morsel, he went out immediately. It was night. John 13:30

title: John 13:31–38
context: When Judas has gone, Jesus says now the Son of Man is glorified, and God in Him. He will be with them only a little longer; they cannot follow now. A new commandment: love one another as He has loved them; by this all will know they are His disciples. Peter asks why he cannot follow now and vows his life. Jesus answers with the rooster: the denier before dawn.
text: John 13:31–38 John When Judas has gone, Jesus says now the Son of Man is glorified, and God in Him. He will be with them only a little longer; they cannot follow now. A new commandment: love one another as He has loved them; by this all will know they are His disciples. Peter asks why he cannot follow now and vows his life. Jesus answers with the rooster: the denier before dawn. When he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him. John 13:31 If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and he will glorify him immediately. John 13:32 Little children, I will be with you a little while longer. You will seek me, and as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you can’t come,’ so now I tell you. John 13:33 A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another. John 13:34 By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” John 13:35 Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered, “Where I am going, you can’t follow now, but you will follow afterwards.” John 13:36 Peter said to him, “Lord, why can’t I follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.” John 13:37 Jesus answered him, “Will you lay down your life for me? Most certainly I tell you, the rooster won’t crow until you have denied me three times. John 13:38

title: John 14:1–14
context: Let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. He goes to prepare a place, and will come again. Thomas asks the way; Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life—no one comes to the Father except through Him. Philip asks to see the Father; to see Jesus is to see the Father. Those who believe will do His works, and whatever they ask in His name He will do it, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
text: John 14:1–14 John Let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. He goes to prepare a place, and will come again. Thomas asks the way; Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life—no one comes to the Father except through Him. Philip asks to see the Father; to see Jesus is to see the Father. Those who believe will do His works, and whatever they ask in His name He will do it, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. John 14:1 In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you. John 14:2 If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also. John 14:3 You know where I go, and you know the way.” John 14:4 Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going. How can we know the way?” John 14:5 Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me. John 14:6 If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on, you know him and have seen him.” John 14:7 Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” John 14:8 Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you such a long time, and do you not know me, Philip? He who has seen me has seen the Father. How do you say, ‘Show us the Father’? John 14:9 Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? The words that I tell you, I speak not from myself; but the Father who lives in me does his works. John 14:10 Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me; or else believe me for the very works’ sake. John 14:11 Most certainly I tell you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will do also; and he will do greater works than these, because I am going to my Father. John 14:12 Whatever you will ask in my name, I will do it, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. John 14:13 If you will ask anything in my name, I will do it. John 14:14

title: John 14:15–31
context: If they love Him they will keep His commandments. He will ask the Father, who will give another Counselor, that he may be with them forever—the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive. He will not leave them as orphans; He and the Father will make their home with the one who loves and keeps. The Helper will teach and remind. Peace He leaves; the prince of the world comes, and has no claim on Him. He does as the Father commanded so that the world may know He loves the Father, and as the Father commanded me, even so I do. Arise, let’s go.
text: John 14:15–31 John If they love Him they will keep His commandments. He will ask the Father, who will give another Counselor, that he may be with them forever—the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive. He will not leave them as orphans; He and the Father will make their home with the one who loves and keeps. The Helper will teach and remind. Peace He leaves; the prince of the world comes, and has no claim on Him. He does as the Father commanded so that the world may know He loves the Father, and as the Father commanded me, even so I do. Arise, let’s go. If you love me, keep my commandments. John 14:15 I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever: John 14:16 the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive, for it doesn’t see him and doesn’t know him. You know him, for he lives with you and will be in you. John 14:17 I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you. John 14:18 Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Because I live, you will live also. John 14:19 In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you. John 14:20 One who has my commandments and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.” John 14:21 Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are about to reveal yourself to us, and not to the world?” John 14:22 Jesus answered him, “If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him. John 14:23 He who doesn’t love me doesn’t keep my words. The word which you hear isn’t mine, but the Father’s who sent me. John 14:24 “I have said these things to you while still living with you. John 14:25 But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you. John 14:26 Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful. John 14:27 You heard how I told you, ‘I am going away, and I will come back to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced because I said ‘I am going to my Father;’ for the Father is greater than I. John 14:28 Now I have told you before it happens so that when it happens, you may believe. John 14:29 I will no more speak much with you, for the prince of the world comes, and he has nothing in me. John 14:30 But that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father commanded me, even so I do. Arise, let’s go from here. John 14:31

title: John 15:1–17
context: On the night before his death, Jesus describes himself as the true vine and his Father as the vinedresser. Branches that bear no fruit are taken away; fruitful ones are pruned to bear more. The disciples must abide in him, because apart from him they can do nothing. Anyone who does not abide is thrown away like a withered branch and burned. Jesus calls them to abide in his love by keeping his commands, above all to love one another as he loved them. He calls them friends and reminds them that they did not choose him; he chose them and appointed them to bear lasting fruit. Verses 2 and 6 are central to the perseverance debate, and verse 16 to the election debate.
text: John 15:1–17 John On the night before his death, Jesus describes himself as the true vine and his Father as the vinedresser. Branches that bear no fruit are taken away; fruitful ones are pruned to bear more. The disciples must abide in him, because apart from him they can do nothing. Anyone who does not abide is thrown away like a withered branch and burned. Jesus calls them to abide in his love by keeping his commands, above all to love one another as he loved them. He calls them friends and reminds them that they did not choose him; he chose them and appointed them to bear lasting fruit. Verses 2 and 6 are central to the perseverance debate, and verse 16 to the election debate. “I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer. John 15:1 Every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit, he takes away. Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit. John 15:2 You are already pruned clean because of the word which I have spoken to you. John 15:3 Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me. John 15:4 I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing. John 15:5 If a man doesn’t remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch and is withered; and they gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burned. John 15:6 If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, you will ask whatever you desire, and it will be done for you. John 15:7 “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples. John 15:8 Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love. John 15:9 If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, even as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love. John 15:10 I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full. John 15:11 “This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you. John 15:12 Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends. John 15:13 You are my friends if you do whatever I command you. John 15:14 No longer do I call you servants, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you. John 15:15 You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you. John 15:16 “I command these things to you, that you may love one another. John 15:17

title: John 15:18–27
context: Jesus warns the disciples that the world will hate them because it hated him first. They are not of the world, since he chose them out of it, and a servant is not greater than his master. Those who reject Jesus have no excuse, because he spoke and did works no one else did, yet they hated him without cause, fulfilling Scripture. The Spirit of truth, whom Jesus will send from the Father, will bear witness about him, and the disciples will bear witness too. Both traditions draw comfort and responsibility from the passage. They differ on what “I chose you out of the world” implies and on the guilt of those who saw and heard.
text: John 15:18–27 John Jesus warns the disciples that the world will hate them because it hated him first. They are not of the world, since he chose them out of it, and a servant is not greater than his master. Those who reject Jesus have no excuse, because he spoke and did works no one else did, yet they hated him without cause, fulfilling Scripture. The Spirit of truth, whom Jesus will send from the Father, will bear witness about him, and the disciples will bear witness too. Both traditions draw comfort and responsibility from the passage. They differ on what “I chose you out of the world” implies and on the guilt of those who saw and heard. If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before it hated you. John 15:18 If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, since I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. John 15:19 Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours. John 15:20 But they will do all these things to you for my name’s sake, because they don’t know him who sent me. John 15:21 If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin. John 15:22 He who hates me, hates my Father also. John 15:23 If I hadn’t done among them the works which no one else did, they wouldn’t have had sin. But now they have seen and also hated both me and my Father. John 15:24 But this happened so that the word may be fulfilled which was written in their law, ‘They hated me without a cause.’ John 15:25 “When the Counselor has come, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me. John 15:26 You will also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning. John 15:27

title: John 16:1–15
context: Jesus warns the Eleven so they will not fall away: synagogue expulsion and killing done as service to God, because the persecutors know neither the Father nor Him. It is to their advantage that He goes, for then He will send the Helper, who convicts the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment, and who guides them into all the truth, glorifying the Son.
text: John 16:1–15 John Jesus warns the Eleven so they will not fall away: synagogue expulsion and killing done as service to God, because the persecutors know neither the Father nor Him. It is to their advantage that He goes, for then He will send the Helper, who convicts the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment, and who guides them into all the truth, glorifying the Son. “I have said these things to you so that you wouldn’t be caused to stumble. John 16:1 They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time is coming that whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God. John 16:2 They will do these things because they have not known the Father nor me. John 16:3 But I have told you these things so that when the time comes, you may remember that I told you about them. I didn’t tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you. John 16:4 But now I am going to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’ John 16:5 But because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your heart. John 16:6 Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is to your advantage that I go away; for if I don’t go away, the Counselor won’t come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you. John 16:7 When he has come, he will convict the world about sin, about righteousness, and about judgment; John 16:8 about sin, because they don’t believe in me; John 16:9 about righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you won’t see me any more; John 16:10 about judgment, because the prince of this world has been judged. John 16:11 “I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t bear them now. John 16:12 However, when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming. John 16:13 He will glorify me, for he will take from what is mine and will declare it to you. John 16:14 All things that the Father has are mine; therefore I said that he takes of mine and will declare it to you. John 16:15

title: John 16:16–33
context: A little while: they will not see Him, then see Him. Sorrow will turn to joy like birth pangs to a child. In that day they will ask the Father in His name; the Father Himself loves them. He came from the Father and returns. Their new confidence is met with a question and a prediction of scattering—yet He is not alone, and in Him they may have peace: in the world tribulation, but He has overcome the world.
text: John 16:16–33 John A little while: they will not see Him, then see Him. Sorrow will turn to joy like birth pangs to a child. In that day they will ask the Father in His name; the Father Himself loves them. He came from the Father and returns. Their new confidence is met with a question and a prediction of scattering—yet He is not alone, and in Him they may have peace: in the world tribulation, but He has overcome the world. “A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me.” John 16:16 Some of his disciples therefore said to one another, “What is this that he says to us, ‘A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me;’ and, ‘Because I go to the Father’?” John 16:17 They said therefore, “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We don’t know what he is saying.” John 16:18 Therefore Jesus perceived that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, “Do you inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said, ‘A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me’? John 16:19 Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy. John 16:20 A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world. John 16:21 Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you. John 16:22 “In that day you will ask me no questions. Most certainly I tell you, whatever you may ask of the Father in my name, he will give it to you. John 16:23 Until now, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be made full. John 16:24 “I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. But the time is coming when I will no more speak to you in figures of speech, but will tell you plainly about the Father. John 16:25 In that day you will ask in my name; and I don’t say to you that I will pray to the Father for you, John 16:26 for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me, and have believed that I came from God. John 16:27 I came from the Father and have come into the world. Again, I leave the world and go to the Father.” John 16:28 His disciples said to him, “Behold, now you are speaking plainly, and using no figures of speech. John 16:29 Now we know that you know all things, and don’t need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came from God.” John 16:30 Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe? John 16:31 Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. John 16:32 I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.” John 16:33

title: John 17:1–5
context: Jesus begins his high priestly prayer as his hour arrives. He asks the Father to glorify the Son so that the Son may glorify him. The Father has given the Son authority over all flesh to give eternal life to all whom the Father has given him. Eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent. Jesus has finished the work given him and asks to be glorified with the glory he had with the Father before the world existed. Verse 2 contributes to the debate over election.
text: John 17:1–5 John Jesus begins his high priestly prayer as his hour arrives. He asks the Father to glorify the Son so that the Son may glorify him. The Father has given the Son authority over all flesh to give eternal life to all whom the Father has given him. Eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent. Jesus has finished the work given him and asks to be glorified with the glory he had with the Father before the world existed. Verse 2 contributes to the debate over election. Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you; John 17:1 even as you gave him authority over all flesh, so he will give eternal life to all whom you have given him. John 17:2 This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ. John 17:3 I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do. John 17:4 Now, Father, glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed. John 17:5

title: John 17:20–26
context: Jesus extends his prayer to all who will believe through the apostles’ word. He prays that they may all be one, as the Father and Son are one, so that the world may believe the Father sent him. He has given them his glory, so that the world may know the Father loved them as he loved the Son. He asks that those the Father has given him may be with him to see his glory. The world has not known the Father, but Jesus has made his name known and will continue to do so, so that the Father’s love may be in them. Both traditions draw deeply from this prayer.
text: John 17:20–26 John Jesus extends his prayer to all who will believe through the apostles’ word. He prays that they may all be one, as the Father and Son are one, so that the world may believe the Father sent him. He has given them his glory, so that the world may know the Father loved them as he loved the Son. He asks that those the Father has given him may be with him to see his glory. The world has not known the Father, but Jesus has made his name known and will continue to do so, so that the Father’s love may be in them. Both traditions draw deeply from this prayer. “Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word, John 17:20 that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me. John 17:21 The glory which you have given me, I have given to them, that they may be one, even as we are one, John 17:22 I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, even as you loved me. John 17:23 Father, I desire that they also whom you have given me be with me where I am, that they may see my glory which you have given me, for you loved me before the foundation of the world. John 17:24 Righteous Father, the world hasn’t known you, but I knew you; and these knew that you sent me. John 17:25 I made known to them your name, and will make it known; that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.” John 17:26

title: John 17:6–19
context: Jesus prays for his disciples, the people the Father gave him out of the world. They have kept God’s word and believed that Jesus came from the Father. Jesus says he is praying for them, not for the world, and asks the Father to keep them in his name. He kept them while he was with them, and none was lost except the son of destruction, so that Scripture might be fulfilled. He does not ask that they be taken out of the world but kept from the evil one, and sanctified in the truth. Both traditions see Christ’s care for his own here. They differ on the scope of his prayer and on what Judas’s loss means.
text: John 17:6–19 John Jesus prays for his disciples, the people the Father gave him out of the world. They have kept God’s word and believed that Jesus came from the Father. Jesus says he is praying for them, not for the world, and asks the Father to keep them in his name. He kept them while he was with them, and none was lost except the son of destruction, so that Scripture might be fulfilled. He does not ask that they be taken out of the world but kept from the evil one, and sanctified in the truth. Both traditions see Christ’s care for his own here. They differ on the scope of his prayer and on what Judas’s loss means. “I revealed your name to the people whom you have given me out of the world. They were yours, and you have given them to me. They have kept your word. John 17:6 Now they have known that all things whatever you have given me are from you, John 17:7 for the words which you have given me I have given to them; and they received them, and knew for sure that I came from you. They have believed that you sent me. John 17:8 I pray for them. I don’t pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, for they are yours. John 17:9 All things that are mine are yours, and yours are mine, and I am glorified in them. John 17:10 I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them through your name which you have given me, that they may be one, even as we are. John 17:11 While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. I have kept those whom you have given me. None of them is lost except the son of destruction, that the Scripture might be fulfilled. John 17:12 But now I come to you, and I say these things in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves. John 17:13 I have given them your word. The world hated them because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. John 17:14 I pray not that you would take them from the world, but that you would keep them from the evil one. John 17:15 They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. John 17:16 Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth. John 17:17 As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent them into the world. John 17:18 For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth. John 17:19

title: John 18:1–11
context: After the prayer of chapter 17, Jesus goes with his disciples over the Kidron into a garden Judas knows. Knowing all the things that were happening, he comes forward, names himself “I am he,” and the arrest party falls. He shields those the Father gave him, forbids Peter’s sword, and drinks the cup the Father has given.
text: John 18:1–11 John After the prayer of chapter 17, Jesus goes with his disciples over the Kidron into a garden Judas knows. Knowing all the things that were happening, he comes forward, names himself “I am he,” and the arrest party falls. He shields those the Father gave him, forbids Peter’s sword, and drinks the cup the Father has given. When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered. John 18:1 Now Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, for Jesus often met there with his disciples. John 18:2 Judas then, having taken a detachment of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons. John 18:3 Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were happening to him, went out and said to them, “Who are you looking for?” John 18:4 They answered him, “Jesus of Nazareth.” Jesus said to them, “I am he.” Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them. John 18:5 When therefore he said to them, “I am he,” they went backward and fell to the ground. John 18:6 Again therefore he asked them, “Who are you looking for?” They said, “Jesus of Nazareth.” John 18:7 Jesus answered, “I told you that I am he. If therefore you seek me, let these go their way,” John 18:8 that the word might be fulfilled which he spoke, “Of those whom you have given me, I have lost none.” John 18:9 Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus. John 18:10 Jesus therefore said to Peter, “Put the sword into its sheath. The cup which the Father has given me, shall I not surely drink it?” John 18:11

title: John 18:12–27
context: The band arrests and binds the One who just dropped them with a word. He is led first to Annas, then toward Caiaphas—the counselor of expedient death. Peter follows, is brought in, and three times says “I am not.” Between denials Jesus answers openly; an officer strikes him; a rooster crows.
text: John 18:12–27 John The band arrests and binds the One who just dropped them with a word. He is led first to Annas, then toward Caiaphas—the counselor of expedient death. Peter follows, is brought in, and three times says “I am not.” Between denials Jesus answers openly; an officer strikes him; a rooster crows. So the detachment, the commanding officer, and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him, John 18:12 and led him to Annas first, for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year. John 18:13 Now it was Caiaphas who advised the Jews that it was expedient that one man should perish for the people. John 18:14 Simon Peter followed Jesus, as did another disciple. Now that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest; John 18:15 but Peter was standing at the door outside. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to her who kept the door, and brought in Peter. John 18:16 Then the maid who kept the door said to Peter, “Are you also one of this man’s disciples?” He said, “I am not.” John 18:17 Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals, for it was cold. They were warming themselves. Peter was with them, standing and warming himself. John 18:18 The high priest therefore asked Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching. John 18:19 Jesus answered him, “I spoke openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where the Jews always meet. I said nothing in secret. John 18:20 Why do you ask me? Ask those who have heard me what I said to them. Behold, they know the things which I said.” John 18:21 When he had said this, one of the officers standing by slapped Jesus with his hand, saying, “Do you answer the high priest like that?” John 18:22 Jesus answered him, “If I have spoken evil, testify of the evil; but if well, why do you beat me?” John 18:23 Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas, the high priest. John 18:24 Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore to him, “You aren’t also one of his disciples, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.” John 18:25 One of the servants of the high priest, being a relative of him whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Didn’t I see you in the garden with him?” John 18:26 Peter therefore denied it again, and immediately the rooster crowed. John 18:27

title: John 18:28–40
context: At dawn they bring Jesus from Caiaphas to Pilate yet will not enter, lest they be defiled for Passover. Death-power is Rome’s, fulfilling the kind of death he had said. Inside, he confesses a kingdom not of this world and a birth-purpose to testify to the truth: everyone who is of the truth listens to his voice. Pilate asks what truth is, finds no guilt, and the crowd chooses Barabbas.
text: John 18:28–40 John At dawn they bring Jesus from Caiaphas to Pilate yet will not enter, lest they be defiled for Passover. Death-power is Rome’s, fulfilling the kind of death he had said. Inside, he confesses a kingdom not of this world and a birth-purpose to testify to the truth: everyone who is of the truth listens to his voice. Pilate asks what truth is, finds no guilt, and the crowd chooses Barabbas. They led Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. It was early, and they themselves didn’t enter into the Praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
