John 18:28 Pilate therefore went out to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?” John 18:29 They answered him, “If this man weren’t an evildoer, we wouldn’t have delivered him up to you.” John 18:30 Pilate therefore said to them, “Take him yourselves, and judge him according to your law.” Therefore the Jews said to him, “It is illegal for us to put anyone to death,” John 18:31 that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke, signifying by what kind of death he should die. John 18:32 Pilate therefore entered again into the Praetorium, called Jesus, and said to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” John 18:33 Jesus answered him, “Do you say this by yourself, or did others tell you about me?” John 18:34 Pilate answered, “I’m not a Jew, am I? Your own nation and the chief priests delivered you to me. What have you done?” John 18:35 Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is not of this world. If my Kingdom were of this world, then my servants would fight, that I wouldn’t be delivered to the Jews. But now my Kingdom is not from here.” John 18:36 Pilate therefore said to him, “Are you a king then?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this reason I have been born, and for this reason I have come into the world, that I should testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.” John 18:37 Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” When he had said this, he went out again to the Jews, and said to them, “I find no basis for a charge against him. John 18:38 But you have a custom that I should release someone to you at the Passover. Therefore, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” John 18:39 Then they all shouted again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber. John 18:40

title: John 19:1–16
context: Pilate flogs Jesus; soldiers crown him with thorns and mock the King. The governor presents the man, finds no guilt, then hears the charge that he made himself the Son of God. Jesus names authority from above; Caesar's friendship outweighs justice; the priests confess no king but Caesar. Jesus is delivered to be crucified.
text: John 19:1–16 John Pilate flogs Jesus; soldiers crown him with thorns and mock the King. The governor presents the man, finds no guilt, then hears the charge that he made himself the Son of God. Jesus names authority from above; Caesar's friendship outweighs justice; the priests confess no king but Caesar. Jesus is delivered to be crucified. So Pilate then took Jesus and flogged him. John 19:1 The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment. John 19:2 They kept saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they kept slapping him. John 19:3 Then Pilate went out again, and said to them, “Behold, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no basis for a charge against him.” John 19:4 Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Pilate said to them, “Behold, the man!” John 19:5 When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no basis for a charge against him.” John 19:6 The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.” John 19:7 When therefore Pilate heard this saying, he was more afraid. John 19:8 He entered into the Praetorium again, and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer. John 19:9 Pilate therefore said to him, “Aren’t you speaking to me? Don’t you know that I have power to release you and have power to crucify you?” John 19:10 Jesus answered, “You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given to you from above. Therefore he who delivered me to you has greater sin.” John 19:11 At this, Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you aren’t Caesar’s friend! Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar!” John 19:12 When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called “The Pavement”, but in Hebrew, “Gabbatha.” John 19:13 Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, “Behold, your King!” John 19:14 They cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar!” John 19:15 So then he delivered him to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus and led him away. John 19:16

title: John 19:17–30
context: Jesus goes out, bearing his cross, to Golgotha and is crucified between two others. Pilate's trilingual title stands. Soldiers divide garments and cast lots for the tunic. The women and the beloved disciple are given to one another. Knowing all is finished, Jesus thirsts, receives sour wine, says It is finished, and gives up his spirit.
text: John 19:17–30 John Jesus goes out, bearing his cross, to Golgotha and is crucified between two others. Pilate's trilingual title stands. Soldiers divide garments and cast lots for the tunic. The women and the beloved disciple are given to one another. Knowing all is finished, Jesus thirsts, receives sour wine, says It is finished, and gives up his spirit. He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”, which is called in Hebrew, “Golgotha”, John 19:17 where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the middle. John 19:18 Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. There was written, “JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.” John 19:19 Therefore many of the Jews read this title, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek. John 19:20 The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate, “Don’t write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but, ‘he said, “I am King of the Jews.”’” John 19:21 Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.” John 19:22 Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the tunic. Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout. John 19:23 Then they said to one another, “Let’s not tear it, but cast lots for it to decide whose it will be,” that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says, “They parted my garments among them. They cast lots for my clothing.” Therefore the soldiers did these things. John 19:24 But standing by Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. John 19:25 Therefore when Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing there, he said to his mother, “Woman, behold, your son!” John 19:26 Then he said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother!” From that hour, the disciple took her to his own home. John 19:27 After this, Jesus, seeing that all things were now finished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, “I am thirsty!” John 19:28 Now a vessel full of vinegar was set there; so they put a sponge full of the vinegar on hyssop, and held it at his mouth. John 19:29 When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished!” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit. John 19:30

title: John 19:31–42
context: Because it is Preparation and a high Sabbath, the Jews ask that legs be broken. Jesus is already dead; a spear brings blood and water. Scripture of unbroken bones and the pierced one is fulfilled. Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus—who had come by night—bury Jesus with a great weight of spices in a new garden tomb close at hand.
text: John 19:31–42 John Because it is Preparation and a high Sabbath, the Jews ask that legs be broken. Jesus is already dead; a spear brings blood and water. Scripture of unbroken bones and the pierced one is fulfilled. Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus—who had come by night—bury Jesus with a great weight of spices in a new garden tomb close at hand. Therefore the Jews, because it was the Preparation Day, so that the bodies wouldn’t remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a special one), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away. John 19:31 Therefore the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first and of the other who was crucified with him; John 19:32 but when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they didn’t break his legs. John 19:33 However, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out. John 19:34 He who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, that you may believe. John 19:35 For these things happened that the Scripture might be fulfilled, “A bone of him will not be broken.” John 19:36 Again another Scripture says, “They will look on him whom they pierced.” John 19:37 After these things, Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body. Pilate gave him permission. He came therefore and took away his body. John 19:38 Nicodemus, who at first came to Jesus by night, also came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds. John 19:39 So they took Jesus’ body, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury. John 19:40 Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden. In the garden was a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid. John 19:41 Then, because of the Jews’ Preparation Day (for the tomb was near at hand), they laid Jesus there. John 19:42

title: John 2:1–12
context: At a wedding in Cana the wine runs out. Jesus, whose hour has not yet come, has the stone jars of Jewish purification filled; the water becomes wine. This first sign manifests his glory, and his disciples believe in him. Afterward he goes down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples for a few days.
text: John 2:1–12 John At a wedding in Cana the wine runs out. Jesus, whose hour has not yet come, has the stone jars of Jewish purification filled; the water becomes wine. This first sign manifests his glory, and his disciples believe in him. Afterward he goes down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples for a few days. The third day, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there. John 2:1 Jesus also was invited, with his disciples, to the wedding. John 2:2 When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.” John 2:3 Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does that have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.” John 2:4 His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.” John 2:5 Now there were six water pots of stone set there after the Jews’ way of purifying, containing two or three metretes apiece. John 2:6 Jesus said to them, “Fill the water pots with water.” So they filled them up to the brim. John 2:7 He said to them, “Now draw some out, and take it to the ruler of the feast.” So they took it. John 2:8 When the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and didn’t know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast called the bridegroom John 2:9 and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk freely, then that which is worse. You have kept the good wine until now!” John 2:10 This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him. John 2:11 After this, he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; and they stayed there a few days. John 2:12

title: John 2:13–25
context: At Passover Jesus goes up to Jerusalem and drives the traders from his Father’s house. The disciples remember the zeal text. Asked for a sign, he answers, “Destroy this temple,” speaking of his body; later they believe the Scripture and his word. Many believe when they see the signs, but Jesus does not entrust himself to them, knowing what is in man.
text: John 2:13–25 John At Passover Jesus goes up to Jerusalem and drives the traders from his Father’s house. The disciples remember the zeal text. Asked for a sign, he answers, “Destroy this temple,” speaking of his body; later they believe the Scripture and his word. Many believe when they see the signs, but Jesus does not entrust himself to them, knowing what is in man. The Passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. John 2:13 He found in the temple those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting. John 2:14 He made a whip of cords and drove all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money and overthrew their tables. John 2:15 To those who sold the doves, he said, “Take these things out of here! Don’t make my Father’s house a marketplace!” John 2:16 His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will eat me up.” John 2:17 The Jews therefore answered him, “What sign do you show us, seeing that you do these things?” John 2:18 Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” John 2:19 The Jews therefore said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple! Will you raise it up in three days?” John 2:20 But he spoke of the temple of his body. John 2:21 When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus had said. John 2:22 Now when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in his name, observing his signs which he did. John 2:23 But Jesus didn’t entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone, John 2:24 and because he didn’t need for anyone to testify concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man. John 2:25

title: John 20:1–10
context: First day of the week, still dark: Mary Magdalene finds the stone taken away, runs to Peter and the beloved disciple, and reports a missing body. They run; linen cloths and a folded face cloth lie in the tomb. The other disciple sees and believes, yet they still do not know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead. They go home. The Lord is not there—and they do not yet know why.
text: John 20:1–10 John First day of the week, still dark: Mary Magdalene finds the stone taken away, runs to Peter and the beloved disciple, and reports a missing body. They run; linen cloths and a folded face cloth lie in the tomb. The other disciple sees and believes, yet they still do not know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead. They go home. The Lord is not there—and they do not yet know why. Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb. John 20:1 Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they have laid him!” John 20:2 Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out, and they went toward the tomb. John 20:3 They both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first. John 20:4 Stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying there; yet he didn’t enter in. John 20:5 Then Simon Peter came, following him, and entered into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying, John 20:6 and the cloth that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself. John 20:7 So then the other disciple who came first to the tomb also entered in, and he saw and believed. John 20:8 For as yet they didn’t know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead. John 20:9 So the disciples went away again to their own homes. John 20:10

title: John 20:11–18
context: Mary stays weeping at the tomb after the men go home. Angels ask why; she wants a body. She turns, mistakes Jesus for the gardener, and hears her name. “Rabboni”—then “Don’t hold”: he is ascending to my Father and your Father, my God and your God. She is sent to the brothers with that news. The first Easter preacher is a woman who came for a corpse and left announcing, “That she had seen the Lord.”
text: John 20:11–18 John Mary stays weeping at the tomb after the men go home. Angels ask why; she wants a body. She turns, mistakes Jesus for the gardener, and hears her name. “Rabboni”—then “Don’t hold”: he is ascending to my Father and your Father, my God and your God. She is sent to the brothers with that news. The first Easter preacher is a woman who came for a corpse and left announcing, “That she had seen the Lord.” But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb, John 20:11 and she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain. John 20:12 They asked her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I don’t know where they have laid him.” John 20:13 When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, and didn’t know that it was Jesus. John 20:14 Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?” She, supposing him to be the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.” John 20:15 Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” which is to say, “Teacher!” John 20:16 Jesus said to her, “Don’t hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’” John 20:17 Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had said these things to her. John 20:18

title: John 20:19–23
context: Evening of that first day: locked doors, fear, and Jesus among them with peace, wounds, and gladness. Then the high-contrast charge: as the Father sent me, I am sending you; he breathes, Receive the Holy Spirit! If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven—if you withhold, it is withheld. Sending, Spirit, and forgiveness arrive together.
text: John 20:19–23 John Evening of that first day: locked doors, fear, and Jesus among them with peace, wounds, and gladness. Then the high-contrast charge: as the Father sent me, I am sending you; he breathes, Receive the Holy Spirit! If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven—if you withhold, it is withheld. Sending, Spirit, and forgiveness arrive together. When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle and said to them, “Peace be to you.” John 20:19 When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord. John 20:20 Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.” John 20:21 When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit! John 20:22 If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.” John 20:23

title: John 20:24–31
context: Thomas missed Jesus’ first appearance and refuses to believe without touching the wounds. A week later Jesus offers exactly that, and Thomas makes the Gospel’s highest confession: ‘My Lord and my God!’ Jesus blesses those who believe without seeing, and John states his purpose: these signs are written so readers may believe and have life.
text: John 20:24–31 John Thomas missed Jesus’ first appearance and refuses to believe without touching the wounds. A week later Jesus offers exactly that, and Thomas makes the Gospel’s highest confession: ‘My Lord and my God!’ Jesus blesses those who believe without seeing, and John states his purpose: these signs are written so readers may believe and have life. But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came. John 20:24 The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.” John 20:25 After eight days, again his disciples were inside and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said, “Peace be to you.” John 20:26 Then he said to Thomas, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.” John 20:27 Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!” John 20:28 Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.” John 20:29 Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book; John 20:30 but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name. John 20:31

title: John 21:1–14
context: After the locked-room appearances, Jesus reveals himself again at the sea of Tiberias. Seven disciples fish all night and catch nothing. At daybreak a stranger on the shore tells them to cast on the right side; the net fills. The beloved disciple names the Lord; Peter plunges into the water. Ashore they find a charcoal fire, fish, and bread. Jesus breakfasts with them. This is the third time he was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.
text: John 21:1–14 John After the locked-room appearances, Jesus reveals himself again at the sea of Tiberias. Seven disciples fish all night and catch nothing. At daybreak a stranger on the shore tells them to cast on the right side; the net fills. The beloved disciple names the Lord; Peter plunges into the water. Ashore they find a charcoal fire, fish, and bread. Jesus breakfasts with them. This is the third time he was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead. After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way. John 21:1 Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together. John 21:2 Simon Peter said to them, “I’m going fishing.” They told him, “We are also coming with you.” They immediately went out and entered into the boat. That night, they caught nothing. John 21:3 But when day had already come, Jesus stood on the beach; yet the disciples didn’t know that it was Jesus. John 21:4 Jesus therefore said to them, “Children, have you anything to eat?” They answered him, “No.” John 21:5 He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” They cast it therefore, and now they weren’t able to draw it in for the multitude of fish. John 21:6 That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!” So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his coat around himself (for he was naked), and threw himself into the sea. John 21:7 But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish. John 21:8 So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of coals there, with fish and bread laid on it. John 21:9 Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.” John 21:10 Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of one hundred fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn. John 21:11 Jesus said to them, “Come and eat breakfast!” None of the disciples dared inquire of him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord. John 21:12 Then Jesus came and took the bread, gave it to them, and the fish likewise. John 21:13 This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead. John 21:14

title: John 21:15–25
context: After breakfast Jesus thrice asks Simon, son of John, whether he loves him, and thrice charges him to feed his lambs and sheep—meeting the threefold denial with restored love and office. He then shows by what death Peter will glorify God and says, Follow me. When Peter asks about the beloved disciple, Jesus answers: If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me. The Gospel closes with that disciple’s true testimony and the world’s inability to contain all Jesus did.
text: John 21:15–25 John After breakfast Jesus thrice asks Simon, son of John, whether he loves him, and thrice charges him to feed his lambs and sheep—meeting the threefold denial with restored love and office. He then shows by what death Peter will glorify God and says, Follow me. When Peter asks about the beloved disciple, Jesus answers: If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me. The Gospel closes with that disciple’s true testimony and the world’s inability to contain all Jesus did. So when they had eaten their breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.” John 21:15 He said to him again a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Tend my sheep.” John 21:16 He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep. John 21:17 Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you don’t want to go.” John 21:18 Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. When he had said this, he said to him, “Follow me.” John 21:19 Then Peter, turning around, saw a disciple following. This was the disciple whom Jesus loved, the one who had also leaned on Jesus’ chest at the supper and asked, “Lord, who is going to betray you?” John 21:20 Peter, seeing him, said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?” John 21:21 Jesus said to him, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.” John 21:22 This saying therefore went out among the brothers that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Jesus didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?” John 21:23 This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and wrote these things. We know that his witness is true. John 21:24 There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written. John 21:25

title: John 3:1–21
context: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler, comes by night. Jesus answers admiration with a requirement: unless one is born anew—of water and Spirit, he can’t see or enter the kingdom. Flesh begets flesh; the Spirit’s work is authentic yet unmanageable, like wind. The Son of Man must be lifted up so that whoever believes may have life. God loved the world and gave His only Son; unbelief is already condemnation because people loved darkness rather than the Light who came.
text: John 3:1–21 John Nicodemus, a Pharisee and ruler, comes by night. Jesus answers admiration with a requirement: unless one is born anew—of water and Spirit, he can’t see or enter the kingdom. Flesh begets flesh; the Spirit’s work is authentic yet unmanageable, like wind. The Son of Man must be lifted up so that whoever believes may have life. God loved the world and gave His only Son; unbelief is already condemnation because people loved darkness rather than the Light who came. Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. John 3:1 He came to Jesus by night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.” John 3:2 Jesus answered him, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.” John 3:3 Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?” John 3:4 Jesus answered, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born of water and Spirit, he can’t enter into God’s Kingdom. John 3:5 That which is born of the flesh is flesh. That which is born of the Spirit is spirit. John 3:6 Don’t marvel that I said to you, ‘You must all be born anew.’ John 3:7 The wind blows where it wants to, and you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.” John 3:8 Nicodemus answered him, “How can these things be?” John 3:9 Jesus answered him, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and don’t understand these things? John 3:10 Most certainly I tell you, we speak that which we know and testify of that which we have seen, and you don’t receive our witness. John 3:11 If I told you earthly things and you don’t believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? John 3:12 No one has ascended into heaven but he who descended out of heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven. John 3:13 As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up, John 3:14 that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. John 3:15 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. John 3:16 For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him. John 3:17 He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God. John 3:18 This is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were evil. John 3:19 For everyone who does evil hates the light and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed. John 3:20 But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.” John 3:21

title: John 3:22–36
context: Jesus and his disciples baptize in Judea while John baptizes nearby. When John’s disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus, John answers that a person can receive only what is given from heaven. He is the friend of the bridegroom and rejoices to hear his voice: he must increase, and I must decrease. The chapter closes by contrasting the one from above with those from the earth. The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, and whoever does not obey the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him. Both traditions find verse 36 decisive. They read verse 27 differently.
text: John 3:22–36 John Jesus and his disciples baptize in Judea while John baptizes nearby. When John’s disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus, John answers that a person can receive only what is given from heaven. He is the friend of the bridegroom and rejoices to hear his voice: he must increase, and I must decrease. The chapter closes by contrasting the one from above with those from the earth. The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, and whoever does not obey the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him. Both traditions find verse 36 decisive. They read verse 27 differently. After these things, Jesus came with his disciples into the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and baptized. John 3:22 John also was baptizing in Enon near Salim, because there was much water there. They came and were baptized; John 3:23 for John was not yet thrown into prison. John 3:24 Therefore a dispute arose on the part of John’s disciples with some Jews about purification. John 3:25 They came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified, behold, he baptizes, and everyone is coming to him.” John 3:26 John answered, “A man can receive nothing unless it has been given him from heaven. John 3:27 You yourselves testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ,’ but, ‘I have been sent before him.’ John 3:28 He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore my joy is made full. John 3:29 He must increase, but I must decrease. John 3:30 “He who comes from above is above all. He who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all. John 3:31 What he has seen and heard, of that he testifies; and no one receives his witness. John 3:32 He who has received his witness has set his seal to this, that God is true. John 3:33 For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God; for God gives the Spirit without measure. John 3:34 The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand. John 3:35 One who believes in the Son has eternal life, but one who disobeys the Son won’t see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.” John 3:36

title: John 4:1–26
context: Jesus leaves Judea, must pass through Samaria, and sits wearied at Jacob’s well. He asks a Samaritan woman for a drink, then offers living water—the gift of God—that becomes a spring to eternal life. He names her life without shaming her out of the conversation, relocates worship from Gerizim-versus-Jerusalem to the Father who seeks worshipers in spirit and truth, and discloses: “I am he, the one who speaks to you.”
text: John 4:1–26 John Jesus leaves Judea, must pass through Samaria, and sits wearied at Jacob’s well. He asks a Samaritan woman for a drink, then offers living water—the gift of God—that becomes a spring to eternal life. He names her life without shaming her out of the conversation, relocates worship from Gerizim-versus-Jerusalem to the Father who seeks worshipers in spirit and truth, and discloses: “I am he, the one who speaks to you.” Therefore when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John John 4:1 (although Jesus himself didn’t baptize, but his disciples), John 4:2 he left Judea and departed into Galilee. John 4:3 He needed to pass through Samaria. John 4:4 So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. John 4:5 Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour. John 4:6 A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.” John 4:7 For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food. John 4:8 The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.) John 4:9 Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.” John 4:10 The woman said to him, “Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. So where do you get that living water? John 4:11 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did his children and his livestock?” John 4:12 Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again, John 4:13 but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.” John 4:14 The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I don’t get thirsty, neither come all the way here to draw.” John 4:15 Jesus said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.” John 4:16 The woman answered, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You said well, ‘I have no husband,’ John 4:17 for you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.” John 4:18 The woman said to him, “Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet. John 4:19 Our fathers worshiped in this mountain, and you Jews say that in Jerusalem is the place where people ought to worship.” John 4:20 Jesus said to her, “Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when neither in this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father. John 4:21 You worship that which you don’t know. We worship that which we know; for salvation is from the Jews. John 4:22 But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such to be his worshipers. John 4:23 God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.” John 4:24 The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah is coming, he who is called Christ. When he has come, he will declare to us all things.” John 4:25 Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one who speaks to you.” John 4:26

title: John 4:27–42
context: The disciples return, startled that He talks with a woman, and stay silent. She leaves her jar, testifies in town, and people come. Jesus refuses their food: His food is the Father’s will. The fields are white; sower and reaper rejoice together. Many Samaritans believe because of her word, then many more because of His, and they confess Him Savior of the world.
text: John 4:27–42 John The disciples return, startled that He talks with a woman, and stay silent. She leaves her jar, testifies in town, and people come. Jesus refuses their food: His food is the Father’s will. The fields are white; sower and reaper rejoice together. Many Samaritans believe because of her word, then many more because of His, and they confess Him Savior of the world. Just then, his disciples came. They marveled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or, “Why do you speak with her?” John 4:27 So the woman left her water pot, went away into the city, and said to the people, John 4:28 “Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done. Can this be the Christ?” John 4:29 They went out of the city, and were coming to him. John 4:30 In the meanwhile, the disciples urged him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.” John 4:31 But he said to them, “I have food to eat that you don’t know about.” John 4:32 The disciples therefore said to one another, “Has anyone brought him something to eat?” John 4:33 Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to accomplish his work. John 4:34 Don’t you say, ‘There are yet four months until the harvest’? Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already. John 4:35 He who reaps receives wages and gathers fruit to eternal life, that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together. John 4:36 For in this the saying is true, ‘One sows, and another reaps.’ John 4:37 I sent you to reap that for which you haven’t labored. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.” John 4:38 From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I have done.” John 4:39 So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there two days. John 4:40 Many more believed because of his word. John 4:41 They said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of your speaking; for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.” John 4:42

title: John 4:43–54
context: After two days Jesus goes to Galilee, where a prophet lacks hometown honor, yet Galileans welcome Him for feast-signs. At Cana an official from Capernaum begs Him to come down before his son dies. Jesus rebukes sign-hunger, then speaks: “Go your way. Your son lives.” The man believes the word, meets servants on the road, matches the hour, and he and his household believe. This is the second sign from Judea to Galilee.
text: John 4:43–54 John After two days Jesus goes to Galilee, where a prophet lacks hometown honor, yet Galileans welcome Him for feast-signs. At Cana an official from Capernaum begs Him to come down before his son dies. Jesus rebukes sign-hunger, then speaks: “Go your way. Your son lives.” The man believes the word, meets servants on the road, matches the hour, and he and his household believe. This is the second sign from Judea to Galilee. After the two days he went out from there and went into Galilee. John 4:43 For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own country. John 4:44 So when he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast. John 4:45 Jesus came therefore again to Cana of Galilee, where he made the water into wine. There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Capernaum. John 4:46 When he heard that Jesus had come out of Judea into Galilee, he went to him and begged him that he would come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death. John 4:47 Jesus therefore said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will in no way believe.” John 4:48 The nobleman said to him, “Sir, come down before my child dies.” John 4:49 Jesus said to him, “Go your way. Your son lives.” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way. John 4:50 As he was going down, his servants met him and reported, saying “Your child lives!” John 4:51 So he inquired of them the hour when he began to get better. They said therefore to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour, the fever left him.” John 4:52 So the father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said to him, “Your son lives.” He believed, as did his whole house. John 4:53 This is again the second sign that Jesus did, having come out of Judea into Galilee. John 4:54

title: John 5:1–18
context: Jesus heals a long-invalid man at Bethesda on the Sabbath, then answers the charge by claiming the Father’s ongoing work—and equality with God.
text: John 5:1–18 John Jesus heals a long-invalid man at Bethesda on the Sabbath, then answers the charge by claiming the Father’s ongoing work—and equality with God. After these things, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. John 5:1 Now in Jerusalem by the sheep gate, there is a pool, which is called in Hebrew, “Bethesda”, having five porches. John 5:2 In these lay a great multitude of those who were sick, blind, lame, or paralyzed, waiting for the moving of the water; John 5:3 A certain man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years. John 5:5 When Jesus saw him lying there, and knew that he had been sick for a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to be made well?” John 5:6 The sick man answered him, “Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, but while I’m coming, another steps down before me.” John 5:7 Jesus said to him, “Arise, take up your mat, and walk.” John 5:8 Immediately, the man was made well, and took up his mat and walked. Now that day was a Sabbath. John 5:9 So the Jews said to him who was cured, “It is the Sabbath. It is not lawful for you to carry the mat.” John 5:10 He answered them, “He who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your mat and walk.’ ” John 5:11 Then they asked him, “Who is the man who said to you, ‘Take up your mat and walk’?” John 5:12 But he who was healed didn’t know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a crowd being in the place. John 5:13 Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, “Behold, you are made well. Sin no more, so that nothing worse happens to you.” John 5:14 The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. John 5:15 For this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him, because he did these things on the Sabbath. John 5:16 But Jesus answered them, “My Father is still working, so I am working, too.” John 5:17 For this cause therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God. John 5:18

title: John 5:19–29
context: After healing on the Sabbath and calling God his Father, Jesus explains his relationship to the Father. The Son does only what he sees the Father doing. As the Father raises the dead and gives life, so the Son gives life to whom he will. The Father has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father. Whoever hears Jesus’ word and believes has eternal life and has passed from death to life. An hour is coming when all in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, to the resurrection of life or of judgment. Both traditions find a high Christology here. They read “gives life to whom he will” and the judgment by deeds differently.
text: John 5:19–29 John After healing on the Sabbath and calling God his Father, Jesus explains his relationship to the Father. The Son does only what he sees the Father doing. As the Father raises the dead and gives life, so the Son gives life to whom he will. The Father has given all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father. Whoever hears Jesus’ word and believes has eternal life and has passed from death to life. An hour is coming when all in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, to the resurrection of life or of judgment. Both traditions find a high Christology here. They read “gives life to whom he will” and the judgment by deeds differently. Jesus therefore answered them, “Most certainly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing. For whatever things he does, these the Son also does likewise. John 5:19 For the Father has affection for the Son, and shows him all things that he himself does. He will show him greater works than these, that you may marvel. John 5:20 For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, even so the Son also gives life to whom he desires. John 5:21 For the Father judges no one, but he has given all judgment to the Son, John 5:22 that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He who doesn’t honor the Son doesn’t honor the Father who sent him. John 5:23 “Most certainly I tell you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life. John 5:24 Most certainly I tell you, the hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice; and those who hear will live. John 5:25 For as the Father has life in himself, even so he gave to the Son also to have life in himself. John 5:26 He also gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man. John 5:27 Don’t marvel at this, for the hour comes in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice John 5:28 and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment. John 5:29

title: John 5:30–47
context: Jesus continues his defense. His judgment is just because he seeks the will of the one who sent him. He points to witnesses: John the Baptist, his own works, the Father himself, and the Scriptures, which testify about him. Yet his hearers refuse to come to him for life. They seek glory from one another rather than from God, and they do not truly believe Moses, who wrote about Jesus. Both traditions see the passage as a powerful case for Christ’s identity. They draw different conclusions from verse 40 and verse 44.
text: John 5:30–47 John Jesus continues his defense. His judgment is just because he seeks the will of the one who sent him. He points to witnesses: John the Baptist, his own works, the Father himself, and the Scriptures, which testify about him. Yet his hearers refuse to come to him for life. They seek glory from one another rather than from God, and they do not truly believe Moses, who wrote about Jesus. Both traditions see the passage as a powerful case for Christ’s identity. They draw different conclusions from verse 40 and verse 44. I can of myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge; and my judgment is righteous, because I don’t seek my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me. John 5:30 “If I testify about myself, my witness is not valid. John 5:31 It is another who testifies about me. I know that the testimony which he testifies about me is true. John 5:32 You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth. John 5:33 But the testimony which I receive is not from man. However, I say these things that you may be saved. John 5:34 He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light. John 5:35 But the testimony which I have is greater than that of John; for the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, the very works that I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me. John 5:36 The Father himself, who sent me, has testified about me. You have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form. John 5:37 You don’t have his word living in you, because you don’t believe him whom he sent. John 5:38 “You search the Scriptures, because you think that in them you have eternal life; and these are they which testify about me. John 5:39 Yet you will not come to me, that you may have life. John 5:40 I don’t receive glory from men. John 5:41 But I know you, that you don’t have God’s love in yourselves. John 5:42 I have come in my Father’s name, and you don’t receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him. John 5:43 How can you believe, who receive glory from one another, and you don’t seek the glory that comes from the only God? John 5:44 “Don’t think that I will accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you, even Moses, on whom you have set your hope. John 5:45 For if you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote about me. John 5:46 But if you don’t believe his writings, how will you believe my words?” John 5:47

title: John 6:1–15
context: After the controversies of chapter 5, Jesus crosses the Sea of Galilee near Passover, feeds about five thousand from five barley loaves and two fish, and withdraws when the crowd would seize him to make him king.
text: John 6:1–15 John After the controversies of chapter 5, Jesus crosses the Sea of Galilee near Passover, feeds about five thousand from five barley loaves and two fish, and withdraws when the crowd would seize him to make him king. After these things, Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias. John 6:1 A great multitude followed him, because they saw his signs which he did on those who were sick. John 6:2 Jesus went up into the mountain, and he sat there with his disciples. John 6:3 Now the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand. John 6:4 Jesus therefore, lifting up his eyes and seeing that a great multitude was coming to him, said to Philip, “Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?” John 6:5 He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he would do. John 6:6 Philip answered him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may receive a little.” John 6:7 One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him, John 6:8 “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?” John 6:9 Jesus said, “Have the people sit down.” Now there was much grass in that place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand. John 6:10 Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down, likewise also of the fish as much as they desired. John 6:11 When they were filled, he said to his disciples, “Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, that nothing be lost.” John 6:12 So they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which were left over by those who had eaten. John 6:13 When therefore the people saw the sign which Jesus did, they said, “This is truly the prophet who comes into the world.” John 6:14 Jesus therefore, perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself. John 6:15

title: John 6:16–21
context: After refusing forced kingship, Jesus’ disciples start across the sea toward Capernaum in the dark. A strong wind rises; they see him walking on the water; he says, “It is I. Don’t be afraid,” and the boat is immediately at the land.
text: John 6:16–21 John After refusing forced kingship, Jesus’ disciples start across the sea toward Capernaum in the dark. A strong wind rises; they see him walking on the water; he says, “It is I. Don’t be afraid,” and the boat is immediately at the land. When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea. John 6:16 They entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum. It was now dark, and Jesus had not come to them. John 6:17 The sea was tossed by a great wind blowing. John 6:18 When therefore they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near to the boat; and they were afraid. John 6:19 But he said to them, “It is I. Don’t be afraid.” John 6:20 They were willing therefore to receive him into the boat. Immediately the boat was at the land where they were going. John 6:21

title: John 6:22–40
context: The day after the feeding of the five thousand, the crowd tracks Jesus to Capernaum. He tells them they seek him for loaves, not signs, and urges them to work for food that endures to eternal life. When they ask what work God requires, he answers that the work of God is to believe in the one he sent. Jesus declares that he is the bread of life: whoever comes to him will never hunger, and whoever believes will never thirst. He adds that all the Father gives him will come to him, that he will never cast out anyone who comes, and that it is the Father’s will that he lose none of those given him and that everyone who looks to the Son and believes should have eternal life. This passage is at the center of the Arminian and Reformed debate over election, grace, and perseverance.
text: John 6:22–40 John The day after the feeding of the five thousand, the crowd tracks Jesus to Capernaum. He tells them they seek him for loaves, not signs, and urges them to work for food that endures to eternal life. When they ask what work God requires, he answers that the work of God is to believe in the one he sent. Jesus declares that he is the bread of life: whoever comes to him will never hunger, and whoever believes will never thirst. He adds that all the Father gives him will come to him, that he will never cast out anyone who comes, and that it is the Father’s will that he lose none of those given him and that everyone who looks to the Son and believes should have eternal life. This passage is at the center of the Arminian and Reformed debate over election, grace, and perseverance. On the next day, the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, except the one in which his disciples had embarked, and that Jesus hadn’t entered with his disciples into the boat, but his disciples had gone away alone. John 6:22 However, boats from Tiberias came near to the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks. John 6:23 When the multitude therefore saw that Jesus wasn’t there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus. John 6:24 When they found him on the other side of the sea, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you come here?” John 6:25 Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled. John 6:26 Don’t work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you. For God the Father has sealed him.” John 6:27 They said therefore to him, “What must we do, that we may work the works of God?” John 6:28 Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.” John 6:29 They said therefore to him, “What then do you do for a sign, that we may see and believe you? What work do you do? John 6:30 Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness. As it is written, ‘He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.’” John 6:31 Jesus therefore said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, it wasn’t Moses who gave you the bread out of heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread out of heaven. John 6:32 For the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven and gives life to the world.” John 6:33 They said therefore to him, “Lord, always give us this bread.” John 6:34 Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty. John 6:35 But I told you that you have seen me, and yet you don’t believe. John 6:36 All those whom the Father gives me will come to me. He who comes to me I will in no way throw out. John 6:37 For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me. John 6:38 This is the will of my Father who sent me, that of all he has given to me I should lose nothing, but should raise him up at the last day. John 6:39 This is the will of the one who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.” John 6:40

title: John 6:41–59
context: The crowd grumbles at Jesus’ claim to be bread from heaven, since they know his family. Jesus answers that no one can come to him unless the Father who sent him draws him, and he will raise that person up on the last day. Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to him. He then presses further: he is the living bread, and the bread he will give for the life of the world is his flesh. Unless they eat his flesh and drink his blood, they have no life. Verse 44 is one of the most debated verses between Arminian and Reformed readers. The language of eating and drinking also raises questions about the Lord’s Supper.
text: John 6:41–59 John The crowd grumbles at Jesus’ claim to be bread from heaven, since they know his family. Jesus answers that no one can come to him unless the Father who sent him draws him, and he will raise that person up on the last day. Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to him. He then presses further: he is the living bread, and the bread he will give for the life of the world is his flesh. Unless they eat his flesh and drink his blood, they have no life. Verse 44 is one of the most debated verses between Arminian and Reformed readers. The language of eating and drinking also raises questions about the Lord’s Supper. The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said, “I am the bread which came down out of heaven.” John 6:41 They said, “Isn’t this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say, ‘I have come down out of heaven’?” John 6:42 Therefore Jesus answered them, “Don’t murmur among yourselves. John 6:43 No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I will raise him up in the last day. John 6:44 It is written in the prophets, ‘They will all be taught by God.’ Therefore everyone who hears from the Father and has learned, comes to me. John 6:45 Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God. He has seen the Father. John 6:46 Most certainly, I tell you, he who believes in me has eternal life. John 6:47 I am the bread of life. John 6:48 Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and they died. John 6:49 This is the bread which comes down out of heaven, that anyone may eat of it and not die. John 6:50 I am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.” John 6:51 The Jews therefore contended with one another, saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?” John 6:52 Jesus therefore said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you don’t have life in yourselves. John 6:53 He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day. John 6:54 For my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed. John 6:55 He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood lives in me, and I in him. John 6:56 As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so he who feeds on me will also live because of me. John 6:57 This is the bread which came down out of heaven—not as our fathers ate the manna and died. He who eats this bread will live forever.” John 6:58 He said these things in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum. John 6:59

title: John 6:60–71
context: Many of Jesus’ disciples find his teaching hard and grumble. Jesus says the Spirit gives life and the flesh is no help, and that his words are spirit and life. He knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him, and he repeats that no one can come to him unless it is granted by the Father. Many disciples turn back and no longer walk with him. When Jesus asks the Twelve if they will leave too, Peter answers that only Jesus has the words of eternal life. Jesus responds that he chose the Twelve, yet one of them is a devil. Both traditions use this passage in the debate over perseverance and apostasy.
text: John 6:60–71 John Many of Jesus’ disciples find his teaching hard and grumble. Jesus says the Spirit gives life and the flesh is no help, and that his words are spirit and life. He knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him, and he repeats that no one can come to him unless it is granted by the Father. Many disciples turn back and no longer walk with him. When Jesus asks the Twelve if they will leave too, Peter answers that only Jesus has the words of eternal life. Jesus responds that he chose the Twelve, yet one of them is a devil. Both traditions use this passage in the debate over perseverance and apostasy. Therefore many of his disciples, when they heard this, said, “This is a hard saying! Who can listen to it?” John 6:60 But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said to them, “Does this cause you to stumble? John 6:61 Then what if you would see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before? John 6:62 It is the spirit who gives life. The flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and are life. John 6:63 But there are some of you who don’t believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who didn’t believe, and who it was who would betray him. John 6:64 He said, “For this cause I have said to you that no one can come to me, unless it is given to him by my Father.” John 6:65 At this, many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him. John 6:66 Jesus said therefore to the twelve, “You don’t also want to go away, do you?” John 6:67 Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life. John 6:68 We have come to believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” John 6:69 Jesus answered them, “Didn’t I choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?” John 6:70 Now he spoke of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for it was he who would betray him, being one of the twelve. John 6:71

title: John 7:1–9
context: After the bread-of-life crisis, Jesus remains in Galilee because Judean leaders are seeking to kill him. At the Feast of Booths his brothers urge a public show of works; he answers that his time has not yet come, that the world cannot hate them, and that he will not go up on their timetable—then he stays in Galilee.
text: John 7:1–9 John After the bread-of-life crisis, Jesus remains in Galilee because Judean leaders are seeking to kill him. At the Feast of Booths his brothers urge a public show of works; he answers that his time has not yet come, that the world cannot hate them, and that he will not go up on their timetable—then he stays in Galilee. After these things, Jesus was walking in Galilee, for he wouldn’t walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him. John 7:1 Now the feast of the Jews, the Feast of Booths, was at hand. John 7:2 His brothers therefore said to him, “Depart from here and go into Judea, that your disciples also may see your works which you do. John 7:3 For no one does anything in secret while he seeks to be known openly. If you do these things, reveal yourself to the world.” John 7:4 For even his brothers didn’t believe in him. John 7:5 Jesus therefore said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready. John 7:6 The world can’t hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it, that its works are evil. John 7:7 You go up to the feast. I am not yet going up to this feast, because my time is not yet fulfilled.” John 7:8 Having said these things to them, he stayed in Galilee. John 7:9

title: John 7:10–24
context: After his brothers go up, Jesus goes to the feast privately. Jerusalem mutters and fears. Mid-feast he teaches in the temple: his teaching is from the One who sent him; anyone whose will is to do God’s will will know the teaching’s origin. He exposes Sabbath hypocrisy over Moses’ circumcision and calls them to judge with right judgment, not appearances.
text: John 7:10–24 John After his brothers go up, Jesus goes to the feast privately. Jerusalem mutters and fears. Mid-feast he teaches in the temple: his teaching is from the One who sent him; anyone whose will is to do God’s will will know the teaching’s origin. He exposes Sabbath hypocrisy over Moses’ circumcision and calls them to judge with right judgment, not appearances. But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not publicly, but as it were in secret. John 7:10 The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, “Where is he?” John 7:11 There was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him. Some said, “He is a good man.” Others said, “Not so, but he leads the multitude astray.” John 7:12 Yet no one spoke openly of him for fear of the Jews. John 7:13 But when it was now the middle of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple and taught. John 7:14 The Jews therefore marveled, saying, “How does this man know letters, having never been educated?” John 7:15 Jesus therefore answered them, “My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me. John 7:16 If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or if I am speaking from myself. John 7:17 He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory, but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and no unrighteousness is in him. John 7:18 Didn’t Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill me?” John 7:19 The multitude answered, “You have a demon! Who seeks to kill you?” John 7:20 Jesus answered them, “I did one work and you all marvel because of it. John 7:21 Moses has given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers), and on the Sabbath you circumcise a boy. John 7:22 If a boy receives circumcision on the Sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a man completely healthy on the Sabbath? John 7:23 Don’t judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.” John 7:24

title: John 7:25–36
context: Jerusalemites wonder that the sought man teaches openly. They “know where he comes from,” so he cannot be the Christ. He cries that they do not know the One who sent him; they seek to arrest him, but his hour has not come, and many believe because of the signs. Officers are sent. He says he goes to the Sender: they will seek and not find; where he is they cannot come. They joke about the Dispersion.
text: John 7:25–36 John Jerusalemites wonder that the sought man teaches openly. They “know where he comes from,” so he cannot be the Christ. He cries that they do not know the One who sent him; they seek to arrest him, but his hour has not come, and many believe because of the signs. Officers are sent. He says he goes to the Sender: they will seek and not find; where he is they cannot come. They joke about the Dispersion. Therefore some of them of Jerusalem said, “Isn’t this he whom they seek to kill? John 7:25 Behold, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is truly the Christ? John 7:26 However, we know where this man comes from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.” John 7:27 Jesus therefore cried out in the temple, teaching and saying, “You both know me, and know where I am from. I have not come of myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you don’t know. John 7:28 I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.” John 7:29 They sought therefore to take him; but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come. John 7:30 But of the multitude, many believed in him. They said, “When the Christ comes, he won’t do more signs than those which this man has done, will he?” John 7:31 The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him. John 7:32 Then Jesus said, “I will be with you a little while longer, then I go to him who sent me. John 7:33 You will seek me and won’t find me. You can’t come where I am.” John 7:34 The Jews therefore said among themselves, “Where will this man go that we won’t find him? Will he go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks? John 7:35 What is this word that he said, ‘You will seek me, and won’t find me;’ and ‘Where I am, you can’t come’?” John 7:36

title: John 7:37–52
context: On the last, great day of Booths, Jesus stands and cries that if anyone thirsts, he should come and drink; rivers of living water will flow from the believer’s heart—the Spirit, not yet given because Jesus is not yet glorified. The crowd divides over Prophet, Christ, and Galilee. Officers return empty: no man ever spoke like this man. Pharisees scorn the accursed crowd; Nicodemus asks for a hearing and is mocked. Chapter 7 ends at v. 52; 7:53 belongs with the pericope of 8:1–11.
text: John 7:37–52 John On the last, great day of Booths, Jesus stands and cries that if anyone thirsts, he should come and drink; rivers of living water will flow from the believer’s heart—the Spirit, not yet given because Jesus is not yet glorified. The crowd divides over Prophet, Christ, and Galilee. Officers return empty: no man ever spoke like this man. Pharisees scorn the accursed crowd; Nicodemus asks for a hearing and is mocked. Chapter 7 ends at v. 52; 7:53 belongs with the pericope of 8:1–11. Now on the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink! John 7:37 He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water.” John 7:38 But he said this about the Spirit, which those believing in him were to receive. For the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus wasn’t yet glorified. John 7:39 Many of the multitude therefore, when they heard these words, said, “This is truly the prophet.” John 7:40 Others said, “This is the Christ.” But some said, “What, does the Christ come out of Galilee? John 7:41 Hasn’t the Scripture said that the Christ comes of the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?” John 7:42 So a division arose in the multitude because of him. John 7:43 Some of them would have arrested him, but no one laid hands on him. John 7:44 The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said to them, “Why didn’t you bring him?” John 7:45 The officers answered, “No man ever spoke like this man!” John 7:46 The Pharisees therefore answered them, “You aren’t also led astray, are you? John 7:47 Have any of the rulers or any of the Pharisees believed in him? John 7:48 But this multitude that doesn’t know the law is cursed.” John 7:49 Nicodemus (he who came to him by night, being one of them) said to them, John 7:50 “Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him personally and knows what he does?” John 7:51 They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see that no prophet has arisen out of Galilee.” John 7:52

title: John 8:1–11
context: Many modern editions print 7:53–8:11 as a bracketed unit: “Everyone went to his own house” (7:53) after Nicodemus stalled the council, then “but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.” A heading warns that the earliest manuscripts do not include 7:53–8:11; a footnote notes that some copies omit it, others place it here, after 7:36, after 21:25, or after Luke 21:38, with variations. The double brackets [[ ]] enclose the pericope adulterae. This file numbers only 8:1–11; 7:53 belongs in this context, not as a chapter-8 verse. Still the passage is to be read pastorally: at dawn Jesus teaches in the temple; scribes and Pharisees thrust a woman caught in adultery into the midst to trap him between Moses’ sentence and his mercy; he writes on the ground, sends the sinless-first stone, and tells her, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.”

Still the passage is to be read pastorally: at dawn Jesus teaches in the temple; scribes and Pharisees thrust a woman caught in adultery into the midst to trap him between Moses’ sentence and his mercy; he writes on the ground, sends the sinless-first stone, and tells her, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.” but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives. John 8:1 Now very early in the morning, he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him. He sat down and taught them. John 8:2 The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle, John 8:3 they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act. John 8:4 Now in our law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say about her?” John 8:5 They said this testing him, that they might have something to accuse him of. But Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger. John 8:6 But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.” John 8:7 Again he stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger. John 8:8 They, when they heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the oldest, even to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman where she was, in the middle. John 8:9 Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?” John 8:10 She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.” John 8:11

title: John 8:12–20
context: After the bracketed pericope, John resumes the temple discourse of Tabernacles. Jesus names himself the light of the world and promises that whoever follows him will not walk in the darkness. Pharisees object that self-witness is invalid. He answers with origin and destiny, refuses flesh-judgment, and claims the two-witness rule of their Law: he and the Father who sent him. They ask where his Father is; he says they know neither him nor the Father. He speaks these words in the treasury; no one arrests him, because his hour has not yet come.
text: John 8:12–20 John After the bracketed pericope, John resumes the temple discourse of Tabernacles. Jesus names himself the light of the world and promises that whoever follows him will not walk in the darkness. Pharisees object that self-witness is invalid. He answers with origin and destiny, refuses flesh-judgment, and claims the two-witness rule of their Law: he and the Father who sent him. They ask where his Father is; he says they know neither him nor the Father. He speaks these words in the treasury; no one arrests him, because his hour has not yet come. Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.” John 8:12 The Pharisees therefore said to him, “You testify about yourself. Your testimony is not valid.” John 8:13 Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, for I know where I came from, and where I am going; but you don’t know where I came from, or where I am going. John 8:14 You judge according to the flesh. I judge no one. John 8:15 Even if I do judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone, but I am with the Father who sent me. John 8:16 It’s also written in your law that the testimony of two people is valid. John 8:17 I am one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.” John 8:18 They said therefore to him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered, “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.” John 8:19 Jesus spoke these words in the treasury, as he taught in the temple. Yet no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come. John 8:20

title: John 8:21–30
context: Still in the temple, Jesus says he is going away; they will seek him and die in their sin; where he goes they cannot come. They joke about suicide. He contrasts below and above, this world and not of this world, and warns that unless they believe that “I am he” they will die in their sins. They ask who he is. He speaks of the true Sender and of being lifted up as Son of Man—then they will know that I am he. The Father has not left him alone, for he always does what pleases him. As he says these things, many believed in him.
text: John 8:21–30 John Still in the temple, Jesus says he is going away; they will seek him and die in their sin; where he goes they cannot come. They joke about suicide. He contrasts below and above, this world and not of this world, and warns that unless they believe that “I am he” they will die in their sins. They ask who he is. He speaks of the true Sender and of being lifted up as Son of Man—then they will know that I am he. The Father has not left him alone, for he always does what pleases him. As he says these things, many believed in him. Jesus said therefore again to them, “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sins. Where I go, you can’t come.” John 8:21 The Jews therefore said, “Will he kill himself, because he says, ‘Where I am going, you can’t come’?” John 8:22 He said to them, “You are from beneath. I am from above. You are of this world. I am not of this world. John 8:23 I said therefore to you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.” John 8:24 They said therefore to him, “Who are you?” Jesus said to them, “Just what I have been saying to you from the beginning. John 8:25 I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you. However, he who sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these I say to the world.” John 8:26 They didn’t understand that he spoke to them about the Father.
