context: From the healed paralytic, Jesus passes to a tax booth and calls Matthew. Table fellowship with tax collectors and sinners draws Pharisaic objection; Jesus answers with the physician saying and Hosea’s word: He desires mercy, and He came to call sinners, not the self-assured “righteous.”
text: Matthew 9:9–13 Matthew From the healed paralytic, Jesus passes to a tax booth and calls Matthew. Table fellowship with tax collectors and sinners draws Pharisaic objection; Jesus answers with the physician saying and Hosea’s word: He desires mercy, and He came to call sinners, not the self-assured “righteous.” As Jesus passed by from there, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax collection office. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him. Matthew 9:9 As he sat in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with Jesus and his disciples. Matthew 9:10 When the Pharisees saw it, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” Matthew 9:11 When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do. Matthew 9:12 But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” Matthew 9:13

title: Psalm 1:1–6
context: Psalm 1 opens the Psalter as a gateway: the blessed person refuses the counsel, path, and seat of the wicked, delights in the LORD’s law day and night, and stands like a tree by streams—while the wicked are chaff that judgment will not spare, For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.
text: Psalm 1:1–6 Psalms Psalm 1 opens the Psalter as a gateway: the blessed person refuses the counsel, path, and seat of the wicked, delights in the LORD’s law day and night, and stands like a tree by streams—while the wicked are chaff that judgment will not spare, For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish. Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers; Psalms 1:1 but his delight is in the LORD’s law. On his law he meditates day and night. Psalms 1:2 He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper. Psalms 1:3 The wicked are not so, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away. Psalms 1:4 Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous. Psalms 1:5 For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish. Psalms 1:6

title: Psalm 10:1–18
context: Psalm 10 is a cry against the seeming distance of God while the arrogant wicked hotly pursue the poor. The wicked boast of desire, curse and renounce the LORD, refuse to seek him, and say in the heart that there is no God; their ways prosper, judgments feel far off, and they puff at foes while plotting ambush like a lion. They crush the helpless and claim God has forgotten and will never see. The psalm then turns: Arise, LORD—don’t forget the afflicted; you do see trouble and grief, the helpless commit themselves to you, and you have helped the fatherless; break the wicked man’s arm; the LORD is King forever; he hears the desire of the humble, strengthens their heart, and does justice so that earthly man may terrify no more.
text: Psalm 10:1–18 Psalms Psalm 10 is a cry against the seeming distance of God while the arrogant wicked hotly pursue the poor. The wicked boast of desire, curse and renounce the LORD, refuse to seek him, and say in the heart that there is no God; their ways prosper, judgments feel far off, and they puff at foes while plotting ambush like a lion. They crush the helpless and claim God has forgotten and will never see. The psalm then turns: Arise, LORD—don’t forget the afflicted; you do see trouble and grief, the helpless commit themselves to you, and you have helped the fatherless; break the wicked man’s arm; the LORD is King forever; he hears the desire of the humble, strengthens their heart, and does justice so that earthly man may terrify no more. Why do you stand far off, LORD? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble? Psalms 10:1 In arrogance, the wicked hunt down the weak. They are caught in the schemes that they devise. Psalms 10:2 For the wicked boasts of his heart’s cravings. He blesses the greedy and condemns the LORD. Psalms 10:3 The wicked, in the pride of his face, has no room in his thoughts for God. Psalms 10:4 His ways are prosperous at all times. He is arrogant, and your laws are far from his sight. As for all his adversaries, he sneers at them. Psalms 10:5 He says in his heart, “I shall not be shaken. For generations I shall have no trouble.” Psalms 10:6 His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and oppression. Under his tongue is mischief and iniquity. Psalms 10:7 He lies in wait near the villages. From ambushes, he murders the innocent. His eyes are secretly set against the helpless. Psalms 10:8 He lurks in secret as a lion in his ambush. He lies in wait to catch the helpless. He catches the helpless when he draws him in his net. Psalms 10:9 The helpless are crushed. They collapse. They fall under his strength. Psalms 10:10 He says in his heart, “God has forgotten. He hides his face. He will never see it.” Psalms 10:11 Arise, LORD! God, lift up your hand! Don’t forget the helpless. Psalms 10:12 Why does the wicked person condemn God, and say in his heart, “God won’t call me into account”? Psalms 10:13 But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into your hand. You help the victim and the fatherless. Psalms 10:14 Break the arm of the wicked. As for the evil man, seek out his wickedness until you find none. Psalms 10:15 The LORD is King forever and ever! The nations will perish out of his land. Psalms 10:16 LORD, you have heard the desire of the humble. You will prepare their heart. You will cause your ear to hear, Psalms 10:17 to judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that man who is of the earth may terrify no more. Psalms 10:18

title: Psalm 100:1–5
context: A brief psalm of thanksgiving. All the earth is called to serve the LORD with gladness and come before him singing, knowing that he is God, that he made us, and that we are his people and the sheep of his pasture. Worshipers are invited through his gates with thanks and praise, because the LORD is good, his loving kindness is everlasting, and his faithfulness lasts to all generations.
text: Psalm 100:1–5 Psalms A brief psalm of thanksgiving. All the earth is called to serve the LORD with gladness and come before him singing, knowing that he is God, that he made us, and that we are his people and the sheep of his pasture. Worshipers are invited through his gates with thanks and praise, because the LORD is good, his loving kindness is everlasting, and his faithfulness lasts to all generations. Shout for joy to the LORD, all you lands! Psalms 100:1 Serve the LORD with gladness. Come before his presence with singing. Psalms 100:2 Know that the LORD, he is God. It is he who has made us, and we are his. We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture. Psalms 100:3 Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise. Give thanks to him, and bless his name. Psalms 100:4 For the LORD is good. His loving kindness endures forever, his faithfulness to all generations. Psalms 100:5

title: Psalm 101:1–8
context: A Psalm of David, composed between the promise of the kingdom and his possession of it: he vows to sing of loving kindness and justice, walk with integrity in his house, refuse worthless and perverse company, destroy the secret slanderer and the arrogant, favor the faithful who walk blameless, shut deceit from his dwelling, and morning by morning cut off the wicked from the city of the LORD.
text: Psalm 101:1–8 Psalms A Psalm of David, composed between the promise of the kingdom and his possession of it: he vows to sing of loving kindness and justice, walk with integrity in his house, refuse worthless and perverse company, destroy the secret slanderer and the arrogant, favor the faithful who walk blameless, shut deceit from his dwelling, and morning by morning cut off the wicked from the city of the LORD. I will sing of loving kindness and justice. To you, LORD, I will sing praises. Psalms 101:1 I will be careful to live a blameless life. When will you come to me? I will walk within my house with a blameless heart. Psalms 101:2 I will set no vile thing before my eyes. I hate the deeds of faithless men. They will not cling to me. Psalms 101:3 A perverse heart will be far from me. I will have nothing to do with evil. Psalms 101:4 I will silence whoever secretly slanders his neighbor. I won’t tolerate one who is arrogant and conceited. Psalms 101:5 My eyes will be on the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me. He who walks in a perfect way, he will serve me. Psalms 101:6 He who practices deceit won’t dwell within my house. He who speaks falsehood won’t be established before my eyes. Psalms 101:7 Morning by morning, I will destroy all the wicked of the land, to cut off all the workers of iniquity from the LORD’s city. Psalms 101:8

title: Psalm 102:1–28
context: A prayer of one afflicted, when he is faint and pours out his complaint before the LORD: days like smoke, bones like a furnace, loneliness and taunts under God's indignation—then the turn to the LORD enthroned forever, the appointed time to pity Zion, nations fearing his glory, a record for A people which will be created, and the unchanging Creator whose years have no end, so that the children of his servants dwell secure. Verses 25–27 are applied to the Son in Hebrews 1.
text: Psalm 102:1–28 Psalms A prayer of one afflicted, when he is faint and pours out his complaint before the LORD: days like smoke, bones like a furnace, loneliness and taunts under God's indignation—then the turn to the LORD enthroned forever, the appointed time to pity Zion, nations fearing his glory, a record for A people which will be created, and the unchanging Creator whose years have no end, so that the children of his servants dwell secure. Verses 25–27 are applied to the Son in Hebrews 1. Hear my prayer, LORD! Let my cry come to you. Psalms 102:1 Don’t hide your face from me in the day of my distress. Turn your ear to me. Answer me quickly in the day when I call. Psalms 102:2 For my days consume away like smoke. My bones are burned as a torch. Psalms 102:3 My heart is blighted like grass, and withered, for I forget to eat my bread. Psalms 102:4 By reason of the voice of my groaning, my bones stick to my skin. Psalms 102:5 I am like a pelican of the wilderness. I have become as an owl of the waste places. Psalms 102:6 I watch, and have become like a sparrow that is alone on the housetop. Psalms 102:7 My enemies reproach me all day. Those who are mad at me use my name as a curse. Psalms 102:8 For I have eaten ashes like bread, and mixed my drink with tears, Psalms 102:9 because of your indignation and your wrath; for you have taken me up and thrown me away. Psalms 102:10 My days are like a long shadow. I have withered like grass. Psalms 102:11 But you, LORD, will remain forever; your renown endures to all generations. Psalms 102:12 You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for it is time to have pity on her. Yes, the set time has come. Psalms 102:13 For your servants take pleasure in her stones, and have pity on her dust. Psalms 102:14 So the nations will fear the LORD’s name, all the kings of the earth your glory. Psalms 102:15 For the LORD has built up Zion. He has appeared in his glory. Psalms 102:16 He has responded to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer. Psalms 102:17 This will be written for the generation to come. A people which will be created will praise the LORD, Psalms 102:18 for he has looked down from the height of his sanctuary. From heaven, the LORD saw the earth, Psalms 102:19 to hear the groans of the prisoner, to free those who are condemned to death, Psalms 102:20 that men may declare the LORD’s name in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem, Psalms 102:21 when the peoples are gathered together, the kingdoms, to serve the LORD. Psalms 102:22 He weakened my strength along the course. He shortened my days. Psalms 102:23 I said, “My God, don’t take me away in the middle of my days. Your years are throughout all generations. Psalms 102:24 Of old, you laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the work of your hands. Psalms 102:25 They will perish, but you will endure. Yes, all of them will wear out like a garment. You will change them like a cloak, and they will be changed. Psalms 102:26 But you are the same. Your years will have no end. Psalms 102:27 The children of your servants will continue. Their offspring will be established before you.” Psalms 102:28

title: Psalm 103:1–22
context: Of David: the soul is summoned to bless the LORD and forget none of his benefits—forgiveness, healing, redemption from the pit, crowning steadfast love, renewal like the eagle's—then mercy like a father's, sins removed as far as east from west, everlasting love on those who fear him and keep covenant, the throne established in the heavens, and all angels, hosts, and works called to join the soul's praise.
text: Psalm 103:1–22 Psalms Of David: the soul is summoned to bless the LORD and forget none of his benefits—forgiveness, healing, redemption from the pit, crowning steadfast love, renewal like the eagle's—then mercy like a father's, sins removed as far as east from west, everlasting love on those who fear him and keep covenant, the throne established in the heavens, and all angels, hosts, and works called to join the soul's praise. Praise the LORD, my soul! All that is within me, praise his holy name! Psalms 103:1 Praise the LORD, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits, Psalms 103:2 who forgives all your sins, who heals all your diseases, Psalms 103:3 who redeems your life from destruction, who crowns you with loving kindness and tender mercies, Psalms 103:4 who satisfies your desire with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s. Psalms 103:5 The LORD executes righteous acts, and justice for all who are oppressed. Psalms 103:6 He made known his ways to Moses, his deeds to the children of Israel. Psalms 103:7 The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness. Psalms 103:8 He will not always accuse; neither will he stay angry forever. Psalms 103:9 He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us for our iniquities. Psalms 103:10 For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his loving kindness toward those who fear him. Psalms 103:11 As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us. Psalms 103:12 Like a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him. Psalms 103:13 For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust. Psalms 103:14 As for man, his days are like grass. As a flower of the field, so he flourishes. Psalms 103:15 For the wind passes over it, and it is gone. Its place remembers it no more. Psalms 103:16 But the LORD’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children, Psalms 103:17 to those who keep his covenant, to those who remember to obey his precepts. Psalms 103:18 The LORD has established his throne in the heavens. His kingdom rules over all. Psalms 103:19 Praise the LORD, you angels of his, who are mighty in strength, who fulfill his word, obeying the voice of his word. Psalms 103:20 Praise the LORD, all you armies of his, you servants of his, who do his pleasure. Psalms 103:21 Praise the LORD, all you works of his, in all places of his dominion. Praise the LORD, my soul! Psalms 103:22

title: Psalm 104:1–35
context: The psalmist blesses the Lord for creation and providence: light and heavens, earth set on foundations, waters bounded, springs and beasts, sun and moon, sea and Leviathan, creatures waiting on God's open hand. He sends forth His Spirit and renews the ground; glory endures, and the soul answers with lifelong praise—and a plea that the wicked be no more.
text: Psalm 104:1–35 Psalms The psalmist blesses the Lord for creation and providence: light and heavens, earth set on foundations, waters bounded, springs and beasts, sun and moon, sea and Leviathan, creatures waiting on God's open hand. He sends forth His Spirit and renews the ground; glory endures, and the soul answers with lifelong praise—and a plea that the wicked be no more. Bless the LORD, my soul. The LORD, my God, you are very great. You are clothed with honor and majesty. Psalms 104:1 He covers himself with light as with a garment. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain. Psalms 104:2 He lays the beams of his rooms in the waters. He makes the clouds his chariot. He walks on the wings of the wind. Psalms 104:3 He makes his messengers winds, and his servants flames of fire. Psalms 104:4 He laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be moved forever. Psalms 104:5 You covered it with the deep as with a cloak. The waters stood above the mountains. Psalms 104:6 At your rebuke they fled. At the voice of your thunder they hurried away. Psalms 104:7 The mountains rose, the valleys sank down, to the place which you had assigned to them. Psalms 104:8 You have set a boundary that they may not pass over, that they don’t turn again to cover the earth. Psalms 104:9 He sends springs into the valleys. They run among the mountains. Psalms 104:10 They give drink to every animal of the field. The wild donkeys quench their thirst. Psalms 104:11 The birds of the sky nest by them. They sing among the branches. Psalms 104:12 He waters the mountains from his rooms. The earth is filled with the fruit of your works. Psalms 104:13 He causes the grass to grow for the livestock, and plants for man to cultivate, that he may produce food out of the earth: Psalms 104:14 wine that makes the heart of man glad, oil to make his face to shine, and bread that strengthens man’s heart. Psalms 104:15 The LORD’s trees are well watered, the cedars of Lebanon, which he has planted, Psalms 104:16 where the birds make their nests. The stork makes its home in the cypress trees. Psalms 104:17 The high mountains are for the wild goats. The rocks are a refuge for the rock badgers. Psalms 104:18 He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set. Psalms 104:19 You make darkness, and it is night, in which all the animals of the forest prowl. Psalms 104:20 The young lions roar after their prey, and seek their food from God. Psalms 104:21 The sun rises, and they steal away, and lie down in their dens. Psalms 104:22 Man goes out to his work, to his labor until the evening. Psalms 104:23 LORD, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches. Psalms 104:24 There is the sea, great and wide, in which are innumerable living things, both small and large animals. Psalms 104:25 There the ships go, and leviathan, whom you formed to play there. Psalms 104:26 These all wait for you, that you may give them their food in due season. Psalms 104:27 You give to them; they gather. You open your hand; they are satisfied with good. Psalms 104:28 You hide your face; they are troubled. You take away their breath; they die and return to the dust. Psalms 104:29 You send out your Spirit and they are created. You renew the face of the ground. Psalms 104:30 Let the LORD’s glory endure forever. Let the LORD rejoice in his works. Psalms 104:31 He looks at the earth, and it trembles. He touches the mountains, and they smoke. Psalms 104:32 I will sing to the LORD as long as I live. I will sing praise to my God while I have any being. Psalms 104:33 Let my meditation be sweet to him. I will rejoice in the LORD. Psalms 104:34 Let sinners be consumed out of the earth. Let the wicked be no more. Bless the LORD, my soul. Praise the LORD! Psalms 104:35

title: Psalm 105:1–45
context: Israel is called to thank the Lord and remember His wondrous works: the everlasting covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; protection of the patriarchs; Joseph sent ahead through famine and fetters; fruitfulness in Egypt; Moses and Aaron; the plagues; the exodus with silver and gold; cloud, quail, manna, and water from the rock—so the people might keep His statutes. Praise the Lord.
text: Psalm 105:1–45 Psalms Israel is called to thank the Lord and remember His wondrous works: the everlasting covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; protection of the patriarchs; Joseph sent ahead through famine and fetters; fruitfulness in Egypt; Moses and Aaron; the plagues; the exodus with silver and gold; cloud, quail, manna, and water from the rock—so the people might keep His statutes. Praise the Lord. Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name! Make his doings known among the peoples. Psalms 105:1 Sing to him, sing praises to him! Tell of all his marvelous works. Psalms 105:2 Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek the LORD rejoice. Psalms 105:3 Seek the LORD and his strength. Seek his face forever more. Psalms 105:4 Remember his marvelous works that he has done: his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth, Psalms 105:5 you offspring of Abraham, his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones. Psalms 105:6 He is the LORD, our God. His judgments are in all the earth. Psalms 105:7 He has remembered his covenant forever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations, Psalms 105:8 the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac, Psalms 105:9 and confirmed it to Jacob for a statute; to Israel for an everlasting covenant, Psalms 105:10 saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance,” Psalms 105:11 when they were but a few men in number, yes, very few, and foreigners in it. Psalms 105:12 They went about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people. Psalms 105:13 He allowed no one to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes, Psalms 105:14 “Don’t touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!” Psalms 105:15 He called for a famine on the land. He destroyed the food supplies. Psalms 105:16 He sent a man before them. Joseph was sold for a slave. Psalms 105:17 They bruised his feet with shackles. His neck was locked in irons, Psalms 105:18 until the time that his word happened, and the LORD’s word proved him true. Psalms 105:19 The king sent and freed him, even the ruler of peoples, and let him go free. Psalms 105:20 He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all of his possessions, Psalms 105:21 to discipline his princes at his pleasure, and to teach his elders wisdom. Psalms 105:22 Israel also came into Egypt. Jacob lived in the land of Ham. Psalms 105:23 He increased his people greatly, and made them stronger than their adversaries. Psalms 105:24 He turned their heart to hate his people, to conspire against his servants. Psalms 105:25 He sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen. Psalms 105:26 They performed miracles among them, and wonders in the land of Ham. Psalms 105:27 He sent darkness, and made it dark. They didn’t rebel against his words. Psalms 105:28 He turned their waters into blood, and killed their fish. Psalms 105:29 Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the rooms of their kings. Psalms 105:30 He spoke, and swarms of flies came, and lice in all their borders. Psalms 105:31 He gave them hail for rain, with lightning in their land. Psalms 105:32 He struck their vines and also their fig trees, and shattered the trees of their country. Psalms 105:33 He spoke, and the locusts came with the grasshoppers, without number. Psalms 105:34 They ate up every plant in their land, and ate up the fruit of their ground. Psalms 105:35 He struck also all the firstborn in their land, the first fruits of all their manhood. Psalms 105:36 He brought them out with silver and gold. There was not one feeble person among his tribes. Psalms 105:37 Egypt was glad when they departed, for the fear of them had fallen on them. Psalms 105:38 He spread a cloud for a covering, fire to give light in the night. Psalms 105:39 They asked, and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the bread of the sky. Psalms 105:40 He opened the rock, and waters gushed out. They ran as a river in the dry places. Psalms 105:41 For he remembered his holy word, and Abraham, his servant. Psalms 105:42 He brought his people out with joy, his chosen with singing. Psalms 105:43 He gave them the lands of the nations. They took the labor of the peoples in possession, Psalms 105:44 that they might keep his statutes, and observe his laws. Praise the LORD! Psalms 105:45

title: Psalm 106:1–48
context: Israel is called to praise the Lord for His goodness and everlasting steadfast love, then confesses: we and our fathers have sinned—forgetting wonders at the Red Sea, craving in the wilderness, envying Moses and Aaron, the calf at Horeb, despising the pleasant land, Baal of Peor, Meribah, and mixing with the nations—yet God saved for His name's sake, heard their cry, remembered His covenant, and is asked to gather them from the nations for thanks and praise. Amen; Praise the Lord.
text: Psalm 106:1–48 Psalms Israel is called to praise the Lord for His goodness and everlasting steadfast love, then confesses: we and our fathers have sinned—forgetting wonders at the Red Sea, craving in the wilderness, envying Moses and Aaron, the calf at Horeb, despising the pleasant land, Baal of Peor, Meribah, and mixing with the nations—yet God saved for His name's sake, heard their cry, remembered His covenant, and is asked to gather them from the nations for thanks and praise. Amen; Praise the Lord. Praise the LORD! Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 106:1 Who can utter the mighty acts of the LORD, or fully declare all his praise? Psalms 106:2 Blessed are those who keep justice. Blessed is one who does what is right at all times. Psalms 106:3 Remember me, LORD, with the favor that you show to your people. Visit me with your salvation, Psalms 106:4 that I may see the prosperity of your chosen, that I may rejoice in the gladness of your nation, that I may glory with your inheritance. Psalms 106:5 We have sinned with our fathers. We have committed iniquity. We have done wickedly. Psalms 106:6 Our fathers didn’t understand your wonders in Egypt. They didn’t remember the multitude of your loving kindnesses, but were rebellious at the sea, even at the Red Sea. Psalms 106:7 Nevertheless he saved them for his name’s sake, that he might make his mighty power known. Psalms 106:8 He rebuked the Red Sea also, and it was dried up; so he led them through the depths, as through a desert. Psalms 106:9 He saved them from the hand of him who hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy. Psalms 106:10 The waters covered their adversaries. There was not one of them left. Psalms 106:11 Then they believed his words. They sang his praise. Psalms 106:12 They soon forgot his works. They didn’t wait for his counsel, Psalms 106:13 but gave in to craving in the desert, and tested God in the wasteland. Psalms 106:14 He gave them their request, but sent leanness into their soul. Psalms 106:15 They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron, the LORD’s saint. Psalms 106:16 The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram. Psalms 106:17 A fire was kindled in their company. The flame burned up the wicked. Psalms 106:18 They made a calf in Horeb, and worshiped a molten image. Psalms 106:19 Thus they exchanged their glory for an image of a bull that eats grass. Psalms 106:20 They forgot God, their Savior, who had done great things in Egypt, Psalms 106:21 wondrous works in the land of Ham, and awesome things by the Red Sea. Psalms 106:22 Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had Moses, his chosen, not stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, so that he wouldn’t destroy them. Psalms 106:23 Yes, they despised the pleasant land. They didn’t believe his word, Psalms 106:24 but murmured in their tents, and didn’t listen to the LORD’s voice. Psalms 106:25 Therefore he swore to them that he would overthrow them in the wilderness, Psalms 106:26 that he would overthrow their offspring among the nations, and scatter them in the lands. Psalms 106:27 They joined themselves also to Baal Peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead. Psalms 106:28 Thus they provoked him to anger with their deeds. The plague broke in on them. Psalms 106:29 Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, so the plague was stopped. Psalms 106:30 That was credited to him for righteousness, for all generations to come. Psalms 106:31 They angered him also at the waters of Meribah, so that Moses was troubled for their sakes; Psalms 106:32 because they were rebellious against his spirit, he spoke rashly with his lips. Psalms 106:33 They didn’t destroy the peoples, as the LORD commanded them, Psalms 106:34 but mixed themselves with the nations, and learned their works. Psalms 106:35 They served their idols, which became a snare to them. Psalms 106:36 Yes, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons. Psalms 106:37 They shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan. The land was polluted with blood. Psalms 106:38 Thus they were defiled with their works, and prostituted themselves in their deeds. Psalms 106:39 Therefore the LORD burned with anger against his people. He abhorred his inheritance. Psalms 106:40 He gave them into the hand of the nations. Those who hated them ruled over them. Psalms 106:41 Their enemies also oppressed them. They were brought into subjection under their hand. Psalms 106:42 He rescued them many times, but they were rebellious in their counsel, and were brought low in their iniquity. Psalms 106:43 Nevertheless he regarded their distress, when he heard their cry. Psalms 106:44 He remembered for them his covenant, and repented according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses. Psalms 106:45 He made them also to be pitied by all those who carried them captive. Psalms 106:46 Save us, LORD, our God, gather us from among the nations, to give thanks to your holy name, to triumph in your praise! Psalms 106:47 Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting! Let all the people say, “Amen.” Praise the LORD! Psalms 106:48

title: Psalm 107:1–43
context: The redeemed are called to give thanks for the Lord's goodness and everlasting steadfast love: wanderers in desert wastes cry and are led to a city; prisoners in darkness who rebelled are freed as bronze doors shatter; fools sick from sin are healed by His sent word; sailors at their wits' end see the storm stilled and reach their haven—each group urged to thank Him for steadfast love and wondrous works. He turns rivers to desert for the evil of inhabitants and deserts to pools for the hungry; He brings princes low and raises the needy; the upright rejoice, wickedness is silenced, and the wise consider His steadfast love.
text: Psalm 107:1–43 Psalms The redeemed are called to give thanks for the Lord's goodness and everlasting steadfast love: wanderers in desert wastes cry and are led to a city; prisoners in darkness who rebelled are freed as bronze doors shatter; fools sick from sin are healed by His sent word; sailors at their wits' end see the storm stilled and reach their haven—each group urged to thank Him for steadfast love and wondrous works. He turns rivers to desert for the evil of inhabitants and deserts to pools for the hungry; He brings princes low and raises the needy; the upright rejoice, wickedness is silenced, and the wise consider His steadfast love. Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 107:1 Let the redeemed by the LORD say so, whom he has redeemed from the hand of the adversary, Psalms 107:2 and gathered out of the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south. Psalms 107:3 They wandered in the wilderness in a desert way. They found no city to live in. Psalms 107:4 Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them. Psalms 107:5 Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses. Psalms 107:6 He led them also by a straight way, that they might go to a city to live in. Psalms 107:7 Let them praise the LORD for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds to the children of men! Psalms 107:8 For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good. Psalms 107:9 Some sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron, Psalms 107:10 because they rebelled against the words of God, and condemned the counsel of the Most High. Psalms 107:11 Therefore he brought down their heart with labor. They fell down, and there was no one to help. Psalms 107:12 Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them out of their distresses. Psalms 107:13 He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and broke away their chains. Psalms 107:14 Let them praise the LORD for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds to the children of men! Psalms 107:15 For he has broken the gates of bronze, and cut through bars of iron. Psalms 107:16 Fools are afflicted because of their disobedience, and because of their iniquities. Psalms 107:17 Their soul abhors all kinds of food. They draw near to the gates of death. Psalms 107:18 Then they cry to the LORD in their trouble, and he saves them out of their distresses. Psalms 107:19 He sends his word, and heals them, and delivers them from their graves. Psalms 107:20 Let them praise the LORD for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds to the children of men! Psalms 107:21 Let them offer the sacrifices of thanksgiving, and declare his deeds with singing. Psalms 107:22 Those who go down to the sea in ships, who do business in great waters, Psalms 107:23 these see the LORD’s deeds, and his wonders in the deep. Psalms 107:24 For he commands, and raises the stormy wind, which lifts up its waves. Psalms 107:25 They mount up to the sky; they go down again to the depths. Their soul melts away because of trouble. Psalms 107:26 They reel back and forth, and stagger like a drunken man, and are at their wits’ end. Psalms 107:27 Then they cry to the LORD in their trouble, and he brings them out of their distress. Psalms 107:28 He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still. Psalms 107:29 Then they are glad because it is calm, so he brings them to their desired haven. Psalms 107:30 Let them praise the LORD for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds for the children of men! Psalms 107:31 Let them exalt him also in the assembly of the people, and praise him in the seat of the elders. Psalms 107:32 He turns rivers into a desert, water springs into a thirsty ground, Psalms 107:33 and a fruitful land into a salt waste, for the wickedness of those who dwell in it. Psalms 107:34 He turns a desert into a pool of water, and a dry land into water springs. Psalms 107:35 There he makes the hungry live, that they may prepare a city to live in, Psalms 107:36 sow fields, plant vineyards, and reap the fruits of increase. Psalms 107:37 He blesses them also, so that they are multiplied greatly. He doesn’t allow their livestock to decrease. Psalms 107:38 Again, they are diminished and bowed down through oppression, trouble, and sorrow. Psalms 107:39 He pours contempt on princes, and causes them to wander in a trackless waste. Psalms 107:40 Yet he lifts the needy out of their affliction, and increases their families like a flock. Psalms 107:41 The upright will see it, and be glad. All the wicked will shut their mouths. Psalms 107:42 Whoever is wise will pay attention to these things. They will consider the loving kindnesses of the LORD. Psalms 107:43

title: Psalm 108:1–13
context: A Song. A Psalm of David. The psalmist’s heart is steadfast for praise with all his being; he wakes harp and lyre and the dawn; gives thanks among the peoples and nations because God’s loving kindness is great above the heavens and faithfulness reaches the clouds; asks God to be exalted and to deliver the beloved by His right hand; recalls God’s holy promise over Shechem, Succoth, Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah, Moab, Edom, and Philistia; asks who will lead him to the fortified city and Edom; confesses that human help is vain and that with God His people shall do valiantly, for He will tread down their foes.
text: Psalm 108:1–13 Psalms A Song. A Psalm of David. The psalmist’s heart is steadfast for praise with all his being; he wakes harp and lyre and the dawn; gives thanks among the peoples and nations because God’s loving kindness is great above the heavens and faithfulness reaches the clouds; asks God to be exalted and to deliver the beloved by His right hand; recalls God’s holy promise over Shechem, Succoth, Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah, Moab, Edom, and Philistia; asks who will lead him to the fortified city and Edom; confesses that human help is vain and that with God His people shall do valiantly, for He will tread down their foes. My heart is steadfast, God. I will sing and I will make music with my soul. Psalms 108:1 Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake up the dawn. Psalms 108:2 I will give thanks to you, LORD, among the nations. I will sing praises to you among the peoples. Psalms 108:3 For your loving kindness is great above the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies. Psalms 108:4 Be exalted, God, above the heavens! Let your glory be over all the earth. Psalms 108:5 That your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand, and answer us. Psalms 108:6 God has spoken from his sanctuary: “In triumph, I will divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth. Psalms 108:7 Gilead is mine. Manasseh is mine. Ephraim also is my helmet. Judah is my scepter. Psalms 108:8 Moab is my wash pot. I will toss my sandal on Edom. I will shout over Philistia.” Psalms 108:9 Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom? Psalms 108:10 Haven’t you rejected us, God? You don’t go out, God, with our armies. Psalms 108:11 Give us help against the enemy, for the help of man is vain. Psalms 108:12 Through God, we will do valiantly, for it is he who will tread down our enemies. Psalms 108:13

title: Psalm 109:1–31
context: A psalm of David. In this imprecatory lament, David asks the God of his praise not to stay silent while lying mouths and groundless hatred repay his love with accusation. He gives himself to prayer and then asks for justice in kind against a cruel accuser who would not show kindness and loved to curse. He turns to ask God to act for his name’s sake and his loving kindness, confesses his poverty and the scorn he bears, and ends in thanks, because God stands beside the needy to save him from those who condemn him.
text: Psalm 109:1–31 Psalms A psalm of David. In this imprecatory lament, David asks the God of his praise not to stay silent while lying mouths and groundless hatred repay his love with accusation. He gives himself to prayer and then asks for justice in kind against a cruel accuser who would not show kindness and loved to curse. He turns to ask God to act for his name’s sake and his loving kindness, confesses his poverty and the scorn he bears, and ends in thanks, because God stands beside the needy to save him from those who condemn him. God of my praise, don’t remain silent, Psalms 109:1 for they have opened the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of deceit against me. They have spoken to me with a lying tongue. Psalms 109:2 They have also surrounded me with words of hatred, and fought against me without a cause. Psalms 109:3 In return for my love, they are my adversaries; but I am in prayer. Psalms 109:4 They have rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my love. Psalms 109:5 Set a wicked man over him. Let an adversary stand at his right hand. Psalms 109:6 When he is judged, let him come out guilty. Let his prayer be turned into sin. Psalms 109:7 Let his days be few. Let another take his office. Psalms 109:8 Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow. Psalms 109:9 Let his children be wandering beggars. Let them be sought from their ruins. Psalms 109:10 Let the creditor seize all that he has. Let strangers plunder the fruit of his labor. Psalms 109:11 Let there be no one to extend kindness to him, neither let there be anyone to have pity on his fatherless children. Psalms 109:12 Let his posterity be cut off. In the generation following let their name be blotted out. Psalms 109:13 Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered by the LORD. Don’t let the sin of his mother be blotted out. Psalms 109:14 Let them be before the LORD continually, that he may cut off their memory from the earth; Psalms 109:15 because he didn’t remember to show kindness, but persecuted the poor and needy man, the broken in heart, to kill them. Psalms 109:16 Yes, he loved cursing, and it came to him. He didn’t delight in blessing, and it was far from him. Psalms 109:17 He clothed himself also with cursing as with his garment. It came into his inward parts like water, like oil into his bones. Psalms 109:18 Let it be to him as the clothing with which he covers himself, for the belt that is always around him. Psalms 109:19 This is the reward of my adversaries from the LORD, of those who speak evil against my soul. Psalms 109:20 But deal with me, GOD the Lord, for your name’s sake, because your loving kindness is good, deliver me; Psalms 109:21 for I am poor and needy. My heart is wounded within me. Psalms 109:22 I fade away like an evening shadow. I am shaken off like a locust. Psalms 109:23 My knees are weak through fasting. My body is thin and lacks fat. Psalms 109:24 I have also become a reproach to them. When they see me, they shake their head. Psalms 109:25 Help me, LORD, my God. Save me according to your loving kindness; Psalms 109:26 that they may know that this is your hand; that you, LORD, have done it. Psalms 109:27 They may curse, but you bless. When they arise, they will be shamed, but your servant shall rejoice. Psalms 109:28 Let my adversaries be clothed with dishonor. Let them cover themselves with their own shame as with a robe. Psalms 109:29 I will give great thanks to the LORD with my mouth. Yes, I will praise him among the multitude. Psalms 109:30 For he will stand at the right hand of the needy, to save him from those who judge his soul. Psalms 109:31

title: Psalm 11:1–7
context: David is advised to run for the hills while the wicked aim their arrows in the dark. He refuses: the LORD is in his temple and on his heavenly throne, watching and testing everyone. The psalm answers panic with the character of God, who judges the wicked and whose face the upright will see.
text: Psalm 11:1–7 Psalms David is advised to run for the hills while the wicked aim their arrows in the dark. He refuses: the LORD is in his temple and on his heavenly throne, watching and testing everyone. The psalm answers panic with the character of God, who judges the wicked and whose face the upright will see. In the LORD, I take refuge. How can you say to my soul, “Flee as a bird to your mountain”? Psalms 11:1 For, behold, the wicked bend their bows. They set their arrows on the strings, that they may shoot in darkness at the upright in heart. Psalms 11:2 If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do? Psalms 11:3 The LORD is in his holy temple. The LORD is on his throne in heaven. His eyes observe. His eyes examine the children of men. Psalms 11:4 The LORD examines the righteous, but his soul hates the wicked and him who loves violence. Psalms 11:5 On the wicked he will rain blazing coals; fire, sulfur, and scorching wind shall be the portion of their cup. Psalms 11:6 For the LORD is righteous. He loves righteousness. The upright shall see his face. Psalms 11:7

title: Psalm 110:1–7
context: A Psalm of David. The LORD says to David’s Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool; from Zion He sends the mighty scepter to rule amid enemies; a willing people offer themselves in holy garments on the day of power; the LORD swears without changing His mind that this Lord is a priest forever after Melchizedek’s order; the Lord at the right hand shatters kings in the day of wrath, judges the nations, and, drinking of the brook on the way, lifts up His head. Historic Arminian and Reformed confession agrees here on the Messiah’s session, priesthood, and victory.
text: Psalm 110:1–7 Psalms A Psalm of David. The LORD says to David’s Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool; from Zion He sends the mighty scepter to rule amid enemies; a willing people offer themselves in holy garments on the day of power; the LORD swears without changing His mind that this Lord is a priest forever after Melchizedek’s order; the Lord at the right hand shatters kings in the day of wrath, judges the nations, and, drinking of the brook on the way, lifts up His head. Historic Arminian and Reformed confession agrees here on the Messiah’s session, priesthood, and victory. The LORD says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.” Psalms 110:1 The LORD will send out the rod of your strength out of Zion. Rule among your enemies. Psalms 110:2 Your people offer themselves willingly in the day of your power, in holy array. Out of the womb of the morning, you have the dew of your youth. Psalms 110:3 The LORD has sworn, and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.” Psalms 110:4 The Lord is at your right hand. He will crush kings in the day of his wrath. Psalms 110:5 He will judge among the nations. He will heap up dead bodies. He will crush the ruler of the whole earth. Psalms 110:6 He will drink of the brook on the way; therefore he will lift up his head. Psalms 110:7

title: Psalm 111:1–10
context: An alphabetic hymn of praise: the psalmist gives thanks with the whole heart among the upright; celebrates the LORD’s great works studied by those who delight in them; names splendor, enduring righteousness, remembered wonders, grace and mercy; food to those who fear him and everlasting covenant memory; power shown in giving the nations’ inheritance; faithful and just works and trustworthy precepts established forever; redemption sent and covenant commanded forever; holy and awesome Name; the fear of the LORD as wisdom’s beginning, good understanding for those who practice it, and praise that endures forever.
text: Psalm 111:1–10 Psalms An alphabetic hymn of praise: the psalmist gives thanks with the whole heart among the upright; celebrates the LORD’s great works studied by those who delight in them; names splendor, enduring righteousness, remembered wonders, grace and mercy; food to those who fear him and everlasting covenant memory; power shown in giving the nations’ inheritance; faithful and just works and trustworthy precepts established forever; redemption sent and covenant commanded forever; holy and awesome Name; the fear of the LORD as wisdom’s beginning, good understanding for those who practice it, and praise that endures forever. Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart, in the council of the upright, and in the congregation. Psalms 111:1 The LORD’s works are great, pondered by all those who delight in them. Psalms 111:2 His work is honor and majesty. His righteousness endures forever. Psalms 111:3 He has caused his wonderful works to be remembered. The LORD is gracious and merciful. Psalms 111:4 He has given food to those who fear him. He always remembers his covenant. Psalms 111:5 He has shown his people the power of his works, in giving them the heritage of the nations. Psalms 111:6 The works of his hands are truth and justice. All his precepts are sure. Psalms 111:7 They are established forever and ever. They are done in truth and uprightness. Psalms 111:8 He has sent redemption to his people. He has ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awesome! Psalms 111:9 The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom. All those who do his work have a good understanding. His praise endures forever! Psalms 111:10

title: Psalm 112:1–10
context: An alphabetic twin to Psalm 111 turning from God’s works to the blessed fearer: the man who fears the LORD and greatly delights in His commandments is blessed; his offspring mighty, the upright’s generation blessed; wealth with enduring righteousness; light in darkness; generosity and just affairs; never moved, forever remembered; unafraid of bad news, heart firm in trust; steady until he looks on adversaries; free distribution to the poor with enduring righteousness and exalted horn; while the wicked sees, angers, gnashes, melts, and finds his desire perish.
text: Psalm 112:1–10 Psalms An alphabetic twin to Psalm 111 turning from God’s works to the blessed fearer: the man who fears the LORD and greatly delights in His commandments is blessed; his offspring mighty, the upright’s generation blessed; wealth with enduring righteousness; light in darkness; generosity and just affairs; never moved, forever remembered; unafraid of bad news, heart firm in trust; steady until he looks on adversaries; free distribution to the poor with enduring righteousness and exalted horn; while the wicked sees, angers, gnashes, melts, and finds his desire perish. Praise the LORD! Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who delights greatly in his commandments. Psalms 112:1 His offspring will be mighty in the land. The generation of the upright will be blessed. Psalms 112:2 Wealth and riches are in his house. His righteousness endures forever. Psalms 112:3 Light dawns in the darkness for the upright, gracious, merciful, and righteous. Psalms 112:4 It is well with the man who deals graciously and lends. He will maintain his cause in judgment. Psalms 112:5 For he will never be shaken. The righteous will be remembered forever. Psalms 112:6 He will not be afraid of evil news. His heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD. Psalms 112:7 His heart is established. He will not be afraid in the end when he sees his adversaries. Psalms 112:8 He has dispersed, he has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever. His horn will be exalted with honor. Psalms 112:9 The wicked will see it, and be grieved. He shall gnash with his teeth, and melt away. The desire of the wicked will perish. Psalms 112:10

title: Psalm 113:1–9
context: Egyptian Hallel opens: servants are summoned to praise the Lord's name from sunrise to sunset and forever. He is high above the nations, yet looks far down; He raises the poor from dust and ash heap to sit with princes, and settles the barren woman in her home as a home as joyous mother. The first Hallelujah frames condescension and mercy together.
text: Psalm 113:1–9 Psalms Egyptian Hallel opens: servants are summoned to praise the Lord's name from sunrise to sunset and forever. He is high above the nations, yet looks far down; He raises the poor from dust and ash heap to sit with princes, and settles the barren woman in her home as a home as joyous mother. The first Hallelujah frames condescension and mercy together. Praise the LORD! Praise, you servants of the LORD, praise the LORD’s name. Psalms 113:1 Blessed be the LORD’s name, from this time forward and forever more. Psalms 113:2 From the rising of the sun to its going down, the LORD’s name is to be praised. Psalms 113:3 The LORD is high above all nations, his glory above the heavens. Psalms 113:4 Who is like the LORD, our God, who has his seat on high, Psalms 113:5 who stoops down to see in heaven and on the earth? Psalms 113:6 He raises up the poor out of the dust, and lifts up the needy from the ash heap, Psalms 113:7 that he may set him with princes, even with the princes of his people. Psalms 113:8 He settles the barren woman in her home as a joyful mother of children. Praise the LORD! Psalms 113:9

title: Psalm 114:1–8
context: Egyptian Hallel continues: Israel goes out from Egypt and a strange tongue; Judah becomes the Lord's sanctuary and Israel His dominion. Sea and Jordan flee, mountains skip, and the earth is summoned to tremble at the presence of the God of Jacob, who turned rock and flint into water.
text: Psalm 114:1–8 Psalms Egyptian Hallel continues: Israel goes out from Egypt and a strange tongue; Judah becomes the Lord's sanctuary and Israel His dominion. Sea and Jordan flee, mountains skip, and the earth is summoned to tremble at the presence of the God of Jacob, who turned rock and flint into water. When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign language, Psalms 114:1 Judah became his sanctuary, Israel his dominion. Psalms 114:2 The sea saw it, and fled. The Jordan was driven back. Psalms 114:3 The mountains skipped like rams, the little hills like lambs. Psalms 114:4 What was it, you sea, that you fled? You Jordan, that you turned back? Psalms 114:5 You mountains, that you skipped like rams? You little hills, like lambs? Psalms 114:6 Tremble, you earth, at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob, Psalms 114:7 who turned the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a spring of waters. Psalms 114:8

title: Psalm 115:1–18
context: Egyptian Hallel: glory is denied to us and given to the Lord's name for steadfast love and faithfulness. Nations mock, "Where is their God?"—but our God is in the heavens and does all He pleases, while idols of silver and gold are mute and deadening. Israel, Aaron, and all who fear the Lord are called to trust Him as help and shield; He remembers and blesses small and great. The living bless the Lord forever; the dead don’t praise Him.
text: Psalm 115:1–18 Psalms Egyptian Hallel: glory is denied to us and given to the Lord's name for steadfast love and faithfulness. Nations mock, "Where is their God?"—but our God is in the heavens and does all He pleases, while idols of silver and gold are mute and deadening. Israel, Aaron, and all who fear the Lord are called to trust Him as help and shield; He remembers and blesses small and great. The living bless the Lord forever; the dead don’t praise Him. Not to us, LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, for your loving kindness, and for your truth’s sake. Psalms 115:1 Why should the nations say, “Where is their God, now?” Psalms 115:2 But our God is in the heavens. He does whatever he pleases. Psalms 115:3 Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands. Psalms 115:4 They have mouths, but they don’t speak. They have eyes, but they don’t see. Psalms 115:5 They have ears, but they don’t hear. They have noses, but they don’t smell. Psalms 115:6 They have hands, but they don’t feel. They have feet, but they don’t walk, neither do they speak through their throat. Psalms 115:7 Those who make them will be like them; yes, everyone who trusts in them. Psalms 115:8 Israel, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield. Psalms 115:9 House of Aaron, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield. Psalms 115:10 You who fear the LORD, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield. Psalms 115:11 The LORD remembers us. He will bless us. He will bless the house of Israel. He will bless the house of Aaron. Psalms 115:12 He will bless those who fear the LORD, both small and great. Psalms 115:13 May the LORD increase you more and more, you and your children. Psalms 115:14 Blessed are you by the LORD, who made heaven and earth. Psalms 115:15 The heavens are the LORD’s heavens, but he has given the earth to the children of men. Psalms 115:16 The dead don’t praise the LORD, nor any who go down into silence, Psalms 115:17 but we will bless the LORD, from this time forward and forever more. Praise the LORD! Psalms 115:18

title: Psalm 116:1–19
context: Egyptian Hallel thanksgiving: love for the Lord because He heard pleas for mercy; death's snares and Sheol's pangs drive a cry for deliverance. The Lord is gracious, righteous, merciful; He preserves the simple and deals bountifully. Delivered from death, tears, and stumbling, the psalmist walks before the Lord, renders the cup of salvation, pays vows among the people, confesses that precious in the Lord's sight is the death of His saints, and offers thanksgiving in Jerusalem's courts.
text: Psalm 116:1–19 Psalms Egyptian Hallel thanksgiving: love for the Lord because He heard pleas for mercy; death's snares and Sheol's pangs drive a cry for deliverance. The Lord is gracious, righteous, merciful; He preserves the simple and deals bountifully. Delivered from death, tears, and stumbling, the psalmist walks before the Lord, renders the cup of salvation, pays vows among the people, confesses that precious in the Lord's sight is the death of His saints, and offers thanksgiving in Jerusalem's courts. I love the LORD, because he listens to my voice, and my cries for mercy. Psalms 116:1 Because he has turned his ear to me, therefore I will call on him as long as I live. Psalms 116:2 The cords of death surrounded me, the pains of Sheol got a hold of me. I found trouble and sorrow. Psalms 116:3 Then I called on the LORD’s name: “LORD, I beg you, deliver my soul.” Psalms 116:4 The LORD is gracious and righteous. Yes, our God is merciful. Psalms 116:5 The LORD preserves the simple. I was brought low, and he saved me. Psalms 116:6 Return to your rest, my soul, for the LORD has dealt bountifully with you. Psalms 116:7 For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling. Psalms 116:8 I will walk before the LORD in the land of the living. Psalms 116:9 I believed, therefore I said, “I was greatly afflicted.” Psalms 116:10 I said in my haste, “All people are liars.” Psalms 116:11 What will I give to the LORD for all his benefits toward me? Psalms 116:12 I will take the cup of salvation, and call on the LORD’s name. Psalms 116:13 I will pay my vows to the LORD, yes, in the presence of all his people. Psalms 116:14 Precious in the LORD’s sight is the death of his saints. Psalms 116:15 LORD, truly I am your servant. I am your servant, the son of your servant girl. You have freed me from my chains. Psalms 116:16 I will offer to you the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call on the LORD’s name. Psalms 116:17 I will pay my vows to the LORD, yes, in the presence of all his people, Psalms 116:18 in the courts of the LORD’s house, in the middle of you, Jerusalem. Praise the LORD! Psalms 116:19

title: Psalm 117:1–2
context: Shortest psalm in the Egyptian Hallel: all nations and peoples are summoned to praise and extol the Lord, because His steadfast love toward us is great and His faithfulness endures forever. Paul cites this wideness in Romans 15 for Gentile praise beside Jewish mercy.
text: Psalm 117:1–2 Psalms Shortest psalm in the Egyptian Hallel: all nations and peoples are summoned to praise and extol the Lord, because His steadfast love toward us is great and His faithfulness endures forever. Paul cites this wideness in Romans 15 for Gentile praise beside Jewish mercy. Praise the LORD, all you nations! Extol him, all you peoples! Psalms 117:1 For his loving kindness is great toward us. The LORD’s faithfulness endures forever. Praise the LORD! Psalms 117:2

title: Psalm 118:1–29
context: Egyptian Hallel climax: thanksgiving for the Lord's goodness and forever steadfast love, confessed by Israel, Aaron, and all who fear Him. Distress yields to answered freedom; refuge in the Lord outranks trust in man or princes; nations surround, yet the Name cuts off. The Lord is strength, song, and salvation; severe discipline does not end in death. Gates of righteousness open; the stone the builders rejected becomes the cornerstone—the Lord's marvelous doing—and hosanna welcomes the one who comes in the Lord's name.
text: Psalm 118:1–29 Psalms Egyptian Hallel climax: thanksgiving for the Lord's goodness and forever steadfast love, confessed by Israel, Aaron, and all who fear Him. Distress yields to answered freedom; refuge in the Lord outranks trust in man or princes; nations surround, yet the Name cuts off. The Lord is strength, song, and salvation; severe discipline does not end in death. Gates of righteousness open; the stone the builders rejected becomes the cornerstone—the Lord's marvelous doing—and hosanna welcomes the one who comes in the Lord's name. Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 118:1 Let Israel now say that his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 118:2 Let the house of Aaron now say that his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 118:3 Now let those who fear the LORD say that his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 118:4 Out of my distress, I called on the LORD. The LORD answered me with freedom. Psalms 118:5 The LORD is on my side. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me? Psalms 118:6 The LORD is on my side among those who help me. Therefore I will look in triumph at those who hate me. Psalms 118:7 It is better to take refuge in the LORD, than to put confidence in man. Psalms 118:8 It is better to take refuge in the LORD, than to put confidence in princes. Psalms 118:9 All the nations surrounded me, but in the LORD’s name I cut them off. Psalms 118:10 They surrounded me, yes, they surrounded me. In the LORD’s name I indeed cut them off. Psalms 118:11 They surrounded me like bees. They are quenched like the burning thorns. In the LORD’s name I cut them off. Psalms 118:12 You pushed me back hard, to make me fall, but the LORD helped me. Psalms 118:13 The LORD is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. Psalms 118:14 The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous. “The right hand of the LORD does valiantly. Psalms 118:15 The right hand of the LORD is exalted! The right hand of the LORD does valiantly!” Psalms 118:16 I will not die, but live, and declare the LORD’s works. Psalms 118:17 The LORD has punished me severely, but he has not given me over to death. Psalms 118:18 Open to me the gates of righteousness. I will enter into them. I will give thanks to the LORD. Psalms 118:19 This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous will enter into it. Psalms 118:20 I will give thanks to you, for you have answered me, and have become my salvation. Psalms 118:21 The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. Psalms 118:22 This is the LORD’s doing. It is marvelous in our eyes. Psalms 118:23 This is the day that the LORD has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it! Psalms 118:24 Save us now, we beg you, LORD! LORD, we beg you, send prosperity now. Psalms 118:25 Blessed is he who comes in the LORD’s name! We have blessed you out of the LORD’s house. Psalms 118:26 The LORD is God, and he has given us light. Bind the sacrifice with cords, even to the horns of the altar. Psalms 118:27 You are my God, and I will give thanks to you. You are my God, I will exalt you. Psalms 118:28 Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 118:29

title: Psalm 119:1–8
context: Psalm 119 opens with the Aleph stanza: an eight-verse acrostic blessing on those whose ways are blameless and who walk in the Lord’s law. The singer moves from beatitude to petition—longing that his own ways were steadfast to obey God’s statutes—and ends with a vow to keep them joined to a plea not to be utterly forsaken. Both camps hear Scripture’s call to wholehearted obedience and delight; they differ on how such a walk is given and sustained.
text: Psalm 119:1–8 Psalms Psalm 119 opens with the Aleph stanza: an eight-verse acrostic blessing on those whose ways are blameless and who walk in the Lord’s law. The singer moves from beatitude to petition—longing that his own ways were steadfast to obey God’s statutes—and ends with a vow to keep them joined to a plea not to be utterly forsaken. Both camps hear Scripture’s call to wholehearted obedience and delight; they differ on how such a walk is given and sustained. Blessed are those whose ways are blameless, who walk according to the LORD’s law. Psalms 119:1 Blessed are those who keep his statutes, who seek him with their whole heart. Psalms 119:2 Yes, they do nothing wrong. They walk in his ways. Psalms 119:3 You have commanded your precepts, that we should fully obey them. Psalms 119:4 Oh that my ways were steadfast to obey your statutes! Psalms 119:5 Then I wouldn’t be disappointed, when I consider all of your commandments. Psalms 119:6 I will give thanks to you with uprightness of heart, when I learn your righteous judgments. Psalms 119:7 I will observe your statutes. Don’t utterly forsake me. Psalms 119:8

title: Psalm 119:105–112
context: The Nun stanza names the word as lamp and light, confirms an oath to keep righteous rules, and asks life under severe affliction according to the word. Freewill offerings of praise seek acceptance and teaching; life held in the hand still remembers the law; snares do not produce wandering; testimonies are everlasting heritage and heart-joy; the heart is inclined to perform the statutes forever. Both camps walk by Scripture’s light and prize vowed obedience; they differ on whether inclining the heart is a work we begin or a grace we also ask God to work in us.
text: Psalm 119:105–112 Psalms The Nun stanza names the word as lamp and light, confirms an oath to keep righteous rules, and asks life under severe affliction according to the word. Freewill offerings of praise seek acceptance and teaching; life held in the hand still remembers the law; snares do not produce wandering; testimonies are everlasting heritage and heart-joy; the heart is inclined to perform the statutes forever. Both camps walk by Scripture’s light and prize vowed obedience; they differ on whether inclining the heart is a work we begin or a grace we also ask God to work in us. Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path. Psalms 119:105 I have sworn, and have confirmed it, that I will obey your righteous ordinances. Psalms 119:106 I am afflicted very much. Revive me, LORD, according to your word. Psalms 119:107 Accept, I beg you, the willing offerings of my mouth. LORD, teach me your ordinances. Psalms 119:108 My soul is continually in my hand, yet I won’t forget your law. Psalms 119:109 The wicked have laid a snare for me, yet I haven’t gone astray from your precepts. Psalms 119:110 I have taken your testimonies as a heritage forever, for they are the joy of my heart. Psalms 119:111 I have set my heart to perform your statutes forever, even to the end. Psalms 119:112

title: Psalm 119:113–120
context: The Samekh stanza hates the double-minded and loves the law; God is hiding place and shield; hope rests in the word. Evildoers are told to depart so commandments may be kept; upholding according to the promise is asked for life and unashamed hope; held up, the singer regards statutes continually. God spurns those who stray; the wicked are discarded like dross, therefore testimonies are loved; flesh trembles in fear of God and his judgments. Both camps flee to God for safety and ask to be upheld; they differ on how far that upholding is the necessary cause of living and keeping.
text: Psalm 119:113–120 Psalms The Samekh stanza hates the double-minded and loves the law; God is hiding place and shield; hope rests in the word. Evildoers are told to depart so commandments may be kept; upholding according to the promise is asked for life and unashamed hope; held up, the singer regards statutes continually. God spurns those who stray; the wicked are discarded like dross, therefore testimonies are loved; flesh trembles in fear of God and his judgments. Both camps flee to God for safety and ask to be upheld; they differ on how far that upholding is the necessary cause of living and keeping. I hate double-minded men, but I love your law. Psalms 119:113 You are my hiding place and my shield. I hope in your word. Psalms 119:114 Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may keep the commandments of my God. Psalms 119:115 Uphold me according to your word, that I may live. Let me not be ashamed of my hope. Psalms 119:116 Hold me up, and I will be safe, and will have respect for your statutes continually. Psalms 119:117 You reject all those who stray from your statutes, for their deceit is in vain. Psalms 119:118 You put away all the wicked of the earth like dross. Therefore I love your testimonies. Psalms 119:119 My flesh trembles for fear of you. I am afraid of your judgments. Psalms 119:120

title: Psalm 119:121–128
context: The Ayin stanza pleads from a clean conscience under oppression: judgment and righteousness done, a pledge of good sought, eyes failing for salvation and the righteous promise. Steadfast love is asked to teach; the servant seeks understanding; it is time for the LORD to work, because the law is broken; therefore commandments are loved above gold and all precepts esteemed right while every false way is hated. Both camps refuse merit-bargaining and prize Spirit-taught love of the word; they differ on what “I am your servant” implies when understanding is asked.
text: Psalm 119:121–128 Psalms The Ayin stanza pleads from a clean conscience under oppression: judgment and righteousness done, a pledge of good sought, eyes failing for salvation and the righteous promise. Steadfast love is asked to teach; the servant seeks understanding; it is time for the LORD to work, because the law is broken; therefore commandments are loved above gold and all precepts esteemed right while every false way is hated. Both camps refuse merit-bargaining and prize Spirit-taught love of the word; they differ on what “I am your servant” implies when understanding is asked. I have done what is just and righteous. Don’t leave me to my oppressors. Psalms 119:121 Ensure your servant’s well-being. Don’t let the proud oppress me. Psalms 119:122 My eyes fail looking for your salvation, for your righteous word. Psalms 119:123 Deal with your servant according to your loving kindness. Teach me your statutes. Psalms 119:124 I am your servant. Give me understanding, that I may know your testimonies. Psalms 119:125 It is time to act, LORD, for they break your law. Psalms 119:126 Therefore I love your commandments more than gold, yes, more than pure gold. Psalms 119:127 Therefore I consider all of your precepts to be right. I hate every false way. Psalms 119:128

title: Psalm 119:129–136
context: The Pe stanza wonders at the testimonies and therefore keeps them. The entrance of the word lights the simple; the mouth panteth with longing for the commandments. Grace is asked as God’s do to those who love his name; steps are to be steadied by the promise so iniquity gains no dominion; redemption from oppression serves precept-keeping; the shining face and taught statutes are sought; rivers of tears fall because people do not keep the law. Both camps pant for the word and ask to be kept from sin’s rule; they differ on how far the written word alone can direct steps without the Spirit’s inward governance.
text: Psalm 119:129–136 Psalms The Pe stanza wonders at the testimonies and therefore keeps them. The entrance of the word lights the simple; the mouth panteth with longing for the commandments. Grace is asked as God’s do to those who love his name; steps are to be steadied by the promise so iniquity gains no dominion; redemption from oppression serves precept-keeping; the shining face and taught statutes are sought; rivers of tears fall because people do not keep the law. Both camps pant for the word and ask to be kept from sin’s rule; they differ on how far the written word alone can direct steps without the Spirit’s inward governance. Your testimonies are wonderful, therefore my soul keeps them. Psalms 119:129 The entrance of your words gives light. It gives understanding to the simple. Psalms 119:130 I opened my mouth wide and panted, for I longed for your commandments. Psalms 119:131 Turn to me, and have mercy on me, as you always do to those who love your name. Psalms 119:132 Establish my footsteps in your word. Don’t let any iniquity have dominion over me. Psalms 119:133 Redeem me from the oppression of man, so I will observe your precepts. Psalms 119:134 Make your face shine on your servant. Teach me your statutes. Psalms 119:135 Streams of tears run down my eyes, because they don’t observe your law. Psalms 119:136

title: Psalm 119:137–144
context: The Tsadhe stanza confesses the Lord righteous and his rules right; testimonies appointed in righteousness and faithfulness. Zeal consumes because foes forget the words; the promise is well tried and loved; the small and despised still remember precepts. Everlasting righteousness and true law stand; trouble finds the singer yet commandments delight; forever-righteous testimonies lead to the plea for understanding unto life. Both camps rest life on God-given understanding of the word; they differ on how absolute that dependence is when “give me understanding that I may live” is prayed.
text: Psalm 119:137–144 Psalms The Tsadhe stanza confesses the Lord righteous and his rules right; testimonies appointed in righteousness and faithfulness. Zeal consumes because foes forget the words; the promise is well tried and loved; the small and despised still remember precepts. Everlasting righteousness and true law stand; trouble finds the singer yet commandments delight; forever-righteous testimonies lead to the plea for understanding unto life. Both camps rest life on God-given understanding of the word; they differ on how absolute that dependence is when “give me understanding that I may live” is prayed. You are righteous, LORD. Your judgments are upright. Psalms 119:137 You have commanded your statutes in righteousness. They are fully trustworthy. Psalms 119:138 My zeal wears me out, because my enemies ignore your words. Psalms 119:139 Your promises have been thoroughly tested, and your servant loves them. Psalms 119:140 I am small and despised. I don’t forget your precepts. Psalms 119:141 Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness. Your law is truth. Psalms 119:142 Trouble and anguish have taken hold of me. Your commandments are my delight. Psalms 119:143 Your testimonies are righteous forever. Give me understanding, that I may live. Psalms 119:144

title: Psalm 119:145–152
context: The Qoph stanza cries with the whole heart for answer and vows to keep statutes; calling for salvation aims at observing testimonies. Help is sought before dawn with hope in the words; eyes wake before the night watches to meditate on the promise. Hearing according to steadfast love and life according to justice are asked; malicious pursuers draw near yet are far from the law, while the Lord is near and all commandments true; from of old the testimonies are known as founded forever. Both camps cry early and hope in the word; they differ on quickening as moment-by-moment dependence on free mercy mediated by the word.
text: Psalm 119:145–152 Psalms The Qoph stanza cries with the whole heart for answer and vows to keep statutes; calling for salvation aims at observing testimonies. Help is sought before dawn with hope in the words; eyes wake before the night watches to meditate on the promise. Hearing according to steadfast love and life according to justice are asked; malicious pursuers draw near yet are far from the law, while the Lord is near and all commandments true; from of old the testimonies are known as founded forever. Both camps cry early and hope in the word; they differ on quickening as moment-by-moment dependence on free mercy mediated by the word. I have called with my whole heart. Answer me, LORD! I will keep your statutes. Psalms 119:145 I have called to you. Save me! I will obey your statutes. Psalms 119:146 I rise before dawn and cry for help. I put my hope in your words. Psalms 119:147 My eyes stay open through the night watches, that I might meditate on your word. Psalms 119:148 Hear my voice according to your loving kindness. Revive me, LORD, according to your ordinances. Psalms 119:149 They draw near who follow after wickedness. They are far from your law. Psalms 119:150 You are near, LORD. All your commandments are truth. Psalms 119:151 Of old I have known from your testimonies, that you have founded them forever. Psalms 119:152

title: Psalm 119:153–160
context: The Resh stanza asks God to see affliction and deliver because the law is not forgotten; to plead the cause, redeem, and give life according to the promise. Salvation is far from the wicked who do not seek statutes; great mercy grounds another plea for life according to the rules. Many persecutors do not produce swerving; the faithless are viewed with disgust for not keeping commands; love of the precepts is set before God with a plea for life according to steadfast love; the sum of the words are truth. Every righteous rule endures forever. Both camps treat love of the precepts as piety under fire; they differ on whether that love is adduced as Spirit-wrought evidence of adoption or as sincere affection that may embolden the plea without claiming merit.

Psalms 119:154 Salvation is far from the wicked, for they don’t seek your statutes. Psalms 119:155 Great are your tender mercies, LORD. Revive me according to your ordinances. Psalms 119:156 Many are my persecutors and my adversaries. I haven’t swerved from your testimonies. Psalms 119:157 I look at the faithless with loathing, because they don’t observe your word. Psalms 119:158 Consider how I love your precepts. Revive me, LORD, according to your loving kindness. Psalms 119:159 All of your words are truth. Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever. Psalms 119:160

title: Psalm 119:161–168
context: The Sin and Shin stanza holds awe of the word under princely persecution, joy like spoil found, hate of falsehood with love of the law, and sevenfold praise for righteous rules. Great peace belongs to law-lovers who do not stumble; salvation is hoped for while commandments are done; the soul keeps and exceedingly loves the testimonies; precepts are kept because all ways are before God. Both camps prize fear of the word above fear of princes and peace that grows from love of the law; they differ on how that peace and keeping relate to faith’s assurance versus cooperative obedience under grace.
