I love your law. Psalms 119:163 Seven times a day, I praise you, because of your righteous ordinances. Psalms 119:164 Those who love your law have great peace. Nothing causes them to stumble. Psalms 119:165 I have hoped for your salvation, LORD. I have done your commandments. Psalms 119:166 My soul has observed your testimonies. I love them exceedingly. Psalms 119:167 I have obeyed your precepts and your testimonies, for all my ways are before you. Psalms 119:168

title: Psalm 119:169–176
context: The Taw stanza closes the psalm with cry and plea for understanding and deliverance according to the word; lips and tongue will pour praise and sing because God teaches and all commandments are right. The hand is asked for help because precepts have been chosen; salvation is longed for and the law delighted in; the soul asks to live and praise with rules for help. The last line is a lost-sheep plea: gone astray, seek your servant, for the commandments are not forgotten. Both camps end on the Shepherd seeking the servant and refuse despair; they differ on whether the stray primarily confesses remaining-grace wander under grace or, with Calvin, hunted exile that still remembers the law while God must bring the servant home to safety.

Psalms 119:170 Let my lips utter praise, for you teach me your statutes. Psalms 119:171 Let my tongue sing of your word, for all your commandments are righteousness. Psalms 119:176

title: Psalm 119:17–24
context: The Gimel stanza pleads for God’s bounty that the servant may live and keep the word, and for opened eyes to behold wonders in the law. The singer is a sojourner longing for God’s rules, rebukes the insolent who wander, asks relief from scorn, and under plotting princes still meditates—finding delight and counsel in the testimonies. Both camps pray for illumination and cling to Scripture under pressure; they differ on whether the power to keep is free favor of the Spirit alone from the start.

I will live and I will obey your word. Psalms 119:17 Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things out of your law. Psalms 119:18 I am a stranger on the earth. Don’t hide your commandments from me. Psalms 119:19 My soul is consumed with longing for your ordinances at all times. Psalms 119:20 You have rebuked the proud who are cursed, who wander from your commandments. Psalms 119:21 Take reproach and contempt away from me, for I have kept your statutes. Psalms 119:22 Though princes sit and slander me, your servant will meditate on your statutes. Psalms 119:23 Indeed your statutes are my delight, and my counselors. Psalms 119:24

title: Psalm 119:25–32
context: The Daleth stanza begins in the dust: the soul clings low and asks life according to God’s word. Confession of ways, pleas for understanding and strength, removal of false ways, choosing faithfulness, clinging to testimonies, and finally running in the commandments when God enlarges the heart fill the stanza. Both camps pray for quickening by the word; the clear fork is whether the enlarged heart that runs is God’s prior enabling of the unable, or grace replenishing a will that sincerely chooses.

Psalms 119:26 Let me understand the teaching of your precepts! Then I will meditate on your wondrous works. Psalms 119:27 My soul is weary with sorrow; strengthen me according to your word. Psalms 119:28 Keep me from the way of deceit. Grant me your law graciously! Psalms 119:29 I have chosen the way of truth. I have set your ordinances before me. Psalms 119:30 I cling to your statutes, LORD. Don’t let me be disappointed. Psalms 119:31 I run in the path of your commandments, for you have set my heart free. Psalms 119:32

title: Psalm 119:33–40
context: The He stanza is almost wholly petition: teach, give understanding, lead, incline the heart, turn the eyes, confirm the promise, turn away reproach, and give life in righteousness. Delight in the path and longing for the precepts appear, yet every verb leans on God to form the keeper. Both camps pray this way; they differ most sharply on whether “Turn my heart” confesses a will that cannot turn itself until grace bends it, or a grace that assists a seeker already longing.

Psalms 119:34 Direct me in the path of your commandments, for I delight in them. Psalms 119:35 Turn my heart toward your statutes, not toward selfish gain. Psalms 119:36 Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things. Revive me in your ways. Psalms 119:37 Fulfill your promise to your servant, that you may be feared. Psalms 119:38 Take away my disgrace that I dread, for your ordinances are good. Psalms 119:39 Behold, I long for your precepts! Revive me in your righteousness. Psalms 119:40

title: Psalm 119:41–48
context: The Waw stanza asks that the Lord’s steadfast love and salvation come according to his promise, so the singer may answer taunts, keep the word of truth on his lips, walk in a wide place, and speak of the testimonies even before kings. Delight and love for the commandments fill the close. Both camps trust the promise and refuse a mute faith under reproach; they differ on whether bold confession and continual keeping are Spirit-given ability or grace-assisted perseverance in a sincere truster.

Psalms 119:42 Don’t snatch the word of truth out of my mouth, for I put my hope in your ordinances. Psalms 119:43 So I will obey your law continually, forever and ever. Psalms 119:44 I will walk in liberty, for I have sought your precepts. Psalms 119:45 I will also speak of your statutes before kings, and will not be disappointed. Psalms 119:46 I will delight myself in your commandments, because I love them. Psalms 119:47 I reach out my hands for your commandments, which I love. I will meditate on your statutes. Psalms 119:48

title: Psalm 119:49–56
context: The Zayin stanza pleads that God remember the word in which he made the servant hope, finds comfort and life in the promise under affliction, and holds the law amid insolent derision. Old judgments comfort; hot indignation rises at those who forsake the law; statutes become songs in sojourning, and the name is remembered at night. Both camps cling to the promise under scorn; they differ on whether the hope itself is God’s caused work in the servant or the sincere response the promise invites.

Psalms 119:50 The arrogant mock me excessively, but I don’t swerve from your law. Psalms 119:51 I remember your ordinances of old, LORD, and have comforted myself. Psalms 119:52 Indignation has taken hold on me, because of the wicked who forsake your law. Psalms 119:53 Your statutes have been my songs in the house where I live. Psalms 119:54 I have remembered your name, LORD, in the night, and I obey your law. Psalms 119:55 This is my way, that I keep your precepts. Psalms 119:56

title: Psalm 119:57–64
context: The Heth stanza names the Lord as portion and vows to keep his words, entreats favor according to the promise, turns the feet after thinking on one’s ways, and hastens without delay to the commandments. Cords of the wicked cannot erase the law from memory; midnight praise, companionship with those who fear God, and a plea to be taught fill the earth-wide mercy of the Lord. Both camps make God their portion and rush toward obedience; they differ on how such haste and wholehearted entreaty are possible.

Psalms 119:59 I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments. Psalms 119:60 The ropes of the wicked bind me, but I won’t forget your law. Psalms 119:61 At midnight I will rise to give thanks to you, because of your righteous ordinances. Psalms 119:62 I am a friend of all those who fear you, of those who observe your precepts. Psalms 119:63 The earth is full of your loving kindness, LORD. Teach me your statutes. Psalms 119:64

title: Psalm 119:65–72
context: The Teth stanza thanks God for dealing well according to his word, asks good judgment and knowledge, and confesses that affliction checked wandering and taught the statutes. God is good and does good; lies and unfeeling hearts oppose delight in the law; yet affliction is called good, and the law outweighs gold and silver. Both camps bless fatherly correction and prize the word above wealth; they differ on how affliction recovers the wanderer and what “I believe” implies when more light is asked.

Psalms 119:66 Before I was afflicted, I went astray; but now I observe your word. Psalms 119:67 You are good, and do good. Teach me your statutes. Psalms 119:68 The proud have smeared a lie upon me. With my whole heart, I will keep your precepts. Psalms 119:69 Their heart is as callous as the fat, but I delight in your law. Psalms 119:70 It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn your statutes. Psalms 119:71 The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver. Psalms 119:72

title: Psalm 119:73–80
context: The Yodh stanza begins from creation—God’s hands made and fashioned the singer—and asks understanding to learn the commandments. God-fearers will rejoice at hope in the word; affliction is confessed as faithful; steadfast love and mercy are begged for life and comfort because the law is delight. The insolent are left to shame while the servant meditates; the God-fearing are invited to turn; and the heart is asked to be blameless in the statutes. Both camps pray from creaturehood for light and a sound heart; they differ on whether that soundness is the Spirit’s gift against natural blindness or grace assisting sincere aim.

Psalms 119:74 LORD, I know that your judgments are righteous, that in faithfulness you have afflicted me. Psalms 119:75 Please let your loving kindness be for my comfort, according to your word to your servant. Psalms 119:76 Let your tender mercies come to me, that I may live; for your law is my delight. Psalms 119:77 Let the proud be disappointed, for they have overthrown me wrongfully. I will meditate on your precepts. Psalms 119:78 Let those who fear you turn to me. They will know your statutes. Psalms 119:79 Let my heart be blameless toward your decrees, that I may not be disappointed. Psalms 119:80

title: Psalm 119:81–88
context: The Kaph stanza is a cry of delayed hope: the soul faints for salvation, the eyes fail for the promise, and the singer is dried like a wineskin in smoke—yet the statutes are not forgotten. Pits, falsehood, and near-consumption press hard; the close asks life according to steadfast love so that the testimonies may be kept. Both camps honor perseverance under delay and refuse despair; they differ on whether the life that enables keeping is God’s free quickening of the nearly dead or grace restoring a sincere waiter.

I don’t forget your statutes. Psalms 119:83 How many are the days of your servant? When will you execute judgment on those who persecute me? Psalms 119:84 The proud have dug pits for me, contrary to your law. Psalms 119:85 All of your commandments are faithful. They persecute me wrongfully. Help me! Psalms 119:86 They had almost wiped me from the earth, but I didn’t forsake your precepts. Psalms 119:87 Preserve my life according to your loving kindness, so I will obey the statutes of your mouth. Psalms 119:88

title: Psalm 119:89–96
context: The Lamedh stanza lifts the eyes to a word fixed forever in the heavens, faithfulness to all generations, and a world that stands by God’s appointment. Delight in the law preserved the singer from perishing; precepts quicken; belonging to God grounds the plea to be saved; the wicked wait to destroy, yet testimonies are considered; earthly perfection has a limit, but the commandment is exceedingly broad. Both camps rest salvation’s certainty on God’s unchanging word; they differ on how “I am yours; save me, for I have sought” relates grace and seeking.

Psalms 119:91 Unless your law had been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction. Psalms 119:92 I will never forget your precepts, for with them, you have revived me. Psalms 119:93 I am yours. Save me, for I have sought your precepts. Psalms 119:94 The wicked have waited for me, to destroy me. I will consider your statutes. Psalms 119:95 I have seen a limit to all perfection, but your commands are boundless. Psalms 119:96

title: Psalm 119:9–16
context: The Beth stanza asks how a young man keeps his way pure? By living according to God’s word. Wholehearted seeking, storing the word against sin, delight above riches, meditation, and a resolve not to forget the word fill the eight verses. Both camps honor Scripture as the rule that cleanses and delights; they differ on whether seeking God begins in anticipating grace or only as grace already holds the heart.

Wholehearted seeking, storing the word against sin, delight above riches, meditation, and a resolve not to forget the word fill the eight verses. Psalms 119:10 I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you. Psalms 119:11 Blessed are you, LORD. Teach me your statutes. Psalms 119:12 With my lips, I have declared all the ordinances of your mouth. Psalms 119:13 I have rejoiced in the way of your testimonies, as much as in all riches. Psalms 119:14 I will meditate on your precepts, and consider your ways. Psalms 119:15 I will delight myself in your statutes. I will not forget your word. Psalms 119:16

title: Psalm 119:97–104
context: The Mem stanza overflows with love for the law and all-day meditation. The commandment makes wise beyond enemies; testimonies yield more understanding than teachers and the aged; feet are held from evil paths; rules are kept because God has taught; words taste sweeter than honey; precepts give understanding that hates every false way. Both camps prize loving meditation and Spirit-taught obedience; they differ on whether “you have taught me” names the Spirit’s particular drawing or the illumination offered to every docile reader of the word.
text: Psalm 119:97–104 Psalms The Mem stanza overflows with love for the law and all-day meditation. Psalms 119:98 I have more understanding than all my teachers, for your testimonies are my meditation. Psalms 119:99 I understand more than the aged, because I have kept your precepts. Psalms 119:100 I have kept my feet from every evil way, that I might observe your word. Psalms 119:101 I have not turned away from your ordinances, for you have taught me. Psalms 119:102 How sweet are your promises to my taste, more than honey to my mouth! Psalms 119:103 Through your precepts, I get understanding; therefore I hate every false way. Psalms 119:104

title: Psalm 12:1–8
context: Psalm 12 cries Save when the godly seem gone and the faithful vanish among the children of men. Everyone lies with flattering lips, and with a double heart; the proud boast that with the tongue they will prevail and ask who is master over them. The LORD answers the plundered poor and the needy’s groan: I will now arise and set him in the safety he longs for. His words are pure—silver refined seven times—so he will keep and guard his own from this generation forever, even while the wicked prowl on every side and vileness is exalted.

Who is lord over us?” Psalms 12:4 “Because of the oppression of the weak and because of the groaning of the needy, I will now arise,” says the LORD; “I will set him in safety from those who malign him.” Psalms 12:5 The LORD’s words are flawless words, as silver refined in a clay furnace, purified seven times. Psalms 12:6 You will keep them, LORD. You will preserve them from this generation forever. Psalms 12:7 The wicked walk on every side, when what is vile is exalted among the sons of men. Psalms 12:8

title: Psalm 120:1–7
context: A Song of Ascents opens the pilgrimage collection in distress: the singer calls to the LORD from among deceitful neighbors who hate peace. Meshech and Kedar name far-flung, hostile company. The psalm moves from an answered cry to lament over lying tongues and a world that answers peace with war—the pilgrim’s need before Zion’s songs of trust.
text: Psalm 120:1–7 Psalms A Song of Ascents opens the pilgrimage collection in distress: the singer calls to the LORD from among deceitful neighbors who hate peace. Psalms 120:3 Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of juniper. Psalms 120:4 Woe is me, that I live in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar! Psalms 120:5 My soul has had her dwelling too long with him who hates peace. Psalms 120:6 I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war. Psalms 120:7

title: Psalm 121:1–8
context: A Song of Ascents of trust: the pilgrim lifts eyes to the hills and asks where help comes from, then confesses the Maker of heaven and earth as Keeper. The LORD neither slumbers nor sleeps; He is shade, guard from evil, and watcher of going out and coming in—forevermore. Zion’s road is held by God’s vigilance, not by the traveler’s nerve alone.
text: Psalm 121:1–8 Psalms A Song of Ascents of trust: the pilgrim lifts eyes to the hills and asks where help comes from, then confesses the Maker of heaven and earth as Keeper. The LORD neither slumbers nor sleeps; He is shade, guard from evil, and watcher of going out and coming in—forevermore. Zion’s road is held by God’s vigilance, not by the traveler’s nerve alone. I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? Psalms 121:1 My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth. Psalms 121:2 He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber. Psalms 121:3 Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep. Psalms 121:4 The LORD is your keeper. The LORD is your shade on your right hand. Psalms 121:5 The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon by night. Psalms 121:6 The LORD will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul. Psalms 121:7 The LORD will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forward, and forever more. Psalms 121:8

title: Psalm 122:1–9
context: A Song of Ascents Of David: gladness at the summons to the LORD’s house, feet inside Jerusalem’s gates, and praise for a city bound firmly together. Tribes go up to give thanks; Davidic thrones for judgment stand there. The psalm turns to prayer for Jerusalem’s peace—for brothers, companions, and the house of the LORD our God.
text: Psalm 122:1–9 Psalms A Song of Ascents Of David: gladness at the summons to the LORD’s house, feet inside Jerusalem’s gates, and praise for a city bound firmly together. Tribes go up to give thanks; Davidic thrones for judgment stand there. The psalm turns to prayer for Jerusalem’s peace—for brothers, companions, and the house of the LORD our God. I was glad when they said to me, “Let’s go to the LORD’s house!” Psalms 122:1 Our feet are standing within your gates, Jerusalem! Psalms 122:2 Jerusalem is built as a city that is compact together, Psalms 122:3 where the tribes go up, even the LORD’s tribes, according to an ordinance for Israel, to give thanks to the LORD’s name. Psalms 122:4 For there are set thrones for judgment, the thrones of David’s house. Psalms 122:5 Pray for the peace of Jerusalem. Those who love you will prosper. Psalms 122:6 Peace be within your walls, and prosperity within your palaces. Psalms 122:7 For my brothers’ and companions’ sakes, I will now say, “Peace be within you.” Psalms 122:8 For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good. Psalms 122:9

title: Psalm 123:1–4
context: A Song of Ascents of dependent gaze: eyes lift to the One enthroned in the heavens, then linger like servants watching a master’s hand—until mercy comes. The community has had more than enough contempt from the easeful and proud. Pilgrim faith here is patient looking and repeated plea, not self-rescue.
text: Psalm 123:1–4 Psalms A Song of Ascents of dependent gaze: eyes lift to the One enthroned in the heavens, then linger like servants watching a master’s hand—until mercy comes. The community has had more than enough contempt from the easeful and proud. Pilgrim faith here is patient looking and repeated plea, not self-rescue. I lift up my eyes to you, you who sit in the heavens. Psalms 123:1 Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the LORD, our God, until he has mercy on us. Psalms 123:2 Have mercy on us, LORD, have mercy on us, for we have endured much contempt. Psalms 123:3 Our soul is exceedingly filled with the scoffing of those who are at ease, with the contempt of the proud. Psalms 123:4

title: Psalm 124:1–8
context: A Song of Ascents of David: corporate thanksgiving after narrow escape. If the LORD had not been on Israel's side when enemies rose, flood and snare would have finished them. Blessed be the LORD—help is in His name, Maker of heaven and earth. Pilgrim praise names deliverance as God's alone.
text: Psalm 124:1–8 Psalms A Song of Ascents of David: corporate thanksgiving after narrow escape. If the LORD had not been on Israel's side when enemies rose, flood and snare would have finished them. Blessed be the LORD—help is in His name, Maker of heaven and earth. Pilgrim praise names deliverance as God's alone. If it had not been the LORD who was on our side, let Israel now say, Psalms 124:1 if it had not been the LORD who was on our side, when men rose up against us, Psalms 124:2 then they would have swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us, Psalms 124:3 then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have gone over our soul. Psalms 124:4 Then the proud waters would have gone over our soul. Psalms 124:5 Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth. Psalms 124:6 Our soul has escaped like a bird out of the fowler’s snare. The snare is broken, and we have escaped. Psalms 124:7 Our help is in the LORD’s name, who made heaven and earth. Psalms 124:8

title: Psalm 125:1–5
context: A Song of Ascents of trust and surround: those who trust in the LORD stand like Mount Zion; as mountains ring Jerusalem, so the LORD rings His people forever. Wicked rule will not rest on the righteous' lot, lest hands stretch to wrong. Prayer seeks good for the upright; peace rests on Israel while the crooked are led away.
text: Psalm 125:1–5 Psalms A Song of Ascents of trust and surround: those who trust in the LORD stand like Mount Zion; as mountains ring Jerusalem, so the LORD rings His people forever. Wicked rule will not rest on the righteous' lot, lest hands stretch to wrong. Prayer seeks good for the upright; peace rests on Israel while the crooked are led away. Those who trust in the LORD are as Mount Zion, which can’t be moved, but remains forever. Psalms 125:1 As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds his people from this time forward and forever more. Psalms 125:2 For the scepter of wickedness won’t remain over the allotment of the righteous, so that the righteous won’t use their hands to do evil. Psalms 125:3 Do good, LORD, to those who are good, to those who are upright in their hearts. Psalms 125:4 But as for those who turn away to their crooked ways, the LORD will lead them away with the workers of iniquity. Peace be on Israel. Psalms 125:5

title: Psalm 126:1–6
context: A Song of Ascents of restored fortune and tearful sowing: when the LORD restored Zion, laughter and nations' confession followed—'The LORD has done great things.' Prayer asks streams in the Negev. Those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy, coming home with sheaves. Pilgrim hope works through weeping toward harvest.
text: Psalm 126:1–6 Psalms A Song of Ascents of restored fortune and tearful sowing: when the LORD restored Zion, laughter and nations' confession followed—'The LORD has done great things.' Prayer asks streams in the Negev. Those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy, coming home with sheaves. Pilgrim hope works through weeping toward harvest. When the LORD brought back those who returned to Zion, we were like those who dream. Psalms 126:1 Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, “The LORD has done great things for them.” Psalms 126:2 The LORD has done great things for us, and we are glad. Psalms 126:3 Restore our fortunes again, LORD, like the streams in the Negev. Psalms 126:4 Those who sow in tears will reap in joy. Psalms 126:5 He who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will certainly come again with joy, carrying his sheaves. Psalms 126:6

title: Psalm 127:1–5
context: A Song of Ascents of Solomon: house, city, and anxious toil are vain unless the LORD builds, watches, and gives His beloved sleep. Children are His heritage and reward—arrows for a warrior, a full quiver's blessing at the gate. Domestic and civic life hang on God's blessing, not bare human hustle.
text: Psalm 127:1–5 Psalms A Song of Ascents of Solomon: house, city, and anxious toil are vain unless the LORD builds, watches, and gives His beloved sleep. Children are His heritage and reward—arrows for a warrior, a full quiver's blessing at the gate. Domestic and civic life hang on God's blessing, not bare human hustle. Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain. Psalms 127:1 It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones. Psalms 127:2 Behold, children are a heritage of the LORD. The fruit of the womb is his reward. Psalms 127:3 As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of youth. Psalms 127:4 Happy is the man who has his quiver full of them. They won’t be disappointed when they speak with their enemies in the gate. Psalms 127:5

title: Psalm 128:1–6
context: A Song of Ascents of household blessing under the fear of the LORD: the one who walks in His ways eats the fruit of labor, flourishes with wife and children at the table, and is blessed from Zion with Jerusalem’s good and children’s children—peace upon Israel. Domestic joy and Zion’s welfare are named together as gifts of reverent obedience.
text: Psalm 128:1–6 Psalms A Song of Ascents of household blessing under the fear of the LORD: the one who walks in His ways eats the fruit of labor, flourishes with wife and children at the table, and is blessed from Zion with Jerusalem’s good and children’s children—peace upon Israel. Domestic joy and Zion’s welfare are named together as gifts of reverent obedience. Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways. Psalms 128:1 For you will eat the labor of your hands. You will be happy, and it will be well with you. Psalms 128:2 Your wife will be as a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house, your children like olive shoots around your table. Psalms 128:3 Behold, this is how the man who fears the LORD is blessed. Psalms 128:4 May the LORD bless you out of Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life. Psalms 128:5 Yes, may you see your children’s children. Peace be upon Israel. Psalms 128:6

title: Psalm 129:1–8
context: A Song of Ascents of affliction and resilience: Israel is called to say how greatly foes have afflicted her from youth up, yet they have not prevailed. Plowers cut long furrows on the back; the righteous LORD cuts the cords of the wicked. Haters of Zion are wished shame and housetop grass that withers before harvest greeting—no blessing of the LORD upon a barren crop.
text: Psalm 129:1–8 Psalms A Song of Ascents of affliction and resilience: Israel is called to say how greatly foes have afflicted her from youth up, yet they have not prevailed. Plowers cut long furrows on the back; the righteous LORD cuts the cords of the wicked. Haters of Zion are wished shame and housetop grass that withers before harvest greeting—no blessing of the LORD upon a barren crop. Many times they have afflicted me from my youth up. Let Israel now say: Psalms 129:1 many times they have afflicted me from my youth up, yet they have not prevailed against me. Psalms 129:2 The plowers plowed on my back. They made their furrows long. Psalms 129:3 The LORD is righteous. He has cut apart the cords of the wicked. Psalms 129:4 Let them be disappointed and turned backward, all those who hate Zion. Psalms 129:5 Let them be as the grass on the housetops, which withers before it grows up, Psalms 129:6 with which the reaper doesn’t fill his hand, nor he who binds sheaves, his bosom. Psalms 129:7 Neither do those who go by say, “The blessing of the LORD be on you. We bless you in the LORD’s name.” Psalms 129:8

title: Psalm 13:1–6
context: Psalm 13 is David’s fourfold “how long?” under prolonged affliction: he asks whether the LORD will forget him forever and hide his face, while he takes counsel in his soul with sorrow all the day and the enemy is exalted over him. He pleads that God consider and answer, lighten his eyes lest he sleep the sleep of death, and not let the enemy boast of prevailing or foes rejoice at his shaking. Then trust breaks through: he has trusted in steadfast love, his heart shall rejoice in salvation, and he will sing to the LORD, because he has been good to him.
text: Psalm 13:1–6 Psalms Psalm 13 is David’s fourfold “how long?” under prolonged affliction: he asks whether the LORD will forget him forever and hide his face, while he takes counsel in his soul with sorrow all the day and the enemy is exalted over him. He pleads that God consider and answer, lighten his eyes lest he sleep the sleep of death, and not let the enemy boast of prevailing or foes rejoice at his shaking. Then trust breaks through: he has trusted in steadfast love, his heart shall rejoice in salvation, and he will sing to the LORD, because he has been good to him. How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me? Psalms 13:1 How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart every day? How long shall my enemy triumph over me? Psalms 13:2 Behold, and answer me, LORD, my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death; Psalms 13:3 lest my enemy say, “I have prevailed against him;” lest my adversaries rejoice when I fall. Psalms 13:4 But I trust in your loving kindness. My heart rejoices in your salvation. Psalms 13:5 I will sing to the LORD, because he has been good to me. Psalms 13:6

title: Psalm 130:1–8
context: A Song of Ascents from the depths (De profundis): the cry for attentive mercy, the confession that none could stand if the LORD marked iniquities, and the wonder that with Him there is forgiveness—that He may be feared. Waiting and hoping in His word outpace watchmen for morning; Israel is called to hope, for with the LORD is steadfast love and plentiful redemption from all iniquities.
text: Psalm 130:1–8 Psalms A Song of Ascents from the depths (De profundis): the cry for attentive mercy, the confession that none could stand if the LORD marked iniquities, and the wonder that with Him there is forgiveness—that He may be feared. Waiting and hoping in His word outpace watchmen for morning; Israel is called to hope, for with the LORD is steadfast love and plentiful redemption from all iniquities. Out of the depths I have cried to you, LORD. Psalms 130:1 Lord, hear my voice. Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my petitions. Psalms 130:2 If you, LORD, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand? Psalms 130:3 But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared. Psalms 130:4 I wait for the LORD. My soul waits. I hope in his word. Psalms 130:5 My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning. Psalms 130:6 Israel, hope in the LORD, for there is loving kindness with the LORD. Abundant redemption is with him. Psalms 130:7 He will redeem Israel from all their sins. Psalms 130:8

title: Psalm 131:1–3
context: A Song of Ascents Of David: a renunciation of haughty heart and lofty eyes, and of occupying oneself with things too great and marvelous. The soul is calmed and quieted like a weaned child with his mother—then Israel is called to hope in the LORD, from this time forward and forevermore. Pilgrim maturity here is humble rest, not restless grasping.
text: Psalm 131:1–3 Psalms A Song of Ascents Of David: a renunciation of haughty heart and lofty eyes, and of occupying oneself with things too great and marvelous. The soul is calmed and quieted like a weaned child with his mother—then Israel is called to hope in the LORD, from this time forward and forevermore. Pilgrim maturity here is humble rest, not restless grasping. LORD, my heart isn’t arrogant, nor my eyes lofty; nor do I concern myself with great matters, or things too wonderful for me. Psalms 131:1 Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me. Psalms 131:2 Israel, hope in the LORD, from this time forward and forever more. Psalms 131:3

title: Psalm 132:1–18
context: A Song of Ascents: remembrance of David’s hardships and vow to find a dwelling for the LORD—the ark heard of in Ephrathah and found in the field of Jaar, then brought to worship at His footstool. Prayer rises for the LORD and the ark of His might, for priests clothed with righteousness and saints shouting for joy, and for the anointed not to be turned away for David’s sake. God answers with a sure oath to David, Zion chosen as His forever rest, abundant provision, priests clothed with salvation, a horn sprouting for David, a lamp for His anointed, enemies shamed, and the crown shining.
text: Psalm 132:1–18 Psalms A Song of Ascents: remembrance of David’s hardships and vow to find a dwelling for the LORD—the ark heard of in Ephrathah and found in the field of Jaar, then brought to worship at His footstool. Prayer rises for the LORD and the ark of His might, for priests clothed with righteousness and saints shouting for joy, and for the anointed not to be turned away for David’s sake. God answers with a sure oath to David, Zion chosen as His forever rest, abundant provision, priests clothed with salvation, a horn sprouting for David, a lamp for His anointed, enemies shamed, and the crown shining. LORD, remember David and all his affliction, Psalms 132:1 how he swore to the LORD, and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob: Psalms 132:2 “Surely I will not come into the structure of my house, nor go up into my bed; Psalms 132:3 I will not give sleep to my eyes, or slumber to my eyelids, Psalms 132:4 until I find out a place for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.” Psalms 132:5 Behold, we heard of it in Ephrathah. We found it in the field of Jaar. Psalms 132:6 “We will go into his dwelling place. We will worship at his footstool.” Psalms 132:7 Arise, LORD, into your resting place, you, and the ark of your strength. Psalms 132:8 Let your priests be clothed with righteousness. Let your saints shout for joy! Psalms 132:9 For your servant David’s sake, don’t turn away the face of your anointed one. Psalms 132:10 The LORD has sworn to David in truth. He will not turn from it: “I will set the fruit of your body on your throne. Psalms 132:11 If your children will keep my covenant, my testimony that I will teach them, their children also will sit on your throne forever more.” Psalms 132:12 For the LORD has chosen Zion. He has desired it for his habitation. Psalms 132:13 “This is my resting place forever. I will live here, for I have desired it. Psalms 132:14 I will abundantly bless her provision. I will satisfy her poor with bread. Psalms 132:15 I will also clothe her priests with salvation. Her saints will shout aloud for joy. Psalms 132:16 I will make the horn of David to bud there. I have ordained a lamp for my anointed. Psalms 132:17 I will clothe his enemies with shame, but on himself, his crown will shine.” Psalms 132:18

title: Psalm 133:1–3
context: A Song of Ascents Of David: a brief exclamation over how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity—likened to precious oil on Aaron’s head running down on beard and collar, and to Hermon’s dew falling on Zion’s mountains. There the LORD gives the blessing, even life forevermore.
text: Psalm 133:1–3 Psalms A Song of Ascents Of David: a brief exclamation over how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity—likened to precious oil on Aaron’s head running down on beard and collar, and to Hermon’s dew falling on Zion’s mountains. There the LORD gives the blessing, even life forevermore. See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity! Psalms 133:1 It is like the precious oil on the head, that ran down on the beard, even Aaron’s beard, that came down on the edge of his robes, Psalms 133:2 like the dew of Hermon, that comes down on the hills of Zion; for there the LORD gives the blessing, even life forever more. Psalms 133:3

title: Psalm 134:1–3
context: A Song of Ascents and the last of the pilgrim songs: servants of the LORD, who stand by night in the LORD’s house of the LORD are called to bless Him, lifting hands to the holy place. The answering benediction asks the LORD—Maker of heaven and earth—to bless from Zion.
text: Psalm 134:1–3 Psalms A Song of Ascents and the last of the pilgrim songs: servants of the LORD, who stand by night in the LORD’s house of the LORD are called to bless Him, lifting hands to the holy place. The answering benediction asks the LORD—Maker of heaven and earth—to bless from Zion. Look! Praise the LORD, all you servants of the LORD, who stand by night in the LORD’s house! Psalms 134:1 Lift up your hands in the sanctuary. Praise the LORD! Psalms 134:2 May the LORD bless you from Zion, even he who made heaven and earth. Psalms 134:3

title: Psalm 135:1–21
context: Servants standing in the LORD’s house are summoned to praise His name: He is good; He has chosen Jacob as His possession; He does whatever He pleases in heaven, earth, and deeps; He struck Egypt, kings, and Canaan and gave the land as heritage. His name endures; He will vindicate His people. Idols of silver and gold cannot speak, see, or hear—and their makers become like them. Houses of Israel, Aaron, and Levi, and all who fear the LORD, praise Him from Zion.
text: Psalm 135:1–21 Psalms Servants standing in the LORD’s house are summoned to praise His name: He is good; He has chosen Jacob as His possession; He does whatever He pleases in heaven, earth, and deeps; He struck Egypt, kings, and Canaan and gave the land as heritage. His name endures; He will vindicate His people. Idols of silver and gold cannot speak, see, or hear—and their makers become like them. Houses of Israel, Aaron, and Levi, and all who fear the LORD, praise Him from Zion. Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD’s name! Praise him, you servants of the LORD, Psalms 135:1 you who stand in the LORD’s house, in the courts of our God’s house. Psalms 135:2 Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good. Sing praises to his name, for that is pleasant. Psalms 135:3 For the LORD has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel for his own possession. Psalms 135:4 For I know that the LORD is great, that our Lord is above all gods. Psalms 135:5 Whatever the LORD pleased, that he has done, in heaven and in earth, in the seas and in all deeps. Psalms 135:6 He causes the clouds to rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightnings with the rain. He brings the wind out of his treasuries. Psalms 135:7 He struck the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and animal. Psalms 135:8 He sent signs and wonders into the middle of you, Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on all his servants. Psalms 135:9 He struck many nations, and killed mighty kings— Psalms 135:10 Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan— Psalms 135:11 and gave their land for a heritage, a heritage to Israel, his people. Psalms 135:12 Your name, LORD, endures forever; your renown, LORD, throughout all generations. Psalms 135:13 For the LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants. Psalms 135:14 The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands. Psalms 135:15 They have mouths, but they can’t speak. They have eyes, but they can’t see. Psalms 135:16 They have ears, but they can’t hear, neither is there any breath in their mouths. Psalms 135:17 Those who make them will be like them, yes, everyone who trusts in them. Psalms 135:18 House of Israel, praise the LORD! House of Aaron, praise the LORD! Psalms 135:19 House of Levi, praise the LORD! You who fear the LORD, praise the LORD! Psalms 135:20 Blessed be the LORD from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD! Psalms 135:21

title: Psalm 136:1–26
context: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. The refrain answers every line: God of gods and Lord of lords; Maker of heavens, earth, and lights; Redeemer who struck Egypt’s firstborn, brought Israel out with strong hand, divided the Red Sea, led through the wilderness, struck Sihon and Og, and gave the land as heritage to Israel His servant; He remembered us in our low estate, rescued us, and gives food to every creature. Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his loving kindness endures forever.
text: Psalm 136:1–26 Psalms Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. The refrain answers every line: God of gods and Lord of lords; Maker of heavens, earth, and lights; Redeemer who struck Egypt’s firstborn, brought Israel out with strong hand, divided the Red Sea, led through the wilderness, struck Sihon and Og, and gave the land as heritage to Israel His servant; He remembered us in our low estate, rescued us, and gives food to every creature. Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his loving kindness endures forever. Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 136:1 Give thanks to the God of gods, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 136:2 Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:3 to him who alone does great wonders, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:4 to him who by understanding made the heavens, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:5 to him who spread out the earth above the waters, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:6 to him who made the great lights, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:7 the sun to rule by day, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:8 the moon and stars to rule by night, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:9 to him who struck down the Egyptian firstborn, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:10 and brought out Israel from among them, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:11 with a strong hand, and with an outstretched arm, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:12 to him who divided the Red Sea apart, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:13 and made Israel to pass through the middle of it, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:14 but overthrew Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:15 to him who led his people through the wilderness, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:16 to him who struck great kings, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:17 and killed mighty kings, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:18 Sihon king of the Amorites, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:19 Og king of Bashan, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:20 and gave their land as an inheritance, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:21 even a heritage to Israel his servant, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:22 who remembered us in our low estate, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:23 and has delivered us from our adversaries, for his loving kindness endures forever; Psalms 136:24 who gives food to every creature, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 136:25 Oh give thanks to the God of heaven, for his loving kindness endures forever. Psalms 136:26

title: Psalm 137:1–9
context: An exile lament By the rivers of Babylon: captives weep at the memory of Zion, hang lyres on the willows, and refuse to turn the LORD’s song into entertainment for tormentors. Vow follows—Jerusalem above highest joy—then appeal that God remember Edom’s cry to raze the city, and solemn judgment language against Babylon’s doom, including the hard closing line of retributive warfare. Both camps take the imprecation seriously as Scripture under exile grief, not as flippant revenge theater.
text: Psalm 137:1–9 Psalms An exile lament By the rivers of Babylon: captives weep at the memory of Zion, hang lyres on the willows, and refuse to turn the LORD’s song into entertainment for tormentors. Vow follows—Jerusalem above highest joy—then appeal that God remember Edom’s cry to raze the city, and solemn judgment language against Babylon’s doom, including the hard closing line of retributive warfare. Both camps take the imprecation seriously as Scripture under exile grief, not as flippant revenge theater. By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down. Yes, we wept, when we remembered Zion. Psalms 137:1 On the willows in that land, we hung up our harps. Psalms 137:2 For there, those who led us captive asked us for songs. Those who tormented us demanded songs of joy: “Sing us one of the songs of Zion!” Psalms 137:3 How can we sing the LORD’s song in a foreign land? Psalms 137:4 If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill. Psalms 137:5 Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I don’t remember you, if I don’t prefer Jerusalem above my chief joy. Psalms 137:6 Remember, LORD, against the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem, who said, “Raze it! Raze it even to its foundation!” Psalms 137:7 Daughter of Babylon, doomed to destruction, he will be happy who repays you, as you have done to us. Psalms 137:8 Happy shall he be, who takes and dashes your little ones against the rock. Psalms 137:9

title: Psalm 138:1–8
context: A Psalm of David: wholehearted thanks before the gods, worship toward the holy temple for steadfast love and faithfulness, and the claim that God has exalted His name and His word. Answered prayer strengthens the soul; kings will thank the LORD for the words of His mouth and sing of His ways. Though high, yet he looks after the lowly; in trouble He preserves, opposes enemies’ wrath, and fulfills His purpose—steadfast love forever, with the plea not to forsake the work of His hands.

Answered prayer strengthens the soul; kings will thank the LORD for the words of His mouth and sing of His ways. Though high, yet he looks after the lowly; in trouble He preserves, opposes enemies’ wrath, and fulfills His purpose—steadfast love forever, with the plea not to forsake the work of His hands. I will give you thanks with my whole heart. Before the gods, I will sing praises to you. Psalms 138:1 I will bow down toward your holy temple, and give thanks to your Name for your loving kindness and for your truth; for you have exalted your Name and your Word above all. Psalms 138:2 In the day that I called, you answered me. You encouraged me with strength in my soul. Psalms 138:3 All the kings of the earth will give you thanks, LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth. Psalms 138:4 Yes, they will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the LORD’s glory is great! Psalms 138:5 For though the LORD is high, yet he looks after the lowly; but he knows the proud from afar. Psalms 138:6 Though I walk in the middle of trouble, you will revive me. You will stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies. Your right hand will save me. Psalms 138:7 The LORD will fulfill that which concerns me. Your loving kindness, LORD, endures forever. Don’t forsake the works of your own hands. Psalms 138:8

title: Psalm 139:1–24
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The LORD has searched and known the psalmist—sitting, rising, thoughts from afar, path and lying down, words before the tongue, hemmed in by His hand; such knowledge is too wonderful. No flight from Spirit or presence—heaven, Sheol, wings of the morning, uttermost sea, darkness as light. He formed inward parts in the womb; fearfully and wonderfully made; unformed substance and days written in His book. Precious, vast thoughts; then holy distance from the wicked, hatred of those who hate the LORD, and the closing plea: search me, try me, see if any grievous way, and lead in the way everlasting.
text: Psalm 139:1–24 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The LORD has searched and known the psalmist—sitting, rising, thoughts from afar, path and lying down, words before the tongue, hemmed in by His hand; such knowledge is too wonderful. No flight from Spirit or presence—heaven, Sheol, wings of the morning, uttermost sea, darkness as light. He formed inward parts in the womb; fearfully and wonderfully made; unformed substance and days written in His book. Precious, vast thoughts; then holy distance from the wicked, hatred of those who hate the LORD, and the closing plea: search me, try me, see if any grievous way, and lead in the way everlasting. LORD, you have searched me, and you know me. Psalms 139:1 You know my sitting down and my rising up. You perceive my thoughts from afar. Psalms 139:2 You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways. Psalms 139:3 For there is not a word on my tongue, but behold, LORD, you know it altogether. Psalms 139:4 You hem me in behind and before. You laid your hand on me. Psalms 139:5 This knowledge is beyond me. It’s lofty. I can’t attain it. Psalms 139:6 Where could I go from your Spirit? Or where could I flee from your presence? Psalms 139:7 If I ascend up into heaven, you are there. If I make my bed in Sheol, behold, you are there! Psalms 139:8 If I take the wings of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the sea, Psalms 139:9 even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me. Psalms 139:10 If I say, “Surely the darkness will overwhelm me. The light around me will be night,” Psalms 139:11 even the darkness doesn’t hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you. Psalms 139:12 For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my mother’s womb. Psalms 139:13 I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well. Psalms 139:14 My frame wasn’t hidden from you, when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth. Psalms 139:15 Your eyes saw my body. In your book they were all written, the days that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them. Psalms 139:16 How precious to me are your thoughts, God! How vast is their sum! Psalms 139:17 If I would count them, they are more in number than the sand. When I wake up, I am still with you. Psalms 139:18 If only you, God, would kill the wicked. Get away from me, you bloodthirsty men! Psalms 139:19 For they speak against you wickedly. Your enemies take your name in vain. Psalms 139:20 LORD, don’t I hate those who hate you? Am I not grieved with those who rise up against you? Psalms 139:21 I hate them with perfect hatred. They have become my enemies. Psalms 139:22 Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts. Psalms 139:23 See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way. Psalms 139:24

title: Psalm 14:1–7
context: Psalm 14 is David’s indictment of practical atheism and universal corruption: the fool has said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt and do abominable deeds; none does good. The LORD looked down from heaven for any who understand and seek him, and finds that all have turned aside—none who does good, no, not one. Evildoers devour his people as bread, and don’t call on the LORD; yet terror falls, for God is in the generation of the righteous, and the LORD is the poor man’s refuge. The psalm closes longing that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion, and that Jacob would rejoice when the LORD restores his people’s fortunes.
text: Psalm 14:1–7 Psalms Psalm 14 is David’s indictment of practical atheism and universal corruption: the fool has said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt and do abominable deeds; none does good. The LORD looked down from heaven for any who understand and seek him, and finds that all have turned aside—none who does good, no, not one. Evildoers devour his people as bread, and don’t call on the LORD; yet terror falls, for God is in the generation of the righteous, and the LORD is the poor man’s refuge. The psalm closes longing that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion, and that Jacob would rejoice when the LORD restores his people’s fortunes. The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt. They have done abominable deeds. There is no one who does good. Psalms 14:1 The LORD looked down from heaven on the children of men, to see if there were any who understood, who sought after God. Psalms 14:2 They have all gone aside. They have together become corrupt. There is no one who does good, no, not one. Psalms 14:3 Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and don’t call on the LORD? Psalms 14:4 There they were in great fear, for God is in the generation of the righteous. Psalms 14:5 You frustrate the plan of the poor, because the LORD is his refuge. Psalms 14:6 Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, then Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad. Psalms 14:7

title: Psalm 140:1–13
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David: a cry for deliverance from evil and violent men whose hearts plan mischief, whose tongues are serpent-sharp, and whose nets and snares line the path. David confesses the LORD as his God and the strength of his salvation, pleads that wicked desires not be granted, and looks for justice that maintains the afflicted—so the righteous give thanks and the upright dwell in God’s presence.
text: Psalm 140:1–13 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David: a cry for deliverance from evil and violent men whose hearts plan mischief, whose tongues are serpent-sharp, and whose nets and snares line the path. David confesses the LORD as his God and the strength of his salvation, pleads that wicked desires not be granted, and looks for justice that maintains the afflicted—so the righteous give thanks and the upright dwell in God’s presence. Deliver me, LORD, from evil men. Preserve me from violent men: Psalms 140:1 those who devise mischief in their hearts. They continually gather themselves together for war. Psalms 140:2 They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent. Viper’s poison is under their lips. Selah. Psalms 140:3 LORD, keep me from the hands of the wicked. Preserve me from the violent men who have determined to trip my feet. Psalms 140:4 The proud have hidden a snare for me, they have spread the cords of a net by the path. They have set traps for me. Selah. Psalms 140:5 I said to the LORD, “You are my God.” Listen to the cry of my petitions, LORD. Psalms 140:6 LORD, the Lord, the strength of my salvation, you have covered my head in the day of battle. Psalms 140:7 LORD, don’t grant the desires of the wicked. Don’t let their evil plans succeed, or they will become proud. Selah. Psalms 140:8 As for the head of those who surround me, let the mischief of their own lips cover them. Psalms 140:9 Let burning coals fall on them. Let them be thrown into the fire, into miry pits, from where they never rise. Psalms 140:10 An evil speaker won’t be established on the earth. Evil will hunt the violent man to overthrow him. Psalms 140:11 I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the afflicted, and justice for the needy. Psalms 140:12 Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name. The upright will dwell in your presence. Psalms 140:13

title: Psalm 141:1–10
context: A Psalm of David: urgent calling on the LORD that prayer be counted as incense and lifted hands like the evening sacrifice. He asks a guard over mouth and heart against evil company and its delicacies, welcomes righteous rebuke as kindness and oil, and—amid scattered bones and laid traps—keeps eyes toward God his Lord for refuge, that the wicked fall together into their own nets while he passes safely.
text: Psalm 141:1–10 Psalms A Psalm of David: urgent calling on the LORD that prayer be counted as incense and lifted hands like the evening sacrifice. He asks a guard over mouth and heart against evil company and its delicacies, welcomes righteous rebuke as kindness and oil, and—amid scattered bones and laid traps—keeps eyes toward God his Lord for refuge, that the wicked fall together into their own nets while he passes safely. LORD, I have called on you. Come to me quickly! Listen to my voice when I call to you. Psalms 141:1 Let my prayer be set before you like incense; the lifting up of my hands like the evening sacrifice. Psalms 141:2 Set a watch, LORD, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips. Psalms 141:3 Don’t incline my heart to any evil thing, to practice deeds of wickedness with men who work iniquity. Don’t let me eat of their delicacies. Psalms 141:4 Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness; let him reprove me, it is like oil on the head; don’t let my head refuse it; Yet my prayer is always against evil deeds. Psalms 141:5 Their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock. They will hear my words, for they are well spoken. Psalms 141:6 “As when one plows and breaks up the earth, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.” Psalms 141:7 For my eyes are on you, LORD, the Lord. I take refuge in you. Don’t leave my soul destitute. Psalms 141:8 Keep me from the snare which they have laid for me, from the traps of the workers of iniquity. Psalms 141:9 Let the wicked fall together into their own nets while I pass by. Psalms 141:10

title: Psalm 142:1–7
context: A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A Prayer: with voice he cries and pleads for mercy, pours out complaint and trouble before the LORD. When spirit faints, God knows the way—though traps hide on the path and no human refuge remains. He confesses the LORD as refuge and portion in the land of the living, asks deliverance from persecutors too strong for him, and seeks exit from prison for thanks, sure the righteous will surround him as God deals bountifully.
text: Psalm 142:1–7 Psalms A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A Prayer: with voice he cries and pleads for mercy, pours out complaint and trouble before the LORD. When spirit faints, God knows the way—though traps hide on the path and no human refuge remains. He confesses the LORD as refuge and portion in the land of the living, asks deliverance from persecutors too strong for him, and seeks exit from prison for thanks, sure the righteous will surround him as God deals bountifully. I cry with my voice to the LORD. With my voice, I ask the LORD for mercy. Psalms 142:1 I pour out my complaint before him. I tell him my troubles. Psalms 142:2 When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you knew my route. On the path in which I walk, they have hidden a snare for me. Psalms 142:3 Look on my right, and see; for there is no one who is concerned for me. Refuge has fled from me. No one cares for my soul. Psalms 142:4 I cried to you, LORD. I said, “You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.” Psalms 142:5 Listen to my cry, for I am in desperate need. Deliver me from my persecutors, for they are too strong for me. Psalms 142:6 Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name. The righteous will surround me, for you will be good to me. Psalms 142:7

title: Psalm 143:1–12
context: A Psalm of David: he asks the LORD to hear prayer and pleas for mercy—answered in faithfulness and righteousness—yet not to enter into judgment with His servant, for in your sight no man living is righteous before Him. The enemy has pursued, crushed, and darkened his life; spirit faints and heart is appalled. He remembers days of old, meditates on God’s works, stretches out hands, and thirsts like parched land. He seeks a quick answer, morning steadfast love, the way he should go, deliverance and refuge, teaching to do God’s will, the good Spirit on level ground, life preserved for the name’s sake, and steadfast love cutting off adversaries—for he is God’s servant.
text: Psalm 143:1–12 Psalms A Psalm of David: he asks the LORD to hear prayer and pleas for mercy—answered in faithfulness and righteousness—yet not to enter into judgment with His servant, for in your sight no man living is righteous before Him. The enemy has pursued, crushed, and darkened his life; spirit faints and heart is appalled. He remembers days of old, meditates on God’s works, stretches out hands, and thirsts like parched land. He seeks a quick answer, morning steadfast love, the way he should go, deliverance and refuge, teaching to do God’s will, the good Spirit on level ground, life preserved for the name’s sake, and steadfast love cutting off adversaries—for he is God’s servant. Hear my prayer, LORD. Listen to my petitions. In your faithfulness and righteousness, relieve me. Psalms 143:1 Don’t enter into judgment with your servant, for in your sight no man living is righteous. Psalms 143:2 For the enemy pursues my soul. He has struck my life down to the ground. He has made me live in dark places, as those who have been long dead. Psalms 143:3 Therefore my spirit is overwhelmed within me. My heart within me is desolate. Psalms 143:4 I remember the days of old. I meditate on all your doings. I contemplate the work of your hands. Psalms 143:5 I spread out my hands to you. My soul thirsts for you, like a parched land. Selah. Psalms 143:6 Hurry to answer me, LORD. My spirit fails. Don’t hide your face from me, so that I don’t become like those who go down into the pit. Psalms 143:7 Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you. Psalms 143:8 Deliver me, LORD, from my enemies. I flee to you to hide me. Psalms 143:9 Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your Spirit is good. Lead me in the land of uprightness. Psalms 143:10 Revive me, LORD, for your name’s sake. In your righteousness, bring my soul out of trouble. Psalms 143:11 In your loving kindness, cut off my enemies, and destroy all those who afflict my soul, for I am your servant. Psalms 143:12

title: Psalm 144:1–15
context: Of David: blessed be the LORD, his rock, who trains hands for war and fingers for battle—steadfast love, fortress, stronghold, deliverer, shield, and refuge, who subdues my people under him. What is man that God regards him? Man is like a breath; days a passing shadow. He asks the LORD to bow the heavens, touch smoking mountains, flash lightning, stretch out a hand from on high, and rescue from many waters and lying foreigners. He will sing a new song on the ten-stringed harp to the God who gives salvation to kings and rescues David from the cruel sword. He seeks safe sons and daughters, full granaries, thriving flocks and cattle, and no going away, and no outcry in the streets—and blesses the people who are in such gifts fall, whose God is the LORD.
text: Psalm 144:1–15 Psalms Of David: blessed be the LORD, his rock, who trains hands for war and fingers for battle—steadfast love, fortress, stronghold, deliverer, shield, and refuge, who subdues my people under him. What is man that God regards him? Man is like a breath; days a passing shadow. He asks the LORD to bow the heavens, touch smoking mountains, flash lightning, stretch out a hand from on high, and rescue from many waters and lying foreigners. He will sing a new song on the ten-stringed harp to the God who gives salvation to kings and rescues David from the cruel sword. He seeks safe sons and daughters, full granaries, thriving flocks and cattle, and no going away, and no outcry in the streets—and blesses the people who are in such gifts fall, whose God is the LORD. Blessed be the LORD, my rock, who trains my hands to war, and my fingers to battle— Psalms 144:1 my loving kindness, my fortress, my high tower, my deliverer, my shield, and he in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me. Psalms 144:2 LORD, what is man, that you care for him? Or the son of man, that you think of him? Psalms 144:3 Man is like a breath. His days are like a shadow that passes away. Psalms 144:4 Part your heavens, LORD, and come down. Touch the mountains, and they will smoke. Psalms 144:5 Throw out lightning, and scatter them. Send out your arrows, and rout them. Psalms 144:6 Stretch out your hand from above, rescue me, and deliver me out of great waters, out of the hands of foreigners, Psalms 144:7 whose mouths speak deceit, whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood. Psalms 144:8 I will sing a new song to you, God. On a ten-stringed lyre, I will sing praises to you. Psalms 144:9 You are he who gives salvation to kings, who rescues David, his servant, from the deadly sword. Psalms 144:10 Rescue me, and deliver me out of the hands of foreigners, whose mouths speak deceit, whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood. Psalms 144:11 Then our sons will be like well-nurtured plants, our daughters like pillars carved to adorn a palace. Psalms 144:12 Our barns are full, filled with all kinds of provision. Our sheep produce thousands and ten thousands in our fields. Psalms 144:13 Our oxen will pull heavy loads. There is no breaking in, and no going away, and no outcry in our streets. Psalms 144:14 Happy are the people who are in such a situation. Happy are the people whose God is the LORD. Psalms 144:15

title: Psalm 145:1–21
context: A Song of Praise. Of David—an alphabetic (acrostic) hymn: he extols God his King, blessing the name forever, day by day. Great is the LORD; His greatness unsearchable. Generations commend works and mighty acts; he meditates on majesty and wondrous works; they speak of awesome deeds and abundant goodness. The LORD is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love—good to all, mercy over all He has made. Works give thanks; saints bless; they tell kingdom glory and power. His kingdom is everlasting; [He is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.He upholds the falling, raises the bowed down, opens His hand to satisfy the desire of every living thing, is righteous and kind, near to those who call in truth, grants the desire of those who fear Him, preserves those who love Him, and destroys the wicked. Mouth and all flesh bless His holy name forever.
text: Psalm 145:1–21 Psalms A Song of Praise. Of David—an alphabetic (acrostic) hymn: he extols God his King, blessing the name forever, day by day. Great is the LORD; His greatness unsearchable. Generations commend works and mighty acts; he meditates on majesty and wondrous works; they speak of awesome deeds and abundant goodness. The LORD is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love—good to all, mercy over all He has made. Works give thanks; saints bless; they tell kingdom glory and power. His kingdom is everlasting; [He is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.He upholds the falling, raises the bowed down, opens His hand to satisfy the desire of every living thing, is righteous and kind, near to those who call in truth, grants the desire of those who fear Him, preserves those who love Him, and destroys the wicked. Mouth and all flesh bless His holy name forever. I will exalt you, my God, the King. I will praise your name forever and ever. Psalms 145:1 Every day I will praise you. I will extol your name forever and ever. Psalms 145:2 Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised! His greatness is unsearchable. Psalms 145:3 One generation will commend your works to another, and will declare your mighty acts. Psalms 145:4 I will meditate on the glorious majesty of your honor, on your wondrous works. Psalms 145:5 Men will speak of the might of your awesome acts. I will declare your greatness. Psalms 145:6 They will utter the memory of your great goodness, and will sing of your righteousness. Psalms 145:7 The LORD is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great loving kindness. Psalms 145:8 The LORD is good to all. His tender mercies are over all his works. Psalms 145:9 All your works will give thanks to you, LORD. Your saints will extol you. Psalms 145:10 They will speak of the glory of your kingdom, and talk about your power, Psalms 145:11 to make known to the sons of men his mighty acts, the glory of the majesty of his kingdom. Psalms 145:12 Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. Your dominion endures throughout all generations. The LORD is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds. Psalms 145:13 The LORD upholds all who fall, and raises up all those who are bowed down. Psalms 145:14 The eyes of all wait for you. You give them their food in due season. Psalms 145:15 You open your hand, and satisfy the desire of every living thing. Psalms 145:16 The LORD is righteous in all his ways, and gracious in all his works. Psalms 145:17 The LORD is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth. Psalms 145:18 He will fulfill the desire of those who fear him. He also will hear their cry, and will save them. Psalms 145:19 The LORD preserves all those who love him, but he will destroy all the wicked. Psalms 145:20 My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD. Let all flesh bless his holy name forever and ever. Psalms 145:21

title: Psalm 146:1–10
context: First of the final Hallelujah doxologies that close the Psalter: Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD, my soul—while life and being last. Put your trust in princes, in a son of man with no salvation; when spirit departs, and he returns to earth and thoughts perish. Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the LORD, his God—Maker of heaven, earth, sea, and all in them; who keeps truth forever; who executes justice for the oppressed, feeds the hungry, sets prisoners free, opens blind eyes, lifts the bowed down, loves the righteous, watches sojourners, upholds widow and fatherless, and ruins the wicked’s way. The LORD reigns forever, Zion’s God to all generations. Praise the LORD!
text: Psalm 146:1–10 Psalms First of the final Hallelujah doxologies that close the Psalter: Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD, my soul—while life and being last. Put your trust in princes, in a son of man with no salvation; when spirit departs, and he returns to earth and thoughts perish. Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the LORD, his God—Maker of heaven, earth, sea, and all in them; who keeps truth forever; who executes justice for the oppressed, feeds the hungry, sets prisoners free, opens blind eyes, lifts the bowed down, loves the righteous, watches sojourners, upholds widow and fatherless, and ruins the wicked’s way. The LORD reigns forever, Zion’s God to all generations. Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD, my soul. Psalms 146:1 While I live, I will praise the LORD. I will sing praises to my God as long as I exist. Psalms 146:2 Don’t put your trust in princes, in a son of man in whom there is no help. Psalms 146:3 His spirit departs, and he returns to the earth. In that very day, his thoughts perish. Psalms 146:4 Happy is he who has the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the LORD, his God, Psalms 146:5 who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them; who keeps truth forever; Psalms 146:6 who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry. The LORD frees the prisoners. Psalms 146:7 The LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD raises up those who are bowed down. The LORD loves the righteous. Psalms 146:8 The LORD preserves the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and widow, but he turns the way of the wicked upside down. Psalms 146:9 The LORD will reign forever; your God, O Zion, to all generations. Praise the LORD! Psalms 146:10

title: Psalm 147:1–20
context: Final Hallelujah doxologies (146–150) continue: praise is good and fitting; the LORD builds Jerusalem, gathers outcasts, heals the brokenhearted, numbers the stars, lifts the humble, and feeds beasts and ravens. He delights not in horse or human strength but in those who fear Him and hope in his loving kindness. Zion’s gates, peace, and wheat; snow, frost, and ice obey His swift word. He declares statutes to Jacob as to no other nation—shared praise closing toward the Psalter’s end.
text: Psalm 147:1–20 Psalms Final Hallelujah doxologies (146–150) continue: praise is good and fitting; the LORD builds Jerusalem, gathers outcasts, heals the brokenhearted, numbers the stars, lifts the humble, and feeds beasts and ravens. He delights not in horse or human strength but in those who fear Him and hope in his loving kindness. Zion’s gates, peace, and wheat; snow, frost, and ice obey His swift word. He declares statutes to Jacob as to no other nation—shared praise closing toward the Psalter’s end. Praise the LORD, for it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant and fitting to praise him. Psalms 147:1 The LORD builds up Jerusalem. He gathers together the outcasts of Israel. Psalms 147:2 He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds. Psalms 147:3 He counts the number of the stars. He calls them all by their names. Psalms 147:4 Great is our Lord, and mighty in power. His understanding is infinite. Psalms 147:5 The LORD upholds the humble. He brings the wicked down to the ground. Psalms 147:6 Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving. Sing praises on the harp to our God, Psalms 147:7 who covers the sky with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass grow on the mountains. Psalms 147:8 He provides food for the livestock, and for the young ravens when they call. Psalms 147:9 He doesn’t delight in the strength of the horse. He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man. Psalms 147:10 The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his loving kindness. Psalms 147:11 Praise the LORD, Jerusalem! Praise your God, Zion! Psalms 147:12 For he has strengthened the bars of your gates. He has blessed your children within you. Psalms 147:13 He makes peace in your borders. He fills you with the finest of the wheat. Psalms 147:14 He sends out his commandment to the earth. His word runs very swiftly. Psalms 147:15 He gives snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes. Psalms 147:16 He hurls down his hail like pebbles. Who can stand before his cold? Psalms 147:17 He sends out his word, and melts them. He causes his wind to blow, and the waters flow. Psalms 147:18 He shows his word to Jacob, his statutes and his ordinances to Israel. Psalms 147:19 He has not done this for just any nation. They don’t know his ordinances. Praise the LORD! Psalms 147:20

title: Psalm 148:1–14
context: Cosmic Hallelujah in the final doxologies: praise the LORD from the heavens—angels, hosts, sun, moon, shining stars, highest heavens, and waters above—for He commanded and they were created, established by a decree that shall not pass. From the earth: great sea creatures, deeps, fire, hail, snow, clouds, stormy wind, fulfilling his word, mountains, trees, beasts, birds; then kings, peoples, princes, young and old. His name alone is exalted; He has raised the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints, Israel near to Him.
text: Psalm 148:1–14 Psalms Cosmic Hallelujah in the final doxologies: praise the LORD from the heavens—angels, hosts, sun, moon, shining stars, highest heavens, and waters above—for He commanded and they were created, established by a decree that shall not pass. From the earth: great sea creatures, deeps, fire, hail, snow, clouds, stormy wind, fulfilling his word, mountains, trees, beasts, birds; then kings, peoples, princes, young and old. His name alone is exalted; He has raised the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints, Israel near to Him. Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD from the heavens! Praise him in the heights! Psalms 148:1 Praise him, all his angels! Praise him, all his army! Psalms 148:2 Praise him, sun and moon! Praise him, all you shining stars! Psalms 148:3 Praise him, you heavens of heavens, you waters that are above the heavens. Psalms 148:4 Let them praise the LORD’s name, for he commanded, and they were created. Psalms 148:5 He has also established them forever and ever. He has made a decree which will not pass away. Psalms 148:6 Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures, and all depths, Psalms 148:7 lightning and hail, snow and clouds, stormy wind, fulfilling his word, Psalms 148:8 mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars, Psalms 148:9 wild animals and all livestock, small creatures and flying birds, Psalms 148:10 kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all judges of the earth, Psalms 148:11 both young men and maidens, old men and children. Psalms 148:12 Let them praise the LORD’s name, for his name alone is exalted. His glory is above the earth and the heavens. Psalms 148:13 He has lifted up the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints, even of the children of Israel, a people near to him. Praise the LORD! Psalms 148:14

context: Assembly Hallelujah among the final doxologies: sing a new song in the assembly of the saints. Let Israel rejoice in the Maker and Zion be joyful in their King with dancing, tambourine, and lyre. The LORD takes pleasure in His people and crowns the humble with salvation. Godly ones exult; high praises in the throat and two-edged sword in hand execute written judgment—honor for All his saints have this honor. Praise the LORD!
