Psalms 149:2 Let them praise his name in the dance! Let them sing praises to him with tambourine and harp! Psalms 149:3 For the LORD takes pleasure in his people. He crowns the humble with salvation. Psalms 149:4 Let the saints rejoice in honor. Let them sing for joy on their beds. Psalms 149:5 May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a two-edged sword in their hand, Psalms 149:6 to execute vengeance on the nations, and punishments on the peoples; Psalms 149:7 to bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron; Psalms 149:8 to execute on them the written judgment. All his saints have this honor. Praise the LORD! Psalms 149:9

title: Psalm 15:1–5
context: Psalm 15 asks who may sojourn in the LORD’s tent and dwell on his holy hill, then answers with a portrait of integrity: walking blamelessly, doing what is right, speaking truth in the heart; refusing slander, neighbor-harm, and easy reproach; despising the vile while honoring those who fear the LORD; keeping costly oaths; refusing predatory interest and bribes against the innocent—and promising that the one who does these things shall never be shaken.
text: Psalm 15:1–5 Psalms Psalm 15 asks who may sojourn in the LORD’s tent and dwell on his holy hill, then answers with a portrait of integrity: walking blamelessly, doing what is right, speaking truth in the heart; refusing slander, neighbor-harm, and easy reproach; despising the vile while honoring those who fear the LORD; keeping costly oaths; refusing predatory interest and bribes against the innocent—and promising that the one who does these things shall never be shaken. LORD, who shall dwell in your sanctuary? Who shall live on your holy hill? Psalms 15:1 He who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart; Psalms 15:2 he who doesn’t slander with his tongue, nor does evil to his friend, nor casts slurs against his fellow man; Psalms 15:3 in whose eyes a vile man is despised, but who honors those who fear the LORD; he who keeps an oath even when it hurts, and doesn’t change; Psalms 15:4 he who doesn’t lend out his money for usury, nor take a bribe against the innocent. He who does these things shall never be shaken. Psalms 15:5

title: Psalm 150:1–6
context: Closing doxology of the Psalter and last of the final Hallelujahs (146–150): praise God in His sanctuary and in His mighty heavens; praise Him for mighty deeds and according to His excellent greatness. Trumpet, lute, harp, tambourine, dance, strings, pipe, sounding and clashing cymbals—then the widest summons: let everything that has breath praise the LORD. Praise the LORD!

Psalms 150:2 Praise him with the sounding of the trumpet! Praise him with harp and lyre! Psalms 150:3 Praise him with tambourine and dancing! Praise him with stringed instruments and flute! Psalms 150:4 Praise him with loud cymbals! Praise him with resounding cymbals! Psalms 150:5 Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD! Psalms 150:6

title: Psalm 16:1–11
context: Psalm 16 is David’s miktam of refuge and delight: he takes shelter in God, confesses he has no good apart from the LORD, delights in the saints, refuses idol sorrows and bloody libations, and names the LORD as portion, cup, and held lot—pleasant lines and a beautiful inheritance. Counsel by night steadies him; the LORD at his right hand keeps him from being shaken, so heart and flesh rejoice in security. The climax trusts that God will not abandon his soul to Sheol or let his Holy One see corruption, and asks for the path of life—fullness of joy in God’s presence and pleasures forevermore at his right hand. The apostles read the Holy One and incorruption of Christ’s resurrection (Acts 2:25–32; 13:34–37).
text: Psalm 16:1–11 Psalms Psalm 16 is David’s miktam of refuge and delight: he takes shelter in God, confesses he has no good apart from the LORD, delights in the saints, refuses idol sorrows and bloody libations, and names the LORD as portion, cup, and held lot—pleasant lines and a beautiful inheritance. Counsel by night steadies him; the LORD at his right hand keeps him from being shaken, so heart and flesh rejoice in security. The climax trusts that God will not abandon his soul to Sheol or let his Holy One see corruption, and asks for the path of life—fullness of joy in God’s presence and pleasures forevermore at his right hand. The apostles read the Holy One and incorruption of Christ’s resurrection (Acts 2:25–32; 13:34–37). Preserve me, God, for I take refuge in you. Psalms 16:1 My soul, you have said to the LORD, “You are my Lord. Apart from you I have no good thing.” Psalms 16:2 As for the saints who are on the earth, they are the excellent ones in whom is all my delight. Psalms 16:3 Their sorrows shall be multiplied who give gifts to another god. Their drink offerings of blood I will not offer, nor take their names on my lips. Psalms 16:4 The LORD assigned my portion and my cup. You made my lot secure. Psalms 16:5 The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance. Psalms 16:6 I will bless the LORD, who has given me counsel. Yes, my heart instructs me in the night seasons. Psalms 16:7 I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Psalms 16:8 Therefore my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices. My body shall also dwell in safety. Psalms 16:9 For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption. Psalms 16:10 You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more. Psalms 16:11

title: Psalm 17:1–15
context: Psalm 17 is David’s prayer of a just cause: he asks the LORD to hear a cry from lips free of deceit, to let vindication come from God’s presence, and to behold the right. Night-tried and tested, he claims a heart where God will find nothing of the charge, a mouth purposed not to transgress, and steps held to God’s paths by the word of God’s lips—away from the ways of the violent. He calls on God as Savior of those who seek refuge, asking to be kept as the apple of the eye and hidden in the shadow of wings from surrounding deadly enemies—fat-hearted, arrogant, lion-like. He pleads that God arise, confront, and deliver him from men of the world whose portion is this life, and ends contrasting their treasure and children with his own hope: to behold God’s face in righteousness and, when he awakes, to be satisfied with God’s likeness.
text: Psalm 17:1–15 Psalms Psalm 17 is David’s prayer of a just cause: he asks the LORD to hear a cry from lips free of deceit, to let vindication come from God’s presence, and to behold the right. Night-tried and tested, he claims a heart where God will find nothing of the charge, a mouth purposed not to transgress, and steps held to God’s paths by the word of God’s lips—away from the ways of the violent. He calls on God as Savior of those who seek refuge, asking to be kept as the apple of the eye and hidden in the shadow of wings from surrounding deadly enemies—fat-hearted, arrogant, lion-like. He pleads that God arise, confront, and deliver him from men of the world whose portion is this life, and ends contrasting their treasure and children with his own hope: to behold God’s face in righteousness and, when he awakes, to be satisfied with God’s likeness. Hear, LORD, my righteous plea. Give ear to my prayer that doesn’t go out of deceitful lips. Psalms 17:1 Let my sentence come out of your presence. Let your eyes look on equity. Psalms 17:2 You have proved my heart. You have visited me in the night. You have tried me, and found nothing. I have resolved that my mouth shall not disobey. Psalms 17:3 As for the deeds of men, by the word of your lips, I have kept myself from the ways of the violent. Psalms 17:4 My steps have held fast to your paths. My feet have not slipped. Psalms 17:5 I have called on you, for you will answer me, God. Turn your ear to me. Hear my speech. Psalms 17:6 Show your marvelous loving kindness, you who save those who take refuge by your right hand from their enemies. Psalms 17:7 Keep me as the apple of your eye. Hide me under the shadow of your wings, Psalms 17:8 from the wicked who oppress me, my deadly enemies, who surround me. Psalms 17:9 They close up their callous hearts. With their mouth they speak proudly. Psalms 17:10 They have now surrounded us in our steps. They set their eyes to cast us down to the earth. Psalms 17:11 He is like a lion that is greedy of his prey, as it were a young lion lurking in secret places. Psalms 17:12 Arise, LORD, confront him. Cast him down. Deliver my soul from the wicked by your sword, Psalms 17:13 from men by your hand, LORD, from men of the world, whose portion is in this life. You fill the belly of your cherished ones. Your sons have plenty, and they store up wealth for their children. Psalms 17:14 As for me, I shall see your face in righteousness. I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with seeing your form. Psalms 17:15

title: Psalm 18:1–50
context: Psalm 18 is David’s long song of deliverance—also in 2 Samuel 22—sung when the LORD had saved him from all his enemies and from Saul. He opens with whole-souled love to the LORD his strength, heaps names of refuge, and recalls cords of death and torrents of destruction that drove him to cry until God heard from his temple. Then a theophany: earth quaking, heavens bowed, cherub and wind, darkness and hail, thunder, arrows, and foundations laid bare, until God draws him from many waters, rescues him from foes too mighty, and brings him into a broad place because he delighted in him. David pleads righteousness and clean hands in the controversy, kept ways and statutes, blamelessness kept from guilt; God shows himself merciful to the merciful and opposes the crooked, saves the humble, lights the lamp, and proves a perfect way and true word as shield for all who take refuge. Equipped and trained, shielded by salvation and gentleness, he pursues and consumes enemies who cry in vain to the LORD, is made head of nations, and ends blessing the living rock, praising among the nations, and confessing great salvation and forever steadfast love to the anointed, to David and to his offspring, and above all to the Messiah.
text: Psalm 18:1–50 Psalms Psalm 18 is David’s long song of deliverance—also in 2 Samuel 22—sung when the LORD had saved him from all his enemies and from Saul. He opens with whole-souled love to the LORD his strength, heaps names of refuge, and recalls cords of death and torrents of destruction that drove him to cry until God heard from his temple. Then a theophany: earth quaking, heavens bowed, cherub and wind, darkness and hail, thunder, arrows, and foundations laid bare, until God draws him from many waters, rescues him from foes too mighty, and brings him into a broad place because he delighted in him. David pleads righteousness and clean hands in the controversy, kept ways and statutes, blamelessness kept from guilt; God shows himself merciful to the merciful and opposes the crooked, saves the humble, lights the lamp, and proves a perfect way and true word as shield for all who take refuge. Equipped and trained, shielded by salvation and gentleness, he pursues and consumes enemies who cry in vain to the LORD, is made head of nations, and ends blessing the living rock, praising among the nations, and confessing great salvation and forever steadfast love to the anointed, to David and to his offspring, and above all to the Messiah. I love you, LORD, my strength. Psalms 18:1 The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower. Psalms 18:2 I call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; and I am saved from my enemies. Psalms 18:3 The cords of death surrounded me. The floods of ungodliness made me afraid. Psalms 18:4 The cords of Sheol were around me. The snares of death came on me. Psalms 18:5 In my distress I called on the LORD, and cried to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry before him came into his ears. Psalms 18:6 Then the earth shook and trembled. The foundations also of the mountains quaked and were shaken, because he was angry. Psalms 18:7 Smoke went out of his nostrils. Consuming fire came out of his mouth. Coals were kindled by it. Psalms 18:8 He bowed the heavens also, and came down. Thick darkness was under his feet. Psalms 18:9 He rode on a cherub, and flew. Yes, he soared on the wings of the wind. Psalms 18:10 He made darkness his hiding place, his pavilion around him, darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies. Psalms 18:11 At the brightness before him his thick clouds passed, hailstones and coals of fire. Psalms 18:12 The LORD also thundered in the sky. The Most High uttered his voice: hailstones and coals of fire. Psalms 18:13 He sent out his arrows, and scattered them. He routed them with great lightning bolts. Psalms 18:14 Then the channels of waters appeared. The foundations of the world were laid bare at your rebuke, LORD, at the blast of the breath of your nostrils. Psalms 18:15 He sent from on high. He took me. He drew me out of many waters. Psalms 18:16 He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me; for they were too mighty for me. Psalms 18:17 They came on me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support. Psalms 18:18 He brought me out also into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me. Psalms 18:19 The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness. According to the cleanness of my hands, he has recompensed me. Psalms 18:20 For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God. Psalms 18:21 For all his ordinances were before me. I didn’t put away his statutes from me. Psalms 18:22 I was also blameless with him. I kept myself from my iniquity. Psalms 18:23 Therefore the LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his eyesight. Psalms 18:24 With the merciful you will show yourself merciful. With the perfect man, you will show yourself perfect. Psalms 18:25 With the pure, you will show yourself pure. With the crooked you will show yourself shrewd. Psalms 18:26 For you will save the afflicted people, but the arrogant eyes you will bring down. Psalms 18:27 For you will light my lamp, LORD. My God will light up my darkness. Psalms 18:28 For by you, I advance through a troop. By my God, I leap over a wall. Psalms 18:29 As for God, his way is perfect. The LORD’s word is tried. He is a shield to all those who take refuge in him. Psalms 18:30 For who is God, except the LORD? Who is a rock, besides our God, Psalms 18:31 the God who arms me with strength, and makes my way perfect? Psalms 18:32 He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and sets me on my high places. Psalms 18:33 He teaches my hands to war, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze. Psalms 18:34 You have also given me the shield of your salvation. Your right hand sustains me. Your gentleness has made me great. Psalms 18:35 You have enlarged my steps under me, My feet have not slipped. Psalms 18:36 I will pursue my enemies, and overtake them. I won’t turn away until they are consumed. Psalms 18:37 I will strike them through, so that they will not be able to rise. They shall fall under my feet. Psalms 18:38 For you have armed me with strength to the battle. You have subdued under me those who rose up against me. Psalms 18:39 You have also made my enemies turn their backs to me, that I might cut off those who hate me. Psalms 18:40 They cried, but there was no one to save; even to the LORD, but he didn’t answer them. Psalms 18:41 Then I beat them small as the dust before the wind. I cast them out as the mire of the streets. Psalms 18:42 You have delivered me from the strivings of the people. You have made me the head of the nations. A people whom I have not known shall serve me. Psalms 18:43 As soon as they hear of me they shall obey me. The foreigners shall submit themselves to me. Psalms 18:44 The foreigners shall fade away, and shall come trembling out of their strongholds. Psalms 18:45 The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock. Exalted be the God of my salvation, Psalms 18:46 even the God who executes vengeance for me, and subdues peoples under me. Psalms 18:47 He rescues me from my enemies. Yes, you lift me up above those who rise up against me. You deliver me from the violent man. Psalms 18:48 Therefore I will give thanks to you, LORD, among the nations, and will sing praises to your name. Psalms 18:49 He gives great deliverance to his king, and shows loving kindness to his anointed, to David and to his offspring, forever more. Psalms 18:50

title: Psalm 19:1–14
context: Psalm 19 moves from creation’s witness to the Word’s excellence and ends in prayer. The heavens declare God’s glory; day and night pour out speech; their voice goes through all the earth, and the sun runs its course with joy so that nothing is hidden from its heat. Then the psalm prefers the law of the LORD—perfect, sure, right, pure, clean, true—reviving the soul, making wise the simple, rejoicing the heart, enlightening the eyes, more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey. By them the servant is warned, and in keeping them there is great reward; yet who can discern his errors? So David asks to be declared innocent from hidden faults, kept back from presumptuous sins lest they rule him, and that mouth and heart meditation be acceptable to the LORD his rock and redeemer.
text: Psalm 19:1–14 Psalms Psalm 19 moves from creation’s witness to the Word’s excellence and ends in prayer. The heavens declare God’s glory; day and night pour out speech; their voice goes through all the earth, and the sun runs its course with joy so that nothing is hidden from its heat. Then the psalm prefers the law of the LORD—perfect, sure, right, pure, clean, true—reviving the soul, making wise the simple, rejoicing the heart, enlightening the eyes, more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey. By them the servant is warned, and in keeping them there is great reward; yet who can discern his errors? So David asks to be declared innocent from hidden faults, kept back from presumptuous sins lest they rule him, and that mouth and heart meditation be acceptable to the LORD his rock and redeemer. The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork. Psalms 19:1 Day after day they pour out speech, and night after night they display knowledge. Psalms 19:2 There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard. Psalms 19:3 Their voice has gone out through all the earth, their words to the end of the world. In them he has set a tent for the sun, Psalms 19:4 which is as a bridegroom coming out of his room, like a strong man rejoicing to run his course. Psalms 19:5 His going out is from the end of the heavens, his circuit to its ends. There is nothing hidden from its heat. Psalms 19:6 The LORD’s law is perfect, restoring the soul. The LORD’s covenant is sure, making wise the simple. Psalms 19:7 The LORD’s precepts are right, rejoicing the heart. The LORD’s commandment is pure, enlightening the eyes. Psalms 19:8 The fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever. The LORD’s ordinances are true, and righteous altogether. Psalms 19:9 They are more to be desired than gold, yes, than much fine gold, sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb. Psalms 19:10 Moreover your servant is warned by them. In keeping them there is great reward. Psalms 19:11 Who can discern his errors? Forgive me from hidden errors. Psalms 19:12 Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins. Let them not have dominion over me. Then I will be upright. I will be blameless and innocent of great transgression. Psalms 19:13 Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, LORD, my rock, and my redeemer. Psalms 19:14

title: Psalm 2:1–12
context: Psalm 2 sets the nations’ rage and the rulers’ plot against the LORD and his Anointed beside the One who sits in the heavens: he laughs, speaks in wrath, and sets his King on Zion. The decree names the Son—“Today I have become your father”—promises the nations as heritage, and warns with an iron rod; kings must be wise, serve with fear, kiss the Son, and take refuge, lest wrath be quickly kindled.
text: Psalm 2:1–12 Psalms Psalm 2 sets the nations’ rage and the rulers’ plot against the LORD and his Anointed beside the One who sits in the heavens: he laughs, speaks in wrath, and sets his King on Zion. The decree names the Son—“Today I have become your father”—promises the nations as heritage, and warns with an iron rod; kings must be wise, serve with fear, kiss the Son, and take refuge, lest wrath be quickly kindled. Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing? Psalms 2:1 The kings of the earth take a stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his Anointed, saying, Psalms 2:2 “Let’s break their bonds apart, and cast their cords from us.” Psalms 2:3 He who sits in the heavens will laugh. The Lord will have them in derision. Psalms 2:4 Then he will speak to them in his anger, and terrify them in his wrath: Psalms 2:5 “Yet I have set my King on my holy hill of Zion.” Psalms 2:6 I will tell of the decree: The LORD said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father. Psalms 2:7 Ask of me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession. Psalms 2:8 You shall break them with a rod of iron. You shall dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” Psalms 2:9 Now therefore be wise, you kings. Be instructed, you judges of the earth. Psalms 2:10 Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Psalms 2:11 Give sincere homage to the Son, lest he be angry, and you perish on the way, for his wrath will soon be kindled. Blessed are all those who take refuge in him. Psalms 2:12

title: Psalm 20:1–9
context: Psalm 20 is the people’s prayer for the LORD’s anointed in the day of trouble: that the God of Jacob would answer and protect, send help from the sanctuary and support from Zion, remember offerings, grant the heart’s desire, and fulfill petitions—so the congregation may shout for joy and set up banners in God’s name. Confidence rises: the LORD saves his anointed from holy heaven; some trust in chariots and horses, but the faithful trust in the name of the LORD their God, rise while others fall, and cry, Save, LORD! Let the King—answer us when we call.
text: Psalm 20:1–9 Psalms Psalm 20 is the people’s prayer for the LORD’s anointed in the day of trouble: that the God of Jacob would answer and protect, send help from the sanctuary and support from Zion, remember offerings, grant the heart’s desire, and fulfill petitions—so the congregation may shout for joy and set up banners in God’s name. Confidence rises: the LORD saves his anointed from holy heaven; some trust in chariots and horses, but the faithful trust in the name of the LORD their God, rise while others fall, and cry, Save, LORD! Let the King—answer us when we call. May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble. May the name of the God of Jacob set you up on high, Psalms 20:1 send you help from the sanctuary, grant you support from Zion, Psalms 20:2 remember all your offerings, and accept your burned sacrifice. Selah. Psalms 20:3 May he grant you your heart’s desire, and fulfill all your counsel. Psalms 20:4 We will triumph in your salvation. In the name of our God, we will set up our banners. May the LORD grant all your requests. Psalms 20:5 Now I know that the LORD saves his anointed. He will answer him from his holy heaven, with the saving strength of his right hand. Psalms 20:6 Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God. Psalms 20:7 They are bowed down and fallen, but we rise up, and stand upright. Psalms 20:8 Save, LORD! Let the King answer us when we call! Psalms 20:9

title: Psalm 21:1–13
context: Psalm 21 answers Psalm 20’s prayer with thanksgiving for the LORD’s anointed: the king rejoices in God’s strength and salvation; his heart’s desire and lip’s request are granted; rich blessings and a gold crown meet him; he asked life and received length of days forever and ever; glory, splendor, majesty, and gladness in God’s presence mark him; trusting in the LORD and upheld by the Most High’s steadfast love, he shall not be moved. Then the psalm turns outward: the LORD’s hand finds enemies, makes them a blazing oven in wrath, cuts off their offspring, frustrates their mischief, and puts them to flight—until the congregation closes, Be exalted, LORD, in your strength, so we will sing and praise your power.
text: Psalm 21:1–13 Psalms Psalm 21 answers Psalm 20’s prayer with thanksgiving for the LORD’s anointed: the king rejoices in God’s strength and salvation; his heart’s desire and lip’s request are granted; rich blessings and a gold crown meet him; he asked life and received length of days forever and ever; glory, splendor, majesty, and gladness in God’s presence mark him; trusting in the LORD and upheld by the Most High’s steadfast love, he shall not be moved. Then the psalm turns outward: the LORD’s hand finds enemies, makes them a blazing oven in wrath, cuts off their offspring, frustrates their mischief, and puts them to flight—until the congregation closes, Be exalted, LORD, in your strength, so we will sing and praise your power. The king rejoices in your strength, LORD! How greatly he rejoices in your salvation! Psalms 21:1 You have given him his heart’s desire, and have not withheld the request of his lips. Selah. Psalms 21:2 For you meet him with the blessings of goodness. You set a crown of fine gold on his head. Psalms 21:3 He asked life of you and you gave it to him, even length of days forever and ever. Psalms 21:4 His glory is great in your salvation. You lay honor and majesty on him. Psalms 21:5 For you make him most blessed forever. You make him glad with joy in your presence. Psalms 21:6 For the king trusts in the LORD. Through the loving kindness of the Most High, he shall not be moved. Psalms 21:7 Your hand will find out all of your enemies. Your right hand will find out those who hate you. Psalms 21:8 You will make them as a fiery furnace in the time of your anger. The LORD will swallow them up in his wrath. The fire shall devour them. Psalms 21:9 You will destroy their descendants from the earth, their posterity from among the children of men. Psalms 21:10 For they intended evil against you. They plotted evil against you which cannot succeed. Psalms 21:11 For you will make them turn their back, when you aim drawn bows at their face. Psalms 21:12 Be exalted, LORD, in your strength, so we will sing and praise your power. Psalms 21:13

title: Psalm 22:1–31
context: Psalm 22 moves from the forsaken cry—“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”—through scorn, thirst, pierced hands and feet, and lots cast for clothing, to the rescued singer who tells God’s name to his brothers, calls Jacob’s seed to praise, and sees the ends of the earth remember and turn. Shared apostolic christology hears the cross in the opening and the passion details, Hebrews 2 in the congregational praise, and worldwide worship in the closing vows—humiliation answered by exaltation and gospel praise to a people yet unborn.
text: Psalm 22:1–31 Psalms Psalm 22 moves from the forsaken cry—“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”—through scorn, thirst, pierced hands and feet, and lots cast for clothing, to the rescued singer who tells God’s name to his brothers, calls Jacob’s seed to praise, and sees the ends of the earth remember and turn. Shared apostolic christology hears the cross in the opening and the passion details, Hebrews 2 in the congregational praise, and worldwide worship in the closing vows—humiliation answered by exaltation and gospel praise to a people yet unborn. My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning? Psalms 22:1 My God, I cry in the daytime, but you don’t answer; in the night season, and am not silent. Psalms 22:2 But you are holy, you who inhabit the praises of Israel. Psalms 22:3 Our fathers trusted in you. They trusted, and you delivered them. Psalms 22:4 They cried to you, and were delivered. They trusted in you, and were not disappointed. Psalms 22:5 But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised by the people. Psalms 22:6 All those who see me mock me. They insult me with their lips. They shake their heads, saying, Psalms 22:7 “He trusts in the LORD. Let him deliver him. Let him rescue him, since he delights in him.” Psalms 22:8 But you brought me out of the womb. You made me trust while at my mother’s breasts. Psalms 22:9 I was thrown on you from my mother’s womb. You are my God since my mother bore me. Psalms 22:10 Don’t be far from me, for trouble is near. For there is no one to help. Psalms 22:11 Many bulls have surrounded me. Strong bulls of Bashan have encircled me. Psalms 22:12 They open their mouths wide against me, lions tearing prey and roaring. Psalms 22:13 I am poured out like water. All my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax. It is melted within me. Psalms 22:14 My strength is dried up like a potsherd. My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You have brought me into the dust of death. Psalms 22:15 For dogs have surrounded me. A company of evildoers have enclosed me. They have pierced my hands and feet. Psalms 22:16 I can count all of my bones. They look and stare at me. Psalms 22:17 They divide my garments among them. They cast lots for my clothing. Psalms 22:18 But don’t be far off, LORD. You are my help. Hurry to help me! Psalms 22:19 Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog. Psalms 22:20 Save me from the lion’s mouth! Yes, you have rescued me from the horns of the wild oxen. Psalms 22:21 I will declare your name to my brothers. Among the assembly, I will praise you. Psalms 22:22 You who fear the LORD, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, glorify him! Stand in awe of him, all you descendants of Israel! Psalms 22:23 For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard. Psalms 22:24 My praise of you comes in the great assembly. I will pay my vows before those who fear him. Psalms 22:25 The humble shall eat and be satisfied. They shall praise the LORD who seek after him. Let your hearts live forever. Psalms 22:26 All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the LORD. All the relatives of the nations shall worship before you. Psalms 22:27 For the kingdom is the LORD’s. He is the ruler over the nations. Psalms 22:28 All the rich ones of the earth shall eat and worship. All those who go down to the dust shall bow before him, even he who can’t keep his soul alive. Psalms 22:29 Posterity shall serve him. Future generations shall be told about the Lord. Psalms 22:30 They shall come and shall declare his righteousness to a people that shall be born, for he has done it. Psalms 22:31

title: Psalm 23:1–6
context: Psalm 23 is David’s shepherd song of quiet trust: the LORD is his shepherd, so he shall not want—made to lie down in green pastures, led beside still waters, restored in soul, and guided in the paths of righteousness for the LORD’s name’s sake. Even in the valley of the shadow of death he fears no evil, for the Shepherd is with him; rod and staff comfort. The image shifts to a host’s table prepared in enemies’ sight, head anointed, cup overflowing—and ends in sure hope that goodness and mercy will follow all his days, and that he will dwell in the LORD’s house forever.
text: Psalm 23:1–6 Psalms Psalm 23 is David’s shepherd song of quiet trust: the LORD is his shepherd, so he shall not want—made to lie down in green pastures, led beside still waters, restored in soul, and guided in the paths of righteousness for the LORD’s name’s sake. Even in the valley of the shadow of death he fears no evil, for the Shepherd is with him; rod and staff comfort. The image shifts to a host’s table prepared in enemies’ sight, head anointed, cup overflowing—and ends in sure hope that goodness and mercy will follow all his days, and that he will dwell in the LORD’s house forever. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. Psalms 23:1 He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. Psalms 23:2 He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake. Psalms 23:3 Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me. Psalms 23:4 You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over. Psalms 23:5 Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the LORD’s house forever. Psalms 23:6

title: Psalm 24:1–10
context: A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD’s, with its fullness thereof—founded upon the seas—then the question: who may ascend to the LORD’s hill of the LORD and stand in his holy place? Clean hands and a pure heart, no false soul-lifting and no deceitful oath, receive blessing and righteousness from the God of salvation. This is the generation that seeks his face. The gates must lift their heads for the King of glory: the LORD strong and mighty in battle, the LORD of hosts.
text: Psalm 24:1–10 Psalms A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD’s, with its fullness thereof—founded upon the seas—then the question: who may ascend to the LORD’s hill of the LORD and stand in his holy place? Clean hands and a pure heart, no false soul-lifting and no deceitful oath, receive blessing and righteousness from the God of salvation. This is the generation that seeks his face. The gates must lift their heads for the King of glory: the LORD strong and mighty in battle, the LORD of hosts. The earth is the LORD’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it. Psalms 24:1 For he has founded it on the seas, and established it on the floods. Psalms 24:2 Who may ascend to the LORD’s hill? Who may stand in his holy place? Psalms 24:3 He who has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully. Psalms 24:4 He shall receive a blessing from the LORD, righteousness from the God of his salvation. Psalms 24:5 This is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek your face—even Jacob. Selah. Psalms 24:6 Lift up your heads, you gates! Be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in. Psalms 24:7 Who is the King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle. Psalms 24:8 Lift up your heads, you gates; yes, lift them up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in. Psalms 24:9 Who is this King of glory? The LORD of Armies is the King of glory! Selah. Psalms 24:10

title: Psalm 25:1–22
context: A Psalm of David. To you, LORD, I lift up my soul: trust that will not be put to shame, waiting that will not be disappointed, and a plea to know the LORD’s ways and be taught his paths. Mercy and steadfast love from of old are remembered; the sins of youth are not. The LORD who is good and upright instructs sinners and leads the humble; his paths are loving kindness and truth to such as keep his covenant. For his name’s sake he pardons great guilt; the friendship of the LORD is with those who fear him. He makes known his covenant. Afflicted and surrounded by foes, the psalmist asks for deliverance, integrity’s preservation, and Israel’s redemption out of all his troubles.
text: Psalm 25:1–22 Psalms A Psalm of David. To you, LORD, I lift up my soul: trust that will not be put to shame, waiting that will not be disappointed, and a plea to know the LORD’s ways and be taught his paths. Mercy and steadfast love from of old are remembered; the sins of youth are not. The LORD who is good and upright instructs sinners and leads the humble; his paths are loving kindness and truth to such as keep his covenant. For his name’s sake he pardons great guilt; the friendship of the LORD is with those who fear him. He makes known his covenant. Afflicted and surrounded by foes, the psalmist asks for deliverance, integrity’s preservation, and Israel’s redemption out of all his troubles. To you, LORD, I lift up my soul. Psalms 25:1 My God, I have trusted in you. Don’t let me be shamed. Don’t let my enemies triumph over me. Psalms 25:2 Yes, no one who waits for you will be shamed. They will be shamed who deal treacherously without cause. Psalms 25:3 Show me your ways, LORD. Teach me your paths. Psalms 25:4 Guide me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation. I wait for you all day long. Psalms 25:5 LORD, remember your tender mercies and your loving kindness, for they are from old times. Psalms 25:6 Don’t remember the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions. Remember me according to your loving kindness, for your goodness’ sake, LORD. Psalms 25:7 Good and upright is the LORD, therefore he will instruct sinners in the way. Psalms 25:8 He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way. Psalms 25:9 All the paths of the LORD are loving kindness and truth to such as keep his covenant and his testimonies. Psalms 25:10 For your name’s sake, LORD, pardon my iniquity, for it is great. Psalms 25:11 What man is he who fears the LORD? He shall instruct him in the way that he shall choose. Psalms 25:12 His soul will dwell at ease. His offspring will inherit the land. Psalms 25:13 The friendship of the LORD is with those who fear him. He will show them his covenant. Psalms 25:14 My eyes are ever on the LORD, for he will pluck my feet out of the net. Psalms 25:15 Turn to me, and have mercy on me, for I am desolate and afflicted. Psalms 25:16 The troubles of my heart are enlarged. Oh bring me out of my distresses. Psalms 25:17 Consider my affliction and my travail. Forgive all my sins. Psalms 25:18 Consider my enemies, for they are many. They hate me with cruel hatred. Psalms 25:19 Oh keep my soul, and deliver me. Let me not be disappointed, for I take refuge in you. Psalms 25:20 Let integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for you. Psalms 25:21 God, redeem Israel out of all his troubles. Psalms 25:22

title: Psalm 26:1–12
context: Of David. The psalmist asks the LORD to vindicate him for walking in integrity and trusting without wavering; invites God to prove heart and mind; walks by steadfast love and faithfulness; refuses the company of the false and wicked; approaches the altar in innocence with thanksgiving; loves the LORD's house; pleads not to be swept away with the bloodthirsty; renews his integrity while crying for redemption and grace; and stands on level ground to bless the LORD in the great assembly.
text: Psalm 26:1–12 Psalms Of David. The psalmist asks the LORD to vindicate him for walking in integrity and trusting without wavering; invites God to prove heart and mind; walks by steadfast love and faithfulness; refuses the company of the false and wicked; approaches the altar in innocence with thanksgiving; loves the LORD's house; pleads not to be swept away with the bloodthirsty; renews his integrity while crying for redemption and grace; and stands on level ground to bless the LORD in the great assembly. Judge me, LORD, for I have walked in my integrity. I have trusted also in the LORD without wavering. Psalms 26:1 Examine me, LORD, and prove me. Try my heart and my mind. Psalms 26:2 For your loving kindness is before my eyes. I have walked in your truth. Psalms 26:3 I have not sat with deceitful men, neither will I go in with hypocrites. Psalms 26:4 I hate the assembly of evildoers, and will not sit with the wicked. Psalms 26:5 I will wash my hands in innocence, so I will go about your altar, LORD, Psalms 26:6 that I may make the voice of thanksgiving to be heard and tell of all your wondrous deeds. Psalms 26:7 LORD, I love the habitation of your house, the place where your glory dwells. Psalms 26:8 Don’t gather my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloodthirsty men Psalms 26:9 in whose hands is wickedness; their right hand is full of bribes. Psalms 26:10 But as for me, I will walk in my integrity. Redeem me, and be merciful to me. Psalms 26:11 My foot stands in an even place. In the congregations I will bless the LORD. Psalms 26:12

title: Psalm 27:1–14
context: Of David. The psalmist confesses the LORD as his light, salvation, and stronghold so that fear loses its claim; recalls adversaries who stumbled; refuses panic though army and war rise; seeks one thing—to dwell in the LORD's house, gaze on his beauty, and inquire in his temple; trusts shelter, tent, and rock in the day of trouble; looks for his head lifted in praise and song; then cries for grace, answers God's 'Seek my face,' pleads not to be cast off; rests in the LORD who takes him in when father and mother forsake; asks to be taught a level path; begs not to be given up to violent false witnesses; confesses belief that he will look on the LORD's goodness in the land of the living; and exhorts: wait for the LORD; be strong; take courage. Yes, wait for the LORD.
text: Psalm 27:1–14 Psalms Of David. The psalmist confesses the LORD as his light, salvation, and stronghold so that fear loses its claim; recalls adversaries who stumbled; refuses panic though army and war rise; seeks one thing—to dwell in the LORD's house, gaze on his beauty, and inquire in his temple; trusts shelter, tent, and rock in the day of trouble; looks for his head lifted in praise and song; then cries for grace, answers God's 'Seek my face,' pleads not to be cast off; rests in the LORD who takes him in when father and mother forsake; asks to be taught a level path; begs not to be given up to violent false witnesses; confesses belief that he will look on the LORD's goodness in the land of the living; and exhorts: wait for the LORD; be strong; take courage. Yes, wait for the LORD. The LORD is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? The LORD is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid? Psalms 27:1 When evildoers came at me to eat up my flesh, even my adversaries and my foes, they stumbled and fell. Psalms 27:2 Though an army should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear. Though war should rise against me, even then I will be confident. Psalms 27:3 One thing I have asked of the LORD, that I will seek after: that I may dwell in the LORD’s house all the days of my life, to see the LORD’s beauty, and to inquire in his temple. Psalms 27:4 For in the day of trouble, he will keep me secretly in his pavilion. In the secret place of his tabernacle, he will hide me. He will lift me up on a rock. Psalms 27:5 Now my head will be lifted up above my enemies around me. I will offer sacrifices of joy in his tent. I will sing, yes, I will sing praises to the LORD. Psalms 27:6 Hear, LORD, when I cry with my voice. Have mercy also on me, and answer me. Psalms 27:7 When you said, “Seek my face,” my heart said to you, “I will seek your face, LORD.” Psalms 27:8 Don’t hide your face from me. Don’t put your servant away in anger. You have been my help. Don’t abandon me, neither forsake me, God of my salvation. Psalms 27:9 When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up. Psalms 27:10 Teach me your way, LORD. Lead me in a straight path, because of my enemies. Psalms 27:11 Don’t deliver me over to the desire of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen up against me, such as breathe out cruelty. Psalms 27:12 I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living. Psalms 27:13 Wait for the LORD. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for the LORD. Psalms 27:14

title: Psalm 28:1–9
context: Of David. The psalmist calls to the LORD his rock, pleading not to be met with silence lest he become like those who go down into the pit; lifts hands toward the most holy sanctuary with pleas for mercy; begs not to be dragged off with the wicked who speak peace but mischief is in their hearts; asks that workers of evil receive according to their deeds; names their disregard of the LORD's works as the reason they will be torn down and built up no more; then blesses the LORD who has heard; confesses him as strength and shield, trust, help, exultation, and song; declares the LORD the strength of his people and saving refuge of his anointed; and prays: save your people, bless your inheritance. Be their shepherd also, and bear them up forever.
text: Psalm 28:1–9 Psalms Of David. The psalmist calls to the LORD his rock, pleading not to be met with silence lest he become like those who go down into the pit; lifts hands toward the most holy sanctuary with pleas for mercy; begs not to be dragged off with the wicked who speak peace but mischief is in their hearts; asks that workers of evil receive according to their deeds; names their disregard of the LORD's works as the reason they will be torn down and built up no more; then blesses the LORD who has heard; confesses him as strength and shield, trust, help, exultation, and song; declares the LORD the strength of his people and saving refuge of his anointed; and prays: save your people, bless your inheritance. Be their shepherd also, and bear them up forever. To you, LORD, I call. My rock, don’t be deaf to me, lest, if you are silent to me, I would become like those who go down into the pit. Psalms 28:1 Hear the voice of my petitions, when I cry to you, when I lift up my hands toward your Most Holy Place. Psalms 28:2 Don’t draw me away with the wicked, with the workers of iniquity who speak peace with their neighbors, but mischief is in their hearts. Psalms 28:3 Give them according to their work, and according to the wickedness of their doings. Give them according to the operation of their hands. Bring back on them what they deserve. Psalms 28:4 Because they don’t respect the works of the LORD, nor the operation of his hands, he will break them down and not build them up. Psalms 28:5 Blessed be the LORD, because he has heard the voice of my petitions. Psalms 28:6 The LORD is my strength and my shield. My heart has trusted in him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart greatly rejoices. With my song I will thank him. Psalms 28:7 The LORD is their strength. He is a stronghold of salvation to his anointed. Psalms 28:8 Save your people, and bless your inheritance. Be their shepherd also, and bear them up forever. Psalms 28:9

title: Psalm 29:1–11
context: Of David. The psalmist summons heavenly beings to ascribe to the LORD glory and strength; to ascribe the glory due to his name and worship him in the splendor of holiness; then hears the voice of the LORD over the waters as the God of glory thunders; names that voice powerful and full of majesty; watches it break Lebanon's cedars, make Lebanon and Sirion skip, flash forth flames of fire, and shake the wilderness of Kadesh; sees it make the deer calve, and strip the forests bare while in his temple everything says, "Glory!"; confesses the LORD enthroned over the flood and as king forever; and prays that the LORD will give strength to his people and bless them with peace.
text: Psalm 29:1–11 Psalms Of David. The psalmist summons heavenly beings to ascribe to the LORD glory and strength; to ascribe the glory due to his name and worship him in the splendor of holiness; then hears the voice of the LORD over the waters as the God of glory thunders; names that voice powerful and full of majesty; watches it break Lebanon's cedars, make Lebanon and Sirion skip, flash forth flames of fire, and shake the wilderness of Kadesh; sees it make the deer calve, and strip the forests bare while in his temple everything says, "Glory!"; confesses the LORD enthroned over the flood and as king forever; and prays that the LORD will give strength to his people and bless them with peace. Ascribe to the LORD, you sons of the mighty, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength. Psalms 29:1 Ascribe to the LORD the glory due to his name. Worship the LORD in holy array. Psalms 29:2 The LORD’s voice is on the waters. The God of glory thunders, even the LORD on many waters. Psalms 29:3 The LORD’s voice is powerful. The LORD’s voice is full of majesty. Psalms 29:4 The LORD’s voice breaks the cedars. Yes, the LORD breaks in pieces the cedars of Lebanon. Psalms 29:5 He makes them also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young, wild ox. Psalms 29:6 The LORD’s voice strikes with flashes of lightning. Psalms 29:7 The LORD’s voice shakes the wilderness. The LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh. Psalms 29:8 The LORD’s voice makes the deer calve, and strips the forests bare. In his temple everything says, “Glory!” Psalms 29:9 The LORD sat enthroned at the Flood. Yes, the LORD sits as King forever. Psalms 29:10 The LORD will give strength to his people. The LORD will bless his people with peace. Psalms 29:11

title: Psalm 3:1–8
context: Psalm 3 is David’s cry when he fled from Absalom: foes multiply, and many say there is no help for him in God—yet the LORD is a shield about him, his glory, and the lifter of his head. He cries and is answered from the holy hill; he lies down, sleeps, and wakes sustained; he will not fear thousands arrayed against him. He pleads for the LORD to arise and save, for God strikes enemies and breaks the wicked’s teeth—and confesses that salvation belongs to the LORD, whose blessing rests on his people.
text: Psalm 3:1–8 Psalms Psalm 3 is David’s cry when he fled from Absalom: foes multiply, and many say there is no help for him in God—yet the LORD is a shield about him, his glory, and the lifter of his head. He cries and is answered from the holy hill; he lies down, sleeps, and wakes sustained; he will not fear thousands arrayed against him. He pleads for the LORD to arise and save, for God strikes enemies and breaks the wicked’s teeth—and confesses that salvation belongs to the LORD, whose blessing rests on his people. LORD, how my adversaries have increased! Many are those who rise up against me. Psalms 3:1 Many there are who say of my soul, “There is no help for him in God.” Selah. Psalms 3:2 But you, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head. Psalms 3:3 I cry to the LORD with my voice, and he answers me out of his holy hill. Selah. Psalms 3:4 I laid myself down and slept. I awakened, for the LORD sustains me. Psalms 3:5 I will not be afraid of tens of thousands of people who have set themselves against me on every side. Psalms 3:6 Arise, LORD! Save me, my God! For you have struck all of my enemies on the cheek bone. You have broken the teeth of the wicked. Psalms 3:7 Salvation belongs to the LORD. May your blessing be on your people. Selah. Psalms 3:8

title: Psalm 30:1–12
context: A psalm of David for the dedication of the temple. David praises the LORD who lifted him up and did not let his enemies gloat; he cried out and was healed, brought back from Sheol. He calls the saints to give thanks, because God’s anger lasts a moment and his favor a lifetime: weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning. He confesses the pride of his prosperity, the dismay when God hid his face, and his plea for mercy, and ends with mourning turned into dancing and a vow to give thanks forever.
text: Psalm 30:1–12 Psalms A psalm of David for the dedication of the temple. David praises the LORD who lifted him up and did not let his enemies gloat; he cried out and was healed, brought back from Sheol. He calls the saints to give thanks, because God’s anger lasts a moment and his favor a lifetime: weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning. He confesses the pride of his prosperity, the dismay when God hid his face, and his plea for mercy, and ends with mourning turned into dancing and a vow to give thanks forever. I will extol you, LORD, for you have raised me up, and have not made my foes to rejoice over me. Psalms 30:1 LORD my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me. Psalms 30:2 LORD, you have brought up my soul from Sheol. You have kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit. Psalms 30:3 Sing praise to the LORD, you saints of his. Give thanks to his holy name. Psalms 30:4 For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning. Psalms 30:5 As for me, I said in my prosperity, “I shall never be moved.” Psalms 30:6 You, LORD, when you favored me, made my mountain stand strong; but when you hid your face, I was troubled. Psalms 30:7 I cried to you, LORD. I made supplication to the Lord: Psalms 30:8 “What profit is there in my destruction, if I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise you? Shall it declare your truth? Psalms 30:9 Hear, LORD, and have mercy on me. LORD, be my helper.” Psalms 30:10 You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness, Psalms 30:11 to the end that my heart may sing praise to you, and not be silent. LORD my God, I will give thanks to you forever! Psalms 30:12

title: Psalm 31:1–24
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The psalmist takes refuge in the LORD and pleads never to be put to shame, asking deliverance in righteousness, a hearing ear, speedy rescue, rock and fortress; confesses God already as rock and fortress who for his name's sake leads and guides, and who pulls him from the hidden net; commits his spirit into God's hand as the redeemed one before the faithful God; hates regard for worthless idols and trusts the LORD; rejoices in steadfast love that has seen affliction and known the soul's distress, not delivered him to the enemy but set his feet in a large place; then cries for grace in distress—eye, soul, and body wasted—life spent with sorrow, strength failing because of iniquity, bones wasting; becomes a reproach to adversaries and dread to acquaintances who flee; forgotten like the dead, like a broken vessel; hears whispering, terror on every side, schemes against his life; yet trusts and says, You are my God; confesses times in God's hand and asks rescue, shining face, and save in steadfast love; pleads against shame for the caller while the wicked go silently to Sheol and lying lips be mute; marvels at abundant goodness stored for those who fear and take refuge, hiding in presence-cover from plots and strife of tongues; blesses the LORD for wondrous steadfast love in a besieged city; admits saying in alarm he was cut off, yet God heard his pleas; summons the saints to love the LORD who preserves the faithful and repays the proud; and charges all who hope in the LORD to be strong and let the heart take courage.
text: Psalm 31:1–24 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The psalmist takes refuge in the LORD and pleads never to be put to shame, asking deliverance in righteousness, a hearing ear, speedy rescue, rock and fortress; confesses God already as rock and fortress who for his name's sake leads and guides, and who pulls him from the hidden net; commits his spirit into God's hand as the redeemed one before the faithful God; hates regard for worthless idols and trusts the LORD; rejoices in steadfast love that has seen affliction and known the soul's distress, not delivered him to the enemy but set his feet in a large place; then cries for grace in distress—eye, soul, and body wasted—life spent with sorrow, strength failing because of iniquity, bones wasting; becomes a reproach to adversaries and dread to acquaintances who flee; forgotten like the dead, like a broken vessel; hears whispering, terror on every side, schemes against his life; yet trusts and says, You are my God; confesses times in God's hand and asks rescue, shining face, and save in steadfast love; pleads against shame for the caller while the wicked go silently to Sheol and lying lips be mute; marvels at abundant goodness stored for those who fear and take refuge, hiding in presence-cover from plots and strife of tongues; blesses the LORD for wondrous steadfast love in a besieged city; admits saying in alarm he was cut off, yet God heard his pleas; summons the saints to love the LORD who preserves the faithful and repays the proud; and charges all who hope in the LORD to be strong and let the heart take courage. In you, LORD, I take refuge. Let me never be disappointed. Deliver me in your righteousness. Psalms 31:1 Bow down your ear to me. Deliver me speedily. Be to me a strong rock, a house of defense to save me. Psalms 31:2 For you are my rock and my fortress, therefore for your name’s sake lead me and guide me. Psalms 31:3 Pluck me out of the net that they have laid secretly for me, for you are my stronghold. Psalms 31:4 Into your hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, LORD, God of truth. Psalms 31:5 I hate those who regard lying vanities, but I trust in the LORD. Psalms 31:6 I will be glad and rejoice in your loving kindness, for you have seen my affliction. You have known my soul in adversities. Psalms 31:7 You have not shut me up into the hand of the enemy. You have set my feet in a large place. Psalms 31:8 Have mercy on me, LORD, for I am in distress. My eye, my soul, and my body waste away with grief. Psalms 31:9 For my life is spent with sorrow, my years with sighing. My strength fails because of my iniquity. My bones are wasted away. Psalms 31:10 Because of all my adversaries I have become utterly contemptible to my neighbors, a horror to my acquaintances. Those who saw me on the street fled from me. Psalms 31:11 I am forgotten from their hearts like a dead man. I am like broken pottery. Psalms 31:12 For I have heard the slander of many, terror on every side, while they conspire together against me, they plot to take away my life. Psalms 31:13 But I trust in you, LORD. I said, “You are my God.” Psalms 31:14 My times are in your hand. Deliver me from the hand of my enemies, and from those who persecute me. Psalms 31:15 Make your face to shine on your servant. Save me in your loving kindness. Psalms 31:16 Let me not be disappointed, LORD, for I have called on you. Let the wicked be disappointed. Let them be silent in Sheol. Psalms 31:17 Let the lying lips be mute, which speak against the righteous insolently, with pride and contempt. Psalms 31:18 Oh how great is your goodness, which you have laid up for those who fear you, which you have worked for those who take refuge in you, before the sons of men! Psalms 31:19 In the shelter of your presence you will hide them from the plotting of man. You will keep them secretly in a dwelling away from the strife of tongues. Psalms 31:20 Praise be to the LORD, for he has shown me his marvelous loving kindness in a strong city. Psalms 31:21 As for me, I said in my haste, “I am cut off from before your eyes.” Nevertheless you heard the voice of my petitions when I cried to you. Psalms 31:22 Oh love the LORD, all you his saints! The LORD preserves the faithful, and fully recompenses him who behaves arrogantly. Psalms 31:23 Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the LORD. Psalms 31:24

title: Psalm 32:1–11
context: A Maskil of David. The psalmist pronounces blessed the one whose transgression is forgiven and whose sin is covered; blesses the man to whom the LORD doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit; recalls silence that wasted the bones through all-day groaning; names the LORD's hand heavy day and night and strength dried as by summer heat; then acknowledges sin, refuses to cover iniquity, resolves to confess transgressions, and receives forgiveness of the iniquity of his sin; therefore urges everyone godly to offer prayer when the LORD may be found, so that when the great waters overflow, they shall not reach to him; confesses God as hiding place who preserves from trouble and surrounds with shouts of deliverance; hears instruction and teaching in the way he should go, counsel with God's eye upon him; warns not to be like horse or mule without understanding, curbed with bit and bridle; contrasts many sorrows of the wicked with steadfast love surrounding surround him who trusts in the LORD; and summons the righteous to be glad in the LORD and rejoice, and all the upright in heart to shout for joy.
text: Psalm 32:1–11 Psalms A Maskil of David. The psalmist pronounces blessed the one whose transgression is forgiven and whose sin is covered; blesses the man to whom the LORD doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit; recalls silence that wasted the bones through all-day groaning; names the LORD's hand heavy day and night and strength dried as by summer heat; then acknowledges sin, refuses to cover iniquity, resolves to confess transgressions, and receives forgiveness of the iniquity of his sin; therefore urges everyone godly to offer prayer when the LORD may be found, so that when the great waters overflow, they shall not reach to him; confesses God as hiding place who preserves from trouble and surrounds with shouts of deliverance; hears instruction and teaching in the way he should go, counsel with God's eye upon him; warns not to be like horse or mule without understanding, curbed with bit and bridle; contrasts many sorrows of the wicked with steadfast love surrounding surround him who trusts in the LORD; and summons the righteous to be glad in the LORD and rejoice, and all the upright in heart to shout for joy. Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Psalms 32:1 Blessed is the man to whom the LORD doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit. Psalms 32:2 When I kept silence, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long. Psalms 32:3 For day and night your hand was heavy on me. My strength was sapped in the heat of summer. Selah. Psalms 32:4 I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn’t hide my iniquity. I said, I will confess my transgressions to the LORD, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah. Psalms 32:5 For this, let everyone who is godly pray to you in a time when you may be found. Surely when the great waters overflow, they shall not reach to him. Psalms 32:6 You are my hiding place. You will preserve me from trouble. You will surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah. Psalms 32:7 I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you. Psalms 32:8 Don’t be like the horse, or like the mule, which have no understanding, who are controlled by bit and bridle, or else they will not come near to you. Psalms 32:9 Many sorrows come to the wicked, but loving kindness shall surround him who trusts in the LORD. Psalms 32:10 Be glad in the LORD, and rejoice, you righteous! Shout for joy, all you who are upright in heart! Psalms 32:11

title: Psalm 33:1–22
context: The righteous are called to rejoice in the LORD with instruments and a new song, because his word is right and his work faithful, and the earth is full of his loving kindness. He made the heavens by his word and gathered the seas; he spoke, and it was done. He brings the nations’ plans to nothing while his own counsel stands forever. Kings, warriors, and horses cannot save; the LORD’s eye is on those who fear him and hope in his loving kindness, and the psalm closes with the congregation waiting on him as its help and shield.
text: Psalm 33:1–22 Psalms The righteous are called to rejoice in the LORD with instruments and a new song, because his word is right and his work faithful, and the earth is full of his loving kindness. He made the heavens by his word and gathered the seas; he spoke, and it was done. He brings the nations’ plans to nothing while his own counsel stands forever. Kings, warriors, and horses cannot save; the LORD’s eye is on those who fear him and hope in his loving kindness, and the psalm closes with the congregation waiting on him as its help and shield. Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous! Praise is fitting for the upright. Psalms 33:1 Give thanks to the LORD with the lyre. Sing praises to him with the harp of ten strings. Psalms 33:2 Sing to him a new song. Play skillfully with a shout of joy! Psalms 33:3 For the LORD’s word is right. All his work is done in faithfulness. Psalms 33:4 He loves righteousness and justice. The earth is full of the loving kindness of the LORD. Psalms 33:5 By the LORD’s word, the heavens were made: all their army by the breath of his mouth. Psalms 33:6 He gathers the waters of the sea together as a heap. He lays up the deeps in storehouses. Psalms 33:7 Let all the earth fear the LORD. Let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him. Psalms 33:8 For he spoke, and it was done. He commanded, and it stood firm. Psalms 33:9 The LORD brings the counsel of the nations to nothing. He makes the thoughts of the peoples to be of no effect. Psalms 33:10 The counsel of the LORD stands fast forever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations. Psalms 33:11 Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people whom he has chosen for his own inheritance. Psalms 33:12 The LORD looks from heaven. He sees all the sons of men. Psalms 33:13 From the place of his habitation he looks out on all the inhabitants of the earth, Psalms 33:14 he who fashions all of their hearts; and he considers all of their works. Psalms 33:15 There is no king saved by the multitude of an army. A mighty man is not delivered by great strength. Psalms 33:16 A horse is a vain thing for safety, neither does he deliver any by his great power. Psalms 33:17 Behold, the LORD’s eye is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his loving kindness, Psalms 33:18 to deliver their soul from death, to keep them alive in famine. Psalms 33:19 Our soul has waited for the LORD. He is our help and our shield. Psalms 33:20 For our heart rejoices in him, because we have trusted in his holy name. Psalms 33:21 Let your loving kindness be on us, LORD, since we have hoped in you. Psalms 33:22

title: Psalm 34:1–22
context: Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, so that he drove him out, and he went away. The psalmist vows to bless the LORD at all times with continual praise; boasts in the LORD so the humble hear and are glad; summons others to magnify and exalt the name together; testifies that he sought the LORD, who answered and delivered him from all his fears; describes those who look to him as radiant and unashamed; recalls this poor man crying and the LORD saving him from all troubles; confesses the angel of the LORD encamping around those who fear him; invites all to taste and see that the LORD is good and blesses the refugee in him; calls saints to fear the LORD who lack no good thing while young lions hunger; teaches children the fear of the LORD as the path of life, guarded tongue, turned evil, done good, and pursued peace; sets the LORD's eyes and ears toward the righteous. His face against evildoers; promises hearing and deliverance when the righteous cry; draws near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit; acknowledges many afflictions of the righteous yet total deliverance, kept bones, and the wicked slain by affliction; and closes with the LORD redeeming his servants' life so that none who take refuge in him shall be condemned.
text: Psalm 34:1–22 Psalms Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, so that he drove him out, and he went away. The psalmist vows to bless the LORD at all times with continual praise; boasts in the LORD so the humble hear and are glad; summons others to magnify and exalt the name together; testifies that he sought the LORD, who answered and delivered him from all his fears; describes those who look to him as radiant and unashamed; recalls this poor man crying and the LORD saving him from all troubles; confesses the angel of the LORD encamping around those who fear him; invites all to taste and see that the LORD is good and blesses the refugee in him; calls saints to fear the LORD who lack no good thing while young lions hunger; teaches children the fear of the LORD as the path of life, guarded tongue, turned evil, done good, and pursued peace; sets the LORD's eyes and ears toward the righteous. His face against evildoers; promises hearing and deliverance when the righteous cry; draws near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit; acknowledges many afflictions of the righteous yet total deliverance, kept bones, and the wicked slain by affliction; and closes with the LORD redeeming his servants' life so that none who take refuge in him shall be condemned. I will bless the LORD at all times. His praise will always be in my mouth. Psalms 34:1 My soul shall boast in the LORD. The humble shall hear of it and be glad. Psalms 34:2 Oh magnify the LORD with me. Let’s exalt his name together. Psalms 34:3 I sought the LORD, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears. Psalms 34:4 They looked to him, and were radiant. Their faces shall never be covered with shame. Psalms 34:5 This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles. Psalms 34:6 The LORD’s angel encamps around those who fear him, and delivers them. Psalms 34:7 Oh taste and see that the LORD is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him. Psalms 34:8 Oh fear the LORD, you his saints, for there is no lack with those who fear him. Psalms 34:9 The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger, but those who seek the LORD shall not lack any good thing. Psalms 34:10 Come, you children, listen to me. I will teach you the fear of the LORD. Psalms 34:11 Who is someone who desires life, and loves many days, that he may see good? Psalms 34:12 Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking lies. Psalms 34:13 Depart from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it. Psalms 34:14 The LORD’s eyes are toward the righteous. His ears listen to their cry. Psalms 34:15 The LORD’s face is against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth. Psalms 34:16 The righteous cry, and the LORD hears, and delivers them out of all their troubles. Psalms 34:17 The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit. Psalms 34:18 Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him out of them all. Psalms 34:19 He protects all of his bones. Not one of them is broken. Psalms 34:20 Evil shall kill the wicked. Those who hate the righteous shall be condemned. Psalms 34:21 The LORD redeems the soul of his servants. None of those who take refuge in him shall be condemned. Psalms 34:22

title: Psalm 35:1–28
context: Of David. An imprecatory lament: the psalmist calls the LORD to contend with those who contend with him, to take shield and buckler, draw spear and javelin, and say to his soul that he is his salvation; he asks that life-seekers and evil-devisers be put to shame, turned back, driven like chaff, and pursued on dark slippery ways by the angel of the LORD; he grounds the plea in causeless nets and pits, praying that destruction rebound on the hider; he vows soul-rejoicing and bone-deep praise for the God who delivers the poor from the too-strong; he exposes malicious witnesses, evil repaid for good, and his own sackcloth fasting and mother-like mourning for them when sick, answered by their joy at his stumbling, gathering of wretches, and feast-mockery with gnashing teeth; he asks how long the LORD will look on, pledges thanks in the great congregation, begs that wrongful foes not rejoice or wink, names their peace-less deceit against the quiet in the land and their wide-mouthed Aha, and presses God who has seen not to be silent or far but to awake for vindication according to righteousness, shame those who magnify themselves at his calamity, and let delighting allies shout that the LORD is great who delights in his servant's welfare—then his tongue will tell righteousness and praise all day long.
text: Psalm 35:1–28 Psalms Of David. An imprecatory lament: the psalmist calls the LORD to contend with those who contend with him, to take shield and buckler, draw spear and javelin, and say to his soul that he is his salvation; he asks that life-seekers and evil-devisers be put to shame, turned back, driven like chaff, and pursued on dark slippery ways by the angel of the LORD; he grounds the plea in causeless nets and pits, praying that destruction rebound on the hider; he vows soul-rejoicing and bone-deep praise for the God who delivers the poor from the too-strong; he exposes malicious witnesses, evil repaid for good, and his own sackcloth fasting and mother-like mourning for them when sick, answered by their joy at his stumbling, gathering of wretches, and feast-mockery with gnashing teeth; he asks how long the LORD will look on, pledges thanks in the great congregation, begs that wrongful foes not rejoice or wink, names their peace-less deceit against the quiet in the land and their wide-mouthed Aha, and presses God who has seen not to be silent or far but to awake for vindication according to righteousness, shame those who magnify themselves at his calamity, and let delighting allies shout that the LORD is great who delights in his servant's welfare—then his tongue will tell righteousness and praise all day long. Contend, LORD, with those who contend with me. Fight against those who fight against me. Psalms 35:1 Take hold of shield and buckler, and stand up for my help. Psalms 35:2 Brandish the spear and block those who pursue me. Tell my soul, “I am your salvation.” Psalms 35:3 Let those who seek after my soul be disappointed and brought to dishonor. Let those who plot my ruin be turned back and confounded. Psalms 35:4 Let them be as chaff before the wind, the LORD’s angel driving them on. Psalms 35:5 Let their way be dark and slippery, the LORD’s angel pursuing them. Psalms 35:6 For without cause they have hidden their net in a pit for me. Without cause they have dug a pit for my soul. Psalms 35:7 Let destruction come on him unawares. Let his net that he has hidden catch himself. Let him fall into that destruction. Psalms 35:8 My soul shall be joyful in the LORD. It shall rejoice in his salvation. Psalms 35:9 All my bones shall say, “LORD, who is like you, who delivers the poor from him who is too strong for him; yes, the poor and the needy from him who robs him?” Psalms 35:10 Unrighteous witnesses rise up. They ask me about things that I don’t know about. Psalms 35:11 They reward me evil for good, to the bereaving of my soul. Psalms 35:12 But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth. I afflicted my soul with fasting. My prayer returned into my own bosom. Psalms 35:13 I behaved myself as though it had been my friend or my brother. I bowed down mourning, as one who mourns his mother. Psalms 35:14 But in my adversity, they rejoiced, and gathered themselves together. The attackers gathered themselves together against me, and I didn’t know it. They tore at me, and didn’t cease. Psalms 35:15 Like the profane mockers in feasts, they gnashed their teeth at me. Psalms 35:16 Lord, how long will you look on? Rescue my soul from their destruction, my precious life from the lions. Psalms 35:17 I will give you thanks in the great assembly. I will praise you among many people. Psalms 35:18 Don’t let those who are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me; neither let those who hate me without a cause wink their eyes. Psalms 35:19 For they don’t speak peace, but they devise deceitful words against those who are quiet in the land. Psalms 35:20 Yes, they opened their mouth wide against me. They said, “Aha! Aha! Our eye has seen it!” Psalms 35:21 You have seen it, LORD. Don’t keep silent. Lord, don’t be far from me. Psalms 35:22 Wake up! Rise up to defend me, my God! My Lord, contend for me! Psalms 35:23 Vindicate me, LORD my God, according to your righteousness. Don’t let them gloat over me. Psalms 35:24 Don’t let them say in their heart, “Aha! That’s the way we want it!” Don’t let them say, “We have swallowed him up!” Psalms 35:25 Let them be disappointed and confounded together who rejoice at my calamity. Let them be clothed with shame and dishonor who magnify themselves against me. Psalms 35:26 Let those who favor my righteous cause shout for joy and be glad. Yes, let them say continually, “May the LORD be magnified, who has pleasure in the prosperity of his servant!” Psalms 35:27 My tongue shall talk about your righteousness and about your praise all day long. Psalms 35:28

title: Psalm 36:1–12
context: To the choirmaster. Of David, the servant of the Lord. The psalmist hears transgression speaking to the wicked deep in the heart—no fear of God before his eyes; the wicked flatters himself so that iniquity cannot be found out and hated, speaks trouble and deceit, has ceased to be wise and to do good, plots trouble on his bed, sets himself in a way that is not good, and does not reject evil; then the song turns to the LORD whose steadfast love extends to the heavens and faithfulness to the clouds, whose righteousness is like the mountains of God and judgments like the great deep, who saves man and beast; precious steadfast love gathers the children of mankind to take refuge under the shadow of his wings, to feast on the abundance of his house and drink of the river of his delights—for with him is the spring of life, and in his light we will see light; the servant then prays that steadfast love continue to those who know him and righteousness to the upright in heart, that the foot of arrogance not come upon him nor the hand of the wicked drive him away, and points to where the evildoers lie fallen, thrust down, and shall not be able to rise.
text: Psalm 36:1–12 Psalms To the choirmaster. Of David, the servant of the Lord. The psalmist hears transgression speaking to the wicked deep in the heart—no fear of God before his eyes; the wicked flatters himself so that iniquity cannot be found out and hated, speaks trouble and deceit, has ceased to be wise and to do good, plots trouble on his bed, sets himself in a way that is not good, and does not reject evil; then the song turns to the LORD whose steadfast love extends to the heavens and faithfulness to the clouds, whose righteousness is like the mountains of God and judgments like the great deep, who saves man and beast; precious steadfast love gathers the children of mankind to take refuge under the shadow of his wings, to feast on the abundance of his house and drink of the river of his delights—for with him is the spring of life, and in his light we will see light; the servant then prays that steadfast love continue to those who know him and righteousness to the upright in heart, that the foot of arrogance not come upon him nor the hand of the wicked drive him away, and points to where the evildoers lie fallen, thrust down, and shall not be able to rise. A revelation is within my heart about the disobedience of the wicked: There is no fear of God before his eyes. Psalms 36:1 For he flatters himself in his own eyes, too much to detect and hate his sin. Psalms 36:2 The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit. He has ceased to be wise and to do good. Psalms 36:3 He plots iniquity on his bed. He sets himself in a way that is not good. He doesn’t abhor evil. Psalms 36:4 Your loving kindness, LORD, is in the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies. Psalms 36:5 Your righteousness is like the mountains of God. Your judgments are like a great deep. LORD, you preserve man and animal. Psalms 36:6 How precious is your loving kindness, God! The children of men take refuge under the shadow of your wings. Psalms 36:7 They shall be abundantly satisfied with the abundance of your house.
