You will make them drink of the river of your pleasures. Psalms 36:8 For with you is the spring of life. In your light we will see light. Psalms 36:9 Oh continue your loving kindness to those who know you, your righteousness to the upright in heart. Psalms 36:10 Don’t let the foot of pride come against me. Don’t let the hand of the wicked drive me away. Psalms 36:11 There the workers of iniquity are fallen. They are thrust down, and shall not be able to rise. Psalms 36:12

title: Psalm 37:1–40
context: Of David. A wisdom psalm in acrostic-style sequence (kept whole): the singer refuses fretting and envy at evildoers who soon fade like grass; calls for trust, doing good, dwelling, delight in the Lord, committing the way, stillness and patient waiting, and the forsaking of anger that tends only to evil; promises that waiters inherit the land while evildoers are cut off, that in a little while the wicked's place is empty, and that the meek inherit the land with abundant peace; sets the Lord's laugh over plotting teeth, rebound of sword and bow, the better little of the righteous, upheld arms, known days of the blameless, famine supply, and enemies vanishing like smoke; contrasts borrowing wicked with generous righteous, blessing and curse, established steps and upheld falling, lifelong witness that the righteous are not forsaken, open-handed seed who become a blessing, turning from evil to dwell forever, justice-loving preservation of saints, forever inheritance, wisdom-mouth and heart-law that keeps steps, watched righteous not abandoned in trial, waiting that inherits while looking on the cut-off, the green ruthless tree that vanishes without remainder, the blameless whose future is peace against transgressors destroyed, and salvation from the Lord who helps, delivers, and saves those who take refuge in him.
text: Psalm 37:1–40 Psalms Of David. A wisdom psalm in acrostic-style sequence (kept whole): the singer refuses fretting and envy at evildoers who soon fade like grass; calls for trust, doing good, dwelling, delight in the Lord, committing the way, stillness and patient waiting, and the forsaking of anger that tends only to evil; promises that waiters inherit the land while evildoers are cut off, that in a little while the wicked's place is empty, and that the meek inherit the land with abundant peace; sets the Lord's laugh over plotting teeth, rebound of sword and bow, the better little of the righteous, upheld arms, known days of the blameless, famine supply, and enemies vanishing like smoke; contrasts borrowing wicked with generous righteous, blessing and curse, established steps and upheld falling, lifelong witness that the righteous are not forsaken, open-handed seed who become a blessing, turning from evil to dwell forever, justice-loving preservation of saints, forever inheritance, wisdom-mouth and heart-law that keeps steps, watched righteous not abandoned in trial, waiting that inherits while looking on the cut-off, the green ruthless tree that vanishes without remainder, the blameless whose future is peace against transgressors destroyed, and salvation from the Lord who helps, delivers, and saves those who take refuge in him. Don’t fret because of evildoers, neither be envious against those who work unrighteousness. Psalms 37:1 For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither like the green herb. Psalms 37:2 Trust in the LORD, and do good. Dwell in the land, and enjoy safe pasture. Psalms 37:3 Also delight yourself in the LORD, and he will give you the desires of your heart. Psalms 37:4 Commit your way to the LORD. Trust also in him, and he will do this: Psalms 37:5 he will make your righteousness shine out like light, and your justice as the noon day sun. Psalms 37:6 Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen. Psalms 37:7 Cease from anger, and forsake wrath. Don’t fret; it leads only to evildoing. Psalms 37:8 For evildoers shall be cut off, but those who wait for the LORD shall inherit the land. Psalms 37:9 For yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more. Yes, though you look for his place, he isn’t there. Psalms 37:10 But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace. Psalms 37:11 The wicked plots against the just, and gnashes at him with his teeth. Psalms 37:12 The Lord will laugh at him, for he sees that his day is coming. Psalms 37:13 The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, to kill those who are upright on the path. Psalms 37:14 Their sword shall enter into their own heart. Their bows shall be broken. Psalms 37:15 Better is a little that the righteous has, than the abundance of many wicked. Psalms 37:16 For the arms of the wicked shall be broken, but the LORD upholds the righteous. Psalms 37:17 The LORD knows the days of the perfect. Their inheritance shall be forever. Psalms 37:18 They shall not be disappointed in the time of evil. In the days of famine they shall be satisfied. Psalms 37:19 But the wicked shall perish. The enemies of the LORD shall be like the beauty of the fields. They will vanish— vanish like smoke. Psalms 37:20 The wicked borrow, and don’t pay back, but the righteous give generously. Psalms 37:21 For such as are blessed by him shall inherit the land. Those who are cursed by him shall be cut off. Psalms 37:22 A man’s steps are established by the LORD. He delights in his way. Psalms 37:23 Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for the LORD holds him up with his hand. Psalms 37:24 I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his children begging for bread. Psalms 37:25 All day long he deals graciously, and lends. His offspring is blessed. Psalms 37:26 Depart from evil, and do good. Live securely forever. Psalms 37:27 For the LORD loves justice, and doesn’t forsake his saints. They are preserved forever, but the children of the wicked shall be cut off. Psalms 37:28 The righteous shall inherit the land, and live in it forever. Psalms 37:29 The mouth of the righteous talks of wisdom. His tongue speaks justice. Psalms 37:30 The law of his God is in his heart. None of his steps shall slide. Psalms 37:31 The wicked watch the righteous, and seek to kill him. Psalms 37:32 The LORD will not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him when he is judged. Psalms 37:33 Wait for the LORD, and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, you shall see it. Psalms 37:34 I have seen the wicked in great power, spreading himself like a green tree in its native soil. Psalms 37:35 But he passed away, and behold, he was not. Yes, I sought him, but he could not be found. Psalms 37:36 Mark the perfect man, and see the upright, for there is a future for the man of peace. Psalms 37:37 As for transgressors, they shall be destroyed together. The future of the wicked shall be cut off. Psalms 37:38 But the salvation of the righteous is from the LORD. He is their stronghold in the time of trouble. Psalms 37:39 The LORD helps them and rescues them. He rescues them from the wicked and saves them, because they have taken refuge in him. Psalms 37:40

title: Psalm 38:1–22
context: A Psalm of David, for the memorial offering. A penitential psalm: the singer pleads that the LORD not rebuke him in anger nor discipline him in wrath; confesses arrows and hand sunk upon him, no soundness in flesh or health in bones because of indignation and sin, iniquities gone over the head like a burden too heavy; names wounds that stink from foolishness, bowed mourning, sides filled with burning, feeble crushed groaning from the heart's tumult; sets all longing and sighing before the Lord while heart throbs, strength fails, and light of eyes is gone; laments friends and companions aloof from his plague and nearest kin far off, while life-seekers lay snares and meditate treachery; answers as deaf and mute without rebukes; waits for the LORD who will answer, lest enemies rejoice when his foot slips; ready to fall with pain ever before him, he confesses iniquity and is sorry for sin even while vigorous foes hate him wrongfully and render evil for good because he follows after good; closes pleading that the LORD not forsake him or be far, and make haste to help—O Lord, my salvation.
text: Psalm 38:1–22 Psalms A Psalm of David, for the memorial offering. A penitential psalm: the singer pleads that the LORD not rebuke him in anger nor discipline him in wrath; confesses arrows and hand sunk upon him, no soundness in flesh or health in bones because of indignation and sin, iniquities gone over the head like a burden too heavy; names wounds that stink from foolishness, bowed mourning, sides filled with burning, feeble crushed groaning from the heart's tumult; sets all longing and sighing before the Lord while heart throbs, strength fails, and light of eyes is gone; laments friends and companions aloof from his plague and nearest kin far off, while life-seekers lay snares and meditate treachery; answers as deaf and mute without rebukes; waits for the LORD who will answer, lest enemies rejoice when his foot slips; ready to fall with pain ever before him, he confesses iniquity and is sorry for sin even while vigorous foes hate him wrongfully and render evil for good because he follows after good; closes pleading that the LORD not forsake him or be far, and make haste to help—O Lord, my salvation. LORD, don’t rebuke me in your wrath, neither chasten me in your hot displeasure. Psalms 38:1 For your arrows have pierced me, your hand presses hard on me. Psalms 38:2 There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation, neither is there any health in my bones because of my sin. Psalms 38:3 For my iniquities have gone over my head. As a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me. Psalms 38:4 My wounds are loathsome and corrupt because of my foolishness. Psalms 38:5 I am in pain and bowed down greatly. I go mourning all day long. Psalms 38:6 For my waist is filled with burning. There is no soundness in my flesh. Psalms 38:7 I am faint and severely bruised. I have groaned by reason of the anguish of my heart. Psalms 38:8 Lord, all my desire is before you. My groaning is not hidden from you. Psalms 38:9 My heart throbs. My strength fails me. As for the light of my eyes, it has also left me. Psalms 38:10 My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my plague. My kinsmen stand far away. Psalms 38:11 They also who seek after my life lay snares. Those who seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and meditate deceits all day long. Psalms 38:12 But I, as a deaf man, don’t hear. I am as a mute man who doesn’t open his mouth. Psalms 38:13 Yes, I am as a man who doesn’t hear, in whose mouth are no reproofs. Psalms 38:14 For I hope in you, LORD. You will answer, Lord my God. Psalms 38:15 For I said, “Don’t let them gloat over me, or exalt themselves over me when my foot slips.” Psalms 38:16 For I am ready to fall. My pain is continually before me. Psalms 38:17 For I will declare my iniquity. I will be sorry for my sin. Psalms 38:18 But my enemies are vigorous and many. Those who hate me without reason are numerous. Psalms 38:19 They who give evil for good are also adversaries to me, because I follow what is good. Psalms 38:20 Don’t forsake me, LORD. My God, don’t be far from me. Psalms 38:21 Hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation. Psalms 38:22

title: Psalm 39:1–13
context: To the choirmaster: to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. The singer resolves to guard his ways and muzzle his mouth while the wicked are present, yet mute silence proves no avail as distress worsens; heart heats in musing until fire burns and the tongue speaks. He asks the LORD to make him know his end and the measure of his days—how fleeting he is; days are a few handbreadths, lifetime nothing before God, and every man stands as a breath. Man walks like a shadow, in turmoil for nothing, heaping wealth without knowing who will gather. The turn: And Now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you—deliverance from all transgressions, not the reproach of the foolish; mute again because the Lord has done it; plea to remove the stroke as he is overcome by the blow of God's hand; discipline with rebukes for sin consumes what is dear like a moth, and mankind is again a mere breath. He asks hearing for prayer, cry, and tears as sojourner and guest like the fathers, and closes: Were. Oh spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go away and exist no more.
text: Psalm 39:1–13 Psalms To the choirmaster: to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. My hope is in you—deliverance from all transgressions, not the reproach of the foolish; mute again because the Lord has done it; plea to remove the stroke as he is overcome by the blow of God's hand; discipline with rebukes for sin consumes what is dear like a moth, and mankind is again a mere breath. He asks hearing for prayer, cry, and tears as sojourner and guest like the fathers, and closes: Were. Oh spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go away and exist no more. I said, “I will watch my ways, so that I don’t sin with my tongue. I will keep my mouth with a bridle while the wicked is before me.” Psalms 39:1 I was mute with silence. I held my peace, even from good. My sorrow was stirred. Psalms 39:2 My heart was hot within me. While I meditated, the fire burned. I spoke with my tongue: Psalms 39:3 “LORD, show me my end, what is the measure of my days. Let me know how frail I am. Psalms 39:4 Behold, you have made my days hand widths. My lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely every man stands as a breath.” Selah. Psalms 39:5 “Surely every man walks like a shadow. Surely they busy themselves in vain. He heaps up, and doesn’t know who shall gather. Psalms 39:6 Now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you. Psalms 39:7 Deliver me from all my transgressions. Don’t make me the reproach of the foolish. Psalms 39:8 I was mute. I didn’t open my mouth, because you did it. Psalms 39:9 Remove your scourge away from me. I am overcome by the blow of your hand. Psalms 39:10 When you rebuke and correct man for iniquity, you consume his wealth like a moth. Surely every man is but a breath.” Selah. Psalms 39:11 “Hear my prayer, LORD, and give ear to my cry. Don’t be silent at my tears. For I am a stranger with you, a foreigner, as all my fathers were. Psalms 39:12 Oh spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go away and exist no more.” Psalms 39:13

title: Psalm 4:1–8
context: Psalm 4 is David’s evening plea: he calls on the God of his righteousness, who has given relief in distress, and asks grace and a hearing. He rebukes men who turn his honor to shame and chase vain words and lies, then announces that the LORD has set apart for himself the one who is godly and hears when he calls. He urges awe without sin, heart-pondering on the bed, right sacrifices, and trust in the LORD. Against many who ask who will show good, he asks the light of God’s face—and confesses more joy than abundant grain and wine, then lies down in peace, for the LORD alone makes him dwell in safety.
text: Psalm 4:1–8 Psalms Psalm 4 is David’s evening plea: he calls on the God of his righteousness, who has given relief in distress, and asks grace and a hearing. He rebukes men who turn his honor to shame and chase vain words and lies, then announces that the LORD has set apart for himself the one who is godly and hears when he calls. He urges awe without sin, heart-pondering on the bed, right sacrifices, and trust in the LORD. Against many who ask who will show good, he asks the light of God’s face—and confesses more joy than abundant grain and wine, then lies down in peace, for the LORD alone makes him dwell in safety. Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness. Give me relief from my distress. Have mercy on me, and hear my prayer. Psalms 4:1 You sons of men, how long shall my glory be turned into dishonor? Will you love vanity and seek after falsehood? Selah. Psalms 4:2 But know that the LORD has set apart for himself him who is godly; The LORD will hear when I call to him. Psalms 4:3 Stand in awe, and don’t sin. Search your own heart on your bed, and be still. Selah. Psalms 4:4 Offer the sacrifices of righteousness. Put your trust in the LORD. Psalms 4:5 Many say, “Who will show us any good?” LORD, let the light of your face shine on us. Psalms 4:6 You have put gladness in my heart, more than when their grain and their new wine are increased. Psalms 4:7 In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me live in safety. Psalms 4:8

title: Psalm 40:1–17
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The singer waited patiently for the LORD, who inclined and heard his cry; drew him up from the pit of destruction and the miry bog, set his feet on a rock, and made his steps secure; put a new song of praise in his mouth so that Many shall see it, and fear, and trust in the LORD. Blessed is the one who makes the LORD his trust and does not turn to the proud or those who go astray after a lie. God's wondrous deeds and thoughts toward his people multiply beyond telling. Then the turn shared by Hebrews 10: God did not desire sacrifice and offering, but opened the psalmist’s ears; burnt offering and sin offering he has not required. Behold, I have come. It is written about me in the book in the scroll. I delight to do your will, my God. Yes, your law is within my heart. Glad news of deliverance is told in the great congregation without restrained lips; faithfulness, salvation, steadfast love are not concealed. Mercy is not to be restrained; steadfast love and faithfulness preserve. Yet evils encompass beyond number, iniquities overtake so he cannot see, more than the hairs of his head, and the heart fails. Be pleased, LORD, to deliver; make haste to help; shame those who snatch life and delight in hurt, and who cry Aha, Aha. Let seekers rejoice and lovers of salvation say continually, Let the LORD. The close: poor and needy, yet the Lord takes thought; help and deliverer. Don’t delay, my God.
text: Psalm 40:1–17 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The singer waited patiently for the LORD, who inclined and heard his cry; drew him up from the pit of destruction and the miry bog, set his feet on a rock, and made his steps secure; put a new song of praise in his mouth so that Many shall see it, and fear, and trust in the LORD. Blessed is the one who makes the LORD his trust and does not turn to the proud or those who go astray after a lie. God's wondrous deeds and thoughts toward his people multiply beyond telling. Then the turn shared by Hebrews 10: God did not desire sacrifice and offering, but opened the psalmist’s ears; burnt offering and sin offering he has not required. Behold, I have come. It is written about me in the book in the scroll. I delight to do your will, my God. Yes, your law is within my heart. Glad news of deliverance is told in the great congregation without restrained lips; faithfulness, salvation, steadfast love are not concealed. Mercy is not to be restrained; steadfast love and faithfulness preserve. Yet evils encompass beyond number, iniquities overtake so he cannot see, more than the hairs of his head, and the heart fails. Be pleased, LORD, to deliver; make haste to help; shame those who snatch life and delight in hurt, and who cry Aha, Aha. Let seekers rejoice and lovers of salvation say continually, Let the LORD. The close: poor and needy, yet the Lord takes thought; help and deliverer. Don’t delay, my God. I waited patiently for the LORD. He turned to me, and heard my cry. Psalms 40:1 He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand. Psalms 40:2 He has put a new song in my mouth, even praise to our God. Many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD. Psalms 40:3 Blessed is the man who makes the LORD his trust, and doesn’t respect the proud, nor such as turn away to lies. Psalms 40:4 Many, LORD, my God, are the wonderful works which you have done, and your thoughts which are toward us. They can’t be declared back to you. If I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be counted. Psalms 40:5 Sacrifice and offering you didn’t desire. You have opened my ears. You have not required burnt offering and sin offering. Psalms 40:6 Then I said, “Behold, I have come. It is written about me in the book in the scroll. Psalms 40:7 I delight to do your will, my God. Yes, your law is within my heart.” Psalms 40:8 I have proclaimed glad news of righteousness in the great assembly. Behold, I will not seal my lips, LORD, you know. Psalms 40:9 I have not hidden your righteousness within my heart. I have declared your faithfulness and your salvation. I have not concealed your loving kindness and your truth from the great assembly. Psalms 40:10 Don’t withhold your tender mercies from me, LORD. Let your loving kindness and your truth continually preserve me. Psalms 40:11 For innumerable evils have surrounded me. My iniquities have overtaken me, so that I am not able to look up. They are more than the hairs of my head. My heart has failed me. Psalms 40:12 Be pleased, LORD, to deliver me. Hurry to help me, LORD. Psalms 40:13 Let them be disappointed and confounded together who seek after my soul to destroy it. Let them be turned backward and brought to dishonor who delight in my hurt. Psalms 40:14 Let them be desolate by reason of their shame that tell me, “Aha! Aha!” Psalms 40:15 Let all those who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let such as love your salvation say continually, “Let the LORD be exalted!” Psalms 40:16 But I am poor and needy. May the Lord think about me. You are my help and my deliverer. Don’t delay, my God. Psalms 40:17

title: Psalm 41:1–13
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Blessed is he who considers the poor. The LORD will deliver him in the day of evil. The LORD delivers him; protects and keeps him alive; calls him blessed in the land; does not surrender him to enemies; sustains him on the sickbed and restores him in illness. Then the singer turns: O LORD, be gracious; heal me, for I have sinned against you. Enemies speak evil against him: When will he die, and his name perish?—come with empty words while hearts gather iniquity, go out and tell it abroad; whisper together and imagine the worst; say a deadly thing is poured out, he will not rise. Even the close friend in whom he trusted, who ate his bread with me, has lifted up his heel against him—words John 13 applies to Judas against Christ. But you, LORD, have mercy and raise me up. By this he knows the LORD delights in him: the enemy will not shout in triumph. He is upheld because of integrity and set in the LORD's presence forever. The doxology that closes Book I: Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting! Amen and amen.

The LORD will deliver him in the day of evil. Psalms 41:1 The LORD will preserve him, and keep him alive. He shall be blessed on the earth, and he will not surrender him to the will of his enemies. Psalms 41:2 The LORD will sustain him on his sickbed, and restore him from his bed of illness. Psalms 41:3 I said, “LORD, have mercy on me! Heal me, for I have sinned against you.” Psalms 41:4 My enemies speak evil against me: “When will he die, and his name perish?” Psalms 41:5 If he comes to see me, he speaks falsehood. His heart gathers iniquity to itself. When he goes abroad, he tells it. Psalms 41:6 All who hate me whisper together against me. They imagine the worst for me. Psalms 41:7 “An evil disease”, they say, “has afflicted him. Now that he lies he shall rise up no more.” Psalms 41:8 Yes, my own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, who ate bread with me, has lifted up his heel against me. Psalms 41:9 But you, LORD, have mercy on me, and raise me up, that I may repay them. Psalms 41:10 By this I know that you delight in me, because my enemy doesn’t triumph over me. Psalms 41:11 As for me, you uphold me in my integrity, and set me in your presence forever. Psalms 41:12 Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting! Amen and amen. Psalms 41:13

title: Psalm 42:1–11
context: Psalms 42–43 form a single lament that opens Book II. The psalmist, far from the temple near the Jordan and Mount Hermon, thirsts for God like a deer for water while enemies taunt, ‘Where is your God?’ He remembers leading festival crowds to God’s house. Three times he questions his own downcast soul and tells it to hope in God.
text: Psalm 42:1–11 Psalms Psalms 42–43 form a single lament that opens Book II. The psalmist, far from the temple near the Jordan and Mount Hermon, thirsts for God like a deer for water while enemies taunt, ‘Where is your God?’ He remembers leading festival crowds to God’s house. Three times he questions his own downcast soul and tells it to hope in God. As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God. Psalms 42:1 My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God? Psalms 42:2 My tears have been my food day and night, while they continually ask me, “Where is your God?” Psalms 42:3 These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me, how I used to go with the crowd, and led them to God’s house, with the voice of joy and praise, a multitude keeping a holy day. Psalms 42:4 Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence. Psalms 42:5 My God, my soul is in despair within me. Therefore I remember you from the land of the Jordan, the heights of Hermon, from the hill Mizar. Psalms 42:6 Deep calls to deep at the noise of your waterfalls. All your waves and your billows have swept over me. Psalms 42:7 The LORD will command his loving kindness in the daytime. In the night his song shall be with me: a prayer to the God of my life. Psalms 42:8 I will ask God, my rock, “Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?” Psalms 42:9 As with a sword in my bones, my adversaries reproach me, while they continually ask me, “Where is your God?” Psalms 42:10 Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him, the saving help of my countenance, and my God. Psalms 42:11

title: Psalm 43:1–5
context: Often read as the second half of Psalm 42. The psalmist asks God to vindicate him against an ungodly nation and deceitful men, and asks why the God of his strength seems to have cast him off. He prays for God’s light and truth to lead him back to the holy hill and the altar, where he will praise God with the harp. The shared refrain returns and closes the pair: why so downcast, my soul? Hope in God, for I will still praise him, my Savior and my God.
text: Psalm 43:1–5 Psalms Often read as the second half of Psalm 42. The psalmist asks God to vindicate him against an ungodly nation and deceitful men, and asks why the God of his strength seems to have cast him off. He prays for God’s light and truth to lead him back to the holy hill and the altar, where he will praise God with the harp. The shared refrain returns and closes the pair: why so downcast, my soul? Hope in God, for I will still praise him, my Savior and my God. Vindicate me, God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation. Oh, deliver me from deceitful and wicked men. Psalms 43:1 For you are the God of my strength. Why have you rejected me? Why do I go mourning because of the oppression of the enemy? Psalms 43:2 Oh, send out your light and your truth. Let them lead me. Let them bring me to your holy hill, to your tents. Psalms 43:3 Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my exceeding joy. I will praise you on the harp, God, my God. Psalms 43:4 Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him: my Savior, my helper, and my God. Psalms 43:5

title: Psalm 44:1–26
context: A national lament after military defeat. Israel recalls how God won the land for their ancestors, and confesses that they trust him rather than their own weapons. Yet they have been routed and scattered, not for unfaithfulness, since they have kept the covenant. The psalm ends by urging God to wake up and help; Paul quotes v. 22 in Romans 8:36.
text: Psalm 44:1–26 Psalms A national lament after military defeat. Israel recalls how God won the land for their ancestors, and confesses that they trust him rather than their own weapons. Yet they have been routed and scattered, not for unfaithfulness, since they have kept the covenant. The psalm ends by urging God to wake up and help; Paul quotes v. 22 in Romans 8:36. We have heard with our ears, God; our fathers have told us what work you did in their days, in the days of old. Psalms 44:1 You drove out the nations with your hand, but you planted them. You afflicted the peoples, but you spread them abroad. Psalms 44:2 For they didn’t get the land in possession by their own sword, neither did their own arm save them; but your right hand, your arm, and the light of your face, because you were favorable to them. Psalms 44:3 God, you are my King. Command victories for Jacob! Psalms 44:4 Through you, we will push down our adversaries. Through your name, we will tread down those who rise up against us. Psalms 44:5 For I will not trust in my bow, neither will my sword save me. Psalms 44:6 But you have saved us from our adversaries, and have shamed those who hate us. Psalms 44:7 In God we have made our boast all day long. We will give thanks to your name forever. Selah. Psalms 44:8 But now you rejected us, and brought us to dishonor, and don’t go out with our armies. Psalms 44:9 You make us turn back from the adversary. Those who hate us take plunder for themselves. Psalms 44:10 You have made us like sheep for food, and have scattered us among the nations. Psalms 44:11 You sell your people for nothing, and have gained nothing from their sale. Psalms 44:12 You make us a reproach to our neighbors, a scoffing and a derision to those who are around us. Psalms 44:13 You make us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples. Psalms 44:14 All day long my dishonor is before me, and shame covers my face, Psalms 44:15 at the taunt of one who reproaches and verbally abuses, because of the enemy and the avenger. Psalms 44:16 All this has come on us, yet we haven’t forgotten you. We haven’t been false to your covenant. Psalms 44:17 Our heart has not turned back, neither have our steps strayed from your path, Psalms 44:18 though you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals, and covered us with the shadow of death. Psalms 44:19 If we have forgotten the name of our God, or spread out our hands to a strange god, Psalms 44:20 won’t God search this out? For he knows the secrets of the heart. Psalms 44:21 Yes, for your sake we are killed all day long. We are regarded as sheep for the slaughter. Psalms 44:22 Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord? Arise! Don’t reject us forever. Psalms 44:23 Why do you hide your face, and forget our affliction and our oppression? Psalms 44:24 For our soul is bowed down to the dust. Our body clings to the earth. Psalms 44:25 Rise up to help us. Redeem us for your loving kindness’ sake. Psalms 44:26

title: Psalm 45:1–17
context: For the Chief Musician, a contemplation of the sons of Korah; a wedding song. The poet addresses a king of surpassing beauty and grace, girded for battle on behalf of truth, humility, and righteousness, whose throne is addressed as God’s and whose scepter is equity. The bride is then called to forget her father’s house and honor the king; she is brought to him in splendor with her companions, and the song ends with the promise that his sons will be princes and his name remembered through all generations. Hebrews 1 applies verses 6–7 to the Son.
text: Psalm 45:1–17 Psalms For the Chief Musician, a contemplation of the sons of Korah; a wedding song. The poet addresses a king of surpassing beauty and grace, girded for battle on behalf of truth, humility, and righteousness, whose throne is addressed as God’s and whose scepter is equity. The bride is then called to forget her father’s house and honor the king; she is brought to him in splendor with her companions, and the song ends with the promise that his sons will be princes and his name remembered through all generations. Hebrews 1 applies verses 6–7 to the Son. My heart overflows with a noble theme. I recite my verses for the king. My tongue is like the pen of a skillful writer. Psalms 45:1 You are the most excellent of the sons of men. Grace has anointed your lips, therefore God has blessed you forever. Psalms 45:2 Strap your sword on your thigh, O mighty one, in your splendor and your majesty. Psalms 45:3 In your majesty ride on victoriously on behalf of truth, humility, and righteousness. Let your right hand display awesome deeds. Psalms 45:4 Your arrows are sharp. The nations fall under you, with arrows in the heart of the king’s enemies. Psalms 45:5 Your throne, God, is forever and ever. A scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom. Psalms 45:6 You have loved righteousness, and hated wickedness. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows. Psalms 45:7 All your garments smell like myrrh, aloes, and cassia. Out of ivory palaces stringed instruments have made you glad. Psalms 45:8 Kings’ daughters are among your honorable women. At your right hand the queen stands in gold of Ophir. Psalms 45:9 Listen, daughter, consider, and turn your ear. Forget your own people, and also your father’s house. Psalms 45:10 So the king will desire your beauty, honor him, for he is your lord. Psalms 45:11 The daughter of Tyre comes with a gift. The rich among the people entreat your favor. Psalms 45:12 The princess inside is all glorious. Her clothing is interwoven with gold. Psalms 45:13 She shall be led to the king in embroidered work. The virgins, her companions who follow her, shall be brought to you. Psalms 45:14 With gladness and rejoicing they shall be led. They shall enter into the king’s palace. Psalms 45:15 Your sons will take the place of your fathers. You shall make them princes in all the earth. Psalms 45:16 I will make your name to be remembered in all generations. Therefore the peoples shall give you thanks forever and ever. Psalms 45:17

title: Psalm 46:1–11
context: For the Chief Musician, a song of the sons of Korah. God is his people’s refuge and strength, so they will not fear even if the earth shakes and the mountains fall into the sea. A river gladdens the city of God; God is within her, and she will not be moved. Nations rage and kingdoms fall at his voice. The LORD of Armies is with us. The psalm invites the hearer to see his works—he ends wars and burns the weapons—and to be still and know that he is God.
text: Psalm 46:1–11 Psalms For the Chief Musician, a song of the sons of Korah. God is his people’s refuge and strength, so they will not fear even if the earth shakes and the mountains fall into the sea. A river gladdens the city of God; God is within her, and she will not be moved. Nations rage and kingdoms fall at his voice. The LORD of Armies is with us. The psalm invites the hearer to see his works—he ends wars and burns the weapons—and to be still and know that he is God. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Psalms 46:1 Therefore we won’t be afraid, though the earth changes, though the mountains are shaken into the heart of the seas; Psalms 46:2 though its waters roar and are troubled, though the mountains tremble with their swelling. Selah. Psalms 46:3 There is a river, the streams of which make the city of God glad, the holy place of the tents of the Most High. Psalms 46:4 God is within her. She shall not be moved. God will help her at dawn. Psalms 46:5 The nations raged. The kingdoms were moved. He lifted his voice and the earth melted. Psalms 46:6 The LORD of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah. Psalms 46:7 Come, see the LORD’s works, what desolations he has made on the earth. Psalms 46:8 He makes wars cease to the end of the earth. He breaks the bow, and shatters the spear. He burns the chariots in the fire. Psalms 46:9 “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted on the earth.” Psalms 46:10 The LORD of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah. Psalms 46:11

title: Psalm 47:1–9
context: For the Chief Musician, a psalm of the sons of Korah. All nations are summoned to clap and shout, because the LORD Most High is the great King over all the earth who chose Jacob’s inheritance. God goes up with a shout and a trumpet blast, and the call to sing praises rings out again and again. The psalm closes with the princes of the peoples gathered as the people of Abraham’s God, since the shields of the earth belong to him.
text: Psalm 47:1–9 Psalms For the Chief Musician, a psalm of the sons of Korah. All nations are summoned to clap and shout, because the LORD Most High is the great King over all the earth who chose Jacob’s inheritance. God goes up with a shout and a trumpet blast, and the call to sing praises rings out again and again. The psalm closes with the princes of the peoples gathered as the people of Abraham’s God, since the shields of the earth belong to him. Oh clap your hands, all you nations. Shout to God with the voice of triumph! Psalms 47:1 For the LORD Most High is awesome. He is a great King over all the earth. Psalms 47:2 He subdues nations under us, and peoples under our feet. Psalms 47:3 He chooses our inheritance for us, the glory of Jacob whom he loved. Selah. Psalms 47:4 God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet. Psalms 47:5 Sing praises to God! Sing praises! Sing praises to our King! Sing praises! Psalms 47:6 For God is the King of all the earth. Sing praises with understanding. Psalms 47:7 God reigns over the nations. God sits on his holy throne. Psalms 47:8 The princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham. For the shields of the earth belong to God. He is greatly exalted! Psalms 47:9

title: Psalm 48:1–14
context: A song of the sons of Korah. The LORD is great and greatly to be praised in Zion, the city of the great King, where he has shown himself a refuge. Kings gathered against her, saw, and fled in terror. The worshipers ponder God’s loving kindness in the temple, rejoice in his judgments, and are invited to walk around Zion, count its towers, and tell the next generation that this God is their God forever and will guide them.
text: Psalm 48:1–14 Psalms A song of the sons of Korah. The LORD is great and greatly to be praised in Zion, the city of the great King, where he has shown himself a refuge. Kings gathered against her, saw, and fled in terror. The worshipers ponder God’s loving kindness in the temple, rejoice in his judgments, and are invited to walk around Zion, count its towers, and tell the next generation that this God is their God forever and will guide them. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, in his holy mountain. Psalms 48:1 Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the north sides, the city of the great King. Psalms 48:2 God has shown himself in her citadels as a refuge. Psalms 48:3 For, behold, the kings assembled themselves, they passed by together. Psalms 48:4 They saw it, then they were amazed. They were dismayed. They hurried away. Psalms 48:5 Trembling took hold of them there, pain, as of a woman in travail. Psalms 48:6 With the east wind, you break the ships of Tarshish. Psalms 48:7 As we have heard, so we have seen, in the city of the LORD of Armies, in the city of our God. God will establish it forever. Selah. Psalms 48:8 We have thought about your loving kindness, God, in the middle of your temple. Psalms 48:9 As is your name, God, so is your praise to the ends of the earth. Your right hand is full of righteousness. Psalms 48:10 Let Mount Zion be glad! Let the daughters of Judah rejoice because of your judgments. Psalms 48:11 Walk about Zion, and go around her. Number its towers. Psalms 48:12 Notice her bulwarks. Consider her palaces, that you may tell it to the next generation. Psalms 48:13 For this God is our God forever and ever. He will be our guide even to death. Psalms 48:14

title: Psalm 49:1–20
context: For the Chief Musician, a psalm of the sons of Korah. A wisdom psalm addressed to all peoples, rich and poor alike. The psalmist refuses to fear the wealthy who trust in their riches, because no one can pay God a ransom for another’s life; wise and foolish alike die and leave their wealth behind. Those who trust in themselves go down to Sheol like sheep, but God will redeem the psalmist’s soul from the power of Sheol and receive him. The refrain: a man with riches but without understanding is like the animals that perish.
text: Psalm 49:1–20 Psalms For the Chief Musician, a psalm of the sons of Korah. A wisdom psalm addressed to all peoples, rich and poor alike. The psalmist refuses to fear the wealthy who trust in their riches, because no one can pay God a ransom for another’s life; wise and foolish alike die and leave their wealth behind. Those who trust in themselves go down to Sheol like sheep, but God will redeem the psalmist’s soul from the power of Sheol and receive him. The refrain: a man with riches but without understanding is like the animals that perish. Hear this, all you peoples. Listen, all you inhabitants of the world, Psalms 49:1 both low and high, rich and poor together. Psalms 49:2 My mouth will speak words of wisdom. My heart will utter understanding. Psalms 49:3 I will incline my ear to a proverb. I will solve my riddle on the harp. Psalms 49:4 Why should I fear in the days of evil, when iniquity at my heels surrounds me? Psalms 49:5 Those who trust in their wealth, and boast in the multitude of their riches— Psalms 49:6 none of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give God a ransom for him. Psalms 49:7 For the redemption of their life is costly, no payment is ever enough, Psalms 49:8 that he should live on forever, that he should not see corruption. Psalms 49:9 For he sees that wise men die; likewise the fool and the senseless perish, and leave their wealth to others. Psalms 49:10 Their inward thought is that their houses will endure forever, and their dwelling places to all generations. They name their lands after themselves. Psalms 49:11 But man, despite his riches, doesn’t endure. He is like the animals that perish. Psalms 49:12 This is the destiny of those who are foolish, and of those who approve their sayings. Selah. Psalms 49:13 They are appointed as a flock for Sheol. Death shall be their shepherd. The upright shall have dominion over them in the morning. Their beauty shall decay in Sheol, far from their mansion. Psalms 49:14 But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol, for he will receive me. Selah. Psalms 49:15 Don’t be afraid when a man is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased; Psalms 49:16 for when he dies he will carry nothing away. His glory won’t descend after him. Psalms 49:17 Though while he lived he blessed his soul— and men praise you when you do well for yourself— Psalms 49:18 he shall go to the generation of his fathers. They shall never see the light. Psalms 49:19 A man who has riches without understanding, is like the animals that perish. Psalms 49:20

title: Psalm 5:1–12
context: Psalm 5 is David’s morning plea: he asks the LORD to give ear to his words and consider his groaning, addresses him as King and God, and watches after morning preparation. He grounds the request in God’s character—no delight in wickedness, no place for evil, hatred of evildoers, destruction of liars, abhorrence of the bloodthirsty and deceitful. Through abundant steadfast love he will enter God’s house and bow toward the holy temple in fear; he asks to be led in the LORD’s righteousness and given a straight way because of enemies whose mouths lack truth and whose throats are open graves. He asks that the guilty fall by their own counsels and be cast out for rebellion, then asks joy and protection for all who take refuge and love God’s name—for the LORD blesses the righteous and covers him with favor as with a shield.
text: Psalm 5:1–12 Psalms Psalm 5 is David’s morning plea: he asks the LORD to give ear to his words and consider his groaning, addresses him as King and God, and watches after morning preparation. He grounds the request in God’s character—no delight in wickedness, no place for evil, hatred of evildoers, destruction of liars, abhorrence of the bloodthirsty and deceitful. Through abundant steadfast love he will enter God’s house and bow toward the holy temple in fear; he asks to be led in the LORD’s righteousness and given a straight way because of enemies whose mouths lack truth and whose throats are open graves. He asks that the guilty fall by their own counsels and be cast out for rebellion, then asks joy and protection for all who take refuge and love God’s name—for the LORD blesses the righteous and covers him with favor as with a shield. Give ear to my words, LORD. Consider my meditation. Psalms 5:1 Listen to the voice of my cry, my King and my God, for I pray to you. Psalms 5:2 LORD, in the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly. Psalms 5:3 For you are not a God who has pleasure in wickedness. Evil can’t live with you. Psalms 5:4 The arrogant will not stand in your sight. You hate all workers of iniquity. Psalms 5:5 You will destroy those who speak lies. The LORD abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful man. Psalms 5:6 But as for me, in the abundance of your loving kindness I will come into your house. I will bow toward your holy temple in reverence of you. Psalms 5:7 Lead me, LORD, in your righteousness because of my enemies. Make your way straight before my face. Psalms 5:8 For there is no faithfulness in their mouth. Their heart is destruction. Their throat is an open tomb. They flatter with their tongue. Psalms 5:9 Hold them guilty, God. Let them fall by their own counsels. Thrust them out in the multitude of their transgressions, for they have rebelled against you. Psalms 5:10 But let all those who take refuge in you rejoice. Let them always shout for joy, because you defend them. Let them also who love your name be joyful in you. Psalms 5:11 For you will bless the righteous. LORD, you will surround him with favor as with a shield. Psalms 5:12

title: Psalm 50:1–23
context: A psalm of Asaph. God the LORD summons the earth from sunrise to sunset and shines out of Zion to judge his covenant people. He does not rebuke them for lack of sacrifices—every beast of the forest is already his—but calls for thanksgiving, vows kept, and prayer in the day of trouble. To the wicked who recite his covenant while hating discipline, joining thieves and adulterers, and slandering their own brothers, he warns that his silence was not approval. The one who offers thanksgiving honors him and will see God’s salvation.
text: Psalm 50:1–23 Psalms A psalm of Asaph. God the LORD summons the earth from sunrise to sunset and shines out of Zion to judge his covenant people. He does not rebuke them for lack of sacrifices—every beast of the forest is already his—but calls for thanksgiving, vows kept, and prayer in the day of trouble. To the wicked who recite his covenant while hating discipline, joining thieves and adulterers, and slandering their own brothers, he warns that his silence was not approval. The one who offers thanksgiving honors him and will see God’s salvation. The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks, and calls the earth from sunrise to sunset. Psalms 50:1 Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines out. Psalms 50:2 Our God comes, and does not keep silent. A fire devours before him. It is very stormy around him. Psalms 50:3 He calls to the heavens above, to the earth, that he may judge his people: Psalms 50:4 “Gather my saints together to me, those who have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Psalms 50:5 The heavens shall declare his righteousness, for God himself is judge. Selah. Psalms 50:6 “Hear, my people, and I will speak. Israel, I will testify against you. I am God, your God. Psalms 50:7 I don’t rebuke you for your sacrifices. Your burnt offerings are continually before me. Psalms 50:8 I have no need for a bull from your stall, nor male goats from your pens. Psalms 50:9 For every animal of the forest is mine, and the livestock on a thousand hills. Psalms 50:10 I know all the birds of the mountains. The wild animals of the field are mine. Psalms 50:11 If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all that is in it. Psalms 50:12 Will I eat the meat of bulls, or drink the blood of goats? Psalms 50:13 Offer to God the sacrifice of thanksgiving. Pay your vows to the Most High. Psalms 50:14 Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.” Psalms 50:15 But to the wicked God says, “What right do you have to declare my statutes, that you have taken my covenant on your lips, Psalms 50:16 since you hate instruction, and throw my words behind you? Psalms 50:17 When you saw a thief, you consented with him, and have participated with adulterers. Psalms 50:18 “You give your mouth to evil. Your tongue frames deceit. Psalms 50:19 You sit and speak against your brother. You slander your own mother’s son. Psalms 50:20 You have done these things, and I kept silent. You thought that I was just like you. I will rebuke you, and accuse you in front of your eyes. Psalms 50:21 “Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you into pieces, and there be no one to deliver. Psalms 50:22 Whoever offers the sacrifice of thanksgiving glorifies me, and prepares his way so that I will show God’s salvation to him.” Psalms 50:23

title: Psalm 51:1–19
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet went to him after Bathsheba. The king pleads for mercy, confesses native and actual sin, asks for a clean heart and the Spirit’s presence, and widens the prayer to Zion.
text: Psalm 51:1–19 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet went to him after Bathsheba. The king pleads for mercy, confesses native and actual sin, asks for a clean heart and the Spirit’s presence, and widens the prayer to Zion. Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions. Psalms 51:1 Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin. Psalms 51:2 For I know my transgressions. My sin is constantly before me. Psalms 51:3 Against you, and you only, I have sinned, and done that which is evil in your sight, so you may be proved right when you speak, and justified when you judge. Psalms 51:4 Behold, I was born in iniquity. My mother conceived me in sin. Psalms 51:5 Behold, you desire truth in the inward parts. You teach me wisdom in the inmost place. Psalms 51:6 Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean. Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow. Psalms 51:7 Let me hear joy and gladness, that the bones which you have broken may rejoice. Psalms 51:8 Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all of my iniquities. Psalms 51:9 Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me. Psalms 51:10 Don’t throw me from your presence, and don’t take your Holy Spirit from me. Psalms 51:11 Restore to me the joy of your salvation. Uphold me with a willing spirit. Psalms 51:12 Then I will teach transgressors your ways. Sinners will be converted to you. Psalms 51:13 Deliver me from the guilt of bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation. My tongue will sing aloud of your righteousness. Psalms 51:14 Lord, open my lips. My mouth will declare your praise. Psalms 51:15 For you don’t delight in sacrifice, or else I would give it. You have no pleasure in burnt offering. Psalms 51:16 The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart. Psalms 51:17 Do well in your good pleasure to Zion. Build the walls of Jerusalem. Psalms 51:18 Then you will delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt offerings and in whole burnt offerings. Then they will offer bulls on your altar. Psalms 51:19

title: Psalm 52:1–9
context: To the choirmaster. A Maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, “David has come to the house of Ahimelech.” David confronts the boasting tongue that loves evil, trusts God’s coming judgment on the deceitful, and sets himself as a green olive tree trusting steadfast love forever.
text: Psalm 52:1–9 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, “David has come to the house of Ahimelech.” David confronts the boasting tongue that loves evil, trusts God’s coming judgment on the deceitful, and sets himself as a green olive tree trusting steadfast love forever. Why do you boast of mischief, mighty man? God’s loving kindness endures continually. Psalms 52:1 Your tongue plots destruction, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully. Psalms 52:2 You love evil more than good, lying rather than speaking the truth. Selah. Psalms 52:3 You love all devouring words, you deceitful tongue. Psalms 52:4 God will likewise destroy you forever. He will take you up, and pluck you out of your tent, and root you out of the land of the living. Selah. Psalms 52:5 The righteous also will see it, and fear, and laugh at him, saying, Psalms 52:6 “Behold, this is the man who didn’t make God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.” Psalms 52:7 But as for me, I am like a green olive tree in God’s house. I trust in God’s loving kindness forever and ever. Psalms 52:8 I will give you thanks forever, because you have done it. I will hope in your name, for it is good, in the presence of your saints. Psalms 52:9

title: Psalm 53:1–6
context: To the choirmaster: according to Mahalath. A Maskil of David. Near twin to Psalm 14: the fool denies God; all are corrupt; God looks for seekers and finds none who does good; oppressors devour the people; terror falls where none seemed due; Zion’s salvation is longed for.
text: Psalm 53:1–6 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Mahalath. A Maskil of David. Near twin to Psalm 14: the fool denies God; all are corrupt; God looks for seekers and finds none who does good; oppressors devour the people; terror falls where none seemed due; Zion’s salvation is longed for. The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, and have done abominable iniquity. There is no one who does good. Psalms 53:1 God looks down from heaven on the children of men, to see if there are any who understood, who seek after God. Psalms 53:2 Every one of them has gone back. They have become filthy together. There is no one who does good, no, not one. Psalms 53:3 Have the workers of iniquity no knowledge, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and don’t call on God? Psalms 53:4 There they were in great fear, where no fear was, for God has scattered the bones of him who encamps against you. You have put them to shame, because God has rejected them. Psalms 53:5 Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When God brings back his people from captivity, then Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad. Psalms 53:6

title: Psalm 54:1–7
context: To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David, when the Ziphites went and told Saul, “Is not David hiding among us?” David asks to be saved by God’s name and vindicated by might, names ruthless strangers, confesses God as helper, and vows freewill thanks after deliverance.
text: Psalm 54:1–7 Psalms To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David, when the Ziphites went and told Saul, “Is not David hiding among us?” David asks to be saved by God’s name and vindicated by might, names ruthless strangers, confesses God as helper, and vows freewill thanks after deliverance. Save me, God, by your name. Vindicate me in your might. Psalms 54:1 Hear my prayer, God. Listen to the words of my mouth. Psalms 54:2 For strangers have risen up against me. Violent men have sought after my soul. They haven’t set God before them. Selah. Psalms 54:3 Behold, God is my helper. The Lord is the one who sustains my soul. Psalms 54:4 He will repay the evil to my enemies. Destroy them in your truth. Psalms 54:5 With a free will offering, I will sacrifice to you. I will give thanks to your name, LORD, for it is good. Psalms 54:6 For he has delivered me out of all trouble. My eye has seen triumph over my enemies. Psalms 54:7

title: Psalm 55:1–23
context: To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. Betrayed by a familiar friend and oppressed in a city full of violence, David pours out anguish, longs for dove’s wings, prays that God divide the tongues of the wicked, casts his burden on the LORD, and ends in trust while blood and treachery head for the pit.
text: Psalm 55:1–23 Psalms To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. Betrayed by a familiar friend and oppressed in a city full of violence, David pours out anguish, longs for dove’s wings, prays that God divide the tongues of the wicked, casts his burden on the LORD, and ends in trust while blood and treachery head for the pit. Listen to my prayer, God. Don’t hide yourself from my supplication. Psalms 55:1 Attend to me, and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and moan Psalms 55:2 because of the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked. For they bring suffering on me. In anger they hold a grudge against me. Psalms 55:3 My heart is severely pained within me. The terrors of death have fallen on me. Psalms 55:4 Fearfulness and trembling have come on me. Horror has overwhelmed me. Psalms 55:5 I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest. Psalms 55:6 Behold, then I would wander far off. I would lodge in the wilderness.” Selah. Psalms 55:7 “I would hurry to a shelter from the stormy wind and storm.” Psalms 55:8 Confuse them, Lord, and confound their language, for I have seen violence and strife in the city. Psalms 55:9 Day and night they prowl around on its walls. Malice and abuse are also within her. Psalms 55:10 Destructive forces are within her. Threats and lies don’t depart from her streets. Psalms 55:11 For it was not an enemy who insulted me, then I could have endured it. Neither was it he who hated me who raised himself up against me, then I would have hidden myself from him. Psalms 55:12 But it was you, a man like me, my companion, and my familiar friend. Psalms 55:13 We took sweet fellowship together. We walked in God’s house with company. Psalms 55:14 Let death come suddenly on them. Let them go down alive into Sheol. For wickedness is among them, in their dwelling. Psalms 55:15 As for me, I will call on God. The LORD will save me. Psalms 55:16 Evening, morning, and at noon, I will cry out in distress. He will hear my voice. Psalms 55:17 He has redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, although there are many who oppose me. Psalms 55:18 God, who is enthroned forever, will hear and answer them. Selah. They never change and don’t fear God. Psalms 55:19 He raises his hands against his friends. He has violated his covenant. Psalms 55:20 His mouth was smooth as butter, but his heart was war. His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords. Psalms 55:21 Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved. Psalms 55:22 But you, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their days, but I will trust in you. Psalms 55:23

title: Psalm 56:1–13
context: To the choirmaster: according to The Dove on Far-off Terebinths. A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Trampled all day, David confesses fear yet trusts, praises God’s word, asks that tears be kept in God’s bottle, knows God is for him, and vows thank offerings after deliverance to walk in the light of life.
text: Psalm 56:1–13 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to The Dove on Far-off Terebinths. A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Trampled all day, David confesses fear yet trusts, praises God’s word, asks that tears be kept in God’s bottle, knows God is for him, and vows thank offerings after deliverance to walk in the light of life. Be merciful to me, God, for man wants to swallow me up. All day long, he attacks and oppresses me. Psalms 56:1 My enemies want to swallow me up all day long, for they are many who fight proudly against me. Psalms 56:2 When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you. Psalms 56:3 In God, I praise his word. In God, I put my trust. I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me? Psalms 56:4 All day long they twist my words. All their thoughts are against me for evil. Psalms 56:5 They conspire and lurk, watching my steps. They are eager to take my life. Psalms 56:6 Shall they escape by iniquity? In anger cast down the peoples, God. Psalms 56:7 You count my wanderings. You put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book? Psalms 56:8 Then my enemies shall turn back in the day that I call. I know this: that God is for me. Psalms 56:9 In God, I will praise his word. In the LORD, I will praise his word. Psalms 56:10 I have put my trust in God. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me? Psalms 56:11 Your vows are on me, God. I will give thank offerings to you. Psalms 56:12 For you have delivered my soul from death, and prevented my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living. Psalms 56:13

title: Psalm 57:1–11
context: To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul, in the cave. Prayer and complaint under storm (vv. 1–6) then steadfast praise (vv. 7–11): refuge under wings; God Most High who fulfills his purpose; shame for the trampler; lions and sharp tongues; exaltation refrain; net and pit rebound; fixed heart, dawn praise, steadfast love to the heavens.
text: Psalm 57:1–11 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul, in the cave. Prayer and complaint under storm (vv. 1–6) then steadfast praise (vv. 7–11): refuge under wings; God Most High who fulfills his purpose; shame for the trampler; lions and sharp tongues; exaltation refrain; net and pit rebound; fixed heart, dawn praise, steadfast love to the heavens. Be merciful to me, God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of your wings, I will take refuge, until disaster has passed. Psalms 57:1 I cry out to God Most High, to God who accomplishes my requests for me. Psalms 57:2 He will send from heaven, and save me, he rebukes the one who is pursuing me. Selah. God will send out his loving kindness and his truth. Psalms 57:3 My soul is among lions. I lie among those who are set on fire, even the sons of men, whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword. Psalms 57:4 Be exalted, God, above the heavens! Let your glory be above all the earth! Psalms 57:5 They have prepared a net for my steps. My soul is bowed down. They dig a pit before me. They fall into the middle of it themselves. Selah. Psalms 57:6 My heart is steadfast, God. My heart is steadfast. I will sing, yes, I will sing praises. Psalms 57:7 Wake up, my glory! Wake up, lute and harp! I will wake up the dawn. Psalms 57:8 I will give thanks to you, Lord, among the peoples. I will sing praises to you among the nations. Psalms 57:9 For your great loving kindness reaches to the heavens, and your truth to the skies. Psalms 57:10 Be exalted, God, above the heavens. Let your glory be over all the earth. Psalms 57:11

title: Psalm 58:1–11
context: To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David. Imprecatory challenge to unjust gods/rulers who devise wrongs and deal violence; wicked estranged from the womb, serpent venom, deaf to charm; prayer that God break teeth, dissolve snares, sweep away; the righteous rejoice at vengeance; mankind confesses reward for the righteous and a God who judges the earth. Treat both camps’ hearing as serious—not ironic.
text: Psalm 58:1–11 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David. Imprecatory challenge to unjust gods/rulers who devise wrongs and deal violence; wicked estranged from the womb, serpent venom, deaf to charm; prayer that God break teeth, dissolve snares, sweep away; the righteous rejoice at vengeance; mankind confesses reward for the righteous and a God who judges the earth. Treat both camps’ hearing as serious—not ironic. Do you indeed speak righteousness, silent ones? Do you judge blamelessly, you sons of men? Psalms 58:1 No, in your heart you plot injustice. You measure out the violence of your hands on the earth. Psalms 58:2 The wicked go astray from the womb. They are wayward as soon as they are born, speaking lies. Psalms 58:3 Their poison is like the poison of a snake, like a deaf cobra that stops its ear, Psalms 58:4 which doesn’t listen to the voice of charmers, no matter how skillful the charmer may be. Psalms 58:5 Break their teeth, God, in their mouth. Break out the great teeth of the young lions, LORD. Psalms 58:6 Let them vanish like water that flows away. When they draw the bow, let their arrows be made blunt. Psalms 58:7 Let them be like a snail which melts and passes away, like the stillborn child, who has not seen the sun. Psalms 58:8 Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns, he will sweep away the green and the burning alike. Psalms 58:9 The righteous shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance. He shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked, Psalms 58:10 so that men shall say, “Most certainly there is a reward for the righteous. Most certainly there is a God who judges the earth.” Psalms 58:11

title: Psalm 59:1–17
context: To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch his house in order to kill him. Prayer for deliverance from bloodthirsty watchers (vv. 1–7); confidence that the Lord laughs and is fortress (vv. 8–10); plea that enemies totter as lasting warning, then be consumed so the earth knows God rules in Jacob (vv. 11–13); dogs prowling again while the singer praises strength and steadfast love morning by morning (vv. 14–17).
text: Psalm 59:1–17 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch his house in order to kill him. Prayer for deliverance from bloodthirsty watchers (vv. 1–7); confidence that the Lord laughs and is fortress (vv. 8–10); plea that enemies totter as lasting warning, then be consumed so the earth knows God rules in Jacob (vv. 11–13); dogs prowling again while the singer praises strength and steadfast love morning by morning (vv. 14–17). Deliver me from my enemies, my God. Set me on high from those who rise up against me. Psalms 59:1 Deliver me from the workers of iniquity. Save me from the bloodthirsty men. Psalms 59:2 For, behold, they lie in wait for my soul. The mighty gather themselves together against me, not for my disobedience, nor for my sin, LORD. Psalms 59:3 I have done no wrong, yet they are ready to attack me. Rise up, behold, and help me! Psalms 59:4 You, LORD God of Armies, the God of Israel, rouse yourself to punish the nations. Show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah. Psalms 59:5 They return at evening, howling like dogs, and prowl around the city. Psalms 59:6 Behold, they spew with their mouth. Swords are in their lips, “For”, they say, “who hears us?” Psalms 59:7 But you, LORD, laugh at them. You scoff at all the nations. Psalms 59:8 Oh, my Strength, I watch for you, for God is my high tower. Psalms 59:9 My God will go before me with his loving kindness. God will let me look at my enemies in triumph. Psalms 59:10 Don’t kill them, or my people may forget. Scatter them by your power, and bring them down, Lord our shield. Psalms 59:11 For the sin of their mouth, and the words of their lips, let them be caught in their pride, for the curses and lies which they utter. Psalms 59:12 Consume them in wrath. Consume them, and they will be no more. Let them know that God rules in Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah. Psalms 59:13 At evening let them return. Let them howl like a dog, and go around the city. Psalms 59:14 They shall wander up and down for food, and wait all night if they aren’t satisfied. Psalms 59:15 But I will sing of your strength. Yes, I will sing aloud of your loving kindness in the morning. For you have been my high tower, a refuge in the day of my distress. Psalms 59:16 To you, my strength, I will sing praises. For God is my high tower, the God of my mercy. Psalms 59:17

title: Psalm 6:1–10
context: Psalm 6 is David’s plea under divine displeasure: he asks the LORD not to rebuke him in anger or discipline him in wrath, seeks grace and healing while bones and soul are troubled, and cries “how long?” He asks God to turn, deliver his life, and save him for the sake of his loving kindness—for in death there is no memory of God, and in Sheol none give him praise. Weary with moaning, he floods his bed with tears and his eye wastes away because of grief and foes. Then confidence breaks through: workers of evil must depart, for the LORD has heard his weeping, heard his plea, and accepts his prayer—and all his enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled, turning back in shame in a moment.
text: Psalm 6:1–10 Psalms Psalm 6 is David’s plea under divine displeasure: he asks the LORD not to rebuke him in anger or discipline him in wrath, seeks grace and healing while bones and soul are troubled, and cries “how long?” He asks God to turn, deliver his life, and save him for the sake of his loving kindness—for in death there is no memory of God, and in Sheol none give him praise. Weary with moaning, he floods his bed with tears and his eye wastes away because of grief and foes. Then confidence breaks through: workers of evil must depart, for the LORD has heard his weeping, heard his plea, and accepts his prayer—and all his enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled, turning back in shame in a moment. LORD, don’t rebuke me in your anger, neither discipline me in your wrath. Psalms 6:1 Have mercy on me, LORD, for I am faint. LORD, heal me, for my bones are troubled. Psalms 6:2 My soul is also in great anguish. But you, LORD—how long? Psalms 6:3 Return, LORD. Deliver my soul, and save me for your loving kindness’ sake. Psalms 6:4 For in death there is no memory of you. In Sheol, who shall give you thanks? Psalms 6:5 I am weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears. Psalms 6:6 My eye wastes away because of grief. It grows old because of all my adversaries. Psalms 6:7 Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard the voice of my weeping. Psalms 6:8 The LORD has heard my supplication. The LORD accepts my prayer. Psalms 6:9 May all my enemies be ashamed and dismayed. They shall turn back, they shall be disgraced suddenly. Psalms 6:10

title: Psalm 60:1–12
context: To the choirmaster: according to Shushan Eduth. A Miktam of David; for instruction; when he strove with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, and when Joab on his return struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt. After national shaking and a sense of rejection, the people plead restore us; God sets a banner to those who fear him, claims Israel’s land and humiliates the nations, and the close confesses that vain is man’s salvation—with God we will do valiantly.
text: Psalm 60:1–12 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Shushan Eduth. A Miktam of David; for instruction; when he strove with Aram-naharaim and with Aram-zobah, and when Joab on his return struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt. After national shaking and a sense of rejection, the people plead restore us; God sets a banner to those who fear him, claims Israel’s land and humiliates the nations, and the close confesses that vain is man’s salvation—with God we will do valiantly. God, you have rejected us. You have broken us down. You have been angry. Restore us, again. Psalms 60:1 You have made the land tremble. You have torn it. Mend its fractures, for it quakes. Psalms 60:2 You have shown your people hard things. You have made us drink the wine that makes us stagger. Psalms 60:3 You have given a banner to those who fear you, that it may be displayed because of the truth. Selah. Psalms 60:4 So that your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand, and answer us. Psalms 60:5 God has spoken from his sanctuary: “I will triumph. I will divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of Succoth. Psalms 60:6 Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim also is the defense of my head. Judah is my scepter. Psalms 60:7 Moab is my wash basin. I will throw my sandal on Edom. I shout in triumph over Philistia.” Psalms 60:8 Who will bring me into the strong city? Who has led me to Edom? Psalms 60:9 Haven’t you, God, rejected us? You don’t go out with our armies, God. Psalms 60:10 Give us help against the adversary, for the help of man is vain. Psalms 60:11 Through God we will do valiantly, for it is he who will tread down our adversaries. Psalms 60:12

title: Psalm 61:1–8
context: To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. Of David. From the end of the earth with a faint heart David cries for the rock higher than he; God has been refuge and strong tower; he longs to dwell in the tent and under the wings, recalls heard vows and the heritage of those who fear the name, prays for the king’s prolonged life under steadfast love and faithfulness, and vows perpetual praise.
text: Psalm 61:1–8 Psalms To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. Of David. From the end of the earth with a faint heart David cries for the rock higher than he; God has been refuge and strong tower; he longs to dwell in the tent and under the wings, recalls heard vows and the heritage of those who fear the name, prays for the king’s prolonged life under steadfast love and faithfulness, and vows perpetual praise. Hear my cry, God. Listen to my prayer. Psalms 61:1 From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I. Psalms 61:2 For you have been a refuge for me, a strong tower from the enemy. Psalms 61:3 I will dwell in your tent forever. I will take refuge in the shelter of your wings. Selah. Psalms 61:4 For you, God, have heard my vows. You have given me the heritage of those who fear your name. Psalms 61:5 You will prolong the king’s life. His years will be for generations. Psalms 61:6 He shall be enthroned in God’s presence forever. Appoint your loving kindness and truth, that they may preserve him. Psalms 61:7 So I will sing praise to your name forever, that I may fulfill my vows daily. Psalms 61:8

title: Psalm 62:1–12
context: To the choirmaster: according to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. The soul waits in silence for God alone—rock, salvation, fortress; attackers batter like a leaning wall while blessing with lips and cursing within; the soul is charged again to wait; people must trust and pour out the heart; low and high estate are breath in the balances; no trust in extortion or riches; twice heard: power belongs to God, and to the Lord belongs steadfast love, who renders to each according to his work.
text: Psalm 62:1–12 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. The soul waits in silence for God alone—rock, salvation, fortress; attackers batter like a leaning wall while blessing with lips and cursing within; the soul is charged again to wait; people must trust and pour out the heart; low and high estate are breath in the balances; no trust in extortion or riches; twice heard: power belongs to God, and to the Lord belongs steadfast love, who renders to each according to his work. My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him. Psalms 62:1 He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I will never be greatly shaken. Psalms 62:2 How long will you assault a man? Would all of you throw him down, like a leaning wall, like a tottering fence? Psalms 62:3 They fully intend to throw him down from his lofty place. They delight in lies. They bless with their mouth, but they curse inwardly. Selah. Psalms 62:4 My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him. Psalms 62:5 He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress. I will not be shaken. Psalms 62:6 My salvation and my honor is with God. The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God. Psalms 62:7 Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah. Psalms 62:8 Surely men of low degree are just a breath, and men of high degree are a lie. In the balances they will go up. They are together lighter than a breath. Psalms 62:9 Don’t trust in oppression. Don’t become vain in robbery. If riches increase, don’t set your heart on them. Psalms 62:10 God has spoken once; twice I have heard this, that power belongs to God. Psalms 62:11 Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work. Psalms 62:12

title: Psalm 63:1–11
context: A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. The king seeks God earnestly in drought of soul and body; remembers the sanctuary's power and glory; praises steadfast love better than life; finds night meditation and the shadow of God's wings; clings while God's right hand upholds; and trusts that destroyers will fall while the king rejoices and liars' mouths are stopped.
text: Psalm 63:1–11 Psalms A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. The king seeks God earnestly in drought of soul and body; remembers the sanctuary's power and glory; praises steadfast love better than life; finds night meditation and the shadow of God's wings; clings while God's right hand upholds; and trusts that destroyers will fall while the king rejoices and liars' mouths are stopped. God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water. Psalms 63:1 So I have seen you in the sanctuary, watching your power and your glory. Psalms 63:2 Because your loving kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise you. Psalms 63:3 So I will bless you while I live. I will lift up my hands in your name. Psalms 63:4 My soul shall be satisfied as with the richest food. My mouth shall praise you with joyful lips, Psalms 63:5 when I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches. Psalms 63:6 For you have been my help. I will rejoice in the shadow of your wings. Psalms 63:7 My soul stays close to you. Your right hand holds me up. Psalms 63:8 But those who seek my soul to destroy it shall go into the lower parts of the earth. Psalms 63:9 They shall be given over to the power of the sword. They shall be jackal food. Psalms 63:10 But the king shall rejoice in God. Everyone who swears by him will praise him, for the mouth of those who speak lies shall be silenced. Psalms 63:11

title: Psalm 64:1–10
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.
