The psalmist asks God to hear his complaint and preserve him from dread; seeks hiding from secret plots and sharp tongues that shoot from ambush; exposes the wicked's confident secrecy and deep injustice; then watches God shoot His own arrow, turn their tongues against them, awaken holy fear in mankind, and call the righteous to rejoice and take refuge.
text: Psalm 64:1–10 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. The psalmist asks God to hear his complaint and preserve him from dread; seeks hiding from secret plots and sharp tongues that shoot from ambush; exposes the wicked's confident secrecy and deep injustice; then watches God shoot His own arrow, turn their tongues against them, awaken holy fear in mankind, and call the righteous to rejoice and take refuge. Hear my voice, God, in my complaint. Preserve my life from fear of the enemy. Psalms 64:1 Hide me from the conspiracy of the wicked, from the noisy crowd of the ones doing evil; Psalms 64:2 who sharpen their tongue like a sword, and aim their arrows, deadly words, Psalms 64:3 to shoot innocent men from ambushes. They shoot at him suddenly and fearlessly. Psalms 64:4 They encourage themselves in evil plans. They talk about laying snares secretly. They say, “Who will see them?” Psalms 64:5 They plot injustice, saying, “We have made a perfect plan!” Surely man’s mind and heart are cunning. Psalms 64:6 But God will shoot at them. They will be suddenly struck down with an arrow. Psalms 64:7 Their own tongues shall ruin them. All who see them will shake their heads. Psalms 64:8 All mankind shall be afraid. They shall declare the work of God, and shall wisely ponder what he has done. Psalms 64:9 The righteous shall be glad in the LORD, and shall take refuge in him. All the upright in heart shall praise him! Psalms 64:10

title: Psalm 65:1–13
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A Song. Praise is due in Zion and vows are paid; the Hearer of prayer draws all flesh; God atones when iniquities prevail; the chosen are brought near to be satisfied in His house; awesome deeds answer as hope for the ends of the earth; Creator might stills seas and peoples; and His visiting waters crown the year until wilderness, hills, meadows, and valleys shout for joy.
text: Psalm 65:1–13 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A Song. Praise is due in Zion and vows are paid; the Hearer of prayer draws all flesh; God atones when iniquities prevail; the chosen are brought near to be satisfied in His house; awesome deeds answer as hope for the ends of the earth; Creator might stills seas and peoples; and His visiting waters crown the year until wilderness, hills, meadows, and valleys shout for joy. Praise waits for you, God, in Zion. Vows shall be performed to you. Psalms 65:1 You who hear prayer, all men will come to you. Psalms 65:2 Sins overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our transgressions. Psalms 65:3 Blessed is the one whom you choose and cause to come near, that he may live in your courts. We will be filled with the goodness of your house, your holy temple. Psalms 65:4 By awesome deeds of righteousness, you answer us, God of our salvation. You who are the hope of all the ends of the earth, of those who are far away on the sea. Psalms 65:5 By your power, you form the mountains, having armed yourself with strength. Psalms 65:6 You still the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the turmoil of the nations. Psalms 65:7 They also who dwell in faraway places are afraid at your wonders. You call the morning’s dawn and the evening with songs of joy. Psalms 65:8 You visit the earth, and water it. You greatly enrich it. The river of God is full of water. You provide them grain, for so you have ordained it. Psalms 65:9 You drench its furrows. You level its ridges. You soften it with showers. You bless it with a crop. Psalms 65:10 You crown the year with your bounty. Your carts overflow with abundance. Psalms 65:11 The wilderness grasslands overflow. The hills are clothed with gladness. Psalms 65:12 The pastures are covered with flocks. The valleys also are clothed with grain. They shout for joy! They also sing. Psalms 65:13

title: Psalm 66:1–20
context: To the choirmaster. A Song. A Psalm. All the earth is summoned to shout and make God's praise glorious; His awesome deeds make enemies cringe and the earth worship; Exodus memory and forever rule warn the rebellious; peoples bless the God who kept souls alive through refining tests, nets, and fire and water into abundance; the psalmist pays trouble-vows with offerings, tells God-fearers what God did for his soul, and blesses God for hearing prayer without removing steadfast love.
text: Psalm 66:1–20 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Song. A Psalm. All the earth is summoned to shout and make God's praise glorious; His awesome deeds make enemies cringe and the earth worship; Exodus memory and forever rule warn the rebellious; peoples bless the God who kept souls alive through refining tests, nets, and fire and water into abundance; the psalmist pays trouble-vows with offerings, tells God-fearers what God did for his soul, and blesses God for hearing prayer without removing steadfast love. Make a joyful shout to God, all the earth! Psalms 66:1 Sing to the glory of his name! Offer glory and praise! Psalms 66:2 Tell God, “How awesome are your deeds! Through the greatness of your power, your enemies submit themselves to you. Psalms 66:3 All the earth will worship you, and will sing to you; they will sing to your name.” Selah. Psalms 66:4 Come, and see God’s deeds— awesome work on behalf of the children of men. Psalms 66:5 He turned the sea into dry land. They went through the river on foot. There, we rejoiced in him. Psalms 66:6 He rules by his might forever. His eyes watch the nations. Don’t let the rebellious rise up against him. Selah. Psalms 66:7 Praise our God, you peoples! Make the sound of his praise heard, Psalms 66:8 who preserves our life among the living, and doesn’t allow our feet to be moved. Psalms 66:9 For you, God, have tested us. You have refined us, as silver is refined. Psalms 66:10 You brought us into prison. You laid a burden on our backs. Psalms 66:11 You allowed men to ride over our heads. We went through fire and through water, but you brought us to the place of abundance. Psalms 66:12 I will come into your temple with burnt offerings. I will pay my vows to you, Psalms 66:13 which my lips promised, and my mouth spoke, when I was in distress. Psalms 66:14 I will offer to you burnt offerings of fat animals, with the offering of rams, I will offer bulls with goats. Selah. Psalms 66:15 Come and hear, all you who fear God. I will declare what he has done for my soul. Psalms 66:16 I cried to him with my mouth. He was extolled with my tongue. Psalms 66:17 If I cherished sin in my heart, the Lord wouldn’t have listened. Psalms 66:18 But most certainly, God has listened. He has heard the voice of my prayer. Psalms 66:19 Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, nor his loving kindness from me. Psalms 66:20

title: Psalm 67:1–7
context: To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. A Psalm. A Song. Israel asks the Aaronic grace of shining face so that God's way and saving power may be known among all nations; the peoples and nations are summoned to praise, gladness, and joy under equitable judgment and guidance; earth yields increase; and blessing on "us" aims at holy fear to the ends of the earth.
text: Psalm 67:1–7 Psalms To the choirmaster: with stringed instruments. A Psalm. A Song. Israel asks the Aaronic grace of shining face so that God's way and saving power may be known among all nations; the peoples and nations are summoned to praise, gladness, and joy under equitable judgment and guidance; earth yields increase; and blessing on "us" aims at holy fear to the ends of the earth. May God be merciful to us, bless us, and cause his face to shine on us. Selah. Psalms 67:1 That your way may be known on earth, and your salvation among all nations, Psalms 67:2 let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you. Psalms 67:3 Oh let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you will judge the peoples with equity, and govern the nations on earth. Selah. Psalms 67:4 Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you. Psalms 67:5 The earth has yielded its increase. God, even our own God, will bless us. Psalms 67:6 God will bless us. All the ends of the earth shall fear him. Psalms 67:7

title: Psalm 68:1–35
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A Song. God arises; enemies scatter like smoke and wax; the righteous exult; Jah who rides the deserts is Father of orphans and settler of the solitary while rebels parch; Sinai march, abundant rain, and provision for the needy lead to the Lord's word of fleeing kings and dove-bright spoil; Zion, chosen over Bashan's peaks, hosts God's myriad chariots—Sinai now in the sanctuary—and the ascended One who leads captives and receives gifts yes, among the rebellious also, that God may dwell; daily bearing, issues from death, and judgment on guilty heads; procession with singers and Israel's tribes; power summoned, temple gifts, rebuke of war-lovers; Egypt and Cush stretch hands; kingdoms sing to the rider of ancient heavens; awesome God from His sanctuary gives strength—Blessed be God!
text: Psalm 68:1–35 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A Song. God arises; enemies scatter like smoke and wax; the righteous exult; Jah who rides the deserts is Father of orphans and settler of the solitary while rebels parch; Sinai march, abundant rain, and provision for the needy lead to the Lord's word of fleeing kings and dove-bright spoil; Zion, chosen over Bashan's peaks, hosts God's myriad chariots—Sinai now in the sanctuary—and the ascended One who leads captives and receives gifts yes, among the rebellious also, that God may dwell; daily bearing, issues from death, and judgment on guilty heads; procession with singers and Israel's tribes; power summoned, temple gifts, rebuke of war-lovers; Egypt and Cush stretch hands; kingdoms sing to the rider of ancient heavens; awesome God from His sanctuary gives strength—Blessed be God! Let God arise! Let his enemies be scattered! Let them who hate him also flee before him. Psalms 68:1 As smoke is driven away, so drive them away. As wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God. Psalms 68:2 But let the righteous be glad. Let them rejoice before God. Yes, let them rejoice with gladness. Psalms 68:3 Sing to God! Sing praises to his name! Extol him who rides on the clouds: to the LORD, his name! Rejoice before him! Psalms 68:4 A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation. Psalms 68:5 God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land. Psalms 68:6 God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness... Selah. Psalms 68:7 The earth trembled. The sky also poured down rain at the presence of the God of Sinai— at the presence of God, the God of Israel. Psalms 68:8 You, God, sent a plentiful rain. You confirmed your inheritance when it was weary. Psalms 68:9 Your congregation lived therein. You, God, prepared your goodness for the poor. Psalms 68:10 The Lord announced the word. The ones who proclaim it are a great company. Psalms 68:11 “Kings of armies flee! They flee!” She who waits at home divides the plunder, Psalms 68:12 while you sleep among the camp fires, the wings of a dove sheathed with silver, her feathers with shining gold. Psalms 68:13 When the Almighty scattered kings in her, it snowed on Zalmon. Psalms 68:14 The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains. The mountains of Bashan are rugged. Psalms 68:15 Why do you look in envy, you rugged mountains, at the mountain where God chooses to reign? Yes, the LORD will dwell there forever. Psalms 68:16 The chariots of God are tens of thousands and thousands of thousands. The Lord is among them, from Sinai, into the sanctuary. Psalms 68:17 You have ascended on high. You have led away captives. You have received gifts among people, yes, among the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell there. Psalms 68:18 Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, even the God who is our salvation. Selah. Psalms 68:19 God is to us a God of deliverance. To GOD, the Lord, belongs escape from death. Psalms 68:20 But God will strike through the head of his enemies, the hairy scalp of such a one as still continues in his guiltiness. Psalms 68:21 The Lord said, “I will bring you again from Bashan, I will bring you again from the depths of the sea, Psalms 68:22 that you may crush them, dipping your foot in blood, that the tongues of your dogs may have their portion from your enemies.” Psalms 68:23 They have seen your processions, God, even the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary. Psalms 68:24 The singers went before, the minstrels followed after, among the ladies playing with tambourines, Psalms 68:25 “Bless God in the congregations, even the Lord in the assembly of Israel!” Psalms 68:26 There is little Benjamin, their ruler, the princes of Judah, their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali. Psalms 68:27 Your God has commanded your strength. Strengthen, God, that which you have done for us. Psalms 68:28 Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring presents to you. Psalms 68:29 Rebuke the wild animal of the reeds, the multitude of the bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample under foot the bars of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in war. Psalms 68:30 Princes shall come out of Egypt. Ethiopia shall hurry to stretch out her hands to God. Psalms 68:31 Sing to God, you kingdoms of the earth! Sing praises to the Lord— Selah— Psalms 68:32 to him who rides on the heaven of heavens, which are of old; behold, he utters his voice, a mighty voice. Psalms 68:33 Ascribe strength to God! His excellency is over Israel, his strength is in the skies. Psalms 68:34 You are awesome, God, in your sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives strength and power to his people. Praise be to God! Psalms 68:35

title: Psalm 69:1–36
context: To the choirmaster: according to Lilies. Of David. Waters to the neck, zeal for the house, gall and sour wine, imprecations on persecutors, then praise that pleases more than sacrifice and a promise that God will save Zion.
text: Psalm 69:1–36 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Lilies. Of David. Waters to the neck, zeal for the house, gall and sour wine, imprecations on persecutors, then praise that pleases more than sacrifice and a promise that God will save Zion. Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck! Psalms 69:1 I sink in deep mire, where there is no foothold. I have come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me. Psalms 69:2 I am weary with my crying. My throat is dry. My eyes fail looking for my God. Psalms 69:3 Those who hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head. Those who want to cut me off, being my enemies wrongfully, are mighty. I have to restore what I didn’t take away. Psalms 69:4 God, you know my foolishness. My sins aren’t hidden from you. Psalms 69:5 Don’t let those who wait for you be shamed through me, Lord GOD of Armies. Don’t let those who seek you be brought to dishonor through me, God of Israel. Psalms 69:6 Because for your sake, I have borne reproach. Shame has covered my face. Psalms 69:7 I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother’s children. Psalms 69:8 For the zeal of your house consumes me. The reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me. Psalms 69:9 When I wept and I fasted, that was to my reproach. Psalms 69:10 When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them. Psalms 69:11 Those who sit in the gate talk about me. I am the song of the drunkards. Psalms 69:12 But as for me, my prayer is to you, LORD, in an acceptable time. God, in the abundance of your loving kindness, answer me in the truth of your salvation. Psalms 69:13 Deliver me out of the mire, and don’t let me sink. Let me be delivered from those who hate me, and out of the deep waters. Psalms 69:14 Don’t let the flood waters overwhelm me, neither let the deep swallow me up. Don’t let the pit shut its mouth on me. Psalms 69:15 Answer me, LORD, for your loving kindness is good. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, turn to me. Psalms 69:16 Don’t hide your face from your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me speedily! Psalms 69:17 Draw near to my soul and redeem it. Ransom me because of my enemies. Psalms 69:18 You know my reproach, my shame, and my dishonor. My adversaries are all before you. Psalms 69:19 Reproach has broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; for comforters, but I found none. Psalms 69:20 They also gave me poison for my food. In my thirst, they gave me vinegar to drink. Psalms 69:21 Let their table before them become a snare. May it become a retribution and a trap. Psalms 69:22 Let their eyes be darkened, so that they can’t see. Let their backs be continually bent. Psalms 69:23 Pour out your indignation on them. Let the fierceness of your anger overtake them. Psalms 69:24 Let their habitation be desolate. Let no one dwell in their tents. Psalms 69:25 For they persecute him whom you have wounded. They tell of the sorrow of those whom you have hurt. Psalms 69:26 Charge them with crime upon crime. Don’t let them come into your righteousness. Psalms 69:27 Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not be written with the righteous. Psalms 69:28 But I am in pain and distress. Let your salvation, God, protect me. Psalms 69:29 I will praise the name of God with a song, and will magnify him with thanksgiving. Psalms 69:30 It will please the LORD better than an ox, or a bull that has horns and hoofs. Psalms 69:31 The humble have seen it, and are glad. You who seek after God, let your heart live. Psalms 69:32 For the LORD hears the needy, and doesn’t despise his captive people. Psalms 69:33 Let heaven and earth praise him; the seas, and everything that moves therein! Psalms 69:34 For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah. They shall settle there, and own it. Psalms 69:35 The children also of his servants shall inherit it. Those who love his name shall dwell therein. Psalms 69:36

title: Psalm 7:1–17
context: David, slandered by an enemy (the heading names Cush the Benjamite), takes his case to God’s court. He protests his innocence on the specific charge, asks the LORD to rise as judge of the nations, and trusts that the wicked man’s schemes will fall back on his own head. The psalm matters because it teaches the wronged to hand vengeance to a righteous Judge rather than take it, and it ends not in bitterness but in praise to the LORD Most High.
text: Psalm 7:1–17 Psalms David, slandered by an enemy (the heading names Cush the Benjamite), takes his case to God’s court. He protests his innocence on the specific charge, asks the LORD to rise as judge of the nations, and trusts that the wicked man’s schemes will fall back on his own head. The psalm matters because it teaches the wronged to hand vengeance to a righteous Judge rather than take it, and it ends not in bitterness but in praise to the LORD Most High. LORD, my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from all those who pursue me, and deliver me, Psalms 7:1 lest they tear apart my soul like a lion, ripping it in pieces, while there is no one to deliver. Psalms 7:2 LORD, my God, if I have done this, if there is iniquity in my hands, Psalms 7:3 if I have rewarded evil to him who was at peace with me (yes, I have plundered him who without cause was my adversary), Psalms 7:4 let the enemy pursue my soul, and overtake it; yes, let him tread my life down to the earth, and lay my glory in the dust. Selah. Psalms 7:5 Arise, LORD, in your anger. Lift up yourself against the rage of my adversaries. Awake for me. You have commanded judgment. Psalms 7:6 Let the congregation of the peoples surround you. Rule over them on high. Psalms 7:7 The LORD administers judgment to the peoples. Judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness, and to my integrity that is in me. Psalms 7:8 Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end, but establish the righteous; their minds and hearts are searched by the righteous God. Psalms 7:9 My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart. Psalms 7:10 God is a righteous judge, yes, a God who has indignation every day. Psalms 7:11 If a man doesn’t repent, he will sharpen his sword; he has bent and strung his bow. Psalms 7:12 He has also prepared for himself the instruments of death. He makes ready his flaming arrows. Psalms 7:13 Behold, he travails with iniquity. Yes, he has conceived mischief, and brought out falsehood. Psalms 7:14 He has dug a hole, and has fallen into the pit which he made. Psalms 7:15 The trouble he causes shall return to his own head. His violence shall come down on the crown of his own head. Psalms 7:16 I will give thanks to the LORD according to his righteousness, and will sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High. Psalms 7:17

title: Psalm 70:1–5
context: To the choirmaster. Of David, for the memorial offering. A short cry nearly twin to Psalm 40:13–17: make haste to deliver; shame those who seek the life and gloat; let seekers rejoice and say God is great; the poor and needy beg the help and deliverer not to delay.
text: Psalm 70:1–5 Psalms To the choirmaster. Of David, for the memorial offering. A short cry nearly twin to Psalm 40:13–17: make haste to deliver; shame those who seek the life and gloat; let seekers rejoice and say God is great; the poor and needy beg the help and deliverer not to delay. Hurry, God, to deliver me. Come quickly to help me, LORD. Psalms 70:1 Let them be disappointed and confounded who seek my soul. Let those who desire my ruin be turned back in disgrace. Psalms 70:2 Let them be turned because of their shame who say, “Aha! Aha!” Psalms 70:3 Let all those who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation continually say, “Let God be exalted!” Psalms 70:4 But I am poor and needy. Come to me quickly, God. You are my help and my deliverer. LORD, don’t delay. Psalms 70:5

title: Psalm 71:1–24
context: An aged believer’s plea: refuge and rock from youth through gray hairs; enemies say God has forsaken him; he asks not to be cast off in old age, vows endless praise of mighty deeds, and looks to be revived to tell the next generation—tongue talking of God’s righteousness all the day.
text: Psalm 71:1–24 Psalms An aged believer’s plea: refuge and rock from youth through gray hairs; enemies say God has forsaken him; he asks not to be cast off in old age, vows endless praise of mighty deeds, and looks to be revived to tell the next generation—tongue talking of God’s righteousness all the day. In you, LORD, I take refuge. Never let me be disappointed. Psalms 71:1 Deliver me in your righteousness, and rescue me. Turn your ear to me, and save me. Psalms 71:2 Be to me a rock of refuge to which I may always go. Give the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress. Psalms 71:3 Rescue me, my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the hand of the unrighteous and cruel man. Psalms 71:4 For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth. Psalms 71:5 I have relied on you from the womb. You are he who took me out of my mother’s womb. I will always praise you. Psalms 71:6 I am a marvel to many, but you are my strong refuge. Psalms 71:7 My mouth shall be filled with your praise, with your honor all day long. Psalms 71:8 Don’t reject me in my old age. Don’t forsake me when my strength fails. Psalms 71:9 For my enemies talk about me. Those who watch for my soul conspire together, Psalms 71:10 saying, “God has forsaken him. Pursue and take him, for no one will rescue him.” Psalms 71:11 God, don’t be far from me. My God, hurry to help me. Psalms 71:12 Let my accusers be disappointed and consumed. Let them be covered with disgrace and scorn who want to harm me. Psalms 71:13 But I will always hope, and will add to all of your praise. Psalms 71:14 My mouth will tell about your righteousness, and of your salvation all day, though I don’t know its full measure. Psalms 71:15 I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord GOD. I will make mention of your righteousness, even of yours alone. Psalms 71:16 God, you have taught me from my youth. Until now, I have declared your wondrous works. Psalms 71:17 Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don’t forsake me, until I have declared your strength to the next generation, your might to everyone who is to come. Psalms 71:18 God, your righteousness also reaches to the heavens. You have done great things. God, who is like you? Psalms 71:19 You, who have shown us many and bitter troubles, you will let me live. You will bring us up again from the depths of the earth. Psalms 71:20 Increase my honor and comfort me again. Psalms 71:21 I will also praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God. I sing praises to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel. Psalms 71:22 My lips shall shout for joy! My soul, which you have redeemed, sings praises to you! Psalms 71:23 My tongue will also talk about your righteousness all day long, for they are disappointed, and they are confounded, who want to harm me. Psalms 71:24

title: Psalm 72:1–20
context: Of Solomon. A royal prayer that God’s justice and righteousness clothe the king’s son: he judges the poor, crushes the oppressor, endures with sun and moon, rules from sea to sea, receives tribute from kings, delivers the needy, and is blessed forever—so the earth fills with his fame. The prayers by David, the son of Jesse are ended.
text: Psalm 72:1–20 Psalms Of Solomon. A royal prayer that God’s justice and righteousness clothe the king’s son: he judges the poor, crushes the oppressor, endures with sun and moon, rules from sea to sea, receives tribute from kings, delivers the needy, and is blessed forever—so the earth fills with his fame. The prayers by David, the son of Jesse are ended. God, give the king your justice; your righteousness to the royal son. Psalms 72:1 He will judge your people with righteousness, and your poor with justice. Psalms 72:2 The mountains shall bring prosperity to the people. The hills bring the fruit of righteousness. Psalms 72:3 He will judge the poor of the people. He will save the children of the needy, and will break the oppressor in pieces. Psalms 72:4 They shall fear you while the sun endures; and as long as the moon, throughout all generations. Psalms 72:5 He will come down like rain on the mown grass, as showers that water the earth. Psalms 72:6 In his days, the righteous shall flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon is no more. Psalms 72:7 He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth. Psalms 72:8 Those who dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him. His enemies shall lick the dust. Psalms 72:9 The kings of Tarshish and of the islands will bring tribute. The kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. Psalms 72:10 Yes, all kings shall fall down before him. All nations shall serve him. Psalms 72:11 For he will deliver the needy when he cries; the poor, who has no helper. Psalms 72:12 He will have pity on the poor and needy. He will save the souls of the needy. Psalms 72:13 He will redeem their soul from oppression and violence. Their blood will be precious in his sight. Psalms 72:14 He will live; and Sheba’s gold will be given to him. Men will pray for him continually. They will bless him all day long. Psalms 72:15 Abundance of grain shall be throughout the land. Its fruit sways like Lebanon. Let it flourish, thriving like the grass of the field. Psalms 72:16 His name endures forever. His name continues as long as the sun. Men shall be blessed by him. All nations will call him blessed. Psalms 72:17 Praise be to the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds. Psalms 72:18 Blessed be his glorious name forever! Let the whole earth be filled with his glory! Amen and amen. Psalms 72:19 This ends the prayers by David, the son of Jesse. Psalms 72:20

title: Psalm 73:1–28
context: A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to the pure in heart—yet Asaph’s feet almost slipped when he envied the arrogant and the prosperity of the wicked: sleek, untroubled, proud, violent, blasphemous, always at ease. He nearly called clean hands vain under daily rebuke, until the sanctuary of God: there he discerned their end—slippery places, sudden terrors, dream-phantoms. Embittered and beastlike, he is nevertheless held by the right hand, guided by counsel, received to glory; God is his portion forever. Those far from God perish; for him it is good for me to come close to God, the Lord GOD his refuge, that he may tell of all God’s works.
text: Psalm 73:1–28 Psalms A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to the pure in heart—yet Asaph’s feet almost slipped when he envied the arrogant and the prosperity of the wicked: sleek, untroubled, proud, violent, blasphemous, always at ease. He nearly called clean hands vain under daily rebuke, until the sanctuary of God: there he discerned their end—slippery places, sudden terrors, dream-phantoms. Embittered and beastlike, he is nevertheless held by the right hand, guided by counsel, received to glory; God is his portion forever. Those far from God perish; for him it is good for me to come close to God, the Lord GOD his refuge, that he may tell of all God’s works. Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart. Psalms 73:1 But as for me, my feet were almost gone. My steps had nearly slipped. Psalms 73:2 For I was envious of the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. Psalms 73:3 For there are no struggles in their death, but their strength is firm. Psalms 73:4 They are free from burdens of men, neither are they plagued like other men. Psalms 73:5 Therefore pride is like a chain around their neck. Violence covers them like a garment. Psalms 73:6 Their eyes bulge with fat. Their minds pass the limits of conceit. Psalms 73:7 They scoff and speak with malice. In arrogance, they threaten oppression. Psalms 73:8 They have set their mouth in the heavens. Their tongue walks through the earth. Psalms 73:9 Therefore their people return to them, and they drink up waters of abundance. Psalms 73:10 They say, “How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?” Psalms 73:11 Behold, these are the wicked. Being always at ease, they increase in riches. Psalms 73:12 Surely I have cleansed my heart in vain, and washed my hands in innocence, Psalms 73:13 For all day long I have been plagued, and punished every morning. Psalms 73:14 If I had said, “I will speak thus”, behold, I would have betrayed the generation of your children. Psalms 73:15 When I tried to understand this, it was too painful for me— Psalms 73:16 until I entered God’s sanctuary, and considered their latter end. Psalms 73:17 Surely you set them in slippery places. You throw them down to destruction. Psalms 73:18 How they are suddenly destroyed! They are completely swept away with terrors. Psalms 73:19 As a dream when one wakes up, so, Lord, when you awake, you will despise their fantasies. Psalms 73:20 For my soul was grieved. I was embittered in my heart. Psalms 73:21 I was so senseless and ignorant. I was a brute beast before you. Psalms 73:22 Nevertheless, I am continually with you. You have held my right hand. Psalms 73:23 You will guide me with your counsel, and afterward receive me to glory. Psalms 73:24 Whom do I have in heaven? There is no one on earth whom I desire besides you. Psalms 73:25 My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. Psalms 73:26 For, behold, those who are far from you shall perish. You have destroyed all those who are unfaithful to you. Psalms 73:27 But it is good for me to come close to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may tell of all your works. Psalms 73:28

title: Psalm 74:1–23
context: A Maskil of Asaph. The sanctuary is smashed: why cast off forever? Enemies roar in the meeting place, hack carved work, burn the dwelling, and burn every meeting place of God in the land. No signs, no prophet. Yet God is King from of old who split sea and crushed Leviathan; he is asked to remember the covenant, not forget the life of the poor, and rise against foolish taunt.
text: Psalm 74:1–23 Psalms A Maskil of Asaph. The sanctuary is smashed: why cast off forever? Enemies roar in the meeting place, hack carved work, burn the dwelling, and burn every meeting place of God in the land. No signs, no prophet. Yet God is King from of old who split sea and crushed Leviathan; he is asked to remember the covenant, not forget the life of the poor, and rise against foolish taunt. God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture? Psalms 74:1 Remember your congregation, which you purchased of old, which you have redeemed to be the tribe of your inheritance: Mount Zion, in which you have lived. Psalms 74:2 Lift up your feet to the perpetual ruins, all the evil that the enemy has done in the sanctuary. Psalms 74:3 Your adversaries have roared in the middle of your assembly. They have set up their standards as signs. Psalms 74:4 They behaved like men wielding axes, cutting through a thicket of trees. Psalms 74:5 Now they break all its carved work down with hatchet and hammers. Psalms 74:6 They have burned your sanctuary to the ground. They have profaned the dwelling place of your Name. Psalms 74:7 They said in their heart, “We will crush them completely.” They have burned up all the places in the land where God was worshiped. Psalms 74:8 We see no miraculous signs. There is no longer any prophet, neither is there among us anyone who knows how long. Psalms 74:9 How long, God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme your name forever? Psalms 74:10 Why do you draw back your hand, even your right hand? Take it from your chest and consume them! Psalms 74:11 Yet God is my King of old, working salvation throughout the earth. Psalms 74:12 You divided the sea by your strength. You broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters. Psalms 74:13 You broke the heads of Leviathan in pieces. You gave him as food to people and desert creatures. Psalms 74:14 You opened up spring and stream. You dried up mighty rivers. Psalms 74:15 The day is yours, the night is also yours. You have prepared the light and the sun. Psalms 74:16 You have set all the boundaries of the earth. You have made summer and winter. Psalms 74:17 Remember this, that the enemy has mocked you, LORD. Foolish people have blasphemed your name. Psalms 74:18 Don’t deliver the soul of your dove to wild beasts. Don’t forget the life of your poor forever. Psalms 74:19 Honor your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the earth. Psalms 74:20 Don’t let the oppressed return ashamed. Let the poor and needy praise your name. Psalms 74:21 Arise, God! Plead your own cause. Remember how the foolish man mocks you all day. Psalms 74:22 Don’t forget the voice of your adversaries. The tumult of those who rise up against you ascends continually. Psalms 74:23

title: Psalm 75:1–10
context: To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Psalm of Asaph. A Song. Thanksgiving because God’s name is near; God speaks of set-time judgment, steady pillars, and a rebuke to boastful horns; not east or west but God puts down and lifts up; the foaming cup waits for the wicked; Asaph will declare forever while horns of the wicked are cut off and the righteous lifted.
text: Psalm 75:1–10 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Do Not Destroy. A Psalm of Asaph. A Song. Thanksgiving because God’s name is near; God speaks of set-time judgment, steady pillars, and a rebuke to boastful horns; not east or west but God puts down and lifts up; the foaming cup waits for the wicked; Asaph will declare forever while horns of the wicked are cut off and the righteous lifted. We give thanks to you, God. We give thanks, for your Name is near. Men tell about your wondrous works. Psalms 75:1 When I choose the appointed time, I will judge blamelessly. Psalms 75:2 The earth and all its inhabitants quake. I firmly hold its pillars. Selah. Psalms 75:3 I said to the arrogant, “Don’t boast!” I said to the wicked, “Don’t lift up the horn. Psalms 75:4 Don’t lift up your horn on high. Don’t speak with a stiff neck.” Psalms 75:5 For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor yet from the south, comes exaltation. Psalms 75:6 But God is the judge. He puts down one, and lifts up another. Psalms 75:7 For in the LORD’s hand there is a cup, full of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out. Indeed the wicked of the earth drink and drink it to its very dregs. Psalms 75:8 But I will declare this forever: I will sing praises to the God of Jacob. Psalms 75:9 I will cut off all the horns of the wicked, but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up. Psalms 75:10

title: Psalm 76:1–12
context: Of Asaph. A song. God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel; his tent is in Salem, his dwelling in Zion. There he broke the weapons of war; he is more than mountains of prey; stouthearted warriors sank into sleep at his rebuke. He alone is to be feared; from heaven he uttered judgment to save the humble. The wrath of man shall praise him; vows are to be paid and gifts brought to the One who cuts off the spirit of princes and is feared by the kings of the earth.
text: Psalm 76:1–12 Psalms Of Asaph. A song. God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel; his tent is in Salem, his dwelling in Zion. There he broke the weapons of war; he is more than mountains of prey; stouthearted warriors sank into sleep at his rebuke. He alone is to be feared; from heaven he uttered judgment to save the humble. The wrath of man shall praise him; vows are to be paid and gifts brought to the One who cuts off the spirit of princes and is feared by the kings of the earth. In Judah, God is known. His name is great in Israel. Psalms 76:1 His tabernacle is also in Salem. His dwelling place in Zion. Psalms 76:2 There he broke the flaming arrows of the bow, the shield, and the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah. Psalms 76:3 Glorious are you, and excellent, more than mountains of game. Psalms 76:4 Valiant men lie plundered, they have slept their last sleep. None of the men of war can lift their hands. Psalms 76:5 At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse are cast into a dead sleep. Psalms 76:6 You, even you, are to be feared. Who can stand in your sight when you are angry? Psalms 76:7 You pronounced judgment from heaven. The earth feared, and was silent, Psalms 76:8 when God arose to judgment, to save all the afflicted ones of the earth. Selah. Psalms 76:9 Surely the wrath of man praises you. The survivors of your wrath are restrained. Psalms 76:10 Make vows to the LORD your God, and fulfill them! Let all of his neighbors bring presents to him who is to be feared. Psalms 76:11 He will cut off the spirit of princes. He is feared by the kings of the earth. Psalms 76:12

title: Psalm 77:1–20
context: Of Asaph. The psalmist cries aloud to God in trouble, stretches out his hand by night, refuses comfort, and finds even the memory of God a cause of moaning. Sleepless and speechless, he considers the days of old, searches his spirit, and asks whether the Lord will spurn forever, whether steadfast love and promise have ceased, whether grace and compassion are shut in anger. He then appeals to the years when the Most High stretched out his right hand, remembers the LORD's deeds and wonders, confesses God's holy way, and recounts the Exodus: redeemed people, trembling waters, storm and lightning, a path through the sea with unseen footprints, and a flock led by Moses and Aaron.
text: Psalm 77:1–20 Psalms Of Asaph. The psalmist cries aloud to God in trouble, stretches out his hand by night, refuses comfort, and finds even the memory of God a cause of moaning. Sleepless and speechless, he considers the days of old, searches his spirit, and asks whether the Lord will spurn forever, whether steadfast love and promise have ceased, whether grace and compassion are shut in anger. He then appeals to the years when the Most High stretched out his right hand, remembers the LORD's deeds and wonders, confesses God's holy way, and recounts the Exodus: redeemed people, trembling waters, storm and lightning, a path through the sea with unseen footprints, and a flock led by Moses and Aaron. My cry goes to God! Indeed, I cry to God for help, and for him to listen to me. Psalms 77:1 In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and didn’t get tired. My soul refused to be comforted. Psalms 77:2 I remember God, and I groan. I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed. Selah. Psalms 77:3 You hold my eyelids open. I am so troubled that I can’t speak. Psalms 77:4 I have considered the days of old, the years of ancient times. Psalms 77:5 I remember my song in the night. I consider in my own heart; my spirit diligently inquires: Psalms 77:6 “Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he be favorable no more? Psalms 77:7 Has his loving kindness vanished forever? Does his promise fail for generations? Psalms 77:8 Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he, in anger, withheld his compassion?” Selah. Psalms 77:9 Then I thought, “I will appeal to this: the years of the right hand of the Most High.” Psalms 77:10 I will remember the LORD’s deeds; for I will remember your wonders of old. Psalms 77:11 I will also meditate on all your work, and consider your doings. Psalms 77:12 Your way, God, is in the sanctuary. What god is great like God? Psalms 77:13 You are the God who does wonders. You have made your strength known among the peoples. Psalms 77:14 You have redeemed your people with your arm, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah. Psalms 77:15 The waters saw you, God. The waters saw you, and they writhed. The depths also convulsed. Psalms 77:16 The clouds poured out water. The skies resounded with thunder. Your arrows also flashed around. Psalms 77:17 The voice of your thunder was in the whirlwind. The lightnings lit up the world. The earth trembled and shook. Psalms 77:18 Your way was through the sea, your paths through the great waters. Your footsteps were not known. Psalms 77:19 You led your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron. Psalms 77:20

title: Psalm 78:1–72
context: A Maskil of Asaph. Give ear to teaching and dark sayings of old: fathers must tell the coming generation the LORD's glorious deeds, that children set their hope in God and not be a stubborn generation. Ephraim turned back in battle; Israel forgot wonders in Egypt and Zoan—sea, cloud, rock-water—yet rebelled in the desert, tested God for craving, and didn’t trust in his saving power. Manna and quail, wrath on the strong, flattery after slaughter, compassion that atoned and restrained anger: still they rebelled and limited the Holy One. He struck Egypt's firstborn, led his flock to the holy land, then forsook Shiloh when high places provoked him; power and glory went captive until he shamed the foe. He rejected Joseph's tent, chose Judah and Mount Zion which he loved, built his sanctuary, and chose David from the sheepfolds to shepherd Israel with upright heart and skillful hand.
text: Psalm 78:1–72 Psalms A Maskil of Asaph. Give ear to teaching and dark sayings of old: fathers must tell the coming generation the LORD's glorious deeds, that children set their hope in God and not be a stubborn generation. Ephraim turned back in battle; Israel forgot wonders in Egypt and Zoan—sea, cloud, rock-water—yet rebelled in the desert, tested God for craving, and didn’t trust in his saving power. Manna and quail, wrath on the strong, flattery after slaughter, compassion that atoned and restrained anger: still they rebelled and limited the Holy One. He struck Egypt's firstborn, led his flock to the holy land, then forsook Shiloh when high places provoked him; power and glory went captive until he shamed the foe. He rejected Joseph's tent, chose Judah and Mount Zion which he loved, built his sanctuary, and chose David from the sheepfolds to shepherd Israel with upright heart and skillful hand. Hear my teaching, my people. Turn your ears to the words of my mouth. Psalms 78:1 I will open my mouth in a parable. I will utter dark sayings of old, Psalms 78:2 which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us. Psalms 78:3 We will not hide them from their children, telling to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, his strength, and his wondrous deeds that he has done. Psalms 78:4 For he established a covenant in Jacob, and appointed a teaching in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children; Psalms 78:5 that the generation to come might know, even the children who should be born; who should arise and tell their children, Psalms 78:6 that they might set their hope in God, and not forget God’s deeds, but keep his commandments, Psalms 78:7 and might not be as their fathers— a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation that didn’t make their hearts loyal, whose spirit was not steadfast with God. Psalms 78:8 The children of Ephraim, being armed and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle. Psalms 78:9 They didn’t keep God’s covenant, and refused to walk in his law. Psalms 78:10 They forgot his doings, his wondrous deeds that he had shown them. Psalms 78:11 He did marvelous things in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan. Psalms 78:12 He split the sea, and caused them to pass through. He made the waters stand as a heap. Psalms 78:13 In the daytime he also led them with a cloud, and all night with a light of fire. Psalms 78:14 He split rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink abundantly as out of the depths. Psalms 78:15 He brought streams also out of the rock, and caused waters to run down like rivers. Psalms 78:16 Yet they still went on to sin against him, to rebel against the Most High in the desert. Psalms 78:17 They tempted God in their heart by asking food according to their desire. Psalms 78:18 Yes, they spoke against God. They said, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness? Psalms 78:19 Behold, he struck the rock, so that waters gushed out, and streams overflowed. Can he give bread also? Will he provide meat for his people?” Psalms 78:20 Therefore the LORD heard, and was angry. A fire was kindled against Jacob, anger also went up against Israel, Psalms 78:21 because they didn’t believe in God, and didn’t trust in his salvation. Psalms 78:22 Yet he commanded the skies above, and opened the doors of heaven. Psalms 78:23 He rained down manna on them to eat, and gave them food from the sky. Psalms 78:24 Man ate the bread of angels. He sent them food to the full. Psalms 78:25 He caused the east wind to blow in the sky. By his power he guided the south wind. Psalms 78:26 He also rained meat on them as the dust, winged birds as the sand of the seas. Psalms 78:27 He let them fall in the middle of their camp, around their habitations. Psalms 78:28 So they ate, and were well filled. He gave them their own desire. Psalms 78:29 They didn’t turn from their cravings. Their food was yet in their mouths, Psalms 78:30 when the anger of God went up against them, killed some of their strongest, and struck down the young men of Israel. Psalms 78:31 For all this they still sinned, and didn’t believe in his wondrous works. Psalms 78:32 Therefore he consumed their days in vanity, and their years in terror. Psalms 78:33 When he killed them, then they inquired after him. They returned and sought God earnestly. Psalms 78:34 They remembered that God was their rock, the Most High God, their redeemer. Psalms 78:35 But they flattered him with their mouth, and lied to him with their tongue. Psalms 78:36 For their heart was not right with him, neither were they faithful in his covenant. Psalms 78:37 But he, being merciful, forgave iniquity, and didn’t destroy them. Yes, many times he turned his anger away, and didn’t stir up all his wrath. Psalms 78:38 He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes away, and doesn’t come again. Psalms 78:39 How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness, and grieved him in the desert! Psalms 78:40 They turned again and tempted God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel. Psalms 78:41 They didn’t remember his hand, nor the day when he redeemed them from the adversary; Psalms 78:42 how he set his signs in Egypt, his wonders in the field of Zoan, Psalms 78:43 he turned their rivers into blood, and their streams, so that they could not drink. Psalms 78:44 He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them; and frogs, which destroyed them. Psalms 78:45 He also gave their increase to the caterpillar, and their labor to the locust. Psalms 78:46 He destroyed their vines with hail, their sycamore fig trees with frost. Psalms 78:47 He also gave over their livestock to the hail, and their flocks to hot thunderbolts. Psalms 78:48 He threw on them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, indignation, and trouble, and a band of angels of evil. Psalms 78:49 He made a path for his anger. He didn’t spare their soul from death, but gave their life over to the pestilence, Psalms 78:50 and struck all the firstborn in Egypt, the chief of their strength in the tents of Ham. Psalms 78:51 But he led out his own people like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock. Psalms 78:52 He led them safely, so that they weren’t afraid, but the sea overwhelmed their enemies. Psalms 78:53 He brought them to the border of his sanctuary, to this mountain, which his right hand had taken. Psalms 78:54 He also drove out the nations before them, allotted them for an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents. Psalms 78:55 Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, and didn’t keep his testimonies, Psalms 78:56 but turned back, and dealt treacherously like their fathers. They were twisted like a deceitful bow. Psalms 78:57 For they provoked him to anger with their high places, and moved him to jealousy with their engraved images. Psalms 78:58 When God heard this, he was angry, and greatly abhorred Israel, Psalms 78:59 so that he abandoned the tent of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men, Psalms 78:60 and delivered his strength into captivity, his glory into the adversary’s hand. Psalms 78:61 He also gave his people over to the sword, and was angry with his inheritance. Psalms 78:62 Fire devoured their young men. Their virgins had no wedding song. Psalms 78:63 Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows couldn’t weep. Psalms 78:64 Then the Lord awakened as one out of sleep, like a mighty man who shouts by reason of wine. Psalms 78:65 He struck his adversaries backward. He put them to a perpetual reproach. Psalms 78:66 Moreover he rejected the tent of Joseph, and didn’t choose the tribe of Ephraim, Psalms 78:67 But chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion which he loved. Psalms 78:68 He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth which he has established forever. Psalms 78:69 He also chose David his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds; Psalms 78:70 from following the ewes that have their young, he brought him to be the shepherd of Jacob, his people, and Israel, his inheritance. Psalms 78:71 So he was their shepherd according to the integrity of his heart, and guided them by the skillfulness of his hands. Psalms 78:72

title: Psalm 79:1–13
context: Of Asaph. The nations have entered God's inheritance, defiled the holy temple, and laid Jerusalem in ruins; the bodies of his servants are given to birds and beasts, blood poured out with none to bury them, and Israel becomes a taunt to neighbors. How long will anger and jealousy burn? Pour out wrath on the nations that don’t know him—they have devour Jacob. Do not remember former iniquities; let compassion meet the low; help and atone for the glory of the name. Why should the nations ask where their God is? Let the avenging of servants' blood be known; hear the prisoners' groans; preserve those doomed to die; return sevenfold the taunts aimed at the Lord. Yet his people, sheep of his pasture, will give thanks forever and recount his praise from generation to generation.
text: Psalm 79:1–13 Psalms Of Asaph. The nations have entered God's inheritance, defiled the holy temple, and laid Jerusalem in ruins; the bodies of his servants are given to birds and beasts, blood poured out with none to bury them, and Israel becomes a taunt to neighbors. How long will anger and jealousy burn? Pour out wrath on the nations that don’t know him—they have devour Jacob. Do not remember former iniquities; let compassion meet the low; help and atone for the glory of the name. Why should the nations ask where their God is? Let the avenging of servants' blood be known; hear the prisoners' groans; preserve those doomed to die; return sevenfold the taunts aimed at the Lord. Yet his people, sheep of his pasture, will give thanks forever and recount his praise from generation to generation. God, the nations have come into your inheritance. They have defiled your holy temple. They have laid Jerusalem in heaps. Psalms 79:1 They have given the dead bodies of your servants to be food for the birds of the sky, the flesh of your saints to the animals of the earth. Psalms 79:2 They have shed their blood like water around Jerusalem. There was no one to bury them. Psalms 79:3 We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scoffing and derision to those who are around us. Psalms 79:4 How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire? Psalms 79:5 Pour out your wrath on the nations that don’t know you, on the kingdoms that don’t call on your name, Psalms 79:6 for they have devoured Jacob, and destroyed his homeland. Psalms 79:7 Don’t hold the iniquities of our forefathers against us. Let your tender mercies speedily meet us, for we are in desperate need. Psalms 79:8 Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name. Deliver us, and forgive our sins, for your name’s sake. Psalms 79:9 Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?” Let it be known among the nations, before our eyes, that vengeance for your servants’ blood is being poured out. Psalms 79:10 Let the sighing of the prisoner come before you. According to the greatness of your power, preserve those who are sentenced to death. Psalms 79:11 Pay back to our neighbors seven times into their bosom their reproach with which they have reproached you, Lord. Psalms 79:12 So we, your people and sheep of your pasture, will give you thanks forever. We will praise you forever, to all generations. Psalms 79:13

title: Psalm 8:1–9
context: Psalm 8 marvels that the LORD’s majestic name fills all the earth and his glory stands above the heavens—yet he stills foes through the mouths of babies and infants. Under the work of his fingers the psalmist asks what frail man is, that God is mindful of him and cares for the son of man; yet humanity is crowned with glory and honor and given ruler over the works of God’s hands, all things under his feet. Hebrews 2 hears the crown and the “little while lower” fulfilled in Jesus the Son of Man—so praise returns: LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!
text: Psalm 8:1–9 Psalms Psalm 8 marvels that the LORD’s majestic name fills all the earth and his glory stands above the heavens—yet he stills foes through the mouths of babies and infants. Under the work of his fingers the psalmist asks what frail man is, that God is mindful of him and cares for the son of man; yet humanity is crowned with glory and honor and given ruler over the works of God’s hands, all things under his feet. Hebrews 2 hears the crown and the “little while lower” fulfilled in Jesus the Son of Man—so praise returns: LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your glory above the heavens! Psalms 8:1 From the lips of babes and infants you have established strength, because of your adversaries, that you might silence the enemy and the avenger. Psalms 8:2 When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have ordained, Psalms 8:3 what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him? Psalms 8:4 For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor. Psalms 8:5 You make him ruler over the works of your hands. You have put all things under his feet: Psalms 8:6 All sheep and cattle, yes, and the animals of the field, Psalms 8:7 the birds of the sky, the fish of the sea, and whatever passes through the paths of the seas. Psalms 8:8 LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! Psalms 8:9

title: Psalm 80:1–19
context: To the choirmaster: according to Lilies. A Testimony. Of Asaph, a Psalm. The Shepherd of Israel who leads Joseph and sits enthroned on the cherubim is asked to shine forth and stir up might before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. The refrain cries restore us, Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved. How long will the Lord of hosts be angry with his people's prayers? They have eaten bread of tears and drunk tears in full measure; neighbors contend and enemies laugh. The vine brought from Egypt, planted and deeply rooted to sea and River, has walls broken down so passersby pluck it and boar and field-beasts ravage it. Turn again, look from heaven, regard the vine and the son made strong; it is burned and cut down. Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of man; then we will not turn back—give life, and we will call on your name. Turn us again, LORD God of Armies. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved.
text: Psalm 80:1–19 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to Lilies. A Testimony. Of Asaph, a Psalm. The Shepherd of Israel who leads Joseph and sits enthroned on the cherubim is asked to shine forth and stir up might before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. The refrain cries restore us, Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved. How long will the Lord of hosts be angry with his people's prayers? They have eaten bread of tears and drunk tears in full measure; neighbors contend and enemies laugh. The vine brought from Egypt, planted and deeply rooted to sea and River, has walls broken down so passersby pluck it and boar and field-beasts ravage it. Turn again, look from heaven, regard the vine and the son made strong; it is burned and cut down. Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of man; then we will not turn back—give life, and we will call on your name. Turn us again, LORD God of Armies. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved. Hear us, Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit above the cherubim, shine out. Psalms 80:1 Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your might! Come to save us! Psalms 80:2 Turn us again, God. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved. Psalms 80:3 LORD God of Armies, how long will you be angry against the prayer of your people? Psalms 80:4 You have fed them with the bread of tears, and given them tears to drink in large measure. Psalms 80:5 You make us a source of contention to our neighbors. Our enemies laugh among themselves. Psalms 80:6 Turn us again, God of Armies. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved. Psalms 80:7 You brought a vine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations, and planted it. Psalms 80:8 You cleared the ground for it. It took deep root, and filled the land. Psalms 80:9 The mountains were covered with its shadow. Its boughs were like God’s cedars. Psalms 80:10 It sent out its branches to the sea, its shoots to the River. Psalms 80:11 Why have you broken down its walls, so that all those who pass by the way pluck it? Psalms 80:12 The boar out of the wood ravages it. The wild animals of the field feed on it. Psalms 80:13 Turn again, we beg you, God of Armies. Look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vine, Psalms 80:14 the stock which your right hand planted, the branch that you made strong for yourself. Psalms 80:15 It’s burned with fire. It’s cut down. They perish at your rebuke. Psalms 80:16 Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of man whom you made strong for yourself. Psalms 80:17 So we will not turn away from you. Revive us, and we will call on your name. Psalms 80:18 Turn us again, LORD God of Armies. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved. Psalms 80:19

title: Psalm 81:1–16
context: To the choirmaster: according to The Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing aloud to God, our strength! Make a joyful shout to the God of Jacob; raise song with tambourine, lyre, and harp; blow the trumpet at new moon and feast. It is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob—a decree in Joseph for a covenant, when he went out over Egypt. God relieved the shoulder of burden and freed hands from the basket; in distress they called and he delivered, answering in thunder's secret place and testing at Meribah. Hear, O my people—no strange god; I am the LORD who brought you from Egypt; open wide, and I will fill. But my people didn’t listen; Israel would not submit; so he gave them over to stubborn hearts, that they might walk in their own counsels. Oh that they would listen and walk in his ways—he would subdue enemies; haters would cringe; he would feed with finest wheat and honey from the rock.
text: Psalm 81:1–16 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to The Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing aloud to God, our strength! Make a joyful shout to the God of Jacob; raise song with tambourine, lyre, and harp; blow the trumpet at new moon and feast. It is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob—a decree in Joseph for a covenant, when he went out over Egypt. God relieved the shoulder of burden and freed hands from the basket; in distress they called and he delivered, answering in thunder's secret place and testing at Meribah. Hear, O my people—no strange god; I am the LORD who brought you from Egypt; open wide, and I will fill. But my people didn’t listen; Israel would not submit; so he gave them over to stubborn hearts, that they might walk in their own counsels. Oh that they would listen and walk in his ways—he would subdue enemies; haters would cringe; he would feed with finest wheat and honey from the rock. Sing aloud to God, our strength! Make a joyful shout to the God of Jacob! Psalms 81:1 Raise a song, and bring here the tambourine, the pleasant lyre with the harp. Psalms 81:2 Blow the trumpet at the New Moon, at the full moon, on our feast day. Psalms 81:3 For it is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob. Psalms 81:4 He appointed it in Joseph for a covenant, when he went out over the land of Egypt, I heard a language that I didn’t know. Psalms 81:5 “I removed his shoulder from the burden. His hands were freed from the basket. Psalms 81:6 You called in trouble, and I delivered you. I answered you in the secret place of thunder. I tested you at the waters of Meribah.” Selah. Psalms 81:7 “Hear, my people, and I will testify to you, Israel, if you would listen to me! Psalms 81:8 There shall be no strange god in you, neither shall you worship any foreign god. Psalms 81:9 I am the LORD, your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it. Psalms 81:10 But my people didn’t listen to my voice. Israel desired none of me. Psalms 81:11 So I let them go after the stubbornness of their hearts, that they might walk in their own counsels. Psalms 81:12 Oh that my people would listen to me, that Israel would walk in my ways! Psalms 81:13 I would soon subdue their enemies, and turn my hand against their adversaries. Psalms 81:14 The haters of the LORD would cringe before him, and their punishment would last forever. Psalms 81:15 But he would have also fed them with the finest of the wheat. I will satisfy you with honey out of the rock.” Psalms 81:16

title: Psalm 82:1–8
context: God stands in the divine council to judge the ‘gods,’ whether understood as unjust human rulers or spiritual powers. They are charged with favoring the wicked and failing the weak, the orphan, and the poor. Though called sons of the Most High, they will die like men. Jesus cites v. 6 in John 10:34.
text: Psalm 82:1–8 Psalms God stands in the divine council to judge the ‘gods,’ whether understood as unjust human rulers or spiritual powers. They are charged with favoring the wicked and failing the weak, the orphan, and the poor. Though called sons of the Most High, they will die like men. Jesus cites v. 6 in John 10:34. God presides in the great assembly. He judges among the gods. Psalms 82:1 “How long will you judge unjustly, and show partiality to the wicked?” Selah. Psalms 82:2 “Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Maintain the rights of the poor and oppressed. Psalms 82:3 Rescue the weak and needy. Deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.” Psalms 82:4 They don’t know, neither do they understand. They walk back and forth in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken. Psalms 82:5 I said, “You are gods, all of you are sons of the Most High. Psalms 82:6 Nevertheless you shall die like men, and fall like one of the rulers.” Psalms 82:7 Arise, God, judge the earth, for you inherit all of the nations. Psalms 82:8

title: Psalm 83:1–18
context: A Song. A Psalm of Asaph. O God, do not keep silence—enemies make an uproar, crafty plans against his people and treasured ones, conspiring to wipe out Israel's name. Edom, Ishmaelites, Moab, Hagrites, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, Philistia, Tyre, and Asshur join as the strong arm of Lot's children. Do to them as to Midian, Sisera, and Jabin; make nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, princes like Zebah and Zalmunna, who seized God's pastures. Make them whirling dust and chaff; pursue with tempest; fill faces with confusion, that they may seek the LORD's name—yet put to shame forever and perish in disgrace, that men may know the LORD alone is Most High over all the earth.
text: Psalm 83:1–18 Psalms A Song. A Psalm of Asaph. O God, do not keep silence—enemies make an uproar, crafty plans against his people and treasured ones, conspiring to wipe out Israel's name. Edom, Ishmaelites, Moab, Hagrites, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, Philistia, Tyre, and Asshur join as the strong arm of Lot's children. Do to them as to Midian, Sisera, and Jabin; make nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, princes like Zebah and Zalmunna, who seized God's pastures. Make them whirling dust and chaff; pursue with tempest; fill faces with confusion, that they may seek the LORD's name—yet put to shame forever and perish in disgrace, that men may know the LORD alone is Most High over all the earth. God, don’t keep silent. Don’t keep silent, and don’t be still, God. Psalms 83:1 For, behold, your enemies are stirred up. Those who hate you have lifted up their heads. Psalms 83:2 They conspire with cunning against your people. They plot against your cherished ones. Psalms 83:3 “Come,” they say, “let’s destroy them as a nation, that the name of Israel may be remembered no more.” Psalms 83:4 For they have conspired together with one mind. They form an alliance against you. Psalms 83:5 The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites; Moab, and the Hagrites; Psalms 83:6 Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek; Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre; Psalms 83:7 Assyria also is joined with them. They have helped the children of Lot. Selah. Psalms 83:8 Do to them as you did to Midian, as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the river Kishon; Psalms 83:9 who perished at Endor, who became as dung for the earth. Psalms 83:10 Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, yes, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna, Psalms 83:11 who said, “Let’s take possession of God’s pasture lands.” Psalms 83:12 My God, make them like tumbleweed, like chaff before the wind. Psalms 83:13 As the fire that burns the forest, as the flame that sets the mountains on fire, Psalms 83:14 so pursue them with your tempest, and terrify them with your storm. Psalms 83:15 Fill their faces with confusion, that they may seek your name, LORD. Psalms 83:16 Let them be disappointed and dismayed forever. Yes, let them be confounded and perish; Psalms 83:17 that they may know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth. Psalms 83:18

title: Psalm 84:1–12
context: To the choirmaster: according to The Gittith. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. How lovely is the LORD of hosts' dwelling; the soul longs and faints for his courts; heart and my flesh cry out for the living God. Yes sparrow and swallow nest near the altars. Blessed are those who dwell in his house, ever praising; blessed those whose strength is in him, highways to Zion in the heart. Through Baca they make springs; they go from strength to strength and appear in Zion. Hear, O God of Jacob; behold our shield; look on your anointed. A day in the courts beats a thousand elsewhere; better a doorkeeper in God's house than tents of wickedness. The LORD God is sun and shield; he withholds no good from the upright. Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD of hosts.
text: Psalm 84:1–12 Psalms To the choirmaster: according to The Gittith. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. How lovely is the LORD of hosts' dwelling; the soul longs and faints for his courts; heart and my flesh cry out for the living God. Yes sparrow and swallow nest near the altars. Blessed are those who dwell in his house, ever praising; blessed those whose strength is in him, highways to Zion in the heart. Through Baca they make springs; they go from strength to strength and appear in Zion. Hear, O God of Jacob; behold our shield; look on your anointed. A day in the courts beats a thousand elsewhere; better a doorkeeper in God's house than tents of wickedness. The LORD God is sun and shield; he withholds no good from the upright. Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD of hosts. How lovely are your dwellings, LORD of Armies! Psalms 84:1 My soul longs, and even faints for the courts of the LORD. My heart and my flesh cry out for the living God. Psalms 84:2 Yes, the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may have her young, near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King, and my God. Psalms 84:3 Blessed are those who dwell in your house. They are always praising you. Selah. Psalms 84:4 Blessed are those whose strength is in you, who have set their hearts on a pilgrimage. Psalms 84:5 Passing through the valley of Weeping, they make it a place of springs. Yes, the autumn rain covers it with blessings. Psalms 84:6 They go from strength to strength. Every one of them appears before God in Zion. Psalms 84:7 LORD, God of Armies, hear my prayer. Listen, God of Jacob. Selah. Psalms 84:8 Behold, God our shield, look at the face of your anointed. Psalms 84:9 For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness. Psalms 84:10 For the LORD God is a sun and a shield. The LORD will give grace and glory. He withholds no good thing from those who walk blamelessly. Psalms 84:11 LORD of Armies, blessed is the man who trusts in you. Psalms 84:12

title: Psalm 85:1–13
context: To the choirmaster. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. LORD, you have been favorable to your land and restored Jacob's fortunes; you forgave iniquity and covered all sin; you withdrew wrath and turned from hot anger. Restore us again, God of our salvation; put away indignation. Will anger last forever? Will you revive us that your people may rejoice? Show steadfast love and grant salvation. I will hear what God, the LORD, will speak—peace to his people and saints, if they not turn to folly. Salvation is near those who fear him, that glory may dwell in the land. Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace kiss; faithfulness springs from the ground; righteousness looks down from the sky. The LORD gives what is good; the land yields increase. Righteousness goes before him and makes his footsteps a way.
text: Psalm 85:1–13 Psalms To the choirmaster. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. LORD, you have been favorable to your land and restored Jacob's fortunes; you forgave iniquity and covered all sin; you withdrew wrath and turned from hot anger. Restore us again, God of our salvation; put away indignation. Will anger last forever? Will you revive us that your people may rejoice? Show steadfast love and grant salvation. I will hear what God, the LORD, will speak—peace to his people and saints, if they not turn to folly. Salvation is near those who fear him, that glory may dwell in the land. Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace kiss; faithfulness springs from the ground; righteousness looks down from the sky. The LORD gives what is good; the land yields increase. Righteousness goes before him and makes his footsteps a way. LORD, you have been favorable to your land. You have restored the fortunes of Jacob. Psalms 85:1 You have forgiven the iniquity of your people. You have covered all their sin. Selah. Psalms 85:2 You have taken away all your wrath. You have turned from the fierceness of your anger. Psalms 85:3 Turn us, God of our salvation, and cause your indignation toward us to cease. Psalms 85:4 Will you be angry with us forever? Will you draw out your anger to all generations? Psalms 85:5 Won’t you revive us again, that your people may rejoice in you? Psalms 85:6 Show us your loving kindness, LORD. Grant us your salvation. Psalms 85:7 I will hear what God, the LORD, will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, his saints; but let them not turn again to folly. Psalms 85:8 Surely his salvation is near those who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land. Psalms 85:9 Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other. Psalms 85:10 Truth springs out of the earth. Righteousness has looked down from heaven. Psalms 85:11 Yes, the LORD will give that which is good. Our land will yield its increase. Psalms 85:12 Righteousness goes before him, and prepares the way for his steps. Psalms 85:13

title: Psalm 86:1–17
context: A Prayer of David. Incline your ear, O Lord, for I am poor and needy; preserve the godly servant who trusts in you. Be gracious; gladden the soul lifted up to you—for you are good, and ready to forgive, abundant in loving kindness to all those who call. There is no one like you among the gods; all nations shall worship and glorify your name. Teach me your way; Make my heart undivided to fear your name. Great is your steadfast love; you delivered my soul from Sheol. Insolent men rise, but you are merciful and gracious; turn, strengthen, save the son of your servant. Show a sign of favor that haters may be ashamed.
text: Psalm 86:1–17 Psalms A Prayer of David. Incline your ear, O Lord, for I am poor and needy; preserve the godly servant who trusts in you. Be gracious; gladden the soul lifted up to you—for you are good, and ready to forgive, abundant in loving kindness to all those who call. There is no one like you among the gods; all nations shall worship and glorify your name. Teach me your way; Make my heart undivided to fear your name. Great is your steadfast love; you delivered my soul from Sheol. Insolent men rise, but you are merciful and gracious; turn, strengthen, save the son of your servant. Show a sign of favor that haters may be ashamed. Hear, LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy. Psalms 86:1 Preserve my soul, for I am godly. You, my God, save your servant who trusts in you. Psalms 86:2 Be merciful to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long. Psalms 86:3 Bring joy to the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, do I lift up my soul. Psalms 86:4 For you, Lord, are good, and ready to forgive, abundant in loving kindness to all those who call on you. Psalms 86:5 Hear, LORD, my prayer. Listen to the voice of my petitions. Psalms 86:6 In the day of my trouble I will call on you, for you will answer me. Psalms 86:7 There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, nor any deeds like your deeds. Psalms 86:8 All nations you have made will come and worship before you, Lord. They shall glorify your name. Psalms 86:9 For you are great, and do wondrous things. You are God alone. Psalms 86:10 Teach me your way, LORD. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name. Psalms 86:11 I will praise you, Lord my God, with my whole heart. I will glorify your name forever more. Psalms 86:12 For your loving kindness is great toward me. You have delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol. Psalms 86:13 God, the proud have risen up against me. A company of violent men have sought after my soul, and they don’t hold regard for you before them. Psalms 86:14 But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth. Psalms 86:15 Turn to me, and have mercy on me! Give your strength to your servant. Save the son of your servant. Psalms 86:16 Show me a sign of your goodness, that those who hate me may see it, and be shamed, because you, LORD, have helped me, and comforted me. Psalms 86:17

title: Psalm 87:1–7
context: A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. A Song. On the holy mount stands the city God founded; the LORD loves Zion's gates more than all Jacob's dwellings. Glorious things are spoken of the city of God. Rahab and Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush are named among those who know him—"This one was born there." Of Zion it will be said that This one and that one was born in her; the Most High establishes her. The LORD will count, when he writes up the peoples: born there. Singers and dancers: "All my springs are in you."
text: Psalm 87:1–7 Psalms A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. A Song. On the holy mount stands the city God founded; the LORD loves Zion's gates more than all Jacob's dwellings. Glorious things are spoken of the city of God. Rahab and Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush are named among those who know him—"This one was born there." Of Zion it will be said that This one and that one was born in her; the Most High establishes her. The LORD will count, when he writes up the peoples: born there. Singers and dancers: "All my springs are in you." His foundation is in the holy mountains. Psalms 87:1 The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob. Psalms 87:2 Glorious things are spoken about you, city of God. Selah. Psalms 87:3 I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who acknowledge me. Behold, Philistia, Tyre, and also Ethiopia: “This one was born there.” Psalms 87:4 Yes, of Zion it will be said, “This one and that one was born in her;” the Most High himself will establish her. Psalms 87:5 The LORD will count, when he writes up the peoples, “This one was born there.” Selah. Psalms 87:6 Those who sing as well as those who dance say, “All my springs are in you.” Psalms 87:7

title: Psalm 88:1–18
context: A Song. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. To the choirmaster: according to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, the God of my salvation, I have day and night; let my prayer come before you. Soul full of troubles; life near Sheol; counted with those going down to the pit; like the slain forgotten.
