You lay me in the lowest pit; your wrath lies heavy; waves afflict; acquaintances far; eye wastes; daily call. Will you show wonders to the dead? Kindness in the grave? Wonders in darkness? Yet I cry; morning prayer. Why cast off? Why hide your face? Afflicted from youth; wrath sweeps; terrors destroy; surround like a flood. Lover and friend shun me; companions become darkness.
text: Psalm 88:1–18 Psalms A Song. A Psalm of the Sons of Korah. To the choirmaster: according to Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite. O LORD, the God of my salvation, I have day and night; let my prayer come before you. Soul full of troubles; life near Sheol; counted with those going down to the pit; like the slain forgotten. You lay me in the lowest pit; your wrath lies heavy; waves afflict; acquaintances far; eye wastes; daily call. Will you show wonders to the dead? Kindness in the grave? Wonders in darkness? Yet I cry; morning prayer. Why cast off? Why hide your face? Afflicted from youth; wrath sweeps; terrors destroy; surround like a flood. Lover and friend shun me; companions become darkness. LORD, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you. Psalms 88:1 Let my prayer enter into your presence. Turn your ear to my cry. Psalms 88:2 For my soul is full of troubles. My life draws near to Sheol. Psalms 88:3 I am counted among those who go down into the pit. I am like a man who has no help, Psalms 88:4 set apart among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more. They are cut off from your hand. Psalms 88:5 You have laid me in the lowest pit, in the darkest depths. Psalms 88:6 Your wrath lies heavily on me. You have afflicted me with all your waves. Selah. Psalms 88:7 You have taken my friends from me. You have made me an abomination to them. I am confined, and I can’t escape. Psalms 88:8 My eyes are dim from grief. I have called on you daily, LORD. I have spread out my hands to you. Psalms 88:9 Do you show wonders to the dead? Do the departed spirits rise up and praise you? Selah. Psalms 88:10 Is your loving kindness declared in the grave? Or your faithfulness in Destruction? Psalms 88:11 Are your wonders made known in the dark? Or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness? Psalms 88:12 But to you, LORD, I have cried. In the morning, my prayer comes before you. Psalms 88:13 LORD, why do you reject my soul? Why do you hide your face from me? Psalms 88:14 I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up. While I suffer your terrors, I am distracted. Psalms 88:15 Your fierce wrath has gone over me. Your terrors have cut me off. Psalms 88:16 They came around me like water all day long. They completely engulfed me. Psalms 88:17 You have put lover and friend far from me, and my friends into darkness. Psalms 88:18

title: Psalm 89:1–52
context: A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the loving kindness of the LORD forever and make known his faithfulness to all generations. Steadfast love built up forever; faithfulness established in the heavens. Covenant with the chosen; sworn to David—offspring and throne for all generations. Heavens praise wonders; none like the Lord among the holy ones; God of hosts mighty, faithfulness all around; sea ruled; Rahab crushed; heavens and earth his; Tabor and Hermon praise; righteousness and justice the foundation of the throne; hesed and faithfulness go before him. Blessed who learn to acclaim you. Of old in vision: David found, anointed, hand established; foes crushed; firstborn highest of kings; covenant firm; offspring forever as days of heaven; if children forsake—rod and stripes, yet steadfast love not removed, faithfulness not false, oath by holiness. But now cast off and rejected; covenant renounced in appearance; crown defiled in dust; walls breached; foes exalted; throne cast down; days of youth cut short. How long will you hide? Remember short time; where is steadfast love of old sworn to David? Servants mocked; footsteps of the anointed scorned. Blessed be the LORD forever more. Amen, and Amen.
text: Psalm 89:1–52 Psalms A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing of the loving kindness of the LORD forever and make known his faithfulness to all generations. Steadfast love built up forever; faithfulness established in the heavens. Covenant with the chosen; sworn to David—offspring and throne for all generations. I will sing of the loving kindness of the LORD forever. With my mouth, I will make known your faithfulness to all generations. Psalms 89:1 I indeed declare, “Love stands firm forever. You established the heavens. Your faithfulness is in them.” Psalms 89:2 “I have made a covenant with my chosen one, I have sworn to David, my servant, Psalms 89:3 ‘I will establish your offspring forever, and build up your throne to all generations.’” Selah. Psalms 89:4 The heavens will praise your wonders, LORD, your faithfulness also in the assembly of the holy ones. Psalms 89:5 For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD? Who among the sons of the heavenly beings is like the LORD, Psalms 89:6 a very awesome God in the council of the holy ones, to be feared above all those who are around him? Psalms 89:7 LORD, God of Armies, who is a mighty one, like you? LORD, your faithfulness is around you. Psalms 89:8 You rule the pride of the sea. When its waves rise up, you calm them. Psalms 89:9 You have broken Rahab in pieces, like one of the slain. You have scattered your enemies with your mighty arm. Psalms 89:10 The heavens are yours. The earth also is yours, the world and its fullness. You have founded them. Psalms 89:11 You have created the north and the south. Tabor and Hermon rejoice in your name. Psalms 89:12 You have a mighty arm. Your hand is strong, and your right hand is exalted. Psalms 89:13 Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne. Loving kindness and truth go before your face. Psalms 89:14 Blessed are the people who learn to acclaim you. They walk in the light of your presence, LORD. Psalms 89:15 In your name they rejoice all day. In your righteousness, they are exalted. Psalms 89:16 For you are the glory of their strength. In your favor, our horn will be exalted. Psalms 89:17 For our shield belongs to the LORD, our king to the Holy One of Israel. Psalms 89:18 Then you spoke in vision to your saints, and said, “I have given strength to the warrior. I have exalted a young man from the people. Psalms 89:19 I have found David, my servant. I have anointed him with my holy oil, Psalms 89:20 with whom my hand shall be established. My arm will also strengthen him. Psalms 89:21 No enemy will tax him. No wicked man will oppress him. Psalms 89:22 I will beat down his adversaries before him, and strike those who hate him. Psalms 89:23 But my faithfulness and my loving kindness will be with him. In my name, his horn will be exalted. Psalms 89:24 I will set his hand also on the sea, and his right hand on the rivers. Psalms 89:25 He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation!’ Psalms 89:26 I will also appoint him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth. Psalms 89:27 I will keep my loving kindness for him forever more. My covenant will stand firm with him. Psalms 89:28 I will also make his offspring endure forever, and his throne as the days of heaven. Psalms 89:29 If his children forsake my law, and don’t walk in my ordinances; Psalms 89:30 if they break my statutes, and don’t keep my commandments; Psalms 89:31 then I will punish their sin with the rod, and their iniquity with stripes. Psalms 89:32 But I will not completely take my loving kindness from him, nor allow my faithfulness to fail. Psalms 89:33 I will not break my covenant, nor alter what my lips have uttered. Psalms 89:34 Once I have sworn by my holiness, I will not lie to David. Psalms 89:35 His offspring will endure forever, his throne like the sun before me. Psalms 89:36 It will be established forever like the moon, the faithful witness in the sky.” Selah. Psalms 89:37 But you have rejected and spurned. You have been angry with your anointed. Psalms 89:38 You have renounced the covenant of your servant. You have defiled his crown in the dust. Psalms 89:39 You have broken down all his hedges. You have brought his strongholds to ruin. Psalms 89:40 All who pass by the way rob him. He has become a reproach to his neighbors. Psalms 89:41 You have exalted the right hand of his adversaries. You have made all of his enemies rejoice. Psalms 89:42 Yes, you turn back the edge of his sword, and haven’t supported him in battle. Psalms 89:43 You have ended his splendor, and thrown his throne down to the ground. Psalms 89:44 You have shortened the days of his youth. You have covered him with shame. Selah. Psalms 89:45 How long, LORD? Will you hide yourself forever? Will your wrath burn like fire? Psalms 89:46 Remember how short my time is, for what vanity you have created all the children of men! Psalms 89:47 What man is he who shall live and not see death, who shall deliver his soul from the power of Sheol? Selah. Psalms 89:48 Lord, where are your former loving kindnesses, which you swore to David in your faithfulness? Psalms 89:49 Remember, Lord, the reproach of your servants, how I bear in my heart the taunts of all the mighty peoples, Psalms 89:50 With which your enemies have mocked, LORD, with which they have mocked the footsteps of your anointed one. Psalms 89:51 Blessed be the LORD forever more. Amen, and Amen. Psalms 89:52

title: Psalm 9:1–20
context: Psalm 9 is David’s thanksgiving and prayer: he gives whole-heart thanks and recounts the LORD’s wonderful deeds, glad and exulting in the Most High as enemies stumble before his presence. God has maintained his just cause from the throne of righteous judgment, rebuked nations, and blotted out the wicked—while the LORD reigns forever for justice, a high tower for the oppressed. Those who know his name trust him; he does not forsake seekers. Praise rises from Zion and deeds are told among the peoples, for he who avenges blood does not forget the afflicted. David then pleads for grace from the gates of death, that he may rejoice in salvation at Zion’s gates. Nations sink in their own pit; the LORD is known by judgment; the wicked return to Sheol, yet the needy are not always forgotten. He asks God to arise, put the nations in fear, and make them know they are but men.
text: Psalm 9:1–20 Psalms Psalm 9 is David’s thanksgiving and prayer: he gives whole-heart thanks and recounts the LORD’s wonderful deeds, glad and exulting in the Most High as enemies stumble before his presence. God has maintained his just cause from the throne of righteous judgment, rebuked nations, and blotted out the wicked—while the LORD reigns forever for justice, a high tower for the oppressed. Those who know his name trust him; he does not forsake seekers. Praise rises from Zion and deeds are told among the peoples, for he who avenges blood does not forget the afflicted. David then pleads for grace from the gates of death, that he may rejoice in salvation at Zion’s gates. Nations sink in their own pit; the LORD is known by judgment; the wicked return to Sheol, yet the needy are not always forgotten. He asks God to arise, put the nations in fear, and make them know they are but men. I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart. I will tell of all your marvelous works. Psalms 9:1 I will be glad and rejoice in you. I will sing praise to your name, O Most High. Psalms 9:2 When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish in your presence. Psalms 9:3 For you have maintained my just cause. You sit on the throne judging righteously. Psalms 9:4 You have rebuked the nations. You have destroyed the wicked. You have blotted out their name forever and ever. Psalms 9:5 The enemy is overtaken by endless ruin. The very memory of the cities which you have overthrown has perished. Psalms 9:6 But the LORD reigns forever. He has prepared his throne for judgment. Psalms 9:7 He will judge the world in righteousness. He will administer judgment to the peoples in uprightness. Psalms 9:8 The LORD will also be a high tower for the oppressed; a high tower in times of trouble. Psalms 9:9 Those who know your name will put their trust in you, for you, LORD, have not forsaken those who seek you. Psalms 9:10 Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion, and declare among the people what he has done. Psalms 9:11 For he who avenges blood remembers them. He doesn’t forget the cry of the afflicted. Psalms 9:12 Have mercy on me, LORD. See my affliction by those who hate me, and lift me up from the gates of death, Psalms 9:13 that I may show all of your praise. I will rejoice in your salvation in the gates of the daughter of Zion. Psalms 9:14 The nations have sunk down in the pit that they made. In the net which they hid, their own foot is taken. Psalms 9:15 The LORD has made himself known. He has executed judgment. The wicked is snared by the work of his own hands. Meditation. Selah. Psalms 9:16 The wicked shall be turned back to Sheol, even all the nations that forget God. Psalms 9:17 For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever. Psalms 9:18 Arise, LORD! Don’t let man prevail. Let the nations be judged in your sight. Psalms 9:19 Put them in fear, LORD. Let the nations know that they are only men. Selah. Psalms 9:20

title: Psalm 90:1–17
context: A Prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations; from everlasting to everlasting, you are God. You turn man to dust. A thousand years are as yesterday. You sweep them away like a flood, like grass. We are consumed in your anger; iniquities set before you; days pass under wrath; seventy or eighty years of toil; who knows the power of your anger? Teach us to count our days for a heart of wisdom. Return; satisfy us with steadfast love; make us glad for days of affliction; let your work appear; let the favor of the Lord establish the work of our hands.
text: Psalm 90:1–17 Psalms A Prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations; from everlasting to everlasting, you are God. You turn man to dust. A thousand years are as yesterday. You sweep them away like a flood, like grass. We are consumed in your anger; iniquities set before you; days pass under wrath; seventy or eighty years of toil; who knows the power of your anger? Teach us to count our days for a heart of wisdom. Return; satisfy us with steadfast love; make us glad for days of affliction; let your work appear; let the favor of the Lord establish the work of our hands. Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations. Psalms 90:1 Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God. Psalms 90:2 You turn man to destruction, saying, “Return, you children of men.” Psalms 90:3 For a thousand years in your sight are just like yesterday when it is past, like a watch in the night. Psalms 90:4 You sweep them away as they sleep. In the morning they sprout like new grass. Psalms 90:5 In the morning it sprouts and springs up. By evening, it is withered and dry. Psalms 90:6 For we are consumed in your anger. We are troubled in your wrath. Psalms 90:7 You have set our iniquities before you, our secret sins in the light of your presence. Psalms 90:8 For all our days have passed away in your wrath. We bring our years to an end as a sigh. Psalms 90:9 The days of our years are seventy, or even by reason of strength eighty years; yet their pride is but labor and sorrow, for it passes quickly, and we fly away. Psalms 90:10 Who knows the power of your anger, your wrath according to the fear that is due to you? Psalms 90:11 So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom. Psalms 90:12 Relent, LORD! How long? Have compassion on your servants! Psalms 90:13 Satisfy us in the morning with your loving kindness, that we may rejoice and be glad all our days. Psalms 90:14 Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil. Psalms 90:15 Let your work appear to your servants, your glory to their children. Psalms 90:16 Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us. Yes, establish the work of our hands. Psalms 90:17

title: Psalm 91:1–16
context: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High abides in the shadow of the Almighty; the LORD is refuge and fortress. He delivers from fowler's snare and deadly pestilence; covers with pinions; faithfulness a shield. No fear of night terror or day arrow, pestilence or noonday destruction. Thousand may fall; it will not come near; only see the wicked's recompense. Because the LORD is your dwelling, no evil befalls; angels charged to guard; bear up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot; tread lion and adder. "Because he has set his love on me, therefore I will deliver him; protect him who knows my name. He calls; I answer; with him in trouble; rescue and honor; long life and salvation."
text: Psalm 91:1–16 Psalms He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High abides in the shadow of the Almighty; the LORD is refuge and fortress. He delivers from fowler's snare and deadly pestilence; covers with pinions; faithfulness a shield. No fear of night terror or day arrow, pestilence or noonday destruction. Thousand may fall; it will not come near; only see the wicked's recompense. Because the LORD is your dwelling, no evil befalls; angels charged to guard; bear up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot; tread lion and adder. "Because he has set his love on me, therefore I will deliver him; protect him who knows my name. He calls; I answer; with him in trouble; rescue and honor; long life and salvation." He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty. Psalms 91:1 I will say of the LORD, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.” Psalms 91:2 For he will deliver you from the snare of the fowler, and from the deadly pestilence. Psalms 91:3 He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart. Psalms 91:4 You shall not be afraid of the terror by night, nor of the arrow that flies by day, Psalms 91:5 nor of the pestilence that walks in darkness, nor of the destruction that wastes at noonday. Psalms 91:6 A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand; but it will not come near you. Psalms 91:7 You will only look with your eyes, and see the recompense of the wicked. Psalms 91:8 Because you have made the LORD your refuge, and the Most High your dwelling place, Psalms 91:9 no evil shall happen to you, neither shall any plague come near your dwelling. Psalms 91:10 For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways. Psalms 91:11 They will bear you up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot against a stone. Psalms 91:12 You will tread on the lion and cobra. You will trample the young lion and the serpent underfoot. Psalms 91:13 “Because he has set his love on me, therefore I will deliver him. I will set him on high, because he has known my name. Psalms 91:14 He will call on me, and I will answer him. I will be with him in trouble. I will deliver him, and honor him. Psalms 91:15 I will satisfy him with long life, and show him my salvation.” Psalms 91:16

title: Psalm 92:1–15
context: A Psalm. A Song for the Sabbath. It is a good thing to give thanks to the LORD and sing to the Most High; declare loving kindness in the morning, and faithfulness by night, with lute, harp, and lyre. Glad in his work; great works; deep thoughts. The stupid cannot know that though the wicked spring up as the grass they are doomed forever—but the LORD is on high forever. Enemies perish; horn exalted; fresh oil; eyes see downfall. The righteous flourish like palm and cedar, planted in the LORD's house, still fruit in old age, to show that the LORD is upright—my rock, no unrighteousness in him.
text: Psalm 92:1–15 Psalms A Psalm. A Song for the Sabbath. It is a good thing to give thanks to the LORD and sing to the Most High; declare loving kindness in the morning, and faithfulness by night, with lute, harp, and lyre. Glad in his work; great works; deep thoughts. The stupid cannot know that though the wicked spring up as the grass they are doomed forever—but the LORD is on high forever. Enemies perish; horn exalted; fresh oil; eyes see downfall. The righteous flourish like palm and cedar, planted in the LORD's house, still fruit in old age, to show that the LORD is upright—my rock, no unrighteousness in him. It is a good thing to give thanks to the LORD, to sing praises to your name, Most High, Psalms 92:1 to proclaim your loving kindness in the morning, and your faithfulness every night, Psalms 92:2 with the ten-stringed lute, with the harp, and with the melody of the lyre. Psalms 92:3 For you, LORD, have made me glad through your work. I will triumph in the works of your hands. Psalms 92:4 How great are your works, LORD! Your thoughts are very deep. Psalms 92:5 A senseless man doesn’t know, neither does a fool understand this: Psalms 92:6 though the wicked spring up as the grass, and all the evildoers flourish, they will be destroyed forever. Psalms 92:7 But you, LORD, are on high forever more. Psalms 92:8 For behold, your enemies, LORD, for behold, your enemies shall perish. All the evildoers will be scattered. Psalms 92:9 But you have exalted my horn like that of the wild ox. I am anointed with fresh oil. Psalms 92:10 My eye has also seen my enemies. My ears have heard of the wicked enemies who rise up against me. Psalms 92:11 The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree. He will grow like a cedar in Lebanon. Psalms 92:12 They are planted in the LORD’s house. They will flourish in our God’s courts. Psalms 92:13 They will still produce fruit in old age. They will be full of sap and green, Psalms 92:14 to show that the LORD is upright. He is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him. Psalms 92:15

title: Psalm 93:1–5
context: The LORD reigns, robed in majesty and strength; the world is established, never moved. His throne is established from long ago; he is from everlasting. Floods lift up voice and roaring; yet mightier than many waters and sea waves is the LORD on high. His decrees are very trustworthy; holiness befits his house forevermore.
text: Psalm 93:1–5 Psalms The LORD reigns, robed in majesty and strength; the world is established, never moved. His throne is established from long ago; he is from everlasting. Floods lift up voice and roaring; yet mightier than many waters and sea waves is the LORD on high. His decrees are very trustworthy; holiness befits his house forevermore. The LORD reigns! He is clothed with majesty! The LORD is armed with strength. The world also is established. It can’t be moved. Psalms 93:1 Your throne is established from long ago. You are from everlasting. Psalms 93:2 The floods have lifted up, LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice. The floods lift up their waves. Psalms 93:3 Above the voices of many waters, the mighty breakers of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty. Psalms 93:4 Your statutes stand firm. Holiness adorns your house, LORD, forever more. Psalms 93:5

title: Psalm 94:1–23
context: O God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out. Rise, Judge of the earth, and repay the proud. How long will the wicked triumph, pour out arrogant words, crush the people, kill widow, sojourner, and fatherless, saying the LORD will not see? Fools are summoned to understand: the Planter of the ear hears; the Former of the eye sees; the Discipliner of nations rebukes; the Lord knows that man's thoughts are breath. Blessed is the one he disciplines and teaches from his law—rest until the pit is dug for the wicked. For he will not forsake his people. Justice will return; the upright follow it. Who rises for me? If the Lord had not helped, the soul would dwell in silence; when the foot slips, steadfast love holds up; when cares multiply, consolations cheer. Wicked rulers framing injustice by statute cannot ally with him. The Lord is stronghold and rock; he will bring back their own iniquity, and will cut them off.
text: Psalm 94:1–23 Psalms O God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out. Rise, Judge of the earth, and repay the proud. How long will the wicked triumph, pour out arrogant words, crush the people, kill widow, sojourner, and fatherless, saying the LORD will not see? Fools are summoned to understand: the Planter of the ear hears; the Former of the eye sees; the Discipliner of nations rebukes; the Lord knows that man's thoughts are breath. Blessed is the one he disciplines and teaches from his law—rest until the pit is dug for the wicked. For he will not forsake his people. Justice will return; the upright follow it. Who rises for me? If the Lord had not helped, the soul would dwell in silence; when the foot slips, steadfast love holds up; when cares multiply, consolations cheer. Wicked rulers framing injustice by statute cannot ally with him. The Lord is stronghold and rock; he will bring back their own iniquity, and will cut them off. LORD, you God to whom vengeance belongs, you God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out. Psalms 94:1 Rise up, you judge of the earth. Pay back the proud what they deserve. Psalms 94:2 LORD, how long will the wicked, how long will the wicked triumph? Psalms 94:3 They pour out arrogant words. All the evildoers boast. Psalms 94:4 They break your people in pieces, LORD, and afflict your heritage. Psalms 94:5 They kill the widow and the alien, and murder the fatherless. Psalms 94:6 They say, “The LORD will not see, neither will Jacob’s God consider.” Psalms 94:7 Consider, you senseless among the people; you fools, when will you be wise? Psalms 94:8 He who implanted the ear, won’t he hear? He who formed the eye, won’t he see? Psalms 94:9 He who disciplines the nations, won’t he punish? He who teaches man knows. Psalms 94:10 The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile. Psalms 94:11 Blessed is the man whom you discipline, LORD, and teach out of your law, Psalms 94:12 that you may give him rest from the days of adversity, until the pit is dug for the wicked. Psalms 94:13 For the LORD won’t reject his people, neither will he forsake his inheritance. Psalms 94:14 For judgment will return to righteousness. All the upright in heart shall follow it. Psalms 94:15 Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand up for me against the evildoers? Psalms 94:16 Unless the LORD had been my help, my soul would have soon lived in silence. Psalms 94:17 When I said, “My foot is slipping!” Your loving kindness, LORD, held me up. Psalms 94:18 In the multitude of my thoughts within me, your comforts delight my soul. Psalms 94:19 Shall the throne of wickedness have fellowship with you, which brings about mischief by statute? Psalms 94:20 They gather themselves together against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood. Psalms 94:21 But the LORD has been my high tower, my God, the rock of my refuge. Psalms 94:22 He has brought on them their own iniquity, and will cut them off in their own wickedness. The LORD, our God, will cut them off. Psalms 94:23

title: Psalm 95:1–11
context: Oh come, sing to the Lord, the rock of our salvation; enter his presence with thanksgiving and songs. He is a great God and King above all gods; depths and heights, sea and dry land are his. Come, worship and kneel before the LORD, our Maker, for he is our God. We the people of his pasture, the sheep in his care. Today, oh that you would hear his voice! Don’t harden your heart, as at Meribah and Massah, when the fathers tested him though they had seen his work. Forty years he loathed that generation—astray in heart, ignorant of his ways—and swore they would not enter his rest.
text: Psalm 95:1–11 Psalms Oh come, sing to the Lord, the rock of our salvation; enter his presence with thanksgiving and songs. He is a great God and King above all gods; depths and heights, sea and dry land are his. Come, worship and kneel before the LORD, our Maker, for he is our God. We the people of his pasture, the sheep in his care. Today, oh that you would hear his voice! Don’t harden your heart, as at Meribah and Massah, when the fathers tested him though they had seen his work. Forty years he loathed that generation—astray in heart, ignorant of his ways—and swore they would not enter his rest. Oh come, let’s sing to the LORD. Let’s shout aloud to the rock of our salvation! Psalms 95:1 Let’s come before his presence with thanksgiving. Let’s extol him with songs! Psalms 95:2 For the LORD is a great God, a great King above all gods. Psalms 95:3 In his hand are the deep places of the earth. The heights of the mountains are also his. Psalms 95:4 The sea is his, and he made it. His hands formed the dry land. Psalms 95:5 Oh come, let’s worship and bow down. Let’s kneel before the LORD, our Maker, Psalms 95:6 for he is our God. We are the people of his pasture, and the sheep in his care. Today, oh that you would hear his voice! Psalms 95:7 Don’t harden your heart, as at Meribah, as in the day of Massah in the wilderness, Psalms 95:8 when your fathers tempted me, tested me, and saw my work. Psalms 95:9 Forty long years I was grieved with that generation, and said, “They are a people who err in their heart. They have not known my ways.” Psalms 95:10 Therefore I swore in my wrath, “They won’t enter into my rest.” Psalms 95:11

title: Psalm 96:1–13
context: Sing to the Lord a new song, all the earth; bless his name; tell his salvation day by day; declare his glory and marvelous works among the nations. Great is the Lord, feared above all gods—for the peoples' gods are idols, but the LORD made the heavens. Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and beauty in his sanctuary. Families of nations, ascribe glory and strength; bring an offering into his courts; worship in holy array. Tremble, all the earth. Say among the nations, The Lord reigns—the world stands firm; he judges the peoples with equity. Let heavens, earth, sea, field, and forest rejoice before the Lord, for he comes to judge the earth in righteousness and faithfulness.
text: Psalm 96:1–13 Psalms Sing to the Lord a new song, all the earth; bless his name; tell his salvation day by day; declare his glory and marvelous works among the nations. Great is the Lord, feared above all gods—for the peoples' gods are idols, but the LORD made the heavens. Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and beauty in his sanctuary. Families of nations, ascribe glory and strength; bring an offering into his courts; worship in holy array. Tremble, all the earth. Say among the nations, The Lord reigns—the world stands firm; he judges the peoples with equity. Let heavens, earth, sea, field, and forest rejoice before the Lord, for he comes to judge the earth in righteousness and faithfulness. Sing to the LORD a new song! Sing to the LORD, all the earth. Psalms 96:1 Sing to the LORD! Bless his name! Proclaim his salvation from day to day! Psalms 96:2 Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples. Psalms 96:3 For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised! He is to be feared above all gods. Psalms 96:4 For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens. Psalms 96:5 Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary. Psalms 96:6 Ascribe to the LORD, you families of nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength. Psalms 96:7 Ascribe to the LORD the glory due to his name. Bring an offering, and come into his courts. Psalms 96:8 Worship the LORD in holy array. Tremble before him, all the earth. Psalms 96:9 Say among the nations, “The LORD reigns.” The world is also established. It can’t be moved. He will judge the peoples with equity. Psalms 96:10 Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice. Let the sea roar, and its fullness! Psalms 96:11 Let the field and all that is in it exult! Then all the trees of the woods shall sing for joy Psalms 96:12 before the LORD; for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, the peoples with his truth. Psalms 96:13

title: Psalm 97:1–12
context: The Lord reigns—let the earth rejoice and many coastlands be glad! Clouds and darkness surround him; righteousness and justice are his throne's foundation. Fire goes before him and burns his adversaries; lightnings light the world; the earth sees and trembles; mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD of the whole earth. The heavens declare his righteousness; all peoples see his glory. Idol-worshipers are put to shame; all gods are summoned to worship him. Zion heard and was glad; Judah's daughters rejoice at his judgments. For he is most high over the earth, exalted far above all gods. Those who love the Lord hate evil; he preserves his saints' lives and delivers them from the wicked. Light is sown for the righteous, joy for the upright. Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous people! Give thanks to his holy Name.
text: Psalm 97:1–12 Psalms The Lord reigns—let the earth rejoice and many coastlands be glad! Clouds and darkness surround him; righteousness and justice are his throne's foundation. Fire goes before him and burns his adversaries; lightnings light the world; the earth sees and trembles; mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD of the whole earth. The heavens declare his righteousness; all peoples see his glory. Idol-worshipers are put to shame; all gods are summoned to worship him. Zion heard and was glad; Judah's daughters rejoice at his judgments. For he is most high over the earth, exalted far above all gods. Those who love the Lord hate evil; he preserves his saints' lives and delivers them from the wicked. Light is sown for the righteous, joy for the upright. Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous people! Give thanks to his holy Name. The LORD reigns! Let the earth rejoice! Let the multitude of islands be glad! Psalms 97:1 Clouds and darkness are around him. Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne. Psalms 97:2 A fire goes before him, and burns up his adversaries on every side. Psalms 97:3 His lightning lights up the world. The earth sees, and trembles. Psalms 97:4 The mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD, at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth. Psalms 97:5 The heavens declare his righteousness. All the peoples have seen his glory. Psalms 97:6 Let all them be shamed who serve engraved images, who boast in their idols. Worship him, all you gods! Psalms 97:7 Zion heard and was glad. The daughters of Judah rejoiced because of your judgments, LORD. Psalms 97:8 For you, LORD, are most high above all the earth. You are exalted far above all gods. Psalms 97:9 You who love the LORD, hate evil! He preserves the souls of his saints. He delivers them out of the hand of the wicked. Psalms 97:10 Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart. Psalms 97:11 Be glad in the LORD, you righteous people! Give thanks to his holy Name. Psalms 97:12

title: Psalm 98:1–9
context: A ‘new song’ celebrates the LORD’s victory and his faithfulness to Israel, now seen by the whole earth. Praise widens in circles: from Israel, to all nations with music, to sea, rivers, and hills. The reason for such joy is that the LORD comes to judge the world in righteousness. Isaac Watts built ‘Joy to the World’ on this psalm.
text: Psalm 98:1–9 Psalms A ‘new song’ celebrates the LORD’s victory and his faithfulness to Israel, now seen by the whole earth. Praise widens in circles: from Israel, to all nations with music, to sea, rivers, and hills. The reason for such joy is that the LORD comes to judge the world in righteousness. Isaac Watts built ‘Joy to the World’ on this psalm. Sing to the LORD a new song, for he has done marvelous things! His right hand and his holy arm have worked salvation for him. Psalms 98:1 The LORD has made known his salvation. He has openly shown his righteousness in the sight of the nations. Psalms 98:2 He has remembered his loving kindness and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God. Psalms 98:3 Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth! Burst out and sing for joy, yes, sing praises! Psalms 98:4 Sing praises to the LORD with the harp, with the harp and the voice of melody. Psalms 98:5 With trumpets and sound of the ram’s horn, make a joyful noise before the King, the LORD. Psalms 98:6 Let the sea roar with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell therein. Psalms 98:7 Let the rivers clap their hands. Let the mountains sing for joy together. Psalms 98:8 Let them sing before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with equity. Psalms 98:9

title: Psalm 99:1–9
context: One of the royal psalms proclaiming that the LORD reigns, structured around the refrain ‘He is holy.’ His holiness shows itself in majesty over the nations, in justice for Jacob, and in answering Moses, Aaron, and Samuel when they prayed. He forgave his people and still disciplined their sins.
text: Psalm 99:1–9 Psalms One of the royal psalms proclaiming that the LORD reigns, structured around the refrain ‘He is holy.’ His holiness shows itself in majesty over the nations, in justice for Jacob, and in answering Moses, Aaron, and Samuel when they prayed. He forgave his people and still disciplined their sins. The LORD reigns! Let the peoples tremble. He sits enthroned among the cherubim. Let the earth be moved. Psalms 99:1 The LORD is great in Zion. He is high above all the peoples. Psalms 99:2 Let them praise your great and awesome name. He is Holy! Psalms 99:3 The King’s strength also loves justice. You establish equity. You execute justice and righteousness in Jacob. Psalms 99:4 Exalt the LORD our God. Worship at his footstool. He is Holy! Psalms 99:5 Moses and Aaron were among his priests, Samuel was among those who call on his name. They called on the LORD, and he answered them. Psalms 99:6 He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud. They kept his testimonies, the statute that he gave them. Psalms 99:7 You answered them, LORD our God. You are a God who forgave them, although you took vengeance for their doings. Psalms 99:8 Exalt the LORD, our God. Worship at his holy hill, for the LORD, our God, is holy! Psalms 99:9

title: Revelation 1:1–3
context: The book opens by naming itself the revelation of Jesus Christ, given by God, sent through an angel, and testified by John. A blessing rests on the one who reads it aloud and on those who hear and keep it, because the time is near.
text: Revelation 1:1–3 Revelation The book opens by naming itself the revelation of Jesus Christ, given by God, sent through an angel, and testified by John. A blessing rests on the one who reads it aloud and on those who hear and keep it, because the time is near. This is the Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show to his servants the things which must happen soon, which he sent and made known by his angel to his servant, John, Revelation 1:1 who testified to God’s word and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, about everything that he saw. Revelation 1:2 Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of the prophecy, and keep the things that are written in it, for the time is near. Revelation 1:3

title: Revelation 1:4–8
context: John greets the seven churches with grace and peace from the eternal God, from the seven Spirits before his throne, and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, firstborn of the dead, and ruler of the kings of the earth. He praises Christ, who loves us and freed us by his blood, and announces his coming with the clouds. God speaks as the Alpha and the Omega, the Almighty.
text: Revelation 1:4–8 Revelation John greets the seven churches with grace and peace from the eternal God, from the seven Spirits before his throne, and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, firstborn of the dead, and ruler of the kings of the earth. He praises Christ, who loves us and freed us by his blood, and announces his coming with the clouds. God speaks as the Alpha and the Omega, the Almighty. John, to the seven assemblies that are in Asia: Grace to you and peace from God, who is and who was and who is to come; and from the seven Spirits who are before his throne; Revelation 1:4 and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To him who loves us, and washed us from our sins by his blood— Revelation 1:5 and he made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God and Father—to him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen. Revelation 1:6 Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, including those who pierced him. All the tribes of the earth will mourn over him. Even so, Amen. Revelation 1:7 “I am the Alpha and the Omega, ” says the Lord God, “who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.” Revelation 1:8

title: Revelation 1:9–20
context: On Patmos, John hears a loud voice on the Lord’s day and turns to see one like a son of man walking among seven golden lampstands. His appearance is glorious and terrifying, and John falls at his feet. Christ lays his hand on him, tells him not to fear, and declares himself the living one who holds the keys of Death and Hades. He commissions John to write and explains the stars and lampstands.
text: Revelation 1:9–20 Revelation On Patmos, John hears a loud voice on the Lord’s day and turns to see one like a son of man walking among seven golden lampstands. His appearance is glorious and terrifying, and John falls at his feet. Christ lays his hand on him, tells him not to fear, and declares himself the living one who holds the keys of Death and Hades. He commissions John to write and explains the stars and lampstands. I John, your brother and partner with you in the oppression, Kingdom, and perseverance in Christ Jesus, was on the isle that is called Patmos because of God’s Word and the testimony of Jesus Christ. Revelation 1:9 I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a loud voice, like a trumpet Revelation 1:10 saying, “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.” Revelation 1:11 I turned to see the voice that spoke with me. Having turned, I saw seven golden lamp stands. Revelation 1:12 And among the lamp stands was one like a son of man, clothed with a robe reaching down to his feet, and with a golden sash around his chest. Revelation 1:13 His head and his hair were white as white wool, like snow. His eyes were like a flame of fire. Revelation 1:14 His feet were like burnished brass, as if it had been refined in a furnace. His voice was like the voice of many waters. Revelation 1:15 He had seven stars in his right hand. Out of his mouth proceeded a sharp two-edged sword. His face was like the sun shining at its brightest. Revelation 1:16 When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me, saying, “Don’t be afraid. I am the first and the last, Revelation 1:17 and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever. Amen. I have the keys of Death and of Hades. Revelation 1:18 Write therefore the things which you have seen, and the things which are, and the things which will happen hereafter. Revelation 1:19 The mystery of the seven stars which you saw in my right hand, and the seven golden lamp stands is this: The seven stars are the angels of the seven assemblies. The seven lamp stands are seven assemblies. Revelation 1:20

title: Revelation 10:1–11
context: A mighty angel stands on sea and land holding a little open scroll. Seven thunders speak, but John is told to seal up what they said. The angel swears that there will be no more delay, and that the mystery of God will be finished at the seventh trumpet. John eats the scroll, sweet in his mouth and bitter in his stomach, and is told he must prophesy again about many peoples and kings.
text: Revelation 10:1–11 Revelation A mighty angel stands on sea and land holding a little open scroll. Seven thunders speak, but John is told to seal up what they said. The angel swears that there will be no more delay, and that the mystery of God will be finished at the seventh trumpet. John eats the scroll, sweet in his mouth and bitter in his stomach, and is told he must prophesy again about many peoples and kings. I saw a mighty angel coming down out of the sky, clothed with a cloud. A rainbow was on his head. His face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire. Revelation 10:1 He had in his hand a little open book. He set his right foot on the sea, and his left on the land. Revelation 10:2 He cried with a loud voice, as a lion roars. When he cried, the seven thunders uttered their voices. Revelation 10:3 When the seven thunders sounded, I was about to write; but I heard a voice from the sky saying, “Seal up the things which the seven thunders said, and don’t write them.” Revelation 10:4 The angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the land lifted up his right hand to the sky Revelation 10:5 and swore by him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things that are in it, the earth and the things that are in it, and the sea and the things that are in it, that there will no longer be delay, Revelation 10:6 but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound, then the mystery of God is finished, as he declared to his servants the prophets. Revelation 10:7 The voice which I heard from heaven, again speaking with me, said, “Go, take the book which is open in the hand of the angel who stands on the sea and on the land.” Revelation 10:8 I went to the angel, telling him to give me the little book. He said to me, “Take it and eat it. It will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.” Revelation 10:9 I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it. It was as sweet as honey in my mouth. When I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter. Revelation 10:10 They told me, “You must prophesy again over many peoples, nations, languages, and kings.” Revelation 10:11

title: Revelation 11:1–14
context: John measures God’s temple and its worshipers but leaves out the outer court, which is trampled for forty-two months. Two witnesses prophesy for 1,260 days with power like Moses and Elijah. When their testimony is finished, the beast kills them, and their bodies lie in the street of the great city. After three and a half days God raises them and takes them to heaven, and an earthquake strikes. This is the second woe.
text: Revelation 11:1–14 Revelation John measures God’s temple and its worshipers but leaves out the outer court, which is trampled for forty-two months. Two witnesses prophesy for 1,260 days with power like Moses and Elijah. When their testimony is finished, the beast kills them, and their bodies lie in the street of the great city. After three and a half days God raises them and takes them to heaven, and an earthquake strikes. This is the second woe. A reed like a rod was given to me. Someone said, “Rise and measure God’s temple, and the altar, and those who worship in it. Revelation 11:1 Leave out the court which is outside of the temple, and don’t measure it, for it has been given to the nations. They will tread the holy city under foot for forty-two months. Revelation 11:2 I will give power to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy one thousand two hundred sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.” Revelation 11:3 These are the two olive trees and the two lamp stands, standing before the Lord of the earth. Revelation 11:4 If anyone desires to harm them, fire proceeds out of their mouth and devours their enemies. If anyone desires to harm them, he must be killed in this way. Revelation 11:5 These have the power to shut up the sky, that it may not rain during the days of their prophecy. They have power over the waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague, as often as they desire. Revelation 11:6 When they have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up out of the abyss will make war with them, and overcome them, and kill them. Revelation 11:7 Their dead bodies will be in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified. Revelation 11:8 From among the peoples, tribes, languages, and nations, people will look at their dead bodies for three and a half days, and will not allow their dead bodies to be laid in a tomb. Revelation 11:9 Those who dwell on the earth will rejoice over them, and they will be glad. They will give gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell on the earth. Revelation 11:10 After the three and a half days, the breath of life from God entered into them, and they stood on their feet. Great fear fell on those who saw them. Revelation 11:11 I heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, “Come up here!” They went up into heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them. Revelation 11:12 In that day there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell. Seven thousand people were killed in the earthquake, and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven. Revelation 11:13 The second woe is past. Behold, the third woe comes quickly. Revelation 11:14

title: Revelation 11:15–19
context: The seventh trumpet sounds, and heaven proclaims that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, who will reign forever. The elders worship God for taking his great power and reigning, for the time of judgment and reward has come. God’s temple in heaven opens, and the ark of his covenant is seen.
text: Revelation 11:15–19 Revelation The seventh trumpet sounds, and heaven proclaims that the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, who will reign forever. The elders worship God for taking his great power and reigning, for the time of judgment and reward has come. God’s temple in heaven opens, and the ark of his covenant is seen. The seventh angel sounded, and great voices in heaven followed, saying, “The kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ. He will reign forever and ever!” Revelation 11:15 The twenty-four elders, who sit on their thrones before God’s throne, fell on their faces and worshiped God, Revelation 11:16 saying: “We give you thanks, Lord God, the Almighty, the one who is and who was, because you have taken your great power and reigned. Revelation 11:17 The nations were angry, and your wrath came, as did the time for the dead to be judged, and to give your bondservants the prophets, their reward, as well as to the saints and those who fear your name, to the small and the great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth.” Revelation 11:18 God’s temple that is in heaven was opened, and the ark of the Lord’s covenant was seen in his temple. Lightnings, sounds, thunders, an earthquake, and great hail followed. Revelation 11:19

title: Revelation 12:1–6
context: A woman clothed with the sun gives birth to a son who will rule the nations, while a great red dragon waits to devour the child. The child is caught up to God and his throne, and the woman flees into the wilderness, where God nourishes her for 1,260 days.
text: Revelation 12:1–6 Revelation A woman clothed with the sun gives birth to a son who will rule the nations, while a great red dragon waits to devour the child. The child is caught up to God and his throne, and the woman flees into the wilderness, where God nourishes her for 1,260 days. A great sign was seen in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars. Revelation 12:1 She was with child. She cried out in pain, laboring to give birth. Revelation 12:2 Another sign was seen in heaven. Behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven crowns. Revelation 12:3 His tail drew one third of the stars of the sky, and threw them to the earth. The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child. Revelation 12:4 She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to rule all the nations with a rod of iron. Her child was caught up to God and to his throne. Revelation 12:5 The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, that there they may nourish her one thousand two hundred sixty days. Revelation 12:6

title: Revelation 12:7–17
context: War breaks out in heaven, and Michael and his angels throw down the dragon, the ancient serpent called the devil and Satan. Heaven celebrates that the accuser is cast down, and the saints overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and their testimony. Enraged, the dragon pursues the woman, who is protected, and then makes war on the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold the testimony of Jesus.
text: Revelation 12:7–17 Revelation War breaks out in heaven, and Michael and his angels throw down the dragon, the ancient serpent called the devil and Satan. Heaven celebrates that the accuser is cast down, and the saints overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and their testimony. Enraged, the dragon pursues the woman, who is protected, and then makes war on the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold the testimony of Jesus. There was war in the sky. Michael and his angels made war on the dragon. The dragon and his angels made war. Revelation 12:7 They didn’t prevail. No place was found for them any more in heaven. Revelation 12:8 The great dragon was thrown down, the old serpent, he who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him. Revelation 12:9 I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, “Now the salvation, the power, and the Kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ has come; for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night. Revelation 12:10 They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death. Revelation 12:11 Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them. Woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil has gone down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has but a short time.” Revelation 12:12 When the dragon saw that he was thrown down to the earth, he persecuted the woman who gave birth to the male child. Revelation 12:13 Two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, so that she might be nourished for a time, times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent. Revelation 12:14 The serpent spewed water out of his mouth after the woman like a river, that he might cause her to be carried away by the stream. Revelation 12:15 The earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon spewed out of his mouth. Revelation 12:16 The dragon grew angry with the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep God’s commandments and hold Jesus’ testimony. Revelation 12:17

title: Revelation 13:1–10
context: A beast rises from the sea with ten horns and seven heads, given power by the dragon. One head seems fatally wounded but is healed, and the world follows the beast in wonder. He blasphemes God and makes war on the saints for forty-two months. Everyone whose name is not written in the Lamb’s book of life worships him. The saints are called to endurance and faith.
text: Revelation 13:1–10 Revelation A beast rises from the sea with ten horns and seven heads, given power by the dragon. One head seems fatally wounded but is healed, and the world follows the beast in wonder. He blasphemes God and makes war on the saints for forty-two months. Everyone whose name is not written in the Lamb’s book of life worships him. The saints are called to endurance and faith. Then I stood on the sand of the sea. I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads. On his horns were ten crowns, and on his heads, blasphemous names. Revelation 13:1 The beast which I saw was like a leopard, and his feet were like those of a bear, and his mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon gave him his power, his throne, and great authority. Revelation 13:2 One of his heads looked like it had been wounded fatally. His fatal wound was healed, and the whole earth marveled at the beast. Revelation 13:3 They worshiped the dragon because he gave his authority to the beast; and they worshiped the beast, saying, “Who is like the beast? Who is able to make war with him?” Revelation 13:4 A mouth speaking great things and blasphemy was given to him. Authority to make war for forty-two months was given to him. Revelation 13:5 He opened his mouth for blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, his dwelling, and those who dwell in heaven. Revelation 13:6 It was given to him to make war with the saints and to overcome them. Authority over every tribe, people, language, and nation was given to him. Revelation 13:7 All who dwell on the earth will worship him, everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who has been killed. Revelation 13:8 If anyone has an ear, let him hear. Revelation 13:9 If anyone is to go into captivity, he will go into captivity. If anyone is to be killed with the sword, he must be killed. Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints. Revelation 13:10

title: Revelation 13:11–18
context: A second beast rises from the earth, with horns like a lamb but speaking like a dragon. He makes the earth worship the first beast, performs signs, and sets up a speaking image. He forces all people to receive a mark on the right hand or forehead, without which no one can buy or sell. The number of the beast is 666.
text: Revelation 13:11–18 Revelation A second beast rises from the earth, with horns like a lamb but speaking like a dragon. He makes the earth worship the first beast, performs signs, and sets up a speaking image. He forces all people to receive a mark on the right hand or forehead, without which no one can buy or sell. The number of the beast is 666. I saw another beast coming up out of the earth. He had two horns like a lamb and it spoke like a dragon. Revelation 13:11 He exercises all the authority of the first beast in his presence. He makes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose fatal wound was healed. Revelation 13:12 He performs great signs, even making fire come down out of the sky to the earth in the sight of people. Revelation 13:13 He deceives my own people who dwell on the earth because of the signs he was granted to do in front of the beast, saying to those who dwell on the earth that they should make an image to the beast who had the sword wound and lived. Revelation 13:14 It was given to him to give breath to the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause as many as wouldn’t worship the image of the beast to be killed. Revelation 13:15 He causes all, the small and the great, the rich and the poor, and the free and the slave, to be given marks on their right hands or on their foreheads; Revelation 13:16 and that no one would be able to buy or to sell unless he has that mark, which is the name of the beast or the number of his name. Revelation 13:17 Here is wisdom. He who has understanding, let him calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man. His number is six hundred sixty-six. Revelation 13:18

title: Revelation 14:1–5
context: The Lamb stands on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who bear his name and his Father’s name. They sing a new song only they can learn, follow the Lamb wherever he goes, and are blameless, redeemed as firstfruits to God and the Lamb.
text: Revelation 14:1–5 Revelation The Lamb stands on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who bear his name and his Father’s name. They sing a new song only they can learn, follow the Lamb wherever he goes, and are blameless, redeemed as firstfruits to God and the Lamb. I saw, and behold, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him a number, one hundred forty-four thousand, having his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads. Revelation 14:1 I heard a sound from heaven like the sound of many waters and like the sound of a great thunder. The sound which I heard was like that of harpists playing on their harps. Revelation 14:2 They sing a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn the song except the one hundred forty-four thousand, those who had been redeemed out of the earth. Revelation 14:3 These are those who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were redeemed by Jesus from among men, the first fruits to God and to the Lamb. Revelation 14:4 In their mouth was found no lie, for they are blameless. Revelation 14:5

title: Revelation 14:14–20
context: One like a son of man sits on a white cloud with a sickle, and the earth is harvested. Another angel gathers the grapes of the earth into the great winepress of God’s wrath, and blood flows from the press for a great distance.
text: Revelation 14:14–20 Revelation One like a son of man sits on a white cloud with a sickle, and the earth is harvested. Another angel gathers the grapes of the earth into the great winepress of God’s wrath, and blood flows from the press for a great distance. I looked, and saw a white cloud, and on the cloud one sitting like a son of man, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle. Revelation 14:14 Another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him who sat on the cloud, “Send your sickle and reap, for the hour to reap has come; for the harvest of the earth is ripe!” Revelation 14:15 He who sat on the cloud thrust his sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped. Revelation 14:16 Another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven. He also had a sharp sickle. Revelation 14:17 Another angel came out from the altar, he who has power over fire, and he called with a great voice to him who had the sharp sickle, saying, “Send your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, for the earth’s grapes are fully ripe!” Revelation 14:18 The angel thrust his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vintage of the earth and threw it into the great wine press of the wrath of God. Revelation 14:19 The wine press was trodden outside of the city, and blood came out of the wine press, up to the bridles of the horses, as far as one thousand six hundred stadia. Revelation 14:20

title: Revelation 14:6–13
context: An angel proclaims an eternal gospel to every nation, calling all to fear God and worship the Creator. A second angel announces Babylon’s fall. A third warns that anyone who worships the beast will drink the wine of God’s wrath. The saints are called to endurance, and a voice blesses those who die in the Lord.
text: Revelation 14:6–13 Revelation An angel proclaims an eternal gospel to every nation, calling all to fear God and worship the Creator. A second angel announces Babylon’s fall. A third warns that anyone who worships the beast will drink the wine of God’s wrath. The saints are called to endurance, and a voice blesses those who die in the Lord. I saw an angel flying in mid heaven, having an eternal Good News to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth—to every nation, tribe, language, and people. Revelation 14:6 He said with a loud voice, “Fear the Lord, and give him glory, for the hour of his judgment has come. Worship him who made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and the springs of waters!” Revelation 14:7 Another, a second angel, followed, saying, “Babylon the great has fallen, which has made all the nations to drink of the wine of the wrath of her sexual immorality.” Revelation 14:8 Another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a great voice, “If anyone worships the beast and his image, and receives a mark on his forehead or on his hand, Revelation 14:9 he also will drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is prepared unmixed in the cup of his anger. He will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb. Revelation 14:10 The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever. They have no rest day and night, those who worship the beast and his image, and whoever receives the mark of his name. Revelation 14:11 Here is the perseverance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.” Revelation 14:12 I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Write, ‘Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.’” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors, for their works follow with them.” Revelation 14:13

title: Revelation 15:1–8
context: Seven angels appear with the seven last plagues, which complete God’s wrath. Beside a sea of glass mixed with fire, those who overcame the beast sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb, praising God’s just and true ways. The heavenly temple opens, the angels receive seven golden bowls of wrath, and the temple fills with smoke from God’s glory.
text: Revelation 15:1–8 Revelation Seven angels appear with the seven last plagues, which complete God’s wrath. Beside a sea of glass mixed with fire, those who overcame the beast sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb, praising God’s just and true ways. The heavenly temple opens, the angels receive seven golden bowls of wrath, and the temple fills with smoke from God’s glory. I saw another great and marvelous sign in the sky: seven angels having the seven last plagues, for in them God’s wrath is finished. Revelation 15:1 I saw something like a sea of glass mixed with fire, and those who overcame the beast, his image, and the number of his name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God. Revelation 15:2 They sang the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, “Great and marvelous are your works, Lord God, the Almighty! Righteous and true are your ways, you King of the nations. Revelation 15:3 Who wouldn’t fear you, Lord, and glorify your name? For you only are holy. For all the nations will come and worship before you. For your righteous acts have been revealed.” Revelation 15:4 After these things I looked, and the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened. Revelation 15:5 The seven angels who had the seven plagues came out, clothed with pure, bright linen, and wearing golden sashes around their chests. Revelation 15:6 One of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever. Revelation 15:7 The temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from his power. No one was able to enter into the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels would be finished. Revelation 15:8

title: Revelation 16:1–11
context: The first five bowls are poured out: sores, a sea turned to blood, rivers turned to blood, scorching sun, and darkness on the beast’s throne. An angel and the altar declare God’s judgments true and righteous. People curse God and do not repent.
text: Revelation 16:1–11 Revelation The first five bowls are poured out: sores, a sea turned to blood, rivers turned to blood, scorching sun, and darkness on the beast’s throne. An angel and the altar declare God’s judgments true and righteous. People curse God and do not repent. I heard a loud voice out of the temple, saying to the seven angels, “Go and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God on the earth!” Revelation 16:1 The first went, and poured out his bowl into the earth, and it became a harmful and painful sore on the people who had the mark of the beast, and who worshiped his image. Revelation 16:2 The second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood as of a dead man. Every living thing in the sea died. Revelation 16:3 The third poured out his bowl into the rivers and springs of water, and they became blood. Revelation 16:4 I heard the angel of the waters saying, “You are righteous, who are and who were, O Holy One, because you have judged these things. Revelation 16:5 For they poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and you have given them blood to drink. They deserve this.” Revelation 16:6 I heard the altar saying, “Yes, Lord God, the Almighty, true and righteous are your judgments.” Revelation 16:7 The fourth poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was given to him to scorch men with fire. Revelation 16:8 People were scorched with great heat, and people blasphemed the name of God who has the power over these plagues. They didn’t repent and give him glory. Revelation 16:9 The fifth poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and his kingdom was darkened. They gnawed their tongues because of the pain, Revelation 16:10 and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores. They still didn’t repent of their works. Revelation 16:11

title: Revelation 16:12–21
context: The sixth bowl dries up the Euphrates for the kings from the east, and demonic spirits gather the kings of the world for battle at Armageddon. Christ warns that he comes like a thief. The seventh bowl brings a voice declaring “It is done,” a great earthquake, the fall of Babylon, and huge hailstones, yet people still curse God.
text: Revelation 16:12–21 Revelation The sixth bowl dries up the Euphrates for the kings from the east, and demonic spirits gather the kings of the world for battle at Armageddon. Christ warns that he comes like a thief. The seventh bowl brings a voice declaring “It is done,” a great earthquake, the fall of Babylon, and huge hailstones, yet people still curse God. The sixth poured out his bowl on the great river, the Euphrates. Its water was dried up, that the way might be prepared for the kings that come from the sunrise. Revelation 16:12 I saw coming out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits, something like frogs; Revelation 16:13 for they are spirits of demons, performing signs, which go out to the kings of the whole inhabited earth, to gather them together for the war of that great day of God the Almighty. Revelation 16:14 “Behold, I come like a thief. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his clothes, so that he doesn’t walk naked, and they see his shame.” Revelation 16:15 He gathered them together into the place which is called in Hebrew, “Harmagedon”. Revelation 16:16 The seventh poured out his bowl into the air. A loud voice came out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, “It is done!” Revelation 16:17 There were lightnings, sounds, and thunders; and there was a great earthquake such as has not happened since there were men on the earth—so great an earthquake and so mighty. Revelation 16:18 The great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. Babylon the great was remembered in the sight of God, to give to her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath. Revelation 16:19 Every island fled away, and the mountains were not found. Revelation 16:20 Great hailstones, about the weight of a talent, came down out of the sky on people. People blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for this plague was exceedingly severe. Revelation 16:21

title: Revelation 17:1–6
context: An angel shows John the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters. She rides a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns, is dressed in luxury, and bears the name Babylon the Great, mother of prostitutes. She is drunk with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus.
text: Revelation 17:1–6 Revelation An angel shows John the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters. She rides a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns, is dressed in luxury, and bears the name Babylon the Great, mother of prostitutes. She is drunk with the blood of the saints and martyrs of Jesus. One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters, Revelation 17:1 with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality. Those who dwell on the earth were made drunken with the wine of her sexual immorality.” Revelation 17:2 He carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness. I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet-colored beast, full of blasphemous names, having seven heads and ten horns. Revelation 17:3 The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of the sexual immorality of the earth. Revelation 17:4 And on her forehead a name was written, “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF THE PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” Revelation 17:5 I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. When I saw her, I wondered with great amazement. Revelation 17:6

title: Revelation 17:7–18
context: The angel explains the beast that was, and is not, and is about to come, the seven heads as seven mountains and seven kings, and the ten horns as kings who will war against the Lamb. The Lamb will overcome them, and those with him are called, chosen, and faithful. In the end the beast and the horns turn on the prostitute and destroy her, because God put it into their hearts to fulfill his purpose.
text: Revelation 17:7–18 Revelation The angel explains the beast that was, and is not, and is about to come, the seven heads as seven mountains and seven kings, and the ten horns as kings who will war against the Lamb. The Lamb will overcome them, and those with him are called, chosen, and faithful. In the end the beast and the horns turn on the prostitute and destroy her, because God put it into their hearts to fulfill his purpose. The angel said to me, “Why do you wonder? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns. Revelation 17:7 The beast that you saw was, and is not; and is about to come up out of the abyss and to go into destruction. Those who dwell on the earth and whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see that the beast was, and is not, and shall be present. Revelation 17:8 Here is the mind that has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits. Revelation 17:9 They are seven kings. Five have fallen, the one is, and the other has not yet come. When he comes, he must continue a little while. Revelation 17:10 The beast that was, and is not, is himself also an eighth, and is of the seven; and he goes to destruction. Revelation 17:11 The ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority as kings with the beast for one hour. Revelation 17:12 These have one mind, and they give their power and authority to the beast. Revelation 17:13 These will war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with him are called, chosen, and faithful.” Revelation 17:14 He said to me, “The waters which you saw, where the prostitute sits, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages. Revelation 17:15 The ten horns which you saw, they and the beast will hate the prostitute, will make her desolate, will strip her naked, will eat her flesh, and will burn her utterly with fire. Revelation 17:16 For God has put in their hearts to do what he has in mind, to be of one mind, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God should be accomplished. Revelation 17:17 The woman whom you saw is the great city which reigns over the kings of the earth.” Revelation 17:18

title: Revelation 18:1–8
context: An angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen. A voice from heaven calls God’s people to come out of her so that they will not share in her sins or her plagues. Her sins have piled up to heaven, and her judgment will come in a single day.
text: Revelation 18:1–8 Revelation An angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen. A voice from heaven calls God’s people to come out of her so that they will not share in her sins or her plagues. Her sins have piled up to heaven, and her judgment will come in a single day. After these things, I saw another angel coming down out of the sky, having great authority. The earth was illuminated with his glory. Revelation 18:1 He cried with a mighty voice, saying, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, and she has become a habitation of demons, a prison of every unclean spirit, and a prison of every unclean and hated bird! Revelation 18:2 For all the nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her sexual immorality, the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the abundance of her luxury.” Revelation 18:3 I heard another voice from heaven, saying, “Come out of her, my people, that you have no participation in her sins, and that you don’t receive of her plagues, Revelation 18:4 for her sins have reached to the sky, and God has remembered her iniquities. Revelation 18:5 Return to her just as she returned, and repay her double as she did, and according to her works. In the cup which she mixed, mix to her double. Revelation 18:6 However much she glorified herself and grew wanton, so much give her of torment and mourning. For she says in her heart, ‘I sit a queen, and am no widow, and will in no way see mourning.’ Revelation 18:7 Therefore in one day her plagues will come: death, mourning, and famine; and she will be utterly burned with fire, for the Lord God who has judged her is strong. Revelation 18:8

title: Revelation 18:9–24
context: Kings, merchants, and seafarers mourn Babylon’s fall from a distance as her wealth vanishes in an hour. Heaven, saints, apostles, and prophets are called to rejoice, because God has judged her. A mighty angel throws a millstone into the sea as a sign that the city will be found no more, for in her was found the blood of prophets and saints.
text: Revelation 18:9–24 Revelation Kings, merchants, and seafarers mourn Babylon’s fall from a distance as her wealth vanishes in an hour. Heaven, saints, apostles, and prophets are called to rejoice, because God has judged her. A mighty angel throws a millstone into the sea as a sign that the city will be found no more, for in her was found the blood of prophets and saints. The kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived wantonly with her will weep and wail over her, when they look at the smoke of her burning, Revelation 18:9 standing far away for the fear of her torment, saying, ‘Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon, the strong city!
