For your judgment has come in one hour.’ Revelation 18:10 The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, for no one buys their merchandise any more: Revelation 18:11 merchandise of gold, silver, precious stones, pearls, fine linen, purple, silk, scarlet, all expensive wood, every vessel of ivory, every vessel made of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble; Revelation 18:12 and cinnamon, incense, perfume, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, and people’s bodies and souls. Revelation 18:13 The fruits which your soul lusted after have been lost to you. All things that were dainty and sumptuous have perished from you, and you will find them no more at all. Revelation 18:14 The merchants of these things, who were made rich by her, will stand far away for the fear of her torment, weeping and mourning, Revelation 18:15 saying, ‘Woe, woe, the great city, she who was dressed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls! Revelation 18:16 For in an hour such great riches are made desolate.’ Every ship master, and everyone who sails anywhere, and mariners, and as many as gain their living by sea, stood far away, Revelation 18:17 and cried out as they looked at the smoke of her burning, saying, ‘What is like the great city?’ Revelation 18:18 They cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and mourning, saying, ‘Woe, woe, the great city, in which all who had their ships in the sea were made rich by reason of her great wealth!’ For she is made desolate in one hour. Revelation 18:19 “Rejoice over her, O heaven, you saints, apostles, and prophets, for God has judged your judgment on her.” Revelation 18:20 A mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying, “Thus with violence will Babylon, the great city, be thrown down, and will be found no more at all. Revelation 18:21 The voice of harpists, minstrels, flute players, and trumpeters will be heard no more at all in you. No craftsman of whatever craft will be found any more at all in you. The sound of a mill will be heard no more at all in you. Revelation 18:22 The light of a lamp will shine no more at all in you. The voice of the bridegroom and of the bride will be heard no more at all in you, for your merchants were the princes of the earth; for with your sorcery all the nations were deceived. Revelation 18:23 In her was found the blood of prophets and of saints, and of all who have been slain on the earth.” Revelation 18:24

title: Revelation 19:1–10
context: After Babylon’s fall, a great multitude in heaven cries “Hallelujah,” praising God for judging the prostitute who corrupted the earth. The elders and living creatures join the praise, and a voice announces that the marriage of the Lamb has come and his bride has made herself ready in fine linen. John is told to write a blessing on those invited to the marriage supper, and when he falls at the angel’s feet he is told to worship God alone.
text: Revelation 19:1–10 Revelation After Babylon’s fall, a great multitude in heaven cries “Hallelujah,” praising God for judging the prostitute who corrupted the earth. The elders and living creatures join the praise, and a voice announces that the marriage of the Lamb has come and his bride has made herself ready in fine linen. John is told to write a blessing on those invited to the marriage supper, and when he falls at the angel’s feet he is told to worship God alone. After these things I heard something like a loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying, “Hallelujah! Salvation, power, and glory belong to our God; Revelation 19:1 for his judgments are true and righteous. For he has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her sexual immorality, and he has avenged the blood of his servants at her hand.” Revelation 19:2 A second said, “Hallelujah! Her smoke goes up forever and ever.” Revelation 19:3 The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits on the throne, saying, “Amen! Hallelujah!” Revelation 19:4 A voice came from the throne, saying, “Give praise to our God, all you his servants, you who fear him, the small and the great!” Revelation 19:5 I heard something like the voice of a great multitude, and like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of mighty thunders, saying, “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God, the Almighty, reigns! Revelation 19:6 Let’s rejoice and be exceedingly glad, and let’s give the glory to him. For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready.” Revelation 19:7 It was given to her that she would array herself in bright, pure, fine linen, for the fine linen is the righteous acts of the saints. Revelation 19:8 He said to me, “Write, ‘Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.’” He said to me, “These are true words of God.” Revelation 19:9 I fell down before his feet to worship him. He said to me, “Look! Don’t do it! I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God, for the testimony of Jesus is the Spirit of Prophecy.” Revelation 19:10

title: Revelation 19:11–21
context: Heaven opens, and a rider on a white horse, called Faithful and True, comes to judge and make war in righteousness. His robe is dipped in blood, his name is the Word of God, and the armies of heaven follow him. A sharp sword comes from his mouth, and on his robe is written King of kings and Lord of lords. An angel summons the birds to a great supper of God, the beast and the false prophet are captured and thrown alive into the lake of fire, and the rest are killed by the sword from the rider’s mouth.
text: Revelation 19:11–21 Revelation Heaven opens, and a rider on a white horse, called Faithful and True, comes to judge and make war in righteousness. His robe is dipped in blood, his name is the Word of God, and the armies of heaven follow him. A sharp sword comes from his mouth, and on his robe is written King of kings and Lord of lords. An angel summons the birds to a great supper of God, the beast and the false prophet are captured and thrown alive into the lake of fire, and the rest are killed by the sword from the rider’s mouth. I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse, and he who sat on it is called Faithful and True. In righteousness he judges and makes war. Revelation 19:11 His eyes are a flame of fire, and on his head are many crowns. He has names written and a name written which no one knows but he himself. Revelation 19:12 He is clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood. His name is called “The Word of God.” Revelation 19:13 The armies which are in heaven, clothed in white, pure, fine linen, followed him on white horses. Revelation 19:14 Out of his mouth proceeds a sharp, double-edged sword that with it he should strike the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod. He treads the wine press of the fierceness of the wrath of God, the Almighty. Revelation 19:15 He has on his garment and on his thigh a name written, “KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS.” Revelation 19:16 I saw an angel standing in the sun. He cried with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that fly in the sky, “Come! Be gathered together to the great supper of God, Revelation 19:17 that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all men, both free and slave, small and great.” Revelation 19:18 I saw the beast, the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against him who sat on the horse and against his army. Revelation 19:19 The beast was taken, and with him the false prophet who worked the signs in his sight, with which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped his image. These two were thrown alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur. Revelation 19:20 The rest were killed with the sword of him who sat on the horse, the sword which came out of his mouth. So all the birds were filled with their flesh. Revelation 19:21

title: Revelation 2:1–7
context: Christ commends the church in Ephesus for its hard work, endurance, and refusal to tolerate false apostles. Yet it has left its first love. He calls it to remember, repent, and do the first works, or he will remove its lampstand. The overcomer will eat from the tree of life.
text: Revelation 2:1–7 Revelation Christ commends the church in Ephesus for its hard work, endurance, and refusal to tolerate false apostles. Yet it has left its first love. He calls it to remember, repent, and do the first works, or he will remove its lampstand. The overcomer will eat from the tree of life. “To the angel of the assembly in Ephesus write: “He who holds the seven stars in his right hand, he who walks among the seven golden lamp stands says these things: Revelation 2:1 “I know your works, and your toil and perseverance, and that you can’t tolerate evil men, and have tested those who call themselves apostles, and they are not, and found them false. Revelation 2:2 You have perseverance and have endured for my name’s sake, and have not grown weary. Revelation 2:3 But I have this against you, that you left your first love. Revelation 2:4 Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works; or else I am coming to you swiftly, and will move your lamp stand out of its place, unless you repent. Revelation 2:5 But this you have, that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate. Revelation 2:6 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of my God. Revelation 2:7

title: Revelation 2:12–17
context: Pergamum lives where Satan’s throne is, yet it held to Christ’s name even when Antipas was killed. But some in the church follow the teaching of Balaam and the Nicolaitans. Christ calls them to repent and promises the overcomer hidden manna and a white stone with a new name.
text: Revelation 2:12–17 Revelation Pergamum lives where Satan’s throne is, yet it held to Christ’s name even when Antipas was killed. But some in the church follow the teaching of Balaam and the Nicolaitans. Christ calls them to repent and promises the overcomer hidden manna and a white stone with a new name. “To the angel of the assembly in Pergamum write: “He who has the sharp two-edged sword says these things: Revelation 2:12 “I know your works and where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. You hold firmly to my name, and didn’t deny my faith in the days of Antipas my witness, my faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells. Revelation 2:13 But I have a few things against you, because you have there some who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to throw a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit sexual immorality. Revelation 2:14 So also you likewise have some who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans. Revelation 2:15 Repent therefore, or else I am coming to you quickly and I will make war against them with the sword of my mouth. Revelation 2:16 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, to him I will give of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written which no one knows but he who receives it. Revelation 2:17

title: Revelation 2:18–29
context: To Thyatira, Christ speaks as the Son of God with eyes like fire. He praises its growing love, faith, and service, but rebukes it for tolerating a false prophetess called Jezebel. She was given time to repent and refused. The rest are told to hold fast until he comes, and the overcomer is promised authority over the nations and the morning star.
text: Revelation 2:18–29 Revelation To Thyatira, Christ speaks as the Son of God with eyes like fire. He praises its growing love, faith, and service, but rebukes it for tolerating a false prophetess called Jezebel. She was given time to repent and refused. The rest are told to hold fast until he comes, and the overcomer is promised authority over the nations and the morning star. “To the angel of the assembly in Thyatira write: “The Son of God, who has his eyes like a flame of fire, and his feet are like burnished brass, says these things: Revelation 2:18 “I know your works, your love, faith, service, patient endurance, and that your last works are more than the first. Revelation 2:19 But I have this against you, that you tolerate your woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess. She teaches and seduces my servants to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols. Revelation 2:20 I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to repent of her sexual immorality. Revelation 2:21 Behold, I will throw her and those who commit adultery with her into a bed of great oppression, unless they repent of her works. Revelation 2:22 I will kill her children with Death, and all the assemblies will know that I am he who searches the minds and hearts. I will give to each one of you according to your deeds. Revelation 2:23 But to you I say, to the rest who are in Thyatira—as many as don’t have this teaching, who don’t know what some call ‘the deep things of Satan’—to you I say, I am not putting any other burden on you. Revelation 2:24 Nevertheless, hold that which you have firmly until I come. Revelation 2:25 He who overcomes, and he who keeps my works to the end, to him I will give authority over the nations. Revelation 2:26 He will rule them with a rod of iron, shattering them like clay pots, as I also have received of my Father; Revelation 2:27 and I will give him the morning star. Revelation 2:28 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. Revelation 2:29

title: Revelation 2:8–11
context: To persecuted Smyrna, Christ speaks as the first and the last, who died and came to life. He knows its oppression and poverty, though it is rich. He warns of imprisonment and calls it to be faithful to death, promising the crown of life and protection from the second death.
text: Revelation 2:8–11 Revelation To persecuted Smyrna, Christ speaks as the first and the last, who died and came to life. He knows its oppression and poverty, though it is rich. He warns of imprisonment and calls it to be faithful to death, promising the crown of life and protection from the second death. “To the angel of the assembly in Smyrna write: “The first and the last, who was dead, and has come to life says these things: Revelation 2:8 “I know your works, oppression, and your poverty (but you are rich), and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but are a synagogue of Satan. Revelation 2:9 Don’t be afraid of the things which you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested; and you will have oppression for ten days. Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life. Revelation 2:10 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. He who overcomes won’t be harmed by the second death. Revelation 2:11

title: Revelation 20:1–6
context: An angel binds the dragon, who is the devil and Satan, for a thousand years and seals him in the abyss so that he can no longer deceive the nations. John sees thrones and the souls of those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, who come to life and reign with Christ for a thousand years. This is the first resurrection, and the second death has no power over those who share in it. The passage is the source of the premillennial, amillennial, and postmillennial positions, and each is held by both Arminian and Reformed believers.
text: Revelation 20:1–6 Revelation An angel binds the dragon, who is the devil and Satan, for a thousand years and seals him in the abyss so that he can no longer deceive the nations. John sees thrones and the souls of those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, who come to life and reign with Christ for a thousand years. This is the first resurrection, and the second death has no power over those who share in it. The passage is the source of the premillennial, amillennial, and postmillennial positions, and each is held by both Arminian and Reformed believers. I saw an angel coming down out of heaven, having the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand. Revelation 20:1 He seized the dragon, the old serpent, who is the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole inhabited earth, and bound him for a thousand years, Revelation 20:2 and cast him into the abyss, and shut it and sealed it over him, that he should deceive the nations no more until the thousand years were finished. After this, he must be freed for a short time. Revelation 20:3 I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them. I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and such as didn’t worship the beast nor his image, and didn’t receive the mark on their forehead and on their hand. They lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years. Revelation 20:4 The rest of the dead didn’t live until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection. Revelation 20:5 Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection. Over these, the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with him one thousand years. Revelation 20:6

title: Revelation 20:7–15
context: When the thousand years end, Satan is released and gathers the nations, Gog and Magog, against the camp of the saints and the beloved city, but fire from heaven consumes them and the devil is thrown into the lake of fire. John then sees a great white throne. The dead, great and small, are judged according to their works from the books, and anyone not found written in the book of life is thrown into the lake of fire, which is the second death.
text: Revelation 20:7–15 Revelation When the thousand years end, Satan is released and gathers the nations, Gog and Magog, against the camp of the saints and the beloved city, but fire from heaven consumes them and the devil is thrown into the lake of fire. John then sees a great white throne. The dead, great and small, are judged according to their works from the books, and anyone not found written in the book of life is thrown into the lake of fire, which is the second death. And after the thousand years, Satan will be released from his prison Revelation 20:7 and he will come out to deceive the nations which are in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them together to the war, whose number is as the sand of the sea. Revelation 20:8 They went up over the width of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city. Fire came down out of heaven from God and devoured them. Revelation 20:9 The devil who deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet are also. They will be tormented day and night forever and ever. Revelation 20:10 I saw a great white throne and him who sat on it, from whose face the earth and the sky fled away. There was found no place for them. Revelation 20:11 I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works. Revelation 20:12 The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them. They were judged, each one according to his works. Revelation 20:13 Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. Revelation 20:14 If anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire. Revelation 20:15

title: Revelation 21:1–8
context: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God like a bride adorned for her husband. A loud voice declares that God’s dwelling is with people; he will wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. The one on the throne says he makes all things new, offers the water of life freely to the thirsty, promises that the one who overcomes will inherit all things, and warns that the faithless and the wicked have their part in the lake of fire.
text: Revelation 21:1–8 Revelation John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God like a bride adorned for her husband. A loud voice declares that God’s dwelling is with people; he will wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. The one on the throne says he makes all things new, offers the water of life freely to the thirsty, promises that the one who overcomes will inherit all things, and warns that the faithless and the wicked have their part in the lake of fire. I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more. Revelation 21:1 I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband. Revelation 21:2 I heard a loud voice out of heaven saying, “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people; and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. Revelation 21:3 He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.” Revelation 21:4 He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.” Revelation 21:5 He said to me, “I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. I will give freely to him who is thirsty from the spring of the water of life. Revelation 21:6 He who overcomes, I will give him these things. I will be his God, and he will be my son. Revelation 21:7 But for the cowardly, unbelieving, sinners, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars, their part is in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.” Revelation 21:8

title: Revelation 21:9–27
context: One of the seven angels shows John the bride, the wife of the Lamb, as the holy city Jerusalem descending from heaven with God’s glory. The city has twelve gates named for the tribes of Israel and twelve foundations named for the apostles. It is measured as a perfect cube, built of gold and precious stones, with gates of pearl. There is no temple, because God and the Lamb are its temple, and no sun or moon, because God’s glory lights it. The nations walk in its light, and only those written in the Lamb’s book of life enter it.
text: Revelation 21:9–27 Revelation One of the seven angels shows John the bride, the wife of the Lamb, as the holy city Jerusalem descending from heaven with God’s glory. The city has twelve gates named for the tribes of Israel and twelve foundations named for the apostles. It is measured as a perfect cube, built of gold and precious stones, with gates of pearl. There is no temple, because God and the Lamb are its temple, and no sun or moon, because God’s glory lights it. The nations walk in its light, and only those written in the Lamb’s book of life enter it. One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls which were loaded with the seven last plagues came, and he spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” Revelation 21:9 He carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, Revelation 21:10 having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal; Revelation 21:11 having a great and high wall with twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written on them, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. Revelation 21:12 On the east were three gates, and on the north three gates, and on the south three gates, and on the west three gates. Revelation 21:13 The wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them twelve names of the twelve Apostles of the Lamb. Revelation 21:14 He who spoke with me had for a measure a golden reed to measure the city, its gates, and its walls. Revelation 21:15 The city is square. Its length is as great as its width. He measured the city with the reed: twelve thousand twelve stadia. Its length, width, and height are equal. Revelation 21:16 Its wall is one hundred forty-four cubits, by the measure of a man, that is, of an angel. Revelation 21:17 The construction of its wall was jasper. The city was pure gold, like pure glass. Revelation 21:18 The foundations of the city’s wall were adorned with all kinds of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, Revelation 21:19 the fifth sardonyx, the sixth sardius, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst. Revelation 21:20 The twelve gates were twelve pearls. Each one of the gates was made of one pearl. The street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass. Revelation 21:21 I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. Revelation 21:22 The city has no need for the sun or moon to shine, for the very glory of God illuminated it and its lamp is the Lamb. Revelation 21:23 The nations will walk in its light. The kings of the earth bring the glory and honor of the nations into it. Revelation 21:24 Its gates will in no way be shut by day (for there will be no night there), Revelation 21:25 and they shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it so that they may enter. Revelation 21:26 There will in no way enter into it anything profane, or one who causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life. Revelation 21:27

title: Revelation 22:1–5
context: John’s vision of the new Jerusalem ends with Eden restored and surpassed. The river of the water of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb, and the tree of life bears fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations. The curse is gone. God’s servants will see his face, bear his name, live in his light, and reign forever.
text: Revelation 22:1–5 Revelation John’s vision of the new Jerusalem ends with Eden restored and surpassed. The river of the water of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb, and the tree of life bears fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations. The curse is gone. God’s servants will see his face, bear his name, live in his light, and reign forever. He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb, Revelation 22:1 in the middle of its street. On this side of the river and on that was the tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruits, yielding its fruit every month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. Revelation 22:2 There will be no curse any more. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will serve him. Revelation 22:3 They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. Revelation 22:4 There will be no night, and they need no lamp light or sun light; for the Lord God will illuminate them. They will reign forever and ever. Revelation 22:5

title: Revelation 22:16–21
context: Jesus confirms that he sent his angel to testify these things to the churches. He is the root and offspring of David and the bright morning star. The Spirit and the bride invite all who hear and all who thirst to come and take the water of life freely. A solemn warning protects the words of the book, and the Bible closes with Christ’s promise to come soon, the church’s answering prayer, and a blessing of grace.
text: Revelation 22:16–21 Revelation Jesus confirms that he sent his angel to testify these things to the churches. He is the root and offspring of David and the bright morning star. The Spirit and the bride invite all who hear and all who thirst to come and take the water of life freely. A solemn warning protects the words of the book, and the Bible closes with Christ’s promise to come soon, the church’s answering prayer, and a blessing of grace. I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you for the assemblies. I am the root and the offspring of David, the Bright and Morning Star.” Revelation 22:16 The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” He who hears, let him say, “Come!” He who is thirsty, let him come. He who desires, let him take the water of life freely. Revelation 22:17 I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues which are written in this book. Revelation 22:18 If anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his part from the tree of life, and out of the holy city, which are written in this book. Revelation 22:19 He who testifies these things says, “Yes, I am coming soon.” Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus! Revelation 22:20 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the saints. Amen. Revelation 22:21

title: Revelation 22:6–15
context: An angel affirms that these words are faithful and true, and Jesus promises to come soon. John falls to worship the angel and is told to worship God alone. The book is not to be sealed, because the time is near. Jesus speaks as the Alpha and the Omega, who brings his reward and repays each one by his work, and he blesses those who will enter the city by its gates.
text: Revelation 22:6–15 Revelation An angel affirms that these words are faithful and true, and Jesus promises to come soon. John falls to worship the angel and is told to worship God alone. The book is not to be sealed, because the time is near. Jesus speaks as the Alpha and the Omega, who brings his reward and repays each one by his work, and he blesses those who will enter the city by its gates. He said to me, “These words are faithful and true. The Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel to show to his bondservants the things which must happen soon.” Revelation 22:6 “Behold, I am coming soon! Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.” Revelation 22:7 Now I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. When I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who had shown me these things. Revelation 22:8 He said to me, “You must not do that! I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers, the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.” Revelation 22:9 He said to me, “Don’t seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is at hand. Revelation 22:10 He who acts unjustly, let him act unjustly still. He who is filthy, let him be filthy still. He who is righteous, let him do righteousness still. He who is holy, let him be holy still.” Revelation 22:11 “Behold, I am coming soon! My reward is with me, to repay to each man according to his work. Revelation 22:12 I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End. Revelation 22:13 Blessed are those who do his commandments, that they may have the right to the tree of life, and may enter in by the gates into the city. Revelation 22:14 Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood. Revelation 22:15

title: Revelation 3:1–6
context: The risen Christ addresses the church in Sardis, which has a name for being alive but is dead. He calls it to wake up, remember what it received, keep it, and repent, or he will come like a thief. A few in Sardis have not soiled their garments, and the one who overcomes is promised white clothing, a name kept in the book of life, and Christ’s confession before the Father.
text: Revelation 3:1–6 Revelation The risen Christ addresses the church in Sardis, which has a name for being alive but is dead. He calls it to wake up, remember what it received, keep it, and repent, or he will come like a thief. A few in Sardis have not soiled their garments, and the one who overcomes is promised white clothing, a name kept in the book of life, and Christ’s confession before the Father. “And to the angel of the assembly in Sardis write: “He who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars says these things: “I know your works, that you have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead. Revelation 3:1 Wake up and strengthen the things that remain, which you were about to throw away, for I have found no works of yours perfected before my God. Revelation 3:2 Remember therefore how you have received and heard. Keep it and repent. If therefore you won’t watch, I will come as a thief, and you won’t know what hour I will come upon you. Revelation 3:3 Nevertheless you have a few names in Sardis that didn’t defile their garments. They will walk with me in white, for they are worthy. Revelation 3:4 He who overcomes will be arrayed in white garments, and I will in no way blot his name out of the book of life, and I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels. Revelation 3:5 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. Revelation 3:6

title: Revelation 3:14–22
context: The last letter goes to Laodicea, a wealthy city whose church is neither hot nor cold. Christ, the Amen and faithful witness, exposes its self-satisfaction: it thinks it is rich, yet it is wretched, poor, blind, and naked. He counsels it to buy from him what it lacks, reminds it that he rebukes those he loves, and stands at the door knocking. Whoever opens will share a meal with him, and the overcomer will share his throne.
text: Revelation 3:14–22 Revelation The last letter goes to Laodicea, a wealthy city whose church is neither hot nor cold. Christ, the Amen and faithful witness, exposes its self-satisfaction: it thinks it is rich, yet it is wretched, poor, blind, and naked. He counsels it to buy from him what it lacks, reminds it that he rebukes those he loves, and stands at the door knocking. Whoever opens will share a meal with him, and the overcomer will share his throne. “To the angel of the assembly in Laodicea write: “The Amen, the Faithful and True Witness, the Beginning of God’s creation, says these things: Revelation 3:14 “I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were cold or hot. Revelation 3:15 So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will vomit you out of my mouth. Revelation 3:16 Because you say, ‘I am rich, and have gotten riches, and have need of nothing,’ and don’t know that you are the wretched one, miserable, poor, blind, and naked; Revelation 3:17 I counsel you to buy from me gold refined by fire, that you may become rich; and white garments, that you may clothe yourself, and that the shame of your nakedness may not be revealed; and eye salve to anoint your eyes, that you may see. Revelation 3:18 As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent. Revelation 3:19 Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me. Revelation 3:20 He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne. Revelation 3:21 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies.” Revelation 3:22

title: Revelation 3:7–13
context: To Philadelphia Christ presents himself as the holy and true one who holds the key of David and opens doors no one can shut. The church has little power but has kept his word and not denied his name. He promises to vindicate it before its opponents, to keep it from the coming hour of testing, and to make the overcomer a permanent pillar in God’s temple, marked with God’s name.
text: Revelation 3:7–13 Revelation To Philadelphia Christ presents himself as the holy and true one who holds the key of David and opens doors no one can shut. The church has little power but has kept his word and not denied his name. He promises to vindicate it before its opponents, to keep it from the coming hour of testing, and to make the overcomer a permanent pillar in God’s temple, marked with God’s name. “To the angel of the assembly in Philadelphia write: “He who is holy, he who is true, he who has the key of David, he who opens and no one can shut, and who shuts and no one opens, says these things: Revelation 3:7 “I know your works (behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut), that you have a little power, and kept my word, and didn’t deny my name. Revelation 3:8 Behold, I make some of the synagogue of Satan, of those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but lie—behold, I will make them to come and worship before your feet, and to know that I have loved you. Revelation 3:9 Because you kept my command to endure, I also will keep you from the hour of testing which is to come on the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth. Revelation 3:10 I am coming quickly! Hold firmly that which you have, so that no one takes your crown. Revelation 3:11 He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he will go out from there no more. I will write on him the name of my God and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from my God, and my own new name. Revelation 3:12 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. Revelation 3:13

title: Revelation 4:1–11
context: John is called up through an open door into heaven and sees a throne with one seated on it, surrounded by a rainbow, twenty-four elders, seven lamps of fire, and four living creatures. The creatures praise God without ceasing as holy, and the elders cast their crowns before the throne, confessing that he is worthy because he created all things.
text: Revelation 4:1–11 Revelation John is called up through an open door into heaven and sees a throne with one seated on it, surrounded by a rainbow, twenty-four elders, seven lamps of fire, and four living creatures. The creatures praise God without ceasing as holy, and the elders cast their crowns before the throne, confessing that he is worthy because he created all things. After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven; and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, was one saying, “Come up here, and I will show you the things which must happen after this.” Revelation 4:1 Immediately I was in the Spirit. Behold, there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne Revelation 4:2 that looked like a jasper stone and a sardius. There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at. Revelation 4:3 Around the throne were twenty-four thrones. On the thrones were twenty-four elders sitting, dressed in white garments, with crowns of gold on their heads. Revelation 4:4 Out of the throne proceed lightnings, sounds, and thunders. There were seven lamps of fire burning before his throne, which are the seven Spirits of God. Revelation 4:5 Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal. In the middle of the throne, and around the throne were four living creatures full of eyes before and behind. Revelation 4:6 The first creature was like a lion, the second creature like a calf, the third creature had a face like a man, and the fourth was like a flying eagle. Revelation 4:7 The four living creatures, each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within. They have no rest day and night, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!” Revelation 4:8 When the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to him who sits on the throne, to him who lives forever and ever, Revelation 4:9 the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne and worship him who lives forever and ever, and throw their crowns before the throne, saying, Revelation 4:10 “Worthy are you, our Lord and God, the Holy One, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, for you created all things, and because of your desire they existed and were created!” Revelation 4:11

title: Revelation 5:1–14
context: The one on the throne holds a scroll sealed with seven seals, and no one is found worthy to open it. John weeps until he is told that the Lion of the tribe of Judah has overcome. He sees a Lamb standing as though slain, who takes the scroll. Heaven bursts into a new song: the Lamb is worthy because he was slain and purchased people for God from every tribe, language, people, and nation. All creation joins the praise.
text: Revelation 5:1–14 Revelation The one on the throne holds a scroll sealed with seven seals, and no one is found worthy to open it. John weeps until he is told that the Lion of the tribe of Judah has overcome. He sees a Lamb standing as though slain, who takes the scroll. Heaven bursts into a new song: the Lamb is worthy because he was slain and purchased people for God from every tribe, language, people, and nation. All creation joins the praise. I saw, in the right hand of him who sat on the throne, a book written inside and outside, sealed shut with seven seals. Revelation 5:1 I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the book, and to break its seals?” Revelation 5:2 No one in heaven above, or on the earth, or under the earth, was able to open the book or to look in it. Revelation 5:3 Then I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the book or to look in it. Revelation 5:4 One of the elders said to me, “Don’t weep. Behold, the Lion who is of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome: he who opens the book and its seven seals.” Revelation 5:5 I saw in the middle of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the middle of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God, sent out into all the earth. Revelation 5:6 Then he came, and he took it out of the right hand of him who sat on the throne. Revelation 5:7 Now when he had taken the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each one having a harp, and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. Revelation 5:8 They sang a new song, saying, “You are worthy to take the book and to open its seals, for you were killed, and bought us for God with your blood out of every tribe, language, people, and nation, Revelation 5:9 and made us kings and priests to our God; and we will reign on the earth.” Revelation 5:10 I looked, and I heard something like a voice of many angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. The number of them was ten thousands of ten thousands, and thousands of thousands, Revelation 5:11 saying with a loud voice, “Worthy is the Lamb who has been killed to receive the power, wealth, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and blessing!” Revelation 5:12 I heard every created thing which is in heaven, on the earth, under the earth, on the sea, and everything in them, saying, “To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be the blessing, the honor, the glory, and the dominion, forever and ever! Amen!” Revelation 5:13 The four living creatures said, “Amen!” Then the elders fell down and worshiped. Revelation 5:14

title: Revelation 6:1–8
context: The Lamb opens the first four seals, and four horsemen ride out: a conqueror on a white horse, a rider on a red horse who takes peace from the earth, a rider on a black horse with scales signaling scarcity, and Death on a pale horse with Hades following. Their power is given and limited.
text: Revelation 6:1–8 Revelation The Lamb opens the first four seals, and four horsemen ride out: a conqueror on a white horse, a rider on a red horse who takes peace from the earth, a rider on a black horse with scales signaling scarcity, and Death on a pale horse with Hades following. Their power is given and limited. I saw that the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder, “Come and see!” Revelation 6:1 Then a white horse appeared, and he who sat on it had a bow. A crown was given to him, and he came out conquering, and to conquer. Revelation 6:2 When he opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come!” Revelation 6:3 Another came out, a red horse. To him who sat on it was given power to take peace from the earth, and that they should kill one another. There was given to him a great sword. Revelation 6:4 When he opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, “Come and see!” And behold, a black horse, and he who sat on it had a balance in his hand. Revelation 6:5 I heard a voice in the middle of the four living creatures saying, “A choenix of wheat for a denarius, and three choenix of barley for a denarius! Don’t damage the oil and the wine!” Revelation 6:6 When he opened the fourth seal, I heard the fourth living creature saying, “Come and see!” Revelation 6:7 And behold, a pale horse, and the name of he who sat on it was Death. Hades followed with him. Authority over one fourth of the earth, to kill with the sword, with famine, with death, and by the wild animals of the earth was given to him. Revelation 6:8

title: Revelation 6:9–17
context: The fifth seal reveals the souls of martyrs under the altar crying out for justice. They receive white robes and are told to wait until the number of their fellow servants is complete. The sixth seal brings cosmic upheaval, and people of every rank hide from the face of the one on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb.
text: Revelation 6:9–17 Revelation The fifth seal reveals the souls of martyrs under the altar crying out for justice. They receive white robes and are told to wait until the number of their fellow servants is complete. The sixth seal brings cosmic upheaval, and people of every rank hide from the face of the one on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb. When he opened the fifth seal, I saw underneath the altar the souls of those who had been killed for the Word of God, and for the testimony of the Lamb which they had. Revelation 6:9 They cried with a loud voice, saying, “How long, Master, the holy and true, until you judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?” Revelation 6:10 A long white robe was given to each of them. They were told that they should rest yet for a while, until their fellow servants and their brothers, who would also be killed even as they were, should complete their course. Revelation 6:11 I saw when he opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake. The sun became black as sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became as blood. Revelation 6:12 The stars of the sky fell to the earth, like a fig tree dropping its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind. Revelation 6:13 The sky was removed like a scroll when it is rolled up. Every mountain and island was moved out of its place. Revelation 6:14 The kings of the earth, the princes, the commanding officers, the rich, the strong, and every slave and free person, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains. Revelation 6:15 They told the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him who sits on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb, Revelation 6:16 for the great day of his wrath has come, and who is able to stand?” Revelation 6:17

title: Revelation 7:1–8
context: Four angels hold back the winds of judgment until the servants of God are sealed on their foreheads. John hears the number of the sealed: 144,000, twelve thousand from each tribe of Israel.
text: Revelation 7:1–8 Revelation Four angels hold back the winds of judgment until the servants of God are sealed on their foreheads. John hears the number of the sealed: 144,000, twelve thousand from each tribe of Israel. After this, I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the earth, or on the sea, or on any tree. Revelation 7:1 I saw another angel ascend from the sunrise, having the seal of the living God. He cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea, Revelation 7:2 saying, “Don’t harm the earth, the sea, or the trees, until we have sealed the bondservants of our God on their foreheads!” Revelation 7:3 I heard the number of those who were sealed, one hundred forty-four thousand, sealed out of every tribe of the children of Israel: Revelation 7:4 of the tribe of Judah twelve thousand were sealed, of the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand, of the tribe of Gad twelve thousand, Revelation 7:5 of the tribe of Asher twelve thousand, of the tribe of Naphtali twelve thousand, of the tribe of Manasseh twelve thousand, Revelation 7:6 of the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand, of the tribe of Levi twelve thousand, of the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand, Revelation 7:7 of the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand, of the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand, and of the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand were sealed. Revelation 7:8

title: Revelation 7:9–17
context: John sees a great multitude no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, standing before the throne in white robes. They cry that salvation belongs to God and the Lamb. An elder explains that these have come out of the great suffering and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb. God shelters them, and the Lamb shepherds them to springs of living water.
text: Revelation 7:9–17 Revelation John sees a great multitude no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, standing before the throne in white robes. They cry that salvation belongs to God and the Lamb. An elder explains that these have come out of the great suffering and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb. God shelters them, and the Lamb shepherds them to springs of living water. After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands. Revelation 7:9 They cried with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!” Revelation 7:10 All the angels were standing around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures; and they fell on their faces before his throne, and worshiped God, Revelation 7:11 saying, “Amen! Blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might, be to our God forever and ever! Amen.” Revelation 7:12 One of the elders answered, saying to me, “These who are arrayed in the white robes, who are they, and where did they come from?” Revelation 7:13 I told him, “My lord, you know.” He said to me, “These are those who came out of the great suffering. They washed their robes and made them white in the Lamb’s blood. Revelation 7:14 Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve him day and night in his temple. He who sits on the throne will spread his tabernacle over them. Revelation 7:15 They will never be hungry or thirsty any more. The sun won’t beat on them, nor any heat; Revelation 7:16 for the Lamb who is in the middle of the throne shepherds them and leads them to springs of life-giving waters. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.” Revelation 7:17

title: Revelation 8:1–5
context: The Lamb opens the seventh seal, and heaven is silent for about half an hour. Seven angels receive seven trumpets. Another angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, then hurls fire from the altar onto the earth.
text: Revelation 8:1–5 Revelation The Lamb opens the seventh seal, and heaven is silent for about half an hour. Seven angels receive seven trumpets. Another angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, then hurls fire from the altar onto the earth. When he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. Revelation 8:1 I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them. Revelation 8:2 Another angel came and stood over the altar, having a golden censer. Much incense was given to him, that he should add it to the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar which was before the throne. Revelation 8:3 The smoke of the incense, with the prayers of the saints, went up before God out of the angel’s hand. Revelation 8:4 The angel took the censer, and he filled it with the fire of the altar, then threw it on the earth. Thunders, sounds, lightnings, and an earthquake followed. Revelation 8:5

title: Revelation 8:6–13
context: The first four trumpets bring partial judgments on a third of the earth, sea, rivers, and heavens, echoing the plagues of Egypt. An eagle cries woe on those who dwell on the earth because of the trumpets still to come.
text: Revelation 8:6–13 Revelation The first four trumpets bring partial judgments on a third of the earth, sea, rivers, and heavens, echoing the plagues of Egypt. An eagle cries woe on those who dwell on the earth because of the trumpets still to come. The seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound. Revelation 8:6 The first sounded, and there followed hail and fire, mixed with blood, and they were thrown to the earth. One third of the earth was burned up, and one third of the trees were burned up, and all green grass was burned up. Revelation 8:7 The second angel sounded, and something like a great burning mountain was thrown into the sea. One third of the sea became blood, Revelation 8:8 and one third of the living creatures which were in the sea died. One third of the ships were destroyed. Revelation 8:9 The third angel sounded, and a great star fell from the sky, burning like a torch, and it fell on one third of the rivers, and on the springs of water. Revelation 8:10 The name of the star is “Wormwood.” One third of the waters became wormwood. Many people died from the waters, because they were made bitter. Revelation 8:11 The fourth angel sounded, and one third of the sun was struck, and one third of the moon, and one third of the stars, so that one third of them would be darkened; and the day wouldn’t shine for one third of it, and the night in the same way. Revelation 8:12 I saw, and I heard an eagle, flying in mid heaven, saying with a loud voice, “Woe! Woe! Woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the other blasts of the trumpets of the three angels, who are yet to sound!” Revelation 8:13

title: Revelation 9:1–12
context: The fifth trumpet opens the abyss, and smoke releases locust-like creatures that torment for five months those who lack God’s seal. Their king is the angel of the abyss, Abaddon or Apollyon. This is the first woe.
text: Revelation 9:1–12 Revelation The fifth trumpet opens the abyss, and smoke releases locust-like creatures that torment for five months those who lack God’s seal. Their king is the angel of the abyss, Abaddon or Apollyon. This is the first woe. The fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star from the sky which had fallen to the earth. The key to the pit of the abyss was given to him. Revelation 9:1 He opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke went up out of the pit, like the smoke from a burning furnace. The sun and the air were darkened because of the smoke from the pit. Revelation 9:2 Then out of the smoke came locusts on the earth, and power was given to them, as the scorpions of the earth have power. Revelation 9:3 They were told that they should not hurt the grass of the earth, neither any green thing, neither any tree, but only those people who don’t have God’s seal on their foreheads. Revelation 9:4 They were given power, not to kill them, but to torment them for five months. Their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a person. Revelation 9:5 In those days people will seek death, and will in no way find it. They will desire to die, and death will flee from them. Revelation 9:6 The shapes of the locusts were like horses prepared for war. On their heads were something like golden crowns, and their faces were like people’s faces. Revelation 9:7 They had hair like women’s hair, and their teeth were like those of lions. Revelation 9:8 They had breastplates like breastplates of iron. The sound of their wings was like the sound of many chariots and horses rushing to war. Revelation 9:9 They have tails like those of scorpions, with stingers. In their tails they have power to harm men for five months. Revelation 9:10 They have over them as king the angel of the abyss. His name in Hebrew is “Abaddon”, but in Greek, he has the name “Apollyon”. Revelation 9:11 The first woe is past. Behold, there are still two woes coming after this. Revelation 9:12

title: Revelation 9:13–21
context: The sixth trumpet releases four angels bound at the Euphrates and a vast cavalry that kills a third of humanity with fire, smoke, and sulfur. Yet the survivors do not repent of their idolatry, murders, sorceries, immorality, or thefts.
text: Revelation 9:13–21 Revelation The sixth trumpet releases four angels bound at the Euphrates and a vast cavalry that kills a third of humanity with fire, smoke, and sulfur. Yet the survivors do not repent of their idolatry, murders, sorceries, immorality, or thefts. The sixth angel sounded. I heard a voice from the horns of the golden altar which is before God, Revelation 9:13 saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet, “Free the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates!” Revelation 9:14 The four angels were freed who had been prepared for that hour and day and month and year, so that they might kill one third of mankind. Revelation 9:15 The number of the armies of the horsemen was two hundred million. I heard the number of them. Revelation 9:16 Thus I saw the horses in the vision and those who sat on them, having breastplates of fiery red, hyacinth blue, and sulfur yellow; and the horses’ heads resembled lions’ heads. Out of their mouths proceed fire, smoke, and sulfur. Revelation 9:17 By these three plagues, one third of mankind was killed: by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur, which proceeded out of their mouths. Revelation 9:18 For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails. For their tails are like serpents, and have heads; and with them they harm. Revelation 9:19 The rest of mankind, who were not killed with these plagues, didn’t repent of the works of their hands, that they wouldn’t worship demons, and the idols of gold, and of silver, and of brass, and of stone, and of wood, which can’t see, hear, or walk. Revelation 9:20 They didn’t repent of their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality, or their thefts. Revelation 9:21

title: Romans 1:1–7
context: Paul opens his longest letter by introducing himself and his gospel to a church he has not yet visited. He is a servant of Christ, called as an apostle and set apart for the good news God promised through the prophets. That good news concerns God’s Son, descended from David and declared Son of God in power by the resurrection. Paul greets the Roman believers as people called to belong to Jesus Christ and called to be saints. Both traditions share most of this ground. The word “called,” used three times, is where they begin to differ.
text: Romans 1:1–7 Romans Paul opens his longest letter by introducing himself and his gospel to a church he has not yet visited. He is a servant of Christ, called as an apostle and set apart for the good news God promised through the prophets. That good news concerns God’s Son, descended from David and declared Son of God in power by the resurrection. Paul greets the Roman believers as people called to belong to Jesus Christ and called to be saints. Both traditions share most of this ground. The word “called,” used three times, is where they begin to differ. Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God, Romans 1:1 which he promised before through his prophets in the holy Scriptures, Romans 1:2 concerning his Son, who was born of the offspring of David according to the flesh, Romans 1:3 who was declared to be the Son of God with power according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord, Romans 1:4 through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations for his name’s sake; Romans 1:5 among whom you are also called to belong to Jesus Christ; Romans 1:6 to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Romans 1:7

title: Romans 1:16–17
context: These two verses state the theme of Romans. Paul is not ashamed of the gospel, because it is God’s power to save everyone who believes, Jew first and also Greek, and in it God’s righteousness is revealed by faith. Luther’s rediscovery of verse 17 helped launch the Reformation, and both Arminian and Reformed Protestants stand on it. Their difference lies in how the gospel’s power relates to the faith of those who hear it.
text: Romans 1:16–17 Romans These two verses state the theme of Romans. Paul is not ashamed of the gospel, because it is God’s power to save everyone who believes, Jew first and also Greek, and in it God’s righteousness is revealed by faith. Luther’s rediscovery of verse 17 helped launch the Reformation, and both Arminian and Reformed Protestants stand on it. Their difference lies in how the gospel’s power relates to the faith of those who hear it. For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek. Romans 1:16 For in it is revealed God’s righteousness from faith to faith. As it is written, “But the righteous shall live by faith.” Romans 1:17

title: Romans 1:18–32
context: Having announced the gospel, Paul shows why it is needed. God’s wrath is revealed against human ungodliness, because people suppress the truth about God that creation makes plain. Refusing to honor him, they turned to idols, and God gave them over to the desires, passions, and corrupt thinking they chose. Both traditions read the passage as a portrait of fallen humanity. They differ mainly on what general revelation means for human ability and on how to describe God’s “giving them up.”
text: Romans 1:18–32 Romans Having announced the gospel, Paul shows why it is needed. God’s wrath is revealed against human ungodliness, because people suppress the truth about God that creation makes plain. Refusing to honor him, they turned to idols, and God gave them over to the desires, passions, and corrupt thinking they chose. Both traditions read the passage as a portrait of fallen humanity. They differ mainly on what general revelation means for human ability and on how to describe God’s “giving them up.” For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men who suppress the truth in unrighteousness, Romans 1:18 because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them. Romans 1:19 For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse. Romans 1:20 Because knowing God, they didn’t glorify him as God, and didn’t give thanks, but became vain in their reasoning, and their senseless heart was darkened. Romans 1:21 Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, Romans 1:22 and traded the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things. Romans 1:23 Therefore God also gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves; Romans 1:24 who exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen. Romans 1:25 For this reason, God gave them up to vile passions. For their women changed the natural function into that which is against nature. Romans 1:26 Likewise also the men, leaving the natural function of the woman, burned in their lust toward one another, men doing what is inappropriate with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error. Romans 1:27 Even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting; Romans 1:28 being filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits, secret slanderers, Romans 1:29 backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Romans 1:30 without understanding, covenant breakers, without natural affection, unforgiving, unmerciful; Romans 1:31 who, knowing the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them. Romans 1:32

title: Romans 1:8–15
context: Before laying out his gospel, Paul tells the Roman church how he prays for them and why he wants to visit. He thanks God that their faith is reported throughout the world, longs to share spiritual blessing with them, and explains that he has often been prevented from coming. He sees himself as a debtor to all kinds of people and is eager to preach the gospel in Rome too. These verses are pastoral common ground, though each tradition draws out its own emphases.
text: Romans 1:8–15 Romans Before laying out his gospel, Paul tells the Roman church how he prays for them and why he wants to visit. He thanks God that their faith is reported throughout the world, longs to share spiritual blessing with them, and explains that he has often been prevented from coming. He sees himself as a debtor to all kinds of people and is eager to preach the gospel in Rome too. These verses are pastoral common ground, though each tradition draws out its own emphases. First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world. Romans 1:8 For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Good News of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you always in my prayers, Romans 1:9 requesting, if by any means now at last I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you. Romans 1:10 For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established; Romans 1:11 that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine. Romans 1:12 Now I don’t desire to have you unaware, brothers, that I often planned to come to you (and was hindered so far), that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles. Romans 1:13 I am debtor both to Greeks and to foreigners, both to the wise and to the foolish. Romans 1:14 So as much as is in me, I am eager to preach the Good News to you also who are in Rome. Romans 1:15

title: Romans 10:1–13
context: Paul turns from God’s choosing to Israel’s response. He prays for Israel’s salvation and grieves that their zeal for God is not based on knowledge: they sought their own righteousness instead of submitting to God’s. Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes, and the word of faith is near: whoever confesses Jesus as Lord and believes God raised him will be saved. Both traditions hear a universal offer here. Arminian readers see it as decisive for reading Romans 9; Reformed readers see it as the means through which God’s election is carried out.
text: Romans 10:1–13 Romans Paul turns from God’s choosing to Israel’s response. He prays for Israel’s salvation and grieves that their zeal for God is not based on knowledge: they sought their own righteousness instead of submitting to God’s. Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes, and the word of faith is near: whoever confesses Jesus as Lord and believes God raised him will be saved. Both traditions hear a universal offer here. Arminian readers see it as decisive for reading Romans 9; Reformed readers see it as the means through which God’s election is carried out. Brothers, my heart’s desire and my prayer to God is for Israel, that they may be saved. Romans 10:1 For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. Romans 10:2 For being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they didn’t subject themselves to the righteousness of God. Romans 10:3 For Christ is the fulfillment of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes. Romans 10:4 For Moses writes about the righteousness of the law, “The one who does them will live by them.” Romans 10:5 But the righteousness which is of faith says this, “Don’t say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down); Romans 10:6 or, ‘Who will descend into the abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.)” Romans 10:7 But what does it say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart;” that is, the word of faith which we preach: Romans 10:8 that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. Romans 10:9 For with the heart one believes resulting in righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made resulting in salvation. Romans 10:10 For the Scripture says, “Whoever believes in him will not be disappointed.” Romans 10:11 For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord is Lord of all, and is rich to all who call on him. Romans 10:12 For, “Whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved.” Romans 10:13

title: Romans 10:14–21
context: Paul traces the chain that leads to salvation: sending, preaching, hearing, believing, and calling. Faith comes by hearing the word of Christ. Israel has heard, yet many have not obeyed, while Gentiles who were not seeking God have found him. The section ends with God holding out his hands all day long to a disobedient people. Arminian readers find here a sincere offer that Israel refused; Reformed readers agree the offer was sincere and see God’s purpose behind both the hearing and the believing.
text: Romans 10:14–21 Romans Paul traces the chain that leads to salvation: sending, preaching, hearing, believing, and calling. Faith comes by hearing the word of Christ. Israel has heard, yet many have not obeyed, while Gentiles who were not seeking God have found him. The section ends with God holding out his hands all day long to a disobedient people. Arminian readers find here a sincere offer that Israel refused; Reformed readers agree the offer was sincere and see God’s purpose behind both the hearing and the believing. How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? How will they hear without a preacher? Romans 10:14 And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!” Romans 10:15 But they didn’t all listen to the glad news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our report?” Romans 10:16 So faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Romans 10:17 But I say, didn’t they hear? Yes, most certainly, “Their sound went out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.” Romans 10:18 But I ask, didn’t Israel know? First Moses says, “I will provoke you to jealousy with that which is no nation. I will make you angry with a nation void of understanding.” Romans 10:19 Isaiah is very bold and says, “I was found by those who didn’t seek me. I was revealed to those who didn’t ask for me.” Romans 10:20 But about Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.” Romans 10:21

title: Romans 11:1–10
context: Has God rejected his people? Paul’s answer is no. He himself is an Israelite, and as in Elijah’s day, God has kept a remnant chosen by grace. The rest were hardened, as Scripture foretold. Reformed readers see in the “election of grace” a clear statement of unconditional election. Arminian readers see a remnant that believes, with hardening as God’s judgment on persistent unbelief.
text: Romans 11:1–10 Romans Has God rejected his people? Paul’s answer is no. He himself is an Israelite, and as in Elijah’s day, God has kept a remnant chosen by grace. The rest were hardened, as Scripture foretold. Reformed readers see in the “election of grace” a clear statement of unconditional election. Arminian readers see a remnant that believes, with hardening as God’s judgment on persistent unbelief. I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. Romans 11:1 God didn’t reject his people, whom he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel: Romans 11:2 “Lord, they have killed your prophets. They have broken down your altars. I am left alone, and they seek my life.” Romans 11:3 But how does God answer him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.” Romans 11:4 Even so too at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. Romans 11:5 And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is of works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work. Romans 11:6 What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he didn’t obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened. Romans 11:7 According as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.” Romans 11:8 David says, “Let their table be made a snare, a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to them. Romans 11:9 Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see. Always keep their backs bent.” Romans 11:10

title: Romans 11:11–24
context: Israel’s stumbling is not final. Through their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke Israel to jealousy, and their full inclusion will mean life from the dead. Paul then uses the image of an olive tree: natural branches were broken off because of unbelief, wild branches were grafted in by faith, and Gentiles must not boast, because God can cut them off and graft Israel back in. Arminian readers find here a clear warning that believers can be cut off; Reformed readers read the warning in terms of the visible people of God and as a means of perseverance.
text: Romans 11:11–24 Romans Israel’s stumbling is not final. Through their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke Israel to jealousy, and their full inclusion will mean life from the dead. Paul then uses the image of an olive tree: natural branches were broken off because of unbelief, wild branches were grafted in by faith, and Gentiles must not boast, because God can cut them off and graft Israel back in. Arminian readers find here a clear warning that believers can be cut off; Reformed readers read the warning in terms of the visible people of God and as a means of perseverance. I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy. Romans 11:11 Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness! Romans 11:12 For I speak to you who are Gentiles. Since then as I am an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry, Romans 11:13 if by any means I may provoke to jealousy those who are my flesh, and may save some of them. Romans 11:14 For if the rejection of them is the reconciling of the world, what would their acceptance be, but life from the dead? Romans 11:15 If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches. Romans 11:16 But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree, Romans 11:17 don’t boast over the branches. But if you boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you. Romans 11:18 You will say then, “Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.” Romans 11:19 True; by their unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by your faith. Don’t be conceited, but fear; Romans 11:20 for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you. Romans 11:21 See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off. Romans 11:22 They also, if they don’t continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again. Romans 11:23 For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree? Romans 11:24

title: Romans 11:25–36
context: Paul reveals a mystery: a partial hardening has come on Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, and so all Israel will be saved. As regards the gospel, Israel are enemies; as regards election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake, because God’s gifts and calling are irrevocable. God has bound all to disobedience so that he may have mercy on all. The section ends with a doxology to the depth of God’s wisdom. Both traditions debate the meaning of “all Israel”; their main difference here concerns how mercy on “all” relates to election.
text: Romans 11:25–36 Romans Paul reveals a mystery: a partial hardening has come on Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, and so all Israel will be saved. As regards the gospel, Israel are enemies; as regards election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake, because God’s gifts and calling are irrevocable. God has bound all to disobedience so that he may have mercy on all. The section ends with a doxology to the depth of God’s wisdom. Both traditions debate the meaning of “all Israel”; their main difference here concerns how mercy on “all” relates to election. For I don’t desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you won’t be wise in your own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, Romans 11:25 and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob. Romans 11:26 This is my covenant with them, when I will take away their sins.” Romans 11:27 Concerning the Good News, they are enemies for your sake. But concerning the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake. Romans 11:28 For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
